entries.name: Mech_ComponentGeometryTest_Candidate
entries.description: Per-candidate coarse geometry test, called by Mech_SelectStruckComponent.

entries.name: Mech_SelectStruckComponent
entries.description: Deterministic single-component selection via real hit geometry -- iterates up to 29 component slots, tracks best match, returns exactly the one struck (no randomness, unlike the explosive path).

entries.name: Collision_FindClusterInNode
entries.description: Linear search over one node's 16-byte clusters for a matching component index (cluster+6). Helper for Collision_FindClusterForComponent.

entries.name: Collision_FindClusterForComponent
entries.description: Walks a collision model's nodes looking for the cluster that owns a given component index, via Collision_FindClusterInNode; returns the cluster and writes the owning node index out. Used by Component_DestroyAndCascade to place a destroyed component's debris, not by the hit test.

entries.name: Collision_CollectNodeAnchors
entries.description: (node, components, nodeIds, points): for each of the node's int16 count (+4) 16-byte cluster records at +6, writes the record's +6 component index to components[i], a pointer to the record's +8 sphere centre to points[i] and the node's own int16 +0 to nodeIds[i]; returns the count. Collision_CollectComponentAnchors calls it per node.

entries.name: Collision_CollectComponentAnchors
entries.description: Walks a loaded .COL model's nodes and emits one (componentIndex, nodeIndex, pointer to the cluster's load-time bounding-sphere centre) triple per cluster into three caller-supplied parallel arrays, returning the count. Per node it delegates to Collision_CollectNodeAnchors, which strides the 16-byte cluster records reading componentIndex at +6 and taking the address of the bound centre at +8. Called once, from Mech_ConfigureLoadout, feeding HercPiece_BindComponentAnchors.

entries.name: CollisionTable_Reserve
entries.description: (n): returns CollisionTable_Count (004987dc) and adds n to it -- the collision twin of DmgTable_Reserve.

entries.name: CollisionTable_Alloc
entries.description: When CollisionTable_Count is non-zero, CollisionTable_Array = Mem_NewArray(CollisionTable_Count * 6). DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it after DmgTable_Alloc.

entries.name: Collision_ReadCluster
entries.description: Reads a cluster's component index into the record's +6, then its sphere array via Collision_ReadSphereArray into +0/+2. The component index is what makes a destroyed section stop blocking shots. Was named Collision_LoadSubSphereFlag: the value it reads is the component index, not a flag, and the branch it guards is on the read succeeding rather than on the value.

entries.name: Collision_ReadNode
entries.description: Reads one node of a collision model: int16 node index (-1 = the object's own frame, otherwise an index resolved through the shape instance's node-transform array) and int16 cluster count, then that many 16-byte clusters via Collision_ReadCluster. Was named Collision_LoadSubSpheres, which described the shape one level off.

entries.name: Collision_ComputeAllBoundingSpheres
entries.description: (model): for each of the int16 count at model+4 16-byte nodes at model+6, Collision_ComputeBoundingSphere(node, node+8) and stores the returned radius at node+0xe. Collision_LoadRecordArray calls it.

entries.name: Collision_LoadRecordArray
entries.description: Reads one object's whole collision model: an int16 node count, then that many 10-byte nodes via Collision_ReadNode, each post-processed by Collision_ComputeBoundingSphere. Called per structure type against dat/BASECOL.DAT (from Base_LoadResources, 00405fac) and per mech/flyer type against col/<NAME>.COL (from Collision_RegisterObject). Format and retail verification in docs/simulation/hit-detection.md.

entries.name: Collision_RegisterObject
entries.description: collide.cpp. Top-level collision-model entry point: allocates the next slot in the fixed collision-object table, then calls Collision_LoadRecordArray.

entries.name: Component_AllDependentsDestroyed
entries.description: Whether every dependent sub-piece a component's .DMG record lists is destroyed (-1). Used only by Component_IsFullyDestroyed.

entries.name: Component_SpillIntoDependents
entries.description: Pours a destroyed component's overflow damage into its dependent sub-pieces, one at a time. The pick is weighted and random: each live dependent contributes its .DMG CritChance to a total, a draw under that total selects one, and if the spill destroys it the remainder goes round again. Returns true only when no live dependents remain -- which is the condition Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade requires before it will cascade.

entries.name: HercPiece_ReadRecord
entries.description: Loads one 18-byte .DMG HercPiece record: max health, debris-flags index pair, bone id (bone/destruction-group key), destruction-flags bitfield, dependent sub-component list pointer+count.

entries.name: HercPiece_CopyRecord
entries.description: (dst, src): copies the 0x12-byte piece record, then gives dst its own copy of the dependent list: Mem_NewArray(count * 4) for the int16 count at +6, filled from src's list (+8).

entries.name: HercPiece_LoadTable
entries.description: Loads the .DMG per-mech component table: the int16 internal count (+0xa) and that many int16 internal maxima (array at +4), then the int16 piece count (+8) and that many 18-byte HercPiece records (array at +0, via HercPiece_ReadRecord).

entries.name: HercPiece_SetInternalMaxima
entries.description: (pieceTable, indices, values, count): for each i < count stores values[i] in the table's int16 internal-maximum array (+4) at indices[i]. Mech_ConfigureLoadout calls it once per weapon mount with count 1.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0040d128; table layout from HercPiece_LoadTable

entries.name: Damage_LoadMechDmgFile
entries.description: damage.cpp dispatch/setup that opens dmg\[herc].DMG (filename built from the mech's own name string) and drives HercPiece_LoadTable. Called from the mech constructor.

entries.name: DmgTable_Reserve
entries.description: (n): returns DmgTable_Count (00498856) and adds n to it. maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate and FlyerType_Register reserve one each.

entries.name: DmgTable_Alloc
entries.description: When DmgTable_Count is non-zero, DmgTable_Array = Mem_NewArray(DmgTable_Count * 0xc). DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it after GunLayout_AllocTable.

entries.name: HercPiece_ReplacePieces
entries.description: (pieceTable, indices, records, count): for each i < count overwrites the 0x12-byte piece at indices[i] (array at +0) with HercPiece_CopyRecord of records[i]. The piece's previous dependent list is not freed. Mech_ConfigureLoadout calls it once per weapon mount with count 1.

entries.name: HercPiece_BindComponentAnchors
entries.description: Writes the .COL-derived anchors into the .DMG piece table: for each of count entries, piece[componentIndices[i]] at stride 0x12 gets +0x0c = nodeIndices[i] and +0x0e = points[i]. These are the two runtime-only HercPiece fields Mech_ComponentPosition reads. The write is UNGUARDED, so the last cluster naming a component wins; every retail mech .COL names each component exactly once, so it never bites.
entries.signature: void __cdecl HercPiece_BindComponentAnchors(int *pieceTable, short count, short *componentIndices, short *nodeIndices, int **points)

entries.name: Component_AllocDamageArrays
entries.description: Allocates the header of pointers at mech+0x206: a 22-entry dependent-subpiece DAMAGE array, a 29-entry main-component DAMAGE array, and a 29-entry active-flag array (all zeroed except the flag array, filled 0x01). Zeroed means undamaged, not destroyed -- these accumulate damage rather than hold remaining health. See Component_ReadDamagePercent.

entries.name: Component_LinkMaxRefData
entries.description: Wires up mech+0x212 (and neighboring fields) as a pointer into per-component maximum/reference data, sourced from the mech's own .DMG-derived pointer plus its Collision_RegisterObject registration record.

entries.name: Component_AddDamage
entries.description: Adds damage to one component/dependent damage entry. An entry already holding -1 (destroyed) absorbs nothing. An entry the damage finishes stores -1 rather than the max and writes the EXCESS back through the damage pointer, which is what Component_SpillIntoDependents runs on. Returns whether the entry is now destroyed.

entries.name: Component_DestroyAndCascade
entries.description: Destroys a component and walks the destruction-dependency group named by its .DMG bone id, destroying every sibling that shares it. Also the whole of what a lost part puts on screen: the .DMG record's +0x03 (the TSCellAnimPart sequence this component drives) gates a fire and is stepped to its blank cell, an explosion goes off at the component's own composed frame -- type 0x11 and a one-per-cascade-group latch at DAT_004a98b0 when the .DMG destruction flags' bit 2 is set, type 10 otherwise -- and the +0x02 debris group is thrown, falling back to group 2 when it states -1.

entries.name: Component_IsFullyDestroyed
entries.description: Component destroyed AND all of its dependents destroyed. The stricter of the two 'is this gone' tests; Mech_ComponentDamageWrite asks it of the two cockpit slots (0 and 1) as the mech's death gate.

entries.name: Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade
entries.description: Subtracts damage from a component's current value (via a helper); if the component crosses into 'destroyed', cascades via Component_DestroyAndCascade.

entries.name: Component_ReadOverallDamage
entries.description: One object's whole damage as a Q8 fraction, 0 pristine and 256 destroyed: every main component and every dependent weighed once against its own maximum, a destroyed one counting as its full maximum. Reached through the object's vtable +0x40 and printed by the MFD status screen's integrity readout.

entries.name: Component_ReadDamagePercent
entries.description: Reads a component's ACCUMULATED DAMAGE as Q8 (0-256), 0 = pristine and 256 = destroyed -- not health. Component_AllocDamageArrays zeroes the arrays at init and the write path (FUN_0040d3ec) ADDS damage to the entry, capping it at the record's max and storing -1 once destroyed; this read substitutes the max for a -1 entry, so a destroyed component reads as fully damaged. Aggregates the component's own value with all its dependent sub-components before computing (totalDamage<<8)/totalMax. Callers read it as damage, not health, including the pod-bonus curves in FUN_00417d08/FUN_00417bec and the mech+0x317 locomotion term.

entries.name: Component_TotalArmor
entries.description: Everything a component has to lose: its own armour plus the maximum of every internal mapped onto it, walking the piece's mapped-internals list. The denominator Component_ReadDamagePercent divides by, and the scale Mech_SpreadImpactDamage multiplies by. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] pointer, [EBP+0xc] word.

entries.name: Shape_TranslatePointLists
entries.description: Adds a point offset into a shape's own geometry, recursing on the part-list types and, at a group, marking the points its polys actually reference (poly+6, plus poly+8 entries from the index list at poly+0x0a) and adding the offset to those only. Used to move a freshly-loaded weapon model to its hardpoint's mount point.

entries.name: WeaponMount_RenderWithDetailBias
entries.description: Vtable +0x1c of GUN_STATE (00498e44) and all ten weapon-mount classes below it, in place of CONFIG_PART's own ConfigPart_Render: pushes g_TSDetailBiasFromHercDetail into the TSDetailPart bias via TSDetailPart_SetBias, runs ConfigPart_Render on the mount -- its weapon model with its own flipbook frames -- and restores the bias to 0. The same bracket Structure_DrawWithDetailBias applies, but from the HERC DETAIL table rather than the STRUCTURE DETAIL one.

entries.name: WeaponMount_MatchGaugeNever
entries.description: GUN_STATE's vtable +0x58 gauge-match slot (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN and the five pods: returns 0 unconditionally, so WeaponMounts_SelectByGauge can never find a pod. The energy and ammunition classes (WeaponMount_EnergyMatchGauge, WeaponMount_AmmoMatchGauge) compare the argument against the mount's own gauge pointer at +0x77 instead. Together with the pod constructor clearing the selectable byte +0x4c, this is why a pod's cockpit row cannot be armed.

entries.name: WeaponMount_EnergyMatchGauge
entries.description: ENERGY_WPN and ELF_WPN vtable +0x58: returns gauge == mount+0x77, the mount's own cockpit gauge. WeaponMounts_SelectByGauge finds the mount a clicked row belongs to with it.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AmmoMatchGauge
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x58: returns gauge == mount+0x77, the same comparison as WeaponMount_EnergyMatchGauge.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CtorBase
entries.description: Base weapon-mount constructor, run by every mount class before its own. Loads the hardpoint's weapon model when the .GL mounting code (+6) is under 4 via WeaponMount_ShapeForMountingCode, installs it with ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames at mount+0x10, translates its point lists to the mount point with Shape_TranslatePointLists, resolves the two .GL aim nodes at +2/+4 (both -1 on every retail chassis), zeroes the flag blocks at +0x33/+0x3b/+0x43, and writes the refire scale 0x400 to +0x63.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CtorEnergy
entries.description: Energy mount constructor (vtable 00498dcc): writes Math_Q10Multiply(820, 1200) = 960 into both the charge target (+0x7b) and the capacitor level (+0x7d), and 20 into the charge rate (+0x7f). All three are literals shared by every energy weapon. Used for weapon ids 6-12, 17, 19, 20 and 22-25, 28.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CreateEnergyGauge
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x64, the gauge factory WeaponMounts_BuildGauges dispatches: CockpitView_CreateEnergyWeaponGauge(CockpitViewInstance, the hardpoint record's row byte +7, mount) into +0x77, then one EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState with the gauge's own block and block[1] set to the raw charge target (+0x7b) -- not the (target << 10) / 1200 WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState pushes.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CtorAmmunition
entries.description: Ammunition mount constructor (vtable 00498d54): reads the magazine size from the template's +0x3a into +0x7b and the same value shifted left 8 into +0x7d, so the mount powers up with a full magazine and its gauge prints +0x7d >> 8. Used for weapon ids 1-5, 13-16, 21 and 26.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetDisplayName
entries.description: The name a weapon gauge prints for a mount. If the mount's resolved PROJ.DAT record (+0x20) is null or its category is non-zero, copies the template's name pointer (+0x52, written by Weapons_LoadResourceTables from the 33-entry array at 00498eb0). If the record is a Missile (category 0), copies MissileAmmoNameTable[record.subtypeId] instead -- so a launcher is named by its loaded ammunition (ARH, SARH, ...), not by its weapon id. Returns a pointer to the shared scratch buffer at 004a9954.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CreateAmmoGauge
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x64, the gauge factory WeaponMounts_BuildGauges dispatches: CockpitView_CreateAmmoWeaponGauge(CockpitViewInstance, the hardpoint record's row byte (+0x18)+7, mount) into +0x77. The energy counterpart is WeaponMount_CreateEnergyGauge.

entries.name: Pod_CtorBase
entries.description: Shared constructor for the five equipment pods, run between WeaponMount_CtorBase and each pod's own. Installs the pod base vtable 00498cdc and writes -1 to the catalog id at pod+0x77. A pod diverges from the weapon-mount layout here: +0x77 is a short catalog id and +0x79 the cockpit gauge handle, where an ammunition mount keeps the gauge handle at +0x77.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl Pod_CtorBase(void *pod, int shapeInstance, int hardpoint, int weaponTemplate)

entries.name: EcmPod_Ctor
entries.description: ECM pod (catalog id 0x12, mech+0x307). Vtable 00498c64.

entries.name: TurboPod_Ctor
entries.description: Turbo Pod (catalog id 0x1f, mech+0x317). Vtable 00498bec, and the only pod whose constructor arms anything: 2000 of charge at +0x7d and the engaged flag at +0x81 clear.

entries.name: TargetingPod_Ctor
entries.description: Targeting Pod (catalog id 0x1d, mech+0x30b). Vtable 00498b74, object size 0x8a -- the extra bytes over the other pods are the component lock at +0x7d/+0x86 and its decay timer at +0x81. It writes none of them, so a pod starts with whatever its arena block holds; the cursor is always set by TargetingPod_ResetComponentLock before anything reads it.

entries.name: ShieldPod_Ctor
entries.description: Shield Pod (catalog id 0x1e, mech+0x30f). Vtable 00498afc.

entries.name: EnergyPod_Ctor
entries.description: Energy Pod (catalog id 0x20, mech+0x313). Vtable 00498a84.

entries.name: EcmPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: ECM pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: TurboPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: Turbo Pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: EnergyPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: Energy Pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: ShieldPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: Shield Pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: TargetingPod_CreateGauge
entries.description: Targeting Pod vtable +0x64.

entries.name: TargetingPod_ResetComponentLock
entries.description: Targeting Pod (mech+0x30b): the selection changed, so restart the component rotation. Sets the cursor pod+0x7d to 0 when the new target exists and its target class (obj+0x1a8) is 0, and to -1 otherwise -- which is what fences component targeting, and with it the target's vtable +0x58/+0x80/+0x84, off everything that is not a HERC. Called once per selection change by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate, which is the only writer of the player's mech+0x1a4.

entries.name: TargetingPod_CycleComponent
entries.description: Targeting Pod: step the component lock on. Asks the target's vtable +0x80 (NextTargetableComponent) for the next component it still has, storing the new cursor in pod+0x7d and letting the slot write the resolved component id into pod+0x86. This is the manual's [Tab]: CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand's scancode 0x0f case calls it directly. TargetingPod_ResolveAimPoint calls it too, to move off a component that has since been shot away.

entries.name: TargetingPod_ResolveAimPoint
entries.description: Targeting Pod: the pod half of Player_ResolveTargetAimPoint. With a live cursor (pod+0x7d >= 0) and pod damage under 0x9b it reports the locked component's position through the target's vtable +0x58 and its id through outComponentId, advancing the lock first if vtable +0x84 says the component is gone; past 0x68 of damage it also runs a 5 s countdown at pod+0x81 that drops the lock. Otherwise it falls back to the target's vtable +0x24 aim node, or the raw origin, and reports no component. The fourth parameter -- the caller passes the target's occupancy-array pointer mech+0x20e -- is never read: [EBP+0x14] is untouched in the whole body.
entries.signature: void __cdecl TargetingPod_ResolveAimPoint(void *pod, void *target, int *outPoint, void *unused, short *outHasComponent, short *outComponentId)

entries.name: WeaponMount_RangeAllows
entries.description: template+0x2c < range < template+0x30, both bounds exclusive: the weapon's engagement window. The lower bound is zero in all 33 retail templates. Asked by Ai_ChooseWeapon, by Ai_FireAtPoint's ELF latch, and by WeaponMounts_MountIsReady, which is what reddens a player's row and makes the firing chain skip a weapon that cannot reach the selected target.

entries.name: WeaponMount_HardpointBoneId
entries.description: Returns the mount's .GL record +0, the hardpoint's bone id. The same id WeaponMount_PrepareShot resolves the firing frame from, so the drawn weapon and its shot ride one node.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetEnergyAmmoType
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x60: writes 0 through its optional out pointer and returns a constant 5. The ammunition counterpart is WeaponMount_GetAmmoType. WeaponMounts_FireTrigger sets DAT_004d25ac and DAT_004d25aa, the electro-optical missile flags, when this returns 3, which an energy mount never can.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetAmmoType
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable+0x60: returns the resolved PROJ.DAT record's subtype id when that record is a Missile (category 0), otherwise 5. Callers treat 5 and 3 as always-available and gate the other values on the manager's per-ammunition-type counters at manager+0x0a. The energy class returns a constant 5 from this slot (FUN_0040e62c).

entries.name: Pod_TriggerHeldNever
entries.description: POD_WPN vtable +0x30 (00498cdc), kept by all five pods: returns 0, so a pod never reports its trigger held.

entries.name: ElfMount_TriggerHeld
entries.description: ElfMountVtable +0x30, a spin-up rather than the plain trigger read WeaponMount_TriggerHeld does. While the latch +0x48 is clear it returns 0 -- no shot -- and a fresh press instead sets +0x47 and resets the cell timer at +0x84; ElfMount_SpinUpAndChargeTick then walks the muzzle-flash flipbook and latches +0x48 at the last cell. Once latched it returns the input device's fire byte, and release clears +0x48 and rewinds the flipbook. ELF2 SKIPS THE SPIN-UP: the function opens by forcing both flags to 1 when template+0x56 (the record's self-index) is 22.

entries.name: GrenadeMount_TriggerHeld
entries.description: GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x30 (00499248), (mount, input): a hold-to-throw trigger. Idle (+0x46 clear), a press (input+0xd) starts it -- +0x46 = 1, +0x81 = 20000 -- and returns 0. While charging it returns 1 on release; held, it adds 1000 to +0x81 per call and returns 1 once that passes 100000, calling Input_LatchButton(1, 1) as it does.

entries.name: WeaponMount_PrepareShot
entries.description: The fire prologue both dispatchers open with. Resolves the firing hardpoint's bone (.GL +0) to its posed node transform, composes the gun convergence (mount+0x24/+0x28, gated on mount+0x5b/+0x5f) under it and the mech's own transform (mech+0x12) over it into the global shot transform at 004a98b8, transforms the muzzle offset into world space at 004a98d8, extracts the firing euler triple to 004a98e4, and arms the refire timer as Math_Q10Multiply(mount+0x63, template+0x4c). Both convergence gates read zero fleet-wide, so the rotation is live.

entries.name: Pod_FireNoOp
entries.description: POD_WPN vtable +0x28 (00498cdc), kept by all five pods: an empty fire dispatch.

entries.name: WeaponMount_FireDispatch_Missile
entries.description: Missile-capable-hardpoint fire dispatcher: checks the mount's cached PROJ.DAT Type field, Type==Missile(0) -> Rocket_Fire, else falls through to the shared Bullet fallback.

entries.name: GrenadeMount_FireDispatch
entries.description: GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x28 (00499248), (mount, a, b): WeaponMount_PrepareShot(mount, a); takes one round off +0x7b when the third argument (a short) is zero; clears the charging latch +0x46; then Grenade_FireNoOp.

entries.name: WeaponMount_FireDispatch_GunBeam
entries.description: Energy/gun mount vtable +0x28, the fire dispatch. Opens with WeaponMount_PrepareShot, then branches on the mount's cached PROJ.DAT Type: Type==4(Beam) spends min(template+0x38, capacitor +0x7d) out of the capacitor and calls Bullet_FireBurst with that as the shot's power, having first copied the muzzle world point into the shot transform's translation; otherwise it builds a travelling Bullet, with a second barrel when template+0x3c==3 and a burst follow-up when template+0x3e==0x13.

entries.name: ElfMount_FireDispatch
entries.description: ElfMountVtable +0x28. WeaponMount_PrepareShot, then one branch -- an ELF is always a Beam record. Two deliberate differences from WeaponMount_FireDispatch_GunBeam's beam branch: the cost template+0x38 is subtracted UNCONDITIONALLY rather than capped at the charge, so the last partial shot takes the capacitor negative and ends the burst through ElfMount_CanFire; and the shot power handed to Bullet_FireBurst is the LITERAL 0x4b0 (1200), not the charge spent, so every shot of a burst lands at full strength however far the capacitor has drained.

entries.name: Pod_CanFireNever
entries.description: POD_WPN vtable +0x2c (00498cdc), kept by all five pods: returns 0, so WeaponMounts_FireTrigger never finds a pod ready.

entries.name: WeaponMount_EnergyCanFire
entries.description: Energy mount vtable+0x2c: not destroyed (+0x49), refire timer (+0x31) expired, and charge (+0x7d) at or above a threshold taken from the template's +0x36/+0x38 pair -- max(+0x36, +0x7b) when +0x36 < +0x38, otherwise +0x38 outright. Both shapes occur in retail data (EMP 350/10000, LAS100 80/80). NOT the test the ELFs use, despite their (400, 70) template -- they have their own class, see ElfMount_CanFire.

entries.name: WeaponMount_EnergyIsSpent
entries.description: ENERGY_WPN and ELF_WPN vtable +0x5c: returns the destroyed byte +0x49, sign-extended. Ai_ChooseWeapon passes over a mount whose +0x5c answers non-zero, and latches 'no weapons left' when every mount does.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AmmoIsSpent
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x5c: returns 1 when the rounds remaining (+0x7b) are zero or the mount is destroyed (+0x49), otherwise 0. Ai_ChooseWeapon passes over a spent mount.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AmmoCanFire
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable+0x2c: not destroyed (+0x49), refire timer (+0x31) expired, and at least one round left (+0x7b != 0).

entries.name: ElfMount_CanFire
entries.description: ElfMountVtable +0x2c, AND THE REASON AN ELF CANNOT BE RE-TRIGGERED UNTIL ITS CAPACITOR IS FULL. Same two template fields as WeaponMount_EnergyCanFire with the branch between them dropped, so the threshold is ALWAYS max(template+0x36, mount+0x7b): !destroyed && (charge >= max(+0x36, chargeTarget) || (mount+0x33 && charge >= template+0x38)). Both ELFs read +0x36 = 400 against a 960 charge target, so a fresh trigger pull needs the full capacitor; the +0x33 clause is the sustain, dropping the bar to one shot's 70 while the mount is firing every tick. No refire-timer term, consistent with both ELF templates carrying a +0x4c of zero.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AutoFireDue
entries.description: Reports a mount as due for an auto-fire follow-up shot: refire timer (+0x31) expired AND the burst-continues flag (+0x4d) set. Only WeaponMount_FireDispatch_GunBeam's multi-shot branch ever sets +0x4d, and never on the beam path, so a beam weapon never reports due.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase
entries.description: Base weapon-mount vtable +0x68, the condition notification Mech_ComponentDamageWrite pushes through every mount with its component's reading before and after the write. A reading of 0x100 destroys the mount, with no roll.
entries.signature: void __cdecl WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase(void *mount, void *mech, int before, int after)

entries.name: WeaponMount_ConditionChangedEnergy
entries.description: ENERGY_WPN and ELF_WPN vtable +0x68: WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase, then sets the charge rate +0x7f to 20, less Math_Q10Multiply(20, ((reading - 0x80) / 0x19) * 100) when the reading (last argument) is past 0x80 -- a damaged energy mount charges more slowly. The two weapon-carrying classes' other override is WeaponMount_ConditionChanged.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ConditionChanged
entries.description: Vtable +0x68 of the ammunition classes, PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN (the energy classes install WeaponMount_ConditionChangedEnergy). Runs the base slot, then, while the mount is not empty (+0x7b) and the reading is past 0x80: a Missile mount rolls rand & 0x3ff < 300 for each 25 points crossed and the first success destroys it; a Bullet mount instead sets its refire scale mount+0x63 = 0x400 - steps * 0x66, which makes a damaged gun fire FASTER since WeaponMount_PrepareShot multiplies by it; a Beam mount gets neither.
entries.signature: void __cdecl WeaponMount_ConditionChanged(void *mount, void *mech, int before, int after)

entries.name: TargetingPod_ConditionChanged
entries.description: Targeting Pod vtable +0x68, and the only pod that overrides the base notification: after WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase it caches the component reading the damage write just produced in pod+0x7f. Every degradation of the pod is a threshold on that cached value. The Shield and Energy pods take the other route and read their damage live through Component_ReadDamagePercent.
entries.signature: void __cdecl TargetingPod_ConditionChanged(void *pod, void *mech, int before, int after)

entries.name: WeaponMount_RefireTick
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable +0x34, and the first thing WeaponMount_ChargeCapacitor does for an energy mount: counts the refire timer (+0x31) down by SimTickDelta via Math_CountdownTimerTick, and shuffles the two 8-byte muzzle-flash flag blocks at +0x33/+0x3b plus the burst frame counter at +0x44. Gated on the mount not being destroyed, so a dead mount's cooldown does not run. Consumes no energy -- an ammunition mount's whole turn at the pool is this.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ChargeCapacitor
entries.description: One energy mount's draw on the pool. Target is the mount's capacity (+0x7b), or zero when told another mount is already charging, minus its stored charge (+0x7d); takes min(chargeRate +0x7f, budget, deficit) and returns the remainder. A non-positive deficit clears the charging flag (+0x43) and bleeds charge back at up to 5/tick. PLAS (catalog id 25) is half-efficiency: its deficit counts double and only half the drawn energy is stored. Ammunition mounts override this with a no-op that consumes nothing.

entries.name: TurboPod_Engage
entries.description: Engages the Turbo Pod: if the engaged flag at pod+0x81 is clear and the charge at pod+0x7d is over 600, sets the flag and plays sound 0x2c (throtl.wav, the same servo the throttle lever uses) -- but only when the pod has a cockpit gauge at +0x79, which no AI machine's pod has. Called from TurboPod_Tick for the player's own row button and directly from Mech_BehaviourFleeThink and Ai_DriveToPoint, which is the only way an AI machine engages one since its pods are never ticked.

entries.name: TurboPod_ChargeTick
entries.description: Turbo Pod vtable +0x34, the only pod that overrides the pool turn -- every other pod inherits WeaponMount_RefireTick there and so consumes nothing. While engaged (pod+0x81) it spends 35 of the charge at pod+0x7d per tick, disengaging and zeroing the charge when it runs out; then, if the mount is not destroyed, it runs WeaponMount_RefireTick and takes min(20, budget, 2000 - charge) back out of the weapons' leftover budget, returning the remainder. 2000 is the value TurboPod_Ctor starts the charge at.

entries.name: Pod_TickBase
entries.description: Pod base vtable +0x50, inherited unchanged by the Shield, Targeting and Energy pods -- the three classes whose gauge row has no button. It is a display refresh and nothing else: it takes the gauge's 8-byte state block through PodGauge_GetStateBlock, replaces byte 1 with the mount's destroyed flag at pod+0x49, leaves byte 0 (the button) and the remaining six bytes as they were, and pushes the block back through PodGauge_SetStateBlock. It reads and writes no pod field. EcmPod_Tick and TurboPod_Tick are the overrides that do the same refresh and act on the button as well.

entries.name: EcmPod_Tick
entries.description: ECM pod vtable +0x50. Reads the pod gauge's on/off byte, mirrors it into pod+0x7d and pod+0x7f, and posts the jamming messages 0x2a and 0x2b on a change; the flag it pushes back carries the destroyed byte at +0x49.

entries.name: TurboPod_Tick
entries.description: Turbo Pod vtable +0x50. Engages when the gauge's button byte is set and the charge at pod+0x7d is over 600, playing sound 0x2c, and disengages when the charge runs out.

entries.name: WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState
entries.description: Energy mount vtable+0x50, called once per mount per frame from WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate. Copies the gauge's state block (EnergyWeaponGauge_GetState), fills it and hands it back through EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState. Block[0] is (charge << 10) / 1200, the LED bar's fill; the fixed 1200 denominator -- not the mount's own capacity -- is why a fully charged weapon fills four-fifths of its bar. Block[1] is the charge bar's slider position, and byte +0x34 (byte 1 of the +0x33 flag block) decides which way it flows: set, the charge target goes out as (target << 10) / 1200; clear, the slider position comes back as the charge target, +0x7b = position * 1200 >> 10. WeaponMount_CtorEnergy, WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel, WeaponMount_ZeroChargeTarget and WeaponMount_DrainCapacitor set it together with +0x3c, which carries it through one pool turn. No press reaches the charge bar, so the position read back is the one last pushed, less the round trip's loss (960 out as 819, back as 959); WeaponMount_RefireTick's AND with the +0x3b block clears it a pool turn later. Also fills the destroyed and mid-charge flags (+0x11, +0x12) and the three caller-supplied bytes (+0x14 selected, +0x15 in current fire group, +0x16 ready). See docs/simulation/weapon-firing.md.

entries.name: WeaponMount_PushAmmoGaugeState
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable+0x50, the sibling of WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState. Decays +0x7d toward capacity*256 at 250/tick if it is above it, then pushes +0x7d >> 8 as the round count the gauge prints, plus the destroyed flag and the three caller-supplied state bytes.

entries.name: GrenadeMount_PushGaugeState
entries.description: GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x50 (00499248): passes its four arguments straight to WeaponMount_PushAmmoGaugeState.

entries.name: ElfMount_SpinUpAndChargeTick
entries.description: ElfMountVtable +0x34. While the spin-up flag +0x47 is set, counts the cell timer at +0x83 down and on expiry either advances the muzzle-flash flipbook one cell or, at the last cell, latches +0x48 and clears +0x47 -- which is what lets ElfMount_TriggerHeld start returning the trigger. Then falls through to WeaponMount_ChargeCapacitor, so an ELF's capacitor charges exactly as an energy mount's does.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x38, reached by WeaponMounts_HandleCommand codes 0x0c/0x0d/0x4a/0x4e ([-], [=], keypad [-], keypad [+]) with the 'up' half as a flag. Moves the charge target (+0x7b) by +/-0x50, clamped to 0..0x4b0. This is the power-level control, which the manual never mentions, and the only thing in the retail build that raises a capacitor past its idle 820. The ammunition and pod classes have a no-op in this slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_WakeCapacitor
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x3c: puts the charge target (+0x7b) back to its idle 0x334 unless the mount is destroyed. Called after a chain toggle when the mount reports a zero arbitration priority, so a capacitor that had been zeroed starts asking for charge again. The ammunition and pod classes have a no-op in this slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DemandFullCharge
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x40: sets the mid-charge flag (+0x43) and raises the charge target (+0x7b) to 0x4b0, the same 1200 the cockpit bar is scaled against. NEVER INVOKED in the retail build -- its only caller, WeaponMounts_DemandFullChargeOnArmed_Dead, is itself unreferenced. What actually raises a capacitor past the idle 820 is WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel, the player's power-level keys.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetEnergyPriority
entries.description: Vtable+0x48 on energy mounts: returns the mount's capacity (+0x7b), or 10000 when its charging flag (+0x43) is set so a mount already mid-charge jumps the arbitration queue and finishes charging. The ammunition mount class returns 0 from this slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_AmmoCountsInCombatRating
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x54: rounds remaining (+0x7b) >= the magazine size (template+0x3a) >> 3. Mech_ComputeCombatRating adds a mount's value (template+0x4e, scaled by its condition) only when this slot answers non-zero, so a launcher or gun below an eighth of a magazine stops counting.

entries.name: WeaponMount_MuzzleOffset
entries.description: Adds the hardpoint's own mount-point offset (.GL +0x10/+0x12/+0x14) to WeaponMountTemplate_SideMuzzleOffset's result and returns the sum, in the firing bone's space. WeaponMount_PrepareShot adds the template's own muzzle triple at +0x40 on top.

entries.name: WeaponMount_Destroy
entries.description: The mount side of weapon-mount destruction, and idempotent -- its whole body sits under a test of the destroyed byte. Clears the weapon model at mount+0x10 and sets mount+0x49, then, for a visibly-mounted hardpoint, spawns the mechwpn2 shape at template+0x26 as debris on a Math_EulerToward bearing. The third argument picks the debris lifetime pair: 0 gives (2, 0x14), anything else (0xff, 0xffff). Ported except the debris.

entries.name: Debris_Dtor
entries.description: DEBRIS vtable +0x08 (00497ed8), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, installs TSObjVtable, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, two more decrements, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0. Meteor_Dtor is the same body.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0040f7e6; class record at 0040f796

entries.name: WeaponMount_AndFlagBlocks
entries.description: dst[i] &= src[i] over 8 bytes. WeaponMount_RefireTick calls it as (mount+0x33, mount+0x3b) and then clears +0x3b, while WeaponMount_PrepareShot sets both on firing -- so +0x33 survives only while the mount fires on every tick and drops on the first tick it sits out. It is an 'is still firing' flag, not 'has ever fired', and ElfMount_CanFire is what reads it.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DrainNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x4c (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN and the five pods: an empty body. The energy classes install WeaponMount_DrainCapacitor, the ammunition classes WeaponMount_DrainAmmo.

entries.name: WeaponMount_IsSpent_Always
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x5c (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN and the five pods: returns 1, so Ai_ChooseWeapon never considers a pod and a pod never keeps the 'no weapons left' latch off.

entries.name: WeaponMount_TriggerHeld
entries.description: Mount vtable +0x30, shared by the energy and ammunition classes: returns the input device struct's byte at +0x0d, the fire button. This is the whole of the trigger -- it is a held state polled every frame, not a command, which is why no scancode case for [Space] exists in Sim_DispatchCommand or WeaponMounts_HandleCommand.

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_ReadRecord
entries.description: Per-record reader for simvol0/dat/WEAPONS.DAT, called from Weapons_LoadResourceTables in a Total-length loop. Reuses HercPiece_ReadRecord (8-byte front + conditional dependent list) and Collision_ReadCluster/Collision_ReadSphereArray (2+2 bytes, then a variable count*8-byte array -- a per-weapon firing/mount-offset sequence, not real collision geometry) verbatim from the .DMG/.COL loaders, then a final raw 48-byte (0x30) block. Byte-exact verified: this exact read sequence consumes the real file's full 3790 content bytes across 33 records with zero remainder. Full writeup in docs/formats/weapons-dat-sim.md.

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_SideMuzzleOffset
entries.description: Given a template and the hardpoint's mounting code (.GL +6: 0 on top, 1 underneath, 2 left, 3 right, 4 invisible), returns a 3-vector at 004a9b74 built from the template's lateral figure at +0x46 and vertical figure at +0x4a. Only one axis is ever nonzero: top/bottom take +/-vertical, left/right take -/+lateral, invisible takes neither. Y is always zero. This is what makes a mirrored hardpoint pair fire from mirrored points off one template.

entries.name: WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks
entries.description: Opens dts/mechwpns and reads every top-level chunk (all type 0x140008) raw into malloc'd buffers: DAT_004a9988[i] is the buffer, DAT_004a9a78[i] its length, DAT_004a9b68 the count. Retail ships 56 weapon shapes. They are kept as bytes rather than parsed once because each mount needs its own copy.

entries.name: WeaponModels_FreeShapeChunks
entries.description: Frees the DAT_004a9988 buffers WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks allocated and nulls each slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ShapeForMountingCode
entries.description: Instantiates one weapon model: reads template[0x22 + mountingCode*2] as an index into the mechwpns chunk table, opens that raw chunk as a memory stream, loads the shape from it, and binds the wpntex atlas at shape+0x26. One fresh copy per mount, because the caller then translates its points and stamps a transform id into it.

entries.name: MechLoadout_FileEquipmentPods
entries.description: Walks the finished weapon-mount list and files five specific weapon ids into the five-pointer pod array at mech+0x307, keyed on the mount template's +0x56 (the SHELL0 gam/WEAPONS.DAT catalog id, written as the record index by Weapons_LoadResourceTables). Slot order is not id order: 0x12 ECM->[0], 0x1d TARG->[1], 0x1e SHLD->[2], 0x20 ENRG->[3], 0x1f TURB->[4]. Assigns rather than accumulates, so a duplicate pod contributes nothing.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_RoundsByMissileType
entries.description: Fills a 5-entry short array with rounds carried per PROJ.DAT missile subtype, by walking the mount array calling each mount's vtable +0x60 (WeaponMount_GetAmmoType) and accumulating its out-parameter (mount+0x7b) into rounds[subtype], skipping the 5 sentinel. THIS is the ammunition count; manager+0x0a is the lock state. Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate uses it to decide which lock timers run.

entries.name: GunLayout_CollectHardpointBones
entries.description: Walks a .GL hardpoint list (26-byte records) and writes one short per hardpoint: the record's bone id when its mounting code at +6 is under 4, else -1. Returns the hardpoint count. The -1 is what keeps the invisible mounting out of the hardpoint splice, which matters because that bone carries real body geometry.

entries.name: Weapons_LoadResourceTables
entries.description: Opens 'wpntex' (textures), 'mechwpn2', 'weapons' (88-byte per-hardpoint mount-template records), then 'proj' -- reads PROJ.DAT's 36-byte records into ProjDat_RecordTable. The 'weapons' resource is simvol0/dat/WEAPONS.DAT, read byte-exact: a UINT16 Total then Total records via WeaponMountTemplate_ReadRecord, consuming exactly the file's full content length with zero remainder across all 33 real records.

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_GetByWeaponId
entries.description: weaponId * 0x58 + _DAT_004a9970 -- direct flat-array index into the loaded WeaponMountTemplate table (simvol0/dat/WEAPONS.DAT's in-memory copy, 88 bytes/record) by SHELL0/GAM/WEAPONS.DAT catalog weapon id. The sim and shell catalogs share one 33-entry order and indexing scheme.

entries.name: GunLayout_GetBySlot
entries.description: index * 6 + _DAT_004a9968 -- flat index into the loaded gun-layout table. Each 6-byte entry is {short count, record*}. Callers reach it through FUN_00420634, which adds the mech type's own allocation index to the base slot cached in _DAT_004a9df4.

entries.name: GunLayout_AllocTable
entries.description: GunLayout_Table = Mem_NewArray(GunLayout_Count * 6). DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it.

entries.name: GunLayout_LoadForMechType
entries.description: Loads one gl\<HERC>.GL hardpoint list into the object pool slot for a mech type: short count, then count 26-byte records. Asserts in GUNLIST.CPP. The record's byte at +0x17 indexes the mission's loadout arrays and its byte at +7 is the cockpit weapon row the resulting mount owns.

entries.name: Proj_LookupRecordByIndex
entries.description: index * 0x24 + ProjDat_RecordTable -- direct flat-array index into PROJ.DAT's in-memory table, distinct from Proj_LookupRecord's (category,subtypeId) linear search. Called by MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts with the value read from a WeaponMountTemplate's PROJ.DAT index (in-memory +0x3e), which is what resolves a real catalog weapon id to its PROJ.DAT damage record for 21 of 32 real weapons directly. Base_ArmedThinkTick and Flyer_AttackRun also call it with the literal 2, for the speed they lead by. See docs/formats/weapons-dat-sim.md.

entries.name: Proj_LookupRecord
entries.description: PROJ.DAT in-memory lookup by (category, subtypeId) -- linear search against ProjDat_RecordTable, first match. Fired shots resolve their record through it again.

entries.name: MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts
entries.description: Called from Mech_ConfigureLoadout (0x004175dc). Given per-hardpoint slot records (stride 0x1a) and two parallel weapon-id/secondary-key lookup tables, for each occupied slot: reads the weapon id, looks up its WeaponMountTemplate (WeaponMountTemplate_GetByWeaponId), reads that template's PROJ.DAT index (in-memory +0x3e), resolves the matching PROJ.DAT record (Proj_LookupRecordByIndex direct-index, or Proj_LookupRecord(0,secondaryKey) search for the 0x22 sentinel), then constructs a weapon-id-specific mount C++ object (one of several vtables/sizes keyed by a big switch on the weapon id) passing the resolved template/PROJ.DAT pointers. This is the mech-loadout-time mechanism that resolves a real catalog weapon id into the shot data direct-fire/beam dispatch consumes. Four live classes: WeaponMount_CtorAmmunition (ids 1-5, 13-16, 21, 26), WeaponMount_CtorEnergy (7-12, 17, 19, 20, 23-25, 28), the five pod constructors (18, 29-32), and the ELF case (6, 22) -- which is the only one that is not just a constructor call: it runs WeaponMount_CtorEnergy and then OVERWRITES the object's vtable pointer with ElfMountVtable. Id 27 (MINE) has no case at all. See docs/simulation/weapon-mounts.md.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_CtorLocal
entries.description: The locally-piloted machine's mount manager (vtable 00499238): runs MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts, then allocates three fire-group arrays (manager+0x1f/+0x25/+0x2b) and picks the initial selection. Writes 'group == wanted' into all three arrays with wanted fixed at 0 for a weapon and -1 for a pod, so every non-pod mount starts in group I and groups II and III start empty; manager+0x1d becomes the first non-pod mount in mount-array order.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_BuildGauges
entries.description: Walks the mount array (pointer at +4, count at +8) and calls each mount's own gauge factory slot, vtable +0x64. The closing call of Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets, so every weapon row's clickables are appended to the flat list after all seven gauges and before the edge strips. An energy row registers two -- ChainedWeaponSelectGadget then the charge bar's WeaponSliderGadget -- which is why the select gadget wins where the bar overlaps it.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_MountForHardpointSlot
entries.description: Linear search of the mount manager's array for the mount whose .GL record's +0x17 equals the argument, or null. Damage components 19-28 are the mounts, so the caller passes component - 19. The match is on the .GL slot, not on a position in the array.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SelectByGauge
entries.description: Arm the mount that owns a given weapon gauge -- what a left click on a weapon row and a number key both end at. Finds the mount whose vtable +0x58 gauge-match slot accepts the gauge (the pod base class returns 0 unconditionally, so a pod never matches), requires the mount's selectable byte +0x4c, calls WeaponMounts_SetSelection and sets the single-fire flag at manager+0x18.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SetSelection
entries.description: The only writer of the armed-mount index at manager+0x1d. Normalises a linked pair onto its first half: if the mount being armed is linked (+0x4b) and its .GL partner offset (slot+0x16) is negative, the partner is armed instead. That is what keeps a linked pair's two rows agreeing about which of them is armed.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_StepSelection
entries.description: Step the armed mount one place through the current fire chain, wrapping. Skips anything not selectable (+0x4c), not in the current chain, or the second half of a linked pair (partner offset must be positive). Does not clear the single-fire flag itself -- the command handler does, which is why the chain switch and the per-frame advance step the selection without giving the chain control back.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergy
entries.description: The weapon half of the Master Energy Pool tick, (manager, budget, selection, arg). Reached through the mount manager's vtable slot 0: GUNLIST's WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergyNoSelection passes -1, PLAYER_GUNLIST's WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergyWithSelection the selection byte manager+0x1d. Serves the selected mount first, then the remaining mounts highest-priority-first by vtable+0x48. Each mount takes its share via vtable+0x34 and passes the remainder on. Once any mount reports itself mid-charge (+0x43), every later mount targets zero instead and bleeds its capacitor back to the pool, so only one energy weapon charges at a time. Returns the unclaimed budget. A player-only infinite-energy debug path refunds all consumption when DAT_004a9ed6==0 and DAT_004a9edc==1.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_MountIsReady
entries.description: The readiness predicate behind BOTH the weapon row's green/red state box and the firing chain's skip: the mount's own vtable+0x2c test, then WeaponMount_RangeAllows against the selected target's range at manager+0x31 (skipped outright when that is zero, i.e. no target), then a missile-lock gate -- vtable+0x60's subtype is exempt for 5 (not a launcher) and 3 (EO, which is pilot-flown and never latches a flag), and otherwise must have its flag set in manager[0x0a + code*2]. A linked mount recurses once into its partner, so a pair is ready only when both halves are. The lock array is written by Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate -- see docs/simulation/missile-lock.md.
entries.signature: short __cdecl WeaponMounts_MountIsReady(void *manager, void *mount, int mountIndex, short followLink)

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ChainReady
entries.description: WeaponMounts_AdvanceToReady's own wrapper around WeaponMounts_MountIsReady, and the only caller of it that is not the gauge push. Returns 1 without asking -- so the chain never steps -- while the single-fire flag manager+0x18 is set or DAT_004d25aa, the flag set while an electro-optical missile is in flight, is up; otherwise forwards to the full predicate with followLink clear.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_AdvanceToReady
entries.description: The firing chain's own advance, run every frame from WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate: if the armed mount cannot fire, step through the chain until one that can is found, and put the original back if none is. Asks WeaponMounts_ChainReady rather than WeaponMounts_MountIsReady directly, which is what gates it off while the single-fire flag (manager+0x18) is set -- the manual's 'select a weapon to single-fire ... once you fire, the current firing chain will resume'. Because the predicate is range-gated, this is also what steps the chain past a weapon that cannot reach the target.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SetChain
entries.description: Switch which of the three fire chains is current (manager+0x1c). If the armed mount is not in the new chain, steps the selection to one that is, then pushes the new number to the console chain button's caption.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate
entries.description: The mount manager's per-frame pass. Stores its range argument -- the distance to the selected target, measured by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate -- into manager+0x31 BEFORE running WeaponMounts_AdvanceToReady, so the chain advance and the row lamps both see this frame's range. Then reads the weapon-panel input block, applies the chain/link commands, and walks every mount calling its vtable+0x50 gauge push with three state bytes: selected (index == manager+0x1d), in the current fire group (groups[manager+0x1c][index]), and ready (WeaponMounts_MountIsReady).

entries.name: WeaponMounts_XorChainBit
entries.description: Flips one mount's membership bit in the currently selected fire chain (manager+0x1f + manager+0x1c*6, indexed by mount index). Membership is toggled, never set, which is why Alt+number and a right click both add and remove.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_IdleAllCapacitors
entries.description: WeaponMounts_HandleCommand's 0x2c case: calls vtable +0x3c (WeaponMount_WakeCapacitor) on every mount, dropping every energy capacitor's target back to the idle 820. The bulk counterpart to WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_DemandFullChargeOnArmed_Dead
entries.description: DEAD CODE. Would call vtable +0x40 (WeaponMount_DemandFullCharge) on the armed mount and clear every other mount's mid-charge flag (+0x43). Has no reference of any kind anywhere in DBSIM.EXE -- neither a CALL rel32 nor a stored address -- so nothing in the retail build reaches it, and WeaponMount_DemandFullCharge is therefore never invoked either.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_FireTrigger
entries.description: The weapon manager's fire entry. Resolves the armed mount and, if it is linked (+0x4b), its partner via the hardpoint's +0x16 offset; requires both to pass vtable +0x2c (can fire) AND both to pass vtable +0x30 (trigger held) before either fires through vtable +0x28. Clears the single-fire flag (+0x18) once the armed mount is no longer ready. Also passes a free-shot flag built from DAT_004a9ed6/DAT_004a9edc, which only the ammunition class reads.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SetTrackLatch
entries.description: (manager): stores 1 at manager+0x14, TRACK's latch. WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate calls it when byte 2 of the console panel's input block is set and clears +0x14 itself otherwise.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ToggleLink
entries.description: Toggle link fire on the armed mount and its .GL partner. Two conditions, both from the chassis: the armed mount's slot+0x16 partner offset is non-zero, and the partner hardpoint carries the SAME weapon id (template+0x56). Both halves' +0x4b flip together. One LINK press runs this three times -- the button's click handler, the manager's next per-frame pass reading the button's latch byte, and that pass writing the byte back -- which nets to one flip.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_HandleCommand
entries.description: The weapon-mount manager's command handler, called from Mech_HandleCommand. 0x202-0x20b (Alt+1..0) toggle a row's fire-chain membership via WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember; 0x11 and 0x211 (W, Alt+W) step the armed weapon via WeaponMounts_StepSelection and clear the single-fire flag at manager+0x18; 0x30 advances the fire chain; 0x2c calls WeaponMounts_IdleAllCapacitors; 0xc/0xd/0x4a/0x4e ([-], [=], keypad [-], keypad [+]) reach the armed mount's vtable +0x38, WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel. There is no firing case: the trigger is polled, not dispatched -- see WeaponMount_TriggerHeld.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember
entries.description: Add or remove one cockpit weapon row from the CURRENT fire chain -- Alt and the row's number key, or a right click on the row. Finds the mount by its .GL fire-chain byte (slot+7), requires the mount template's int32 at 0x30 to be positive (zero for every pod, which is what keeps pods off a chain), then XORs that mount's bit in the current chain array via WeaponMounts_XorChainBit. It does not arm anything. Follows the toggle by waking an energy mount's capacitor when its arbitration priority reads zero.

entries.name: EnergyPod_Dtor
entries.description: ENERGY_POD vtable +0x18 (00498a84), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown -- one RTL destructor-count decrement per class level, HeapBlockOwner_Dtor(this+0x10, 0) on the weapon model's cell-frame holder, TSBase_Dtor(this, 0) -- then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00411174; class record at 00411120

entries.name: WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevelNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x38 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: an empty body. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_AdjustPowerLevel.

entries.name: WeaponMount_WakeCapacitorNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x3c (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: an empty body. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_WakeCapacitor.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DemandFullChargeNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x40 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: an empty body. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_DemandFullCharge.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ZeroChargeTargetNoOp
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x44 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: an empty body. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_ZeroChargeTarget.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetEnergyPriorityZero
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x48 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods and both ammunition classes: returns 0. Only the energy classes install WeaponMount_GetEnergyPriority.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CountsInCombatRating_Always
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x54 (00498e44), kept by POD_WPN, the five pods, ENERGY_WPN and ELF_WPN: returns 1, so every such mount's value counts in Mech_ComputeCombatRating. The ammunition classes install WeaponMount_AmmoCountsInCombatRating.

entries.name: ShieldPod_Dtor
entries.description: SHIELD_POD vtable +0x18 (00498afc), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00411246; class record at 004111f2

entries.name: TargetingPod_Dtor
entries.description: TARGETING_POD vtable +0x18 (00498b74), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004112f8; class record at 004112a0

entries.name: TurboPod_Dtor
entries.description: TURBO_POD vtable +0x18 (00498bec), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004113a6; class record at 00411352

entries.name: EcmPod_Dtor

entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00411450; class record at 00411400

entries.name: Pod_DtorBase

entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004114fa; class record at 004114aa

entries.name: WeaponMount_DtorAmmunition
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN vtable +0x18 (00498d54), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DrainAmmo
entries.description: PROJECTILE_WPN and GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x4c, the slot the energy classes fill with WeaponMount_DrainCapacitor: zeroes the rounds remaining (+0x7b).

entries.name: WeaponMount_DtorEnergy
entries.description: ENERGY_WPN vtable +0x18 (00498dcc), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0041165a; class record at 00411606

entries.name: WeaponMount_ZeroChargeTarget
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x44 (and the ELF table's): zeroes the charge target (+0x7b) and the mid-charge flag (+0x43), and sets +0x34 and +0x3c so the next WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState carries the new target out to the charge bar.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DrainCapacitor
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x4c (and the ELF table's): zeroes the charge (+0x7d) and the charge target (+0x7b), and sets +0x34 and +0x3c as WeaponMount_ZeroChargeTarget does.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DtorBase
entries.description: GUN_STATE vtable +0x18 (00498e44, RTTI 'GUN_STATE', 0x77 bytes, derived from CONFIG_PART), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00411743; class record at 004116ef

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergyWithSelection
entries.description: PLAYER_GUNLIST vtable +0x00 (00499238), (manager, budget, arg): WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergy(manager, budget, the selection byte manager+0x1d, arg) -- the pool turn that serves the selected mount first. The GUNLIST base installs WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergyNoSelection.

entries.name: GrenadeMount_Dtor
entries.description: GRENADE_WPN vtable +0x18 (00499248), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00411969; class record at 004118a6

entries.name: ElfMount_Dtor
entries.description: ELF_WPN vtable +0x18 (ElfMountVtable, 004992c0), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). The weapon-mount teardown (see EnergyPod_Dtor), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004119c3; class record at 004118fa

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergyNoSelection
entries.description: (manager, budget, arg): WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergy(manager, budget, -1, arg), the energy pool turn with no selected mount served first. Its one reference is the stored pointer at 00499338.

entries.name: SimObject_ComponentPositionNoOp
entries.description: ACTOR and FLYER vtable +0x58: push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret. Writes nothing to its out-parameter.

entries.name: SimObject_ComponentNearestAim_None
entries.description: ACTOR and FLYER vtable +0x54: returns -1 (OR EAX,-1), the 'no component' answer Mech_ComponentNearestAim gives when no slot is occupied.

entries.name: SimObject_GetShieldByHeadingZero
entries.description: Vtable +0x34 of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables: returns 0. Only the mech overrides it (Mech_GetShieldByHeading).

entries.name: SimObject_GetSpeedZero
entries.description: Vtable +0x38 of the ACTOR base and all five structure tables: returns 0. The mech (Mech_GetSpeed) and the flyer (Flyer_GetSpeed) override it.

entries.name: SimObject_GetTorsoTwistAngleZero
entries.description: Vtable +0x3c of the ACTOR base, the flyer, BASE, RADAR_BASE and LC_BASE: returns 0. GUN_BASE and VEHICLE replace it with Base_GetTurretAngle, the mech with Mech_GetTorsoTwistAngle.

entries.name: SimObject_ReceiveSquadOrder_Refuse
entries.description: Vtable +0x28 of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables: returns 0, where Mech_ReceiveSquadOrder returns 1 for an order it took.

entries.name: SimObject_HandleCommandNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x2c of the ACTOR base and all five structure tables: returns 0 and acts on nothing. The mech installs Mech_HandleCommand; the flyer has its own stub, Flyer_HandleCommandNoOp.

entries.name: SimObject_GetAimPointZero
entries.description: The shared base's vtable +0x30: memsets both 6-byte out triples to zero, i.e. aim at the object's own origin with no offset. The FlyerVtable installs it unchanged; the structure tables wrap it in Base_GetAimPoint (0040351c) and the mech table replaces it with 004155c4.

entries.name: SimObject_GetAimNodeTransform_None
entries.description: Vtable +0x24 on the flyer and the SimObject base: return 0. Every caller's null branch falls back to the object's raw origin for aiming and to a literal 500 for sight height. The mech's own is Mech_GetAimNodeTransform; all five structure vtables install Base_GetAimNodeTransform (00403548) instead.

entries.name: SimObject_GetBodyRadiusZero
entries.description: ACTOR and FLYER vtable +0x5c: returns 0. The mech installs Mech_GetBodyRadius, the structures Base_GetBodyRadius.

entries.name: SimObject_GetCollisionRadiusZero
entries.description: ACTOR and FLYER vtable +0x7c: returns 0, so a flyer adds nothing to the collision gap a walking machine measures against it. The mech installs Mech_GetCollisionRadius, the structures Base_GetCollisionRadius.

entries.name: SimObject_TickNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x14 of the ACTOR base and all five structure tables: returns 1 in AX and does nothing. The mech and flyer install their behaviour move dispatchers here (Behaviour_DispatchMove, Flyer_DispatchMove).

entries.name: SimObject_CompareCombatRatingStub
entries.description: The shared base's vtable +0x4c: `return 1`. Ai_SelectTarget (00411fa0) dispatches this slot on the ASKING object, so a structure or a flyer -- both of whose tables install this stub -- scores every candidate against column 1 of the four Q10 weight tables at 0049933c/42/48, whatever the ratings actually are. Only the mech table replaces it, with Mech_CompareCombatRating (0041cabc).

entries.name: SimObject_BearingInSensorArc
entries.description: Vtable +0x44 of the ACTOR base, the mech and the flyer: (bearing - obj+0x10 + 0x3800) < 0x7000 unsigned, so +/-78.75 degrees about the object's heading. Callers fold the aim twist into the bearing before calling. The five structure classes install Base_BearingInSensorArc_Always instead.

entries.name: Mech_ShareContact
entries.description: Thin wrapper over Detection_ShareContact, used by Mech_AiOnTakingFire so that being shot spreads the attacker's position to the whole side.

entries.name: SimObject_MissileLockState_Always
entries.description: Vtable +0x6c of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables: returns 1 in AX for every missile subtype. The slot is the launcher's own lock gate and Mech_MissileLockState is the only override, so a missile launched by a flyer or a structure is always handed the launcher's selected target.

entries.name: SimObject_ComponentPresent_Always
entries.description: SimObjectBaseVtable and FlyerVtable +0x84: a bare return 1.

entries.name: SimObject_NextTargetableComponent_None
entries.description: SimObjectBaseVtable and FlyerVtable +0x80: answers -1 and writes -1, so a flyer has no components a targeting pod can single out.

entries.name: SimObject_CreditNeutralisedTargetNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x60 of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables: an empty body. Only the mech (Mech_CreditNeutralisedTarget) credits a kill.

entries.name: SimObject_AiOnLineOfFireBlockedNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x64 of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables: an empty body. Only the mech (Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked) reacts.

entries.name: SimObject_ApplyExplosiveDamage
entries.description: The SimObject base class's vtable +0x70, and the implementation a FLYER uses -- the flyer class does not override the slot. No roll, no component selection, no shields and no range test (the sweep has already made it): applies (blastRadius - (distance - obj[+0x5c])) * damage / blastRadius to component 0 through vtable +0x74. Because the object's own +0x5c is subtracted, a blast inside the body radius scales by more than one -- though a flyer's +0x5c is 0.
entries.signature: void __cdecl SimObject_ApplyExplosiveDamage(SimObject *this, short damage, int *hitPoint, short blastRadius, SimObject *attacker)

entries.name: SimObject_SetOutOfActionCounters
entries.description: Copies ten counter refs to obj+0x1ba and ten ops to obj+0x1ce -- the slots Mech_ReportOutOfAction runs. es2_xref.py finds three calls, all in DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects: a roster mech (record 0x42/0x56), a flyer (0x2e/0x42) and a structure (0x06/0x1a). The mech call sits on the roster side of that function's index < rosterCount test, so the player's squad does not reach it there; Mech_Constructor sets refs 0-2 to -1.

entries.name: Mech_ReportOutOfAction
entries.description: es2_xref.py finds four calls, each immediately before the defeat action at a damage endpoint that puts an object out of the fight: both of Mech_ComponentDamageWrite's branches, Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite and Base_ApplyDamage (the name predates the other two). Ai_ChooseWeapon's weapons-out defeat does not call it: that block's only call is Action_Activate. Calls Group_ReportIfAllOutOfAction for the object's own group, then walks its 10 mission-counter slots (refs at obj+0x1ba, ops at obj+0x1ce) writing DAT_004a9ef4: op 1 zeroes the counter, 2 increments it, 0xd-0x10 store op-0xc, anything else writes nothing.

entries.name: Ai_KnowsObject
entries.description: The AI's knowledge test, far looser than the player's: radar-visible (+0x95) within 999999 units, or a contact this machine holds (this+0xc2 + other[0x4b]) at any range.

entries.name: Ai_TargetStateTier
entries.description: Reads an object's behaviour descriptor through its block at +0x4d and returns the state tier the squad-order abandon check compares against: 2 for descriptor flag bit 5 (in limbo, dead, disabled), 1 for bit 4 (fleeing), else 0.

entries.name: Mech_AiTick
entries.description: One machine's whole AI frame, and the only caller of the three behaviour dispatchers. No-ops unless a descriptor is installed at mech+0x4d. Order: reassess (vtable +0x1c) when the dwell countdown at mech+0x52 has reached 0; Timer_CountDown against that countdown unless descriptor+0x08[0] is set, which is true of every state but deciding, the five combat states, driving off en and fleeing; move (vtable +0x14); then think (vtable +0x18) unless mech+0xaf is set, in which case think is skipped and the flag cleared -- a think returning nonzero zeroes its own countdown. Ends by incrementing the block counter at +0x09 via 00413eb0. ITS ONLY CALLER IS Group_OrderTick (00423a74) at 00423af5, so the AI is driven from the mission-group layer and a machine that is not a live group member never thinks.

entries.name: Formation_RotateAndAddOffset
entries.description: Rotates a formation offset into world space and adds it to a position. Takes the group leader (first entry of the group's member array at group+0xc), lazily builds its rotation matrix from its heading (leader+0xc -> leader+0x12, guarded by the stale flag at leader+0x32 that Mech_AttachToGroup clears), rotates the offset by it, and accumulates into the caller's x/y/z. Also the base-formation attach path's rotator (called from FUN_00405c04); for a heading-only object (no pitch/roll, true of every base) the matrix build (FUN_0047eaac) plus apply (FUN_0047fedc) reduces algebraically to a plain 2D rotation: worldDX = dx*cos(heading) - dy*sin(heading), worldDY = dx*sin(heading) + dy*cos(heading).

entries.name: ObjectList_Add
entries.description: Appends an object to the world's single live-object list and records the slot it landed in at obj+0x4b. That index is what addresses both the per-object contact table (obj+0xc2) and the line-of-sight cache (obj+0x132).

entries.name: ObjectList_Init
entries.description: (list, capacity): list+0 = Mem_NewArray(capacity * 4), int16 list+4 = capacity. DBSim_LoadScriptDat sizes maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList with it.

entries.name: ObjList_SwapRemove
entries.description: (list, obj): list->items[obj+0x4b] = list->items[count - 1], then count (the short at list+6) -= 1, where items is the pointer at list+0. It does not rewrite the moved item's own +0x4b. The deleting destructors of ACTOR and everything derived from it call it on maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList in place of Mem_Delete.

entries.name: ObjectList_Next
entries.description: (list, obj): the entry after obj in the list, wrapping: items(+0)[(obj+0x4b + 1) % count(+6)], where obj+0x4b is the slot ObjectList_Add recorded. Sim_DispatchCommand cycles maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList with it.

entries.name: ObjectList_Prev
entries.description: (list, obj): the entry before obj in the list, wrapping: items(+0)[(obj+0x4b + count - 1) % count(+6)]. The reverse of ObjectList_Next.

entries.name: Ai_IsTargetable
entries.description: Whether an AI machine may target a candidate: not the same side (group+0x12), not destroyed (+0x99), collapsed (+0xb4) or invulnerable (+0xb7), currently known through Ai_KnowsObject, not an out-of-action flyer (+0xa5/+0xa4/+0x99), not the player's own selection while this machine's +0x9a is set, and with mask bit 0x10 not this machine's own object class.

entries.name: Ai_SelectTarget
entries.description: The AI's general target acquisition, used by mechs, flyers and armed structures: (this, mask, coneLimit) walks the live object list and returns the best-scoring candidate. Candidates pass Ai_IsTargetable, then a tier bar of 2*designated+alive; range caps at 1000000 for the group order's designated target and 100000 otherwise. Score starts at Q10(70, 0x1000 - (bearingError >> 3)), is overridden inside 60000 by a range term, then multiplied by four Q10 weight tables at 0049933c/00499342/00499348/0049934e and divided by the number of other holders. Mask: 0x01 restrict the designated bonus, 0x02 drop the shooting-at-me weight, 0x04 drop the crowding divisor, 0x10 reject own class, 0x20 ignore bearing.

entries.name: Sim_DetectionTick
entries.description: The whole sensor model for one tick, from Sim_MainTick after every object update and the input poll. Three passes: tick each object's LOS-cache (+0x1e2) and contact-decay (+0x1e5) timers, running Detection_DecayContacts on expiry; run Detection_Sweep for each live human-side object, holding the locally-piloted machine (+0xa3) back to sweep LAST so squadmates' contacts reach it first; clear the per-tick action latch +0xa2.

entries.name: Detection_DecayContacts
entries.description: Clears the object's own radar visibility (+0x95) then drops every enemy contact it holds that is past 100001 units or has no line of sight, mutually. The range here is measured on the GROUND PLANE only (Math_FastMagnitude2D) where every other range in the sensor model is the 3D approximation, so a flyer directly overhead stays a contact.

entries.name: Detection_LineOfSight
entries.description: Terrain ray between two objects' shape bounding-box centres (vtable +0x24 then +0x1c, or 500 with no shape record), cached per pair in the caller's row table at +0x132. The cache gate tests the OTHER object's countdown at +0x1e3 and reloads the CALLER's -- verified in raw disassembly at 00412617 and 0041263f, so it is the original's own asymmetry and not a decompiler slip. Only human-side objects sweep, so Cybrid timers stay zero and those pairs are re-walked whenever asked.

entries.name: Detection_ShareContact
entries.description: (spotter, contact). Passes a new contact to every deployed object (group+0x14 clear) on the spotter's own side within 100000 units, the spotter included. Inside 50000 it also sets the CONTACT's +0x9e engagement flag and activates that same-side object's OWN +0x1b2 engagement action through Action_Activate unless its +0xa2 ECM gate is raised; the two writes land on different objects (EDI vs EBX, 004127a7/004127ab). Nothing is shared to the other side and a same-side pair is not a contact at all. Called from Detection_Sweep and, with the shooter as contact, from Mech_ShareContact.

entries.name: SimObject_AiEnemySightedNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x48 of the ACTOR base, the flyer and all five structure tables: an empty body. Only the mech (Mech_AiEnemySighted) calls out a contact.

entries.name: Mech_AiEnemySighted
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x48, the enemy-detected callout. For a machine in the player's group, posts squad message 1 through Ai_PostSquadMessage for an object that is not class 1, not yet radar-visible (+0x95), and held as a contact by neither this machine nor the player, latched per object in DAT_004a9b84[obj+0x4b] (set even when the rate limit swallows the callout). DAT_004a9be9 is re-armed to 10000 on each callout and stepped by this function's own Math_CountdownTimerTick(004a9be8) on every non-player call, so it runs down per call-in, not per tick. The local player's own machine sets the latch without calling out.

entries.name: Detection_Sweep
entries.description: One human-side object's look around, over Cybrid objects only -- but it writes both objects' tables, so a Cybrid learns without ever sweeping. Radar painting within 200000 when either object emits and not both are painted, with 140000 the range at which a scanner paints something not emitting back. Looking runs only within 80000: a pair that already knows each other is skipped, otherwise each object's +/-0x3800 sensor arc (vtable +0x44) plus LOS makes the contact -- shared to the spotter's side by Detection_ShareContact, or kept private when the spotter is the player's machine.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectObject
entries.description: The object a group's current order names -- order+0x0e read as an object pointer. Valid when the order's kind discriminator (order+0x0c) is 1, 2 or 3.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectGroup
entries.description: The group record a group's current order names -- order+0x0e read as a group pointer. Valid when the order's kind discriminator (order+0x0c) is 0. Identical code to Group_OrderSubjectObject; the two exist as separately typed accessors.

entries.name: Group_IsWipedOut
entries.description: Whether every member of a mission group is out of the fight -- destroyed (+0x99), immobilised (+0xa4) or disarmed (+0xa5). Returns 0 as soon as one member is still in it. Its ONLY caller is Group_NoRivalOrderOnSubject (00412e74), the guarding-order completion test, so the +0xa5 term means a group of ordinary structures -- which Base_Construct spawns already disarmed -- reads as wiped out from the moment it is built.

entries.name: Group_AllMembersDisarmed
entries.description: True when every member of the mission group (member pointers at group+0x0c, count at group+0x10) is disarmed (+0xa5); an empty group answers true, since the loop returns 1 on running off the end. The group form of objective condition 7 in Mission_EvaluateObjectives.

entries.name: Group_ConditionTier
entries.description: A mission group's 0-4 condition tier: 4 when every member is immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99); else 3 when the lost fraction reaches 650/1024 or the mean overall damage across all members reaches 0xc1; else 2 at 250/1024 or 0x81; else 1 at mean damage 0x33; else 0. The mean includes dead members.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectEngaged
entries.description: Whether the group's current order's subject has been engaged: Group_AnyMemberEngaged of the subject group for order kind 0, the subject object's own +0x9e otherwise. No caller.

entries.name: Group_AnyMemberEngaged
entries.description: True when any member of the group has been engaged (+0x9e). The one helper of Group_StatusLineIndex that is also live: Mission_EvaluateObjectives calls it for objective condition 6.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectCondition
entries.description: The 0-4 condition tier of the subject a group's current order names. For an order naming an object (order+0x0c in 1..3): 4 when destroyed (+0x99) or collapsed (+0xb4), otherwise the object's vtable +0x40 overall damage banded at 0x32/0x80/0xc0. For an order naming a group (order+0x0c == 0): Group_ConditionTier over its members.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectDestroyed
entries.description: Whether Group_OrderSubjectCondition reports tier 4 for the group's current order subject. The completion test for order verb 0 and half of the test for verb 2.

entries.name: Group_NoRivalOrderOnSubject
entries.description: Whether no other mission group on the opposite side, still holding live members, has a current order naming the same subject pointer as this group's. The second half of order verb 2's (guarding) completion test.

entries.name: Group_AnyMemberObjectiveSighted
entries.description: True when any member of the group has +0x9f set. Called only from Group_StatusLineIndex, which is unreachable.

entries.name: Group_AnyMemberDataLinked
entries.description: True when any member of the group has +0xa0 set. Called only from Group_StatusLineIndex, which is unreachable.
