entries.name: Group_AnyMemberScoredAKill
entries.description: True when any member of the group has +0xa6 set. Called only from Group_StatusLineIndex, which is unreachable -- so mech+0xa6, latched by Mech_CreditNeutralisedTarget, has no live reader.

entries.name: Group_StatusLineIndex
entries.description: Maps a mission group and an order verb onto a status line index -- the group report. UNREACHABLE: no relative call in the code section and the dword 00412f90 occurs nowhere in the file, so no table or vtable holds it. The six Group_AnyMember*/Group_OrderSubject* helpers below exist for it, and all but Group_AnyMemberEngaged are dead with it.

entries.name: Mission_StatusForAlert
entries.description: The wrapper both alert paths go through: calls Mission_Status with the script.dat objective selector and the publish flag, and when publish is set also records the answer in DAT_004a9ed0, the status already raised. The poll passes 0; [Q] passes 1, so reading the status yourself is enough to stop the poll announcing it. Returns the status in AX.

entries.name: Mission_PollStatus
entries.description: Sim_MainTick's last act. Steps the 10 s poll interval and the 10 s alert delay, and hands up a status worth raising.

entries.name: Mission_GroupOrderCompleteOnRoute
entries.description: Objective condition 0: finds the group's order slot whose route (+0x08) is the record's waypoint group and answers that slot's completion flag at group+0x70.

entries.name: Mission_EvaluateObjectives
entries.description: Walks the mission's objective array (script.dat block 12) each poll and reduces it to a status: a failure condition holding, every required record holding, or neither, each split by whether the player is clear of threats.

entries.name: Mission_Status
entries.description: The mission judgement: the player's own condition, then the mission box, then Mission_EvaluateObjectives. The third argument suppresses the hold, both box arms and the SYSTEM.STR post.

entries.name: Mission_IsOutsideBox
entries.description: (point, margin): returns 1 when the point's x and y are not strictly inside Mission_Box (004aa6c4) widened by margin on every side, 0 when they are. It reads the box and writes nothing; DBSim_LoadScriptDat builds the box inline. SimObject_IsOutsideMissionBox and SimObject_IsFarOutsideMissionBox call it for Mission_Status's two box arms.

entries.name: SimObject_IsFarOutsideMissionBox
entries.description: (obj): Mission_IsOutsideBox(obj+0x26, 110000) -- whether the object is outside Mission_Box widened by 110000 on every side. Mission_Status answers 8 on it, ahead of the plain box test.

entries.name: SimObject_IsOutsideMissionBox
entries.description: (obj): Mission_IsOutsideBox(obj+0x26, 0) -- whether the object's position is outside Mission_Box. Mission_Status answers 7 on it, and Mission_PollStatus tests it when its poll interval expires.

entries.name: Mission_IsClearOfThreats
entries.description: Whether nothing hostile is working on this object: no live enemy knows it within 80000 (100000 if it is that machine's own selection), and no group whose order names it is still inbound.

entries.name: Group_IsWrittenOff
entries.description: A group's condition tier against its side's threshold -- 3 for a human group, 4 for a Cybrid one.

entries.name: Group_AllMembersClearOfThreats
entries.description: False when the group is written off, or when any member that is not destroyed fails Mission_IsClearOfThreats.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectRouteExhausted
entries.description: Whether the current order's subject has no waypoint left after its route cursor. No caller -- not even Group_StatusLineIndex.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectArrivedAndClear
entries.description: Whether the current order's subject is deployed (its group has no pending deployment action) and clear of threats. Called only from Group_StatusLineIndex, which is unreachable.

entries.name: Shield_Init
entries.description: Initializes the 5-field shield struct (mech+0x222) from the mech-type base capacity (typeRecord+0xc0): max fields = baseValue, current fields = baseValue>>1 (default 50/50 split).

entries.name: Shield_SetMax
entries.description: Trivial setter: writes the shield array's total capacity at shieldStruct+6 (mech+0x228). Only caller is Mech_ComputeShieldCapacity. The base capacity at shieldStruct+8 is left alone, which is why the cockpit rings measure against the pre-pod figure.

entries.name: Shield_RefillToBalance
entries.description: Fills the shield array to its max and splits it at the current balance: front = Q10(balance, max), rear = max - front. Called from Mech_ConfigureLoadout right after Shield_SetMax, so a mech spawns with full shields at whatever capacity its pods bought it.

entries.name: Shield_BalanceAdjust
entries.description: Nudges the shield balance field (mech+0x226) by +/-0x66 (102), clamped to [0, 0x400] (0-1024). Default center 0x200 (512).

entries.name: Shield_RechargeTick
entries.description: Shield recharge primitive: clamps the request to at most 5 units/tick and to the remaining deficit, redistributes front/rear via balance using Math_RateLimitedMoveToward, returns the unclaimed portion.

entries.name: Shield_BalanceInputRead
entries.description: Reads the shield-balance HUD gauge widget's click state; if a flag is set, calls Shield_BalanceAdjust. Also pushes front/rear display percentages back to the widget.

entries.name: Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive
entries.description: Explosion path own separate shield-absorption implementation (parallel to, not shared with, Mech_ShieldAbsorb_DirectFire). scaledDamage = Math_Q10Multiply(1000, damage) comes off the chosen facing (a zero front argument selects the second short, the rear); a negative facing clamps to 0 and the function returns overflow*0x400/1000. THE TWO SCALES ARE EXACT INVERSES -- 1000/1024 in and 1024/1000 out -- so a blast overflow is its own face value and the exchange rate matches direct fire. Reading the input scale as >>8 makes this look like a 4x amplification and a retail bug; the instruction is Math_Q10Multiply and there is no bug.
entries.signature: int __cdecl Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive(short *shieldPair, short front, short damage)

entries.name: Mech_ShieldAbsorb_DirectFire
entries.description: Direct-fire shield absorption: picks front/rear zone by where the muzzle sits in the mech frame, absorbed = min(incomingDamage, remainingShieldInZone), hard cap not threshold gate. Unlike Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive it scales neither its input nor its output. Returns the ray's entry point into the hit cylinder, so a fully absorbed shot still stops the ray.

entries.name: Behaviour_SetState
entries.description: The only writer of a mech's behaviour block at mech+0x4d, and so the AI state machine's single transition primitive -- its 30 call sites are the edge list. Stores the descriptor pointer at +0x00, seeds the timer at +0x05 to descriptor+0x04 plus (DAT_004a9bf4 & 0xf) after stepping that global by 13, zeroes +0x09, memsets +0x0d for 0x28 and +0x35 for 0x10, then sets +0x36 to 1. Callers are responsible for releasing the selected target; Mech_AiSelectBehaviour does so on every path.

entries.name: Behaviour_CountTick
entries.description: (block): the end of every Mech_AiTick. When block+0x36 (set to 1 by Behaviour_SetState) is set it clears it and counts nothing; otherwise it sets block+0x35 to 1 and increments the int block+0x09. So +0x09 counts the AI ticks a state has run, less the one it was installed in.

entries.name: Behaviour_BuildStateTable
entries.description: The unmarked static initialiser that builds all 22 behaviour state descriptors at 004993a4 from the slot blocks at 004998f8: name, dwell time, the 16-bit flag mask expanded through Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits, the three member-function triples and the +0x3c short. Ghidra's analysis does not recognise it as a function; create one at this address to read it.

entries.name: Flyer_BuildStateTable
entries.description: Static initialiser for the Flyer class' own behaviour state table: seven 0x3c-byte descriptors at FlyerBehaviourStateTable (00499cf8), each taking its name from FlyerBehaviourStateNames (00499f98), a dwell immediate, a 16-bit flag mask through Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits, and its three {func,thisDelta,vtableIndex} triples copied from FlyerBehaviourSlotBlocks (00499e9c). Sits immediately after Behaviour_BuildStateTable's RET and is reached only as a C++ static init, so nothing calls it.

entries.name: Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits
entries.description: Unpacks a 16-bit mask into 16 one-byte booleans (bit & 1 each), used on behaviour state descriptor +0x08 by Behaviour_BuildStateTable. Bits 0-5 are the only ones any state sets: 0 stops Mech_AiTick running the dwell countdown (true of every state bar deciding, the five combat states, driving off en and fleeing), 1 marks a state as committed to a fight, 2 as holding a place, 3 as ignoring incoming fire, and 4/5 carry the target state tier Ai_TargetStateTier reads.

entries.name: Mech_ApplySquadCondition
entries.description: Writes a player-squad machine's carried-over condition into its damage arrays at spawn; DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects' squad branch is the only caller (004258de), after Mech_ConfigureLoadout. Arguments are the damage header at mech+0x206 and the 0x7e-byte squad record's three player.mec condition spans: +0x3c external (13), +0x56 internal (10), +0x6a hardpoint (10), each 0-100. Each entry becomes damage (100 - condition) * maximum / 100: components 0-12 against the piece's armour, components 13-18 zeroed; internals 0-8 against their maxima, internal 9 (pilot) and 10-11 zeroed, so the internal span's tenth entry (overall condition) is not read; components 19-28 against the mount's armour plus the maximum of internal 12+i, and past the armour the mount is written -1 and the rest goes to that internal (-1 past its maximum). Internals 12-21 have maximum 0 in retail, so a mount simply takes its share of its own armour. Writes only through the header's two array pointers.

entries.name: Component_FillDamageReadouts
entries.description: Fills the damage-readout buffer from a component-damage object: shorts 1-19 the armour components as Q8 fractions (0x100 when destroyed), 20-31 the twelve dependents on their own, 32-41 ten combined armour+dependent readings. MfdStatusScreen_Paint scans 20-31 for its CRITICAL/INT DAMAGE condition.

entries.name: Component_ReadEntryDamage
entries.description: (header, kind, index): one damage-array entry as Q8 of its maximum, (damage << 8) / max, with no aggregation -- unlike Component_ReadDamagePercent. header is the component system at obj+0x206. Kind 0: dependent (internal) entry index against the .DMG internals' maximum at (header[3])[+4]; kind 1: main entry index against piece index's armour (18-byte piece records at (header[3])[+0]); kind 2: the main entry 19 places further on (+0x26 bytes) against the same piece's armour. A negative (destroyed) entry or a zero maximum reads 0x100.

entries.name: Mech_WeightedArmorRemaining
entries.description: Sum of (maxArmor - damage) * weight / maxArmor over a machine's live components, against the weight table at 00499fe0. maxArmor is the component's .DMG record; a component at or past 150 damage contributes nothing.

entries.name: maybe_MechPool_FlushPhase
entries.description: Subsystem phase 5's mech entry, registered by maybe_MechModule_StaticInit and so run once per frame from Sim_RenderFrame: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(DAT_004a9c02, DAT_004a9bfe). The queue at DAT_004a9c02 is written once by DBSim_LoadScriptDat and read only here -- NOTHING EVER QUEUES A MACHINE ONTO IT, so this drains an empty queue every frame and no mech node is ever returned to the pool during a mission. That is what makes obj+0xb1 un-inheritable for a machine; see docs/simulation/ai-combat-states.md.

entries.name: Mech_GetTorsoTwistAngle
entries.description: Returns mech+0x298. Mech vtable slot +0x3c; the Center Body command (scancode 0x2b) uses it to work out the heading the legs must turn to.

entries.name: Mech_GetSpeed
entries.description: Mech vtable slot +0x38 (vtable 0049a282). Returns Q10(2000, mech+0x28e) for a walker, or mech+0x2bd when the type record's flyer flag (+0x50) is set. Used for its sign by the Center Body branch, and as a speed term by the AI's lead-the-target maths.

entries.name: Mech_GetShieldByHeading
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x34. Given a heading angle, returns the front (+0x222) or rear (+0x224) shield value by which side is within +/-90 degrees.

entries.name: Mech_GetOverallDamage
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x40. The machine's overall damage figure; Mech_AiFleeCheck uses it as the base of its fear value.

entries.name: Mech_GetBodyRadius
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x5c: returns typeRec+0x70 (.DAT offset 110, the body radius), which every retail HERC states as 750. Mech_GetCollisionRadius at 0041552c (vtable +0x7c) is a byte-identical second copy of this function, so a machine's body and collision radii are the same field. Distinct from typeRec+0x1a, the generous shot radius the direct-fire hit test rejects against, and from shape+8, the drawn model's bound.

entries.name: Mech_GetCollisionRadius
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x7c: a byte-identical copy of Mech_GetBodyRadius (00415518), returning the same typeRec+0x70 -- 750 on all 21 retail chassis, so it is never zero for a machine. Read by Mech_CollisionTest of the object being walked into, and by Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance through the same vtable slot.

entries.name: Mech_ComponentPresent
entries.description: MechVtable +0x84. One entry of the occupancy array at mech+0x20e, by component slot. The targeting pod asks it to notice that the component it had locked has been shot off. The index is not bounds-checked; the pod cannot pass a bad one because the cursor and the id it holds are written together by Mech_NextTargetableComponent.

entries.name: Mech_NextTargetableComponent
entries.description: MechVtable +0x80. Steps a targeting pod's component cursor over the seven-entry rotation TargetingPodComponentRotation, skipping any slot the machine has lost (its occupancy array at +0x20e) and wrapping at 7. Answers the new cursor and writes the component id it names through the out-parameter, both -1 when the walk comes back to where it started.

entries.name: Mech_MissileLockState
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x6c: returns manager[0x0a + subtypeId*2], the per-missile-subtype LOCK flag -- NOT an ammunition count. Written every tick for every mech by Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate, which clears all five and sets the ones whose range-derived countdown expired. Rocket_Fire will not attach a target without it; WeaponMounts_MountIsReady gates a missile row's ready box on it. The real per-subtype round count is FUN_0040fbdc's separate local array.

entries.name: Mech_GetAimPoint
entries.description: The mech vtable +0x30: first triple (0, type+0x64, type+0x66), the pilot's eye; second (0, type+0x68, type+0x6a), the outside view's orbit centre.

entries.name: Mech_PlayerFireTick
entries.description: The player's fire path, called once a frame from Sim_PollPlayerInput with the input device struct. Calls WeaponMounts_FireTrigger(mech+0x202, inputDevice, mech); on a shot it also stamps the player's LINE OF FIRE into DAT_004a9c0c -- up to 40 points at 0x1000 spacing along the turret bearing, cut to the selected target's range, count in DAT_004a9d4c, zeroed when the trigger produces nothing. Nothing draws it: its only reader is Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance, which steers the player's own squadmates out of it. The only caller of the trigger path -- AI machines fire from their own think function.

entries.name: Mech_CreditNeutralisedTarget
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x60, told to the machine that just put victim out of the fight. Plain __cdecl on three stack arguments -- every call site pushes three and cleans 12 bytes, so the decompiler's __thiscall rendering with a leading parameter is wrong. victimAlreadyImmobilised suppresses the kill half only: the kill tally at mech+0x2a4, one short per victim target class (+0x1a8), the +0xa6 latch and the scorer's 0x02 callout. The victim's own 0x25/0x04 cry goes out either way, and is the image's only Ai_PostSquadMessage call that forces a post past a destroyed machine.

entries.name: Mech_HandleCommand
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x2c. Offers the command code to the machine's weapon-mount manager (WeaponMounts_HandleCommand) first and returns if that consumed it; otherwise handles the turret, throttle and shield commands itself. The shield commands are scancodes 0x1a/0x1b ([ and ]): it answers both with one Widget_PressChild(CockpitViewInstance+0x1e9, key != 0x1b, 1), pressing the shield gauge's rear child for [ and its front child for ] -- so a bracket key and a click on the meter are one code path from ShieldFacing_OnClick onward, click sound included. A flyer installs a stub at this slot, so the brackets do nothing in a RAZOR.

entries.name: Behaviour_DispatchMove
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x14. Reads the behaviour descriptor at *(mech+0x4d) and calls its +0x24 move triple as (*func)(mech + thisDelta), returning 0 without calling when the triple is entirely zero. This -- not vtable +0x18 -- is how Mech_MovementTick and Razor_MovementTick are reached, which is why neither has an xref.

entries.name: Behaviour_DispatchThink
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x18. Same shape as Behaviour_DispatchMove but reads the descriptor's +0x18 think triple. Every per-state think function in BehaviourStateTable is reached only through here.

entries.name: Behaviour_DispatchReassess
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x1c, reading the descriptor's +0x30 triple. 'Reassess' is a coined name for the slot, from what its two implementations do; the binary carries none. Combat states (attacking, flanking, facing off, attacking base, attacking flyer, fleeing) point it at 0041cf18; every other live state points it straight at Mech_AiSelectBehaviour, and 0041cf18 itself calls that twice.

entries.name: Mech_Constructor
entries.description: The Mech class constructor -- assigns a fully-populated 34-slot vtable at 0x0049a282 (by far the largest of the base-constructor-helper's 13 callers). Calls Damage_LoadMechDmgFile, Shield_Init, Component_AllocHealthArrays, Component_LinkMaxRefData.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyThrottleInput
entries.description: Player throttle handler. Integrates the stick axis into mech+0x290 (throttle, Q10, clamped +/-0x400) at Q8(0x91,-axis) per tick, converts it to a desired speed via Q10(maxRev or maxFwd, throttle), then calls Mech_LocomotionTick. ThrottleLeverMode (0049a06e) gates the clamp: at 0 it spans the full +/-0x400, so the axis held down runs through zero into reverse.

entries.name: Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance
entries.description: Terrain and obstacle avoidance applied to steering and desired speed. AI only -- Mech_LocomotionTick skips it when the mech is PlayerMech. Reduces to the nearer obstruction on each side, both starting at 22000, from three sources: two 20000-unit body-space probes splaying +/-10000 (Sim_RaycastShapes and Terrain_RayWalk), a sweep of live machines at Q10(2000, range) inside a 45-degree arc, and -- for a squad led by the player -- the player's line of fire at Q10(1000, range) inside 67.5 degrees. Steer is +/-((22000 - closest) * gain / 22000), gain 700 or 1000 for the firing line; only the firing line ever cuts the speed. The mirrored reverse mode is written 0 at the top of the function and never set, which also makes the half-speed arm of the speed override unreachable.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyTerrainSlopeToSpeed
entries.description: Adjusts desired speed by dot(terrainNormal, forwardVector)/0x960, signed by direction of travel, clamped to zero on sign flip. Uphill slows, downhill speeds up.

entries.name: Mech_LocomotionTick
entries.description: The Herc control law. Sets speed (mech+0x28e), turn rate (mech+0x28c), heading (mech+0x10) and animation rate (mech+0x2a0); about 60 percent of the body is the gait state machine. Writes no position -- all translation is animation root motion. Turn rate is a tent over speed peaking at half top speed; turn-in-place sets only the animation rate.

entries.name: Mech_Draw
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x00, reached from the ObjList draw-table walk. Runs Mech_SpliceHardpointShapes over every LOD root of the type's shape -- replacing each hardpoint placeholder part with the fitted weapon's shape or a blank record -- and then calls Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel. Gated on DAT_004a9c06.

entries.name: Shape_StampTransformId
entries.description: Writes one transform id into every part of a shape, recursing through the part lists: at a TSGroup/TSBSPGroup (0x140014, 0x14000b) into part+4, and at a TSBSPPart (0x140015) across the whole per-node transform array at +0x1c. Mech_ConfigureLoadout uses it to hang a weapon model on the hardpoint's bone.

entries.name: Mech_ConfigureLoadout
entries.description: Mech loadout (re)configuration, called on spawn/equip changes. Allocates the weapon-mount-manager object at mech+0x202 (malloc 0x14 or 0x35 bytes depending on the 'locally-simulated' flag).

entries.name: Mech_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x78. Spreads a group's members around its spawn point. No-ops for slot 0 (the leader stands on the point exactly); otherwise looks up Formation_GetSlotOffset(group's formation id at group+2, mech+0x49) and hands the offset to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset, which rotates it by the group leader's heading before adding it to the position.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyStartingCondition
entries.description: Applies a mission record's starting condition, as a percentage, once from DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects right after the machine's engagement/defeat actions are resolved. 100 is pristine; bands are >=0x50 untouched, >=0x3c 50 damage, >=0x28 80, >=0x14 120 plus the reactor dependent written off outright, and below 0x14 a WRECK: one of components 7/8 destroyed with 32000 (plus one of 13/14 when typeRec+0x4a>2), mech+0xa4 immobilised and mech+0xb4 collapsed. Each band ends in Mech_SpreadImpactDamage(mech, n, n+0x19). The condition comes from script.dat block 7 +0x84. Args derived from disassembly: two pushes with ADD ESP,0x8 at 004259b0; [EBP+8] mech, [EBP+0xc] word.

entries.name: Mech_SpreadImpactDamage
entries.description: Spreads one impact over the whole machine instead of aiming it. Each of the 29 live components draws its own (rand & 0xff) < odds roll; a component that is caught takes Math_Q8Multiply(rand(maxDamage) + maxDamage/2, Component_TotalArmor(i)) through vtable +0x74, so the share scales with what that component had to lose. maxDamage 0 returns immediately. Callers: the collapse landing in Mech_LocomotionTick (150, 120) and Mech_ApplyStartingCondition. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] mech, [EBP+0xc] and [EBP+0x10] words, plain RET.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Mech_SpreadImpactDamage(MechObject *mech, short maxDamage, short odds)

entries.name: Mech_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Attaches a mech to its mission group: stores the group pointer at mech+0x45 and the member slot index at mech+0x49, then fills in heading and position ONLY IF still at the -0x8000 'unset' sentinel -- which is why a roster record's own position ref wins where set and the group's point is the fallback. Position comes from the group's coordinate pointer (group+0x18), or from FUN_00423b0c against the group's route when that is null. Z is Terrain_HeightQuery plus the mech type's foot offset (typeRecord+0x16), plus 5000 when typeRecord+0x50 is set. Calls mech vtable +0x78 (Mech_ApplyFormationOffset) with the position first. FUN_00421ee8 and FUN_00405c3c are the flyer and base equivalents; the flyer one deliberately does no terrain query and substitutes z=5000 when the coordinate's z is zero.

entries.name: Mech_GetAimNodeTransform
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x24: resolves the type record's +0x0c (.DAT file offset 10, the camera node's shape part id -- the node the cockpit eye rides) through the shape's part lookup (shape vtable +0x20) and returns that node's 0x20-byte transform record at shapeInstance+0x16 + index*0x20, or the zeroed DAT_006c572c when the shape has no such part. Callers take its +0x14 translation as the point to aim at and its +0x1c as a sight height. This is what makes both guidance routines and the HUD target indicator aim at a HERC's cockpit rather than the ground point its model origin sits on.

entries.name: Mech_ComputeShieldCapacity
entries.description: Sibling of Mech_ComputeReactorRate for shield capacity; writes mech+0x228 via Shield_SetMax. Base is typeRecord+0xc0 = record offset 190, the maximum total shield, a fleet-wide 3500. Chassis damage above 0x80 on dependent-subpiece 4 scales it down in five steps to 50%; a Shield Pod in slot mech+0x30f adds up to a second full base (doubling it) on the same five-step pod-damage curve the Energy Pod uses. Called from Mech_ConfigureLoadout (followed by Shield_RefillToBalance) and again from Mech_ComponentDamageWrite, so capacity shrinks as the generator is damaged.

entries.name: Mech_ComputeReactorRate
entries.description: Computes the mech reactor output rate into mech+0x256. Base is a literal 0x14 (20) shared by the whole fleet -- the type record is never read. Replaced outright by Q10(200,20)=3 when mech+0xab (reactor critical) or Q10(600,20)=11 when mech+0xaa (reactor degraded). An Energy Pod in slot mech+0x313 then adds Q10(1024 - 204*(podDamage/51), 20), up to a second full 20 (it doubles output), gated off entirely at 225/256 damage. ONE reference in the whole binary, the tail of Mech_ConfigureLoadout, so the rate is sampled at spawn and never recomputed.

entries.name: Mech_ComponentDamageWrite
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x74. Shared damage-write/cascade endpoint for both damage pathways. Also latches the two reactor-damage flags off dependent-subpiece 5: mech+0xaa past 50% damage, mech+0xab at 75%+, each with an alert sound for the player; the check is gated on BOTH flags being clear, so once the first latches the second can only be reached by a single hit that crosses both thresholds at once. 8-level percentage bucketing with alert sounds, leg-pair status tracking (dependent-array slots {0,1} front legs, {10,11} rear legs on 4-legged types), mech-death trigger on enough destroyed limbs.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyExplosiveDamage
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x70. Args (weaponDamage, hitPos, blastRadius, attacker). Front/rear facing classification (<0x4000 BAM) -> Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive -> per-component roll at 0x802-in-0x1000 across up to 29 slots -> component world position via vtable +0x58 -> linear distance falloff (overflow * (blastRadius-distance)/blastRadius) via mech vtable +0x74. Structurally different from the direct-fire path: many random components with falloff, versus one deterministic component without.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Mech_ApplyExplosiveDamage(MechObject *this, short damage, int *hitPoint, short blastRadius, int *attacker)

entries.name: Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage
entries.description: Splits the armor damage by the PROJ.DAT splash factor (Math_Q10Multiply(shotData+8, shotData+4)) -- NOT a per-weapon-type effectiveness scale. The remainder goes to component health via mech vtable +0x74; the split-off share, when nonzero, becomes a 500-unit secondary explosion through the struck object's OWN +0x70 (a direct call, not a sweep). Also rolls to destroy the struck weapon mount on a damage-band change.

entries.name: Mech_DirectFireHitTest
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x20. Range check -> Mech_ShieldAbsorb_DirectFire -> Mech_SelectStruckComponent -> Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage. The hit-test and damage application are the same call, one level deeper than Sim_RaycastObjectList's caller.

entries.name: Mech_SalvageValue
entries.description: What one machine is worth to the player's side at mission end. Zero when mech+0xb3 is set. Otherwise queues every hardpoint under 0x80 damage to the salvage list as {template+0x56, (0x100-damage)*100/256}, then returns Q10(Mech_WeightedArmorRemaining(mech), typeRec+0x54) with typeRec+0x54 halved when component 0 is at full damage.

entries.name: Mech_IntegrateMotion
entries.description: Sets the animation playback rate from mech+0x2a0, then advances the object by dt = Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(100) via SimObject_ApplyRootMotion.

entries.name: Mech_CollisionTest
entries.description: Returns nonzero when the just-integrated position is refused. Three separate tests: (1) the live-object list, with an ASYMMETRIC gap -- this machine's vtable +0x5c against the other object's +0x7c, and an object whose +0x7c is 0 is skipped entirely; (2) FUN_00404ae4's structure-volume sweep, which covers exactly the structures test 1 skips; (3) terrain steeper than |normal.z| < 0x5aa, which for the player becomes a slide downhill whose landing damages the leg components scaled by the difficulty table at 0049a058. A block against another HERC also calls BOTH parties' +0x70 with a momentum-difference damage at radius 0x4b0, and latches the struck object's +0x68. It additionally records at mech+0x2b0 the last structure (target class 1, obj+0x1a8) whose body radius contains the machine, clearing the field on entry; that is a render-side hand-off, not an aim aid -- maybe_Scene_SubmitFrameObjects reads it every frame and buckets the machine with that structure instead of by its own radius.

entries.name: Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround
entries.description: Per-leg terrain placement over the mech animated node hierarchy. For each entry of mech+0x238 still holding a ground shape: moves the shape to the world position of the node typeRec+0x77[i] names, gives it the machine's heading (euler +0x10) and clears its +0x32 matrix-valid flag -- unconditionally. Then, within 15000 of the camera or for the player, tests the footfall for kind-0 entries (typeRec+0x72[i]) against the gait's thresholds and plays sound 0x1d on a plant.

entries.name: Razor_MovementTick
entries.description: The flyer chassis' per-tick move, the counterpart of Mech_MovementTick and NOT an autopilot. Integrates the world velocity at mech+0x2c5 into the position (skipped once mech+0xa4 is set), then runs six airframe contact probes -- the two wings, the two nacelles, the cockpit and the fuselage, the game's own names for them from STRINGS0 group 14 -- each against the terrain under it and, bar the fuselage, against a ray one tick's travel long. A contact damages that component through Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage with the hand-built shot record at 0049a170, kicks the airframe away from what it touched, and scales the damage by airspeed. Destroying the cockpit or the fuselage latches mech+0xa4 and the aircraft stops moving. Ends with the engine-note pitch and maybe_Mech_ConvergeGunsOnRange. Reached as slot +0x0c of the flyer behaviour class at FlyerBehaviourSlots, not through the mech vtable.

entries.name: Mech_MovementTick
entries.description: Per-tick mech physics step: push transform, integrate motion, clamp Z to Terrain_HeightQuery plus typeRec[+0x16], collision test, restore and reverse speed on hit, place legs. It steers nothing -- every AI movement decision is a think function calling Mech_LocomotionTick. Dispatched from Mech_AiTick through mech vtable +0x14 (Behaviour_DispatchMove) and the behaviour descriptor's +0x24 triple, so Ghidra reports zero xrefs. On a refused move for a non-player machine it arms the unstick manoeuvre: mech+0x26e = 10000, mech+0x254 = a coin-flipped +/-5000 side, mech+0xae = whether it was moving forward.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoTwistTick
entries.description: Torso/turret twist (yaw): rate at mech+0x294, angle at mech+0x298, clamped to +/- typeRec[+0x22]. Rates dt-scaled via Math_IntegrateRateOverTick. Only ACCELERATION is rate-limited -- when |Q8(axis, typeRec[+0x1e])| <= |rate| the rate snaps to it, so releasing or reversing the stick stops the turret dead. Args are (mech, axis, snapTarget, snapEnable); with snapEnable set the turret stops on the tick its angle crosses snapTarget, which is how Mech_CenterTorsoTick lands on centre. Ends by seeking the twist thread (mech+0x230) to (unsigned)angle >> 2 via AnimThread_SeekToPosition -- the turret has no rotation of its own. See docs/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoTwistServoSoundTest
entries.description: Run at the end of Mech_TorsoTwistTick for the locally piloted machine only (mech+0xa3), with that tick's axis input. When |axis| exceeds 0xc0, the twist angle (mech+0x298) differs from the one recorded last call and the static byte at 0049a1c9 is clear, it tests Sound_IsPlaying(0x21) and sets the byte if that sound is not playing; it clears the byte when the axis is zero or the angle has stopped moving; it records the angle in the static word at 0049a1ca. It never starts or stops a sound, and es2_xref.py finds no other reference to either static. See docs/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_ConvergeGunsOnRange
entries.description: Gun convergence, run at the tail of Mech_TorsoPitchTick with that tick's range argument -- the distance to the aim point, so the player's guns and the AI's both toe in on whatever the turret is tracking. For each mount, Math_EulerToward from the muzzle offset (its z less typeRec+0x66, the sight height) to (0, range, 0), stored at mount+0x24 and +0x28; a range of zero clears them. WeaponMount_PrepareShot is the consumer, composing them under the firing bone. Both gates (mount+0x5b/+0x5f, from .GL +0x02/+0x04) read zero on every retail chassis, so the convergence applies fleet-wide.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoPitchTick
entries.description: Torso/turret pitch: rate at mech+0x296, angle at mech+0x29a, clamped to the asymmetric range [typeRec+0x2c, typeRec+0x2a]. Same shape as Mech_TorsoTwistTick, on the pitch thread (mech+0x234) and typeRec[+0x24..+0x2c]. Its third argument is the range to the current target, passed straight to Mech_ConvergeGunsOnRange for gun convergence. See docs/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoPitchServoSoundTest
entries.description: Run at the end of Mech_TorsoPitchTick for the locally piloted machine only (mech+0xa3), with that tick's axis input. When |axis| exceeds 0xc0, the pitch angle (mech+0x29a) differs from the one recorded last call and the static byte at 0049a1cc is clear, it tests Sound_IsPlaying(0x21) and sets the byte if that sound is not playing; it clears the byte when the axis is zero or the angle has stopped moving; it records the angle in the static word at 0049a1ce. It never starts or stops a sound, and es2_xref.py finds no other reference to either static. See docs/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_IsEcmSwitchedOn
entries.description: The machine's jammer answer, stored into mech+0xa1 by Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate. Zero without an ECM pod at mech+0x307. With one, a locally piloted machine (mech+0xa3) answers with the pod's button copy at pod+0x7d and any other machine with its radar mode at mech+0x96, so an AI machine jams exactly while its radar is ACTIVE.

entries.name: Mech_GetEcmPodSwitch
entries.description: Returns the ECM pod's word at pod+0x7f, or 0 without a pod. EcmPod_Tick alone writes it, so it is zero for every machine but the player. Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate raises the engagement-action latch obj+0xa2 on the machine's selected target while it is set.

entries.name: Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate
entries.description: Per-mech-per-tick reactor/energy bookkeeping (integrates reactor output rate into the energy pool at +0x292), then dispatches weapon-energy arbitration and shield-recharge via Shield_RechargeTick.

entries.name: Mech_LockTonePlay
entries.description: Turns mech+0x9b (lock acquired) into the cockpit lock tone: FUN_0046272c(0x15) on a 0x40-coarse-tick blink cadence while set, 0x14 when clear but the target just changed (+0x9d), 0x16 once on loss. Called from the tail of Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate for the locally-piloted machine only.

entries.name: Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate
entries.description: The player's once-a-frame cockpit refresh. Its throttle exchange is the two-way binding between the machine and the cockpit slider: with mech+0x93 clear the gauge's value is written to mech+0x290, and ALSO to mech+0x2d7 when the type record's flyer flag is set, which is the only path by which the slider reaches a RAZOR's flight model. With the flag set the machine's own throttle is handed back to the gauge instead. The speed half it feeds the gauge is mech+0x28e, the walker speed scalar -- see KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

entries.name: Mech_ToggleRadarMode
entries.description: The manual's [R]; its one caller is CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand. Flips mech+0x96 between PASSIVE and ACTIVE, gated on +0xa3 so only the locally-piloted machine toggles, then withdraws and posts the radar-mode message (0x2c/0x2d) and plays the mode tone. The F4 scanner's PASS/ACTIVE buttons are not callers: MfdButton_OnClick writes +0x96 directly. A HERC powers up PASSIVE -- no constructor writes +0x96. Base_Construct latches it on for structure types 5, 6, 0x1d and 0x1e, the radar masts.

entries.name: Mech_ReadDamageReadouts
entries.description: Fills a 42-short display buffer for one machine: entry 0 is the type record's +0x6c, the rest come from Component_FillDamageReadouts.

entries.name: Mech_ReadEntryDamage
entries.description: (mech, kind, index): Component_ReadEntryDamage(mech+0x206, kind, index). Cockpit_PowerUpTick reads internals 0-9 with kind 0 for its announcement, and Player_DependentCondition reads one internal with it.

entries.name: Mech_ComponentNearestAim
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x54. Walks the machine's 29 component slots, places each occupied one through vtable +0x58, and returns the index of the one whose bearing from the given rocket (position at rocket+0x26) is nearest the rocket's heading triple (rocket+0xc), measured as the sum of the absolute differences of Euler elements 0 and 2; -1 when no slot is occupied. Rocket_Fire calls it through the locked target at launch and stores the result in the rocket's node handle (+0x5a), which Rocket_HomingSteer steers at. Base_FirstLiveComponent is the structure class's counterpart.

entries.name: Mech_ComponentPosition
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x58: the world position of one of the 29 .DMG components. Indexes the piece table at *(mech+0x1fa) by componentIndex * 0x12 and reads the two RUNTIME-ONLY HercPiece fields +0x0c (shape part id) and +0x0e (pointer to a short[3] point), which the .DMG loader leaves as -1/null and Mech_ConfigureLoadout fills in from the .COL. A null point returns the MACHINE'S OWN POSITION -- which is most of a HERC, since a mech .COL names only 6-16 of the 29 slots. Otherwise the point goes through the object transform, composing the part's posed node transform first when the part id is > 0 (strictly greater, so part 0 stays in the object frame). A part the shape lacks falls back to the identity transform at 006c572c. Also the accessor a missile takes its lock node's position from.

entries.name: Player_ResolveTargetAimPoint
entries.description: Resolves the point the HUD aims at on the selected target. With a targeting computer fitted (mech+0x30b) and the target inside 30000 units it asks the pod for a component aim point and component id; otherwise it takes the target's vtable +0x24 aim node transformed by the target's own rotation, falls back to the raw origin, and writes 0 to the component id.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyOutnumberedDamage
entries.description: (mech): returns at once when Mission_IsClearOfThreats(mech). Otherwise sums two strengths over every deployed object (group+0x14 clear) not out of weapons (+0xa5), immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99), split by whether its group side (+0x12) matches the mech's: each HERC within 45000 adds its type record's int16 +0x54 (the salvage scale), each flyer (pool 004a9e3d) within 50000 adds 500, and each armed structure (BASES.DAT +0x2e non-zero) within 35000 adds 500. The friendly sum loses 600, floored at 0; then Mech_SpreadImpactDamage(mech, 0x40, 0x40) runs once per 400 by which the hostile sum exceeds it. Group_ApplyOutnumberedDamage calls it.

entries.name: Mech_SquadOrderLineIndex
entries.description: The string index the F7 heads-down comm box prints on a squadmate's OBJECTIVE: line, into STRINGS0 group 40 (ATTACK/TRAVEL/PATROL/FORM UP/GUARD/FLEE/DEAD/IMMOBILE). Starts from the machine's behaviour descriptor +0x3c, then overrides with the standing squad order at mech+0x23e (1->1, 2->2, 3 or 6->4), but only when the machine is neither immobilised (+0xa4) nor destroyed (+0x99), its +0x3c is not 5, and the behaviour block's +0x09 is zero. Sole caller HddGauge_PaintIdle; this settles descriptor +0x3c's role. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] only.

entries.name: Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph
entries.description: Converts a mech's current speed to the KPH figure the HUD prints: currentSpeed * typeRec[+0xc2] / typeRec[+6], where MechType_InitOne sets typeRec[+0xc2] = Math_Q10Multiply(315, maxForwardSpeed) -- so the whole thing reduces to speed * 315/1024 (0.3076). Verified against the manual's HERC specs: OUTLAW's 325 max reads exactly 100 KPH, SAMSON's 190 reads 58 against a quoted 60, COLOSSUS 180 -> 55, MAVERICK 285 -> 88 against 90. Flyers (typeRec[+0x50] != 0, i.e. the Razor) take a different branch through the map-range helper 0047de3c. The 315 looks designer-fitted to make the fastest HERC read a round 100, so this constant should NOT be used to derive the simulation's tick length.

entries.name: Razor_ApplyFlightInput
entries.description: The flyer's input hand-off, called by Sim_PollPlayerInput in place of Mech_ApplyThrottleInput AND both turret ticks -- which is why a RAZOR's turret never moves. Packs the four device axes, Terrain_HeightQuery at the machine's position and four wing-destroyed flags (component array at mech+0x20e, entries 7/8/4/5) into a stack record and calls FlightModel_Step with the type record's flight model at typeRec+0x1dc. The axes are remapped against the walker's: device +0x0e (steer) is the aileron, +0x10 (throttle) the elevator, +0x12 (turret twist) the rudder and +0x14 (turret pitch) the throttle. On a tick the throttle axis moved it copies mech+0x2d7 to mech+0x290 and sets the mech+0x93 dirty flag, so the cockpit gauge follows the flight model.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Razor_ApplyFlightInput(MechObject *mech, int aileron, int elevator, int throttle, int rudder)

entries.name: maybe_MechModule_StaticInit
entries.description: The mech module's C++ static initialiser. Registers LAB_00415464 as subsystem phase 2 (sets word 004a9c06 to 1 and loads the developer keys' move and turn steps 004a9d50/004a9d52 with entry 3, 2000, of the tables at 0049a020/0049a032 -- nothing else; run once per mission from Sim_InitMissionSession) and LAB_0041544c as phase 5 (flush the mech delete queue, run once a frame), zeroes GlobalMechList (004a9bfe, which is the mech pool object itself) and vector-news DAT_004a9c0c. The two registered stubs are undefined functions in Ghidra and have no direct callers -- they are reached only through Subsystem_RunPhase.

entries.name: FlatObj_Destruct
entries.description: FlatObj vtable +0x08: restores TSObjVtable (004a0b98), deletes the shape instance at obj+0x34 through its own +0x18 with flag 3, and frees the object when the flag's low bit is set. ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue calls it with 2 and hands the node back to g_FlatObjPool itself.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_Dtor
entries.description: GUNLIST's destructor, from its class record (0041be41; GUNLIST is the 0x14-byte mount manager, table 00499338): (manager, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, Mem_DeleteArray of the mount-pointer array at +4 when set, then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0041be8d; class record at 0041be41

entries.name: WeaponMounts_DtorLocal
entries.description: PLAYER_GUNLIST's destructor, from its class record (0041bde1; table 00499238): (manager, flags). Rtl_VectorDelete(manager+0x1f, 6, 3, 1, 0041bf94) over the three 6-byte fire-group arrays WeaponMounts_CtorLocal allocates, then GUNLIST's teardown -- Mem_DeleteArray of the array at +4 -- and Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0041bf19; class record at 0041bde1

entries.name: Mech_AiEngageOrderedTarget
entries.description: Installs a squad order's target on the machine (maintaining +0x1a2 and +0x9d) and picks the state for it: a HERC sets mech+0xac and enters Mech_AiCombatReassess, a flyer takes attacking flyer, a structure attacking base.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourPlayerThink
entries.description: Think slot of behaviour states 1 player and 2 player fly. Gated on the machine being its group's leader, and always returns 0. Its first arm is the player's own waypoint arrival: the waypoint after the group's route cursor, inside 10000 units of ground range and not a closed route's terminating duplicate (Route_NextWaypointClosesRoute), posts WAYPOINT REACHED and steps the shared cursor. Three further arms switch on DAT_004a9ed8 into mission-objective work -- MISSION TARGET DETECTED, a 40000-unit goal proximity, and the four-message data-link sequence -- none of which touches the route.

entries.name: Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree
entries.description: The AI's radar switch, not a weapons gate: mech+0x96 is the PASSIVE/ACTIVE scanner mode. Copies mech+0xb2 (the squad's radar order) for a machine whose group is led by the player and mech+0x97 -- the mission file's own standing setting -- for everyone else. Every navigation state calls it; the detection sweep and the anti-radiation seeker are what read the result.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourSleepThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 13 (sleeping). Releases the target, Mech_LocomotionTick(0,0,0), Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree. Still ticked, detectable and able to answer fire.

entries.name: Ai_ClearSquadEngageOrder
entries.description: The tail of every combat think's completion test. Returns 1, and clears a standing squad engage order (mech+0x23e == 4) whose target at mech+0x248 is the one being let go.

entries.name: Ai_ShouldAbandonTarget
entries.description: Whether a combat state should drop its target. Under squad order verb 4, when Ai_TargetStateTier exceeds the order's threshold at mech+0x250. For the group order's designated target, dead or crippled on the human side but only +0x99 destroyed on the Cybrid side. Otherwise out of action (+0xa5, +0xa4 or +0x99). Called from the think functions of attacking, flanking, facing off and driving off en.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourAttackThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 3 (attacking). Skirt gate, combat geometry, then a standoff point 18000 units off the target's beam when the target is facing this machine (|aspect| < 8000) -- reflected through this machine's own position on the reverse arm -- or a plain square-up when it is not. Leaves the built-in 15000/30000 standoff ring.

entries.name: Ai_CircleStep
entries.description: The circling step flanking and attacking base share. On mech+0x60 (a 1000-count break-off, about half a second) it reverses in a straight line; otherwise it circles a target whose |aspect| is under the mech+0x66 hysteresis threshold (0x6000 circling, 0x4000 squared up) by steering at a point 15000 units out from the target on this machine's approach line rotated +/-6000, and squares up on one that is not, standing still while its own turret twist is inside 2000. The break-off is armed only while mech+0x288 (damage taken in the current ~2 s window, which Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate zeroes at each expiry of the +0x285 countdown) is past 100.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourAttackBaseThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 6 (attacking base). Forces the aspect to 32000 when the target's BASES.DAT +0x2e is zero, so Ai_CircleStep stands off instead of circling; standoffs 25000 / -20536, which makes the ring mandatory. Its completion test demands destruction, not merely being out of action, for a structure the mission order names.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourAttackFlyerThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 7 (attacking flyer). No skirt gate; standoffs 0/1000000 put both move-step arms out of reach so the state owns the approach flag outright. Advances only inside 2000 BAM of bearing error with the flyer past 35000 and not facing back. Returns finished past 150000 range.

entries.name: Mech_CompareCombatRating
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x4c. Compares this machine's combat rating (+0x29e) with a candidate's and returns the index the AI's three target-weight tables share: 0 this machine's is higher, 1 within 400, 2 the candidate's is higher. Returns 0 for every non-HERC candidate. Both ratings are jittered by rand & 1000 (AND AX,0x3e8) where rand % 1000 was meant.

entries.name: Ai_SumAttackerRatings
entries.description: Sums mech+0x29e over every machine in GlobalMechList whose target is the object passed in -- the combined combat rating of everything shooting at it, for Mech_AiFleeCheck.

entries.name: Mech_AiFleeCheck
entries.description: Installs the fleeing state (descriptor 00499800) and returns nonzero when it has taken the decision. A machine already out of action flees unless its target is a structure whose BASES.DAT +0x2e is zero. Otherwise fear = Mech_GetOverallDamage plus 5/25/50 per component (0049a328 lists six) past 60/120/180 Q8 damage, and it flees on how many machines hold it as their target: any at fear >= 71, three or a stronger pair at 51-70, three whose average rating beats its own at 31-50, never at 30 or under. Writes 300/600/1000 to mech+0x2aa.

entries.name: Mech_AiSelectAimComponent
entries.description: Chooses the component slot the AI aims at and writes it to mech+0x2a2, or -1. One rand & 0x7f picks a band: slots 7-18 under 0x28 or whenever a targeting computer at mech+0x30b reads under 0xaa at its +0x7f, the weapon-mount slots 19..18+mountCount, mountCount read from the shooter's own manager (this+0x202) under 0x50, else the chassis slots 0-6; a collapsed target (+0xb4) narrows it to slot 0. Within the band it skips slots the target no longer has (target+0x20e) and takes the highest Component_ReadDamagePercent + (rand & 0x3f). RETAIL BUG: the damage is read from this+0x206, the shooter's own components, while the occupancy array walked is the target's.

entries.name: Mech_AiCombatReassess
entries.description: The reassess slot of behaviour states 3-7 and 18. Puts the machine's radar to ACTIVE unless its group is led by the local player; keeps a just-handed target (+0xac) or re-acquires with Ai_SelectTarget, the squad order verb choosing between the order's own target and a free pick; a committed machine under a movement order instead falls into Mech_AiSelectBehaviour and drops the fight. A group's first member re-enters every other uncommitted member, so one machine's fight commits the group. Then runs Mech_AiFleeCheck and, if that did not decide, installs attacking base / attacking flyer for a structure or flyer and facing off / attacking / flanking for a HERC by Mech_CompareCombatRating.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourFleeThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 18 (fleeing). Moves the selected target into the block scratch at mech+0x61 and releases the selection, then reverses with the steer a half turn away while the threat is within 0x3000 of the nose and runs off at +/-0x6000 once turned, flipping side every 4000 ms. Engages the Turbo Pod every tick and still fires at the stash.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourFaceOffThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 5 (facing off), and the whole of state 16 (driving off en). Approach = -1 past 0x1fff of bearing error, else 1; standoffs 16000/35000. Never steers anywhere but at the target.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourFlankThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 4 (flanking). The shared combat shape with Ai_CircleStep between the geometry and the move step. Unreachable in retail: the combat reassess gates it on typeRec+0xc8, zero on all 21 chassis.

entries.name: Ai_NavigationStep
entries.description: The movement half the patrol, search-and-destroy and guard thinks share: Ai_DriveToPoint at mech+0x240 under a standing squad order, Ai_FollowRoute for the group leader, Ai_KeepFormation for everyone else -- so ONLY THE LEADER READS THE ROUTE. Then Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree and Mech_CenterTorsoTick.

entries.name: Mech_AiEnterCombat
entries.description: Thin wrapper that calls Mech_AiCombatReassess; the entry point other AI paths use to force a machine into the combat decision.

entries.name: Ai_NavigationStepThunk
entries.description: A bare tail call to Ai_NavigationStep. Named by no behaviour descriptor.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 12, search/destroy. Mech_BehaviourPatrolThink's shape and the same leader gate, differing in that what it acquires must pass Group_IsOrderTarget -- the group fights only what its order names.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourPatrolThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 8, patrolling. Ai_NavigationStep, drop the target, then a gate that returns for any machine that is neither the group leader nor under a standing squad order -- so only the leader ever acquires. Past it, on the 10000-count (about 4.9 s) block-scratch timer at mech+0x5a: a machine out of action takes fleeing, otherwise it acquires (mask 1) only when the group order verb is 3 or the squad verb is 2, and hands the result to Mech_AiEnterCombat.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourTravelThink
entries.description: Behaviour states 9 and 11, travelling and bulldog travel. Calls Ai_FollowRoute DIRECTLY rather than through Ai_NavigationStep, so every member reads the route and every member can advance the shared cursor. Then drops the target and, on the mech+0x5a timer, acquires into mech+0x5f -- a turret look-at, never written to mech+0x1a4.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourFollowThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 10, following. Mech_BehaviourTravelThink with the route replaced by Group_OrderTargetObject's position and a 25000-unit stop, that stop being a 3D Math_DistanceBetweenPoints range rather than the ground one every steer uses. Touches no route cursor, while verb 6's completion test is a route test -- so a following order can only complete on a group whose route was empty to begin with.

entries.name: Mech_AiGoalPosition
entries.description: Resolves the point a machine is working to: a squad order's target object or its stored point for verbs 3, 5 and 6, otherwise the mission group's current order target via Group_OrderTargetPosition.

entries.name: Ai_LineOfSightBlocked
entries.description: Line of sight from this machine to its selected target, both endpoints lifted to their aim-node origins or by 500 units when there is no node: 0 clear; 1 blocked by something the machine cannot get past (a shape, via Sim_RaycastShapes, or ground too steep to walk); 2 blocked only by ground it could walk over. The trigger for the skirting state.

entries.name: Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x64. Copies the selected target's position to mech+0x31e and sets mech+0xad, which makes the next combat think enter skirting. Its one caller is the tail of Sim_RaycastObjectList: a shot that stopped nearer than the shooter's target and within 0x2000 of the same bearing. The base and flyer classes leave the slot empty.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourSkirtThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 14 (skirting). Walks an arc around whatever blocked the line of fire, at a point 90 degrees off the line to the position stashed at mech+0x31e, re-testing Ai_LineOfSightBlocked every 5000 ms and restoring the stashed descriptor from mech+0x5a when it comes back clear. A terrain block (reading 2) gets no arc.

entries.name: Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked
entries.description: The gate at the top of every combat think. When mech+0xad is set it stashes the current descriptor at mech+0x5a, installs skirting (descriptor 0x499708), records the 3D range to mech+0x31e at mech+0x67, and returns true so the think does nothing else.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourDriveOffThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 16 (driving off en). Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked, then Mech_BehaviourFaceOffThink verbatim. The states differ only in their descriptors: this one holds a place and reassesses through Mech_AiSelectBehaviour.

entries.name: Ai_SelectDefenceTarget
entries.description: Picks the HERC threatening a defended point: over GlobalMechList, candidates passing Ai_IsTargetable and not crippled, scored (limit - distance to the point) / (holders + 1), where limit is 90000, or 980000 when the group's current order names no object. Preferring live candidates, it returns the best. Used by Mech_AiOnTakingFire for the guarding and driving-off states.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourGuardThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 15, guarding. A player squadmate with no standing order holds formation instead; everything else works a standoff ring on Mech_AiGoalPosition -- approach past 30000, hold facing OUTWARD (the -0x8000 in the steering term) between 10000 and 30000, walk away below 10000. Targets through Ai_SelectDefenceTarget, installing driving off en (16) or fleeing (18).

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourRamTick
entries.description: The per-tick MOVE slot of one AI behaviour state, NOT a death throe: block 00499b5c's +0x0c, whose think slot Mech_BehaviourRamThink (0041e570) charges the machine's selected target at full throttle and calls this three times a tick once its charge timer fires. Integrates motion, snaps the machine to terrain height + typeRec+0x16, places its legs, and runs Mech_CollisionTest; on a block (or once mech+0xb1 is latched) it detonates Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep(pos, 3000, 2000, 0, self) and then finishes off every one of its own 29 components with a flat 32000 through vtable +0x74 -- a guaranteed self-destruction, no roll and no falloff. Ghidra's function boundary starts one prologue late at 0041e48e. The mech+0xb1 arm is the 'something ran into me' latch Mech_CollisionTest raises through vtable +0x68 (SimObject_SetRunInto, 0042200c) on whatever blocked it; that byte has exactly one writer and this one reader in the image and is NEVER cleared, so a machine bumped earlier in the mission detonates on its first tick in the state.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourInertThink
entries.description: Behaviour states 20 (dead) and 21 (disabled). Mech_LocomotionTick(mech, 0, 0, 0) and nothing else.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourRamThink
entries.description: The think slot (+0x00) of AI behaviour state block 00499b5c, the ramming attack. Acquires a target through Ai_SelectTarget(this, 6, 0) into mech+0x1a4 every 10000 ms (timer at mech+0x5a), maintaining its +0x1a2 refcount, then steers with Mech_LocomotionTick(turn = (bearing - heading) >> 8, throttle 0x100) -- a QUARTER the steer gain every other state uses. A two-phase flag at mech+0x5f over a countdown at mech+0x62, each phase arming the timer it ENTERS: approaching (0) lasts 8000 + rand(4000), charging (1) lasts 3000 + rand(1500). Charging, it calls Mech_BehaviourRamTick TWICE, interleaved with two more steers -- three RamTicks a tick counting the move slot's own. Both fields start zeroed by Behaviour_SetState, so entering the state charges immediately. Always returns 0.

entries.name: Ai_BuildCombatGeometry
entries.description: Fills the 0x18-byte block every combat think passes down: +0x00 bearing to target, +0x02 bearing error, +0x04 its magnitude, +0x06 the target's aspect (bearing back to me in its turret frame), +0x08 its magnitude, +0x0a 3D range, +0x0e approach flag, +0x10/+0x14 the 15000/30000 standoff pair. The states steer on the aspect, and the copy Ai_AimAndFire is handed has one reader, Ai_ChooseWeapon's shield-facing test.

entries.name: Ai_CombatMoveStep
entries.description: The combat states' movement: sets the block's approach flag from the range against the standoff pair -- choosing the sign so the machine opens or closes the range whichever way it is facing -- stashes it at mech+0x5a, and drives Mech_LocomotionTick with the bearing error >> 6 and +/-0x100. The range arms read the magnitude Ai_BuildCombatGeometry left, before the caller's own steering override is folded in.

entries.name: Mech_CenterTorsoTick
entries.description: The [Backspace] 'Center Turret' command, run every tick while DAT_004d2588 is latched. Drives each torso tick with -clamp(Q10(0xfa, angle), +/-0x100) and snapTarget 0 with the snap enabled, so the turret runs home and stops exactly on centre. Nothing clears the mode on arrival; the input path clears it the moment either turret axis is non-zero.

entries.name: Ai_AimAndFireAtMech
entries.description: Ai_AimAndFire's machine branch. Refuses the shot and centres the turret when the bearing error exceeds the chassis' torso-twist limit (typeRec+0x22: 14000 on 20 of the 21 chassis; PITBULL's 32767 passes every error but 0x7fff and -0x8000). Aims at the chosen component (mech+0x2a2) only when the 3D range is in [5000, 20000); otherwise at the target's aim node origin. Ends in Ai_FireAtPoint.

entries.name: Ai_AimAndFire
entries.description: The aim-and-fire tail every combat think ends on, and which travelling/following call against their look-at object -- so a walking machine shoots at what it watches without selecting it. Switches on the target's class (obj+0x1a8) to pick the aim point: class 0 goes to Ai_AimAndFireAtMech, class 1 to the structure's first live component (vtable +0x54 with a null second argument, then +0x58), anything else to the object's position plus its own aim offset (vtable +0x30). A null third argument means mech+0x1a4.

entries.name: Mech_AiSelectBehaviour
entries.description: Picks and installs the next AI behaviour state. Three mutually exclusive paths: the local player (mech+0xa3) takes 'player fly' or 'player' on the type record's flyer flag typeRec+0x50; a machine in the player's own group with a standing squad order (mech+0x23e) maps verbs 1/2 to 'patrolling', 4 to FUN_0041c0f4 against the order target at mech+0x248, and 6 to 'guarding'; anything else reads its mission group's current order (mech+0x45, array at group+0x44 indexed by group+0x6c, verb = the entry's first short) and maps 0-6 to search/destroy, ramming, guarding, patrolling, sleeping, travelling-or-bulldog-travel (split on typeRec+0x22 vs 0x7d01) and following. A null order entry substitutes verb 0x0b, which matches no case. Every path releases mech+0x1a4, decrements the target's +0x1a2 refcount and sets mech+0x9d, so a state change always drops the target.

entries.name: Mech_ComputeCombatRating
entries.description: Writes the combat rating at mech+0x29e and latches the cache flag mech+0x94, which Mech_DirectFireHitTest (00418ba8) clears on a hit and Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate tests to recompute. Rating = (typeRec+0x44 base + each live weapon mount's value scaled by its condition, for the mounts whose vtable +0x54 answers non-zero -- an ammunition mount only above an eighth of its magazine + each of 19 components' maximum scaled by its condition - a penalty per system over 70% damaged) >> 4, so it falls as the machine is shot apart or runs low.

entries.name: Cockpit_TargetAnglesFromCameraBone
entries.description: Transforms a world point into the pilot eye's frame and returns its azimuth/elevation. The camera part id (typeRec+0x0c) is a shape PART id: the shape find-by-id vtable slot (+0x20) returns the part, its TSBasePart.Transform (+4) is a transform id, and that indexes the per-node transform array at shapeInst+0x16 (0x20 bytes per entry). Composes the inverse of the mech transform (mech+0xc) then the inverse of that node transform, and subtracts typeRec+0x66. The cockpit eye rides the same node, which is where the retail cockpit bob comes from -- no dedicated bob code exists. Chain is uniform across the fleet: part 5 -> transform 11 -> 4 -> 1 for 16 of 18 HERCs, node 1 being the one the walk cycle animates.

entries.name: Ai_ChooseWeapon
entries.description: Scores every mount and returns the best above a floor mapped from mech+0x2aa (fear) through [0,0x400] -> [150,-100]; nothing above the floor means the machine aims and does not shoot. A mount whose vtable +0x5c answers non-zero (destroyed; an ammunition mount also when empty; a pod always) is passed over first. Score is Q10(100, damage credit) - Q10(1000, template+0x34) plus rand(35)*rand(35), where the credit is the armor damage with no shield, the shield damage when the shield holds, and the armor damage + 10000 on the shot that breaks it. Gates launchers on manager+0x0a lock, turns the radar on for an in-range SARH launcher, and latches mech+0xa5 -- no weapons left -- when every mount is absent or spent.

entries.name: Ai_FireAtPoint
entries.description: The AI's fire decision. Reuses the latched mount at mech+0x2ac while it is ready and in range, else spends mech+0xb5 or runs Ai_ChooseWeapon. Aims the turret through Cockpit_TargetAnglesFromCameraBone whether or not anything fires. Leads the point by range*targetSpeed/projectileSpeed along the target's heading, adds the difficulty aim scatter for a Cybrid group only, and fires -- a launcher immediately, a gun only inside 1000 BAM in both axes. Latches ELF and ELF2 back into mech+0x2ac.

entries.name: Mech_AiFriendlyFireComplaint
entries.description: Posts squad message 8 when the player shoots a machine in the player's own group, on a 40000-count (about 19.5 s) cooldown at mech+0x278.

entries.name: Mech_AiOnTakingFire
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x50, called with (attacker, damage) when something hits this machine. Applies no damage. Shares the attacker as a contact through Detection_ShareContact, opens the 30000-count (about 14.6 s) under-fire window at +0x27d, and for a machine in the player's group accumulates the damage at +0x281 and ignores it until the total passes 8000. Otherwise, on a 10000-count (about 4.9 s) retarget cooldown at +0x273, it reacts by the current state's descriptor flag bits: bit 2 (guarding, driving off en) defends the post via Ai_SelectDefenceTarget around Mech_AiGoalPosition (a verb-4 squad order replaces the pick unless the pick is shooting at it; failing both, the attacker), bit 3 (sleeping, ramming, bulldog travel) ignores fire entirely, and anything else re-acquires with Ai_SelectTarget(this, 0x24, 0). Also posts squad message 3, and Mech_AiFriendlyFireComplaint when the player is the shooter.

entries.name: Ai_DriveToPoint
entries.description: The AI's one steering primitive: Mech_LocomotionTick(mech, (Math_HeadingToward(point, mech) - mech.heading) >> 6, speed, 0) with speed = mech+0x252 or 0xaa when that is zero, and a Turbo Pod sprint at 0x100 past 30000 units that only a standing squad order can reach. Returns whether the GROUND-PLANE range is under 10000 -- arrival, which is what Ai_FollowRoute steps the route cursor on.

entries.name: Ai_FollowRoute
entries.description: Drives at the waypoint AFTER the group's route cursor, advancing the cursor through Route_AdvanceCursor when Ai_DriveToPoint reports arrival, and standing still with the throttle at zero when the route has run out. One of four callers of Route_AdvanceCursor, with Mech_BehaviourPlayerThink, Flyer_LeadRouteStep and GroundVehicle_LeaderSteer; all four step the group+0x04 of the group they belong to.

entries.name: Ai_KeepFormation
entries.description: Holds this machine's formation slot on the group leader: the post is the leader's position through Mech_ApplyFormationOffset, so the formation rotates with the leader. Four arms by range and by whether the leader is moving -- match the leader's heading when parked inside 2000, fly formation on a lateral/longitudinal error taken in the leader's frame (Math_TransposeRotation2D on the leader's Q14 matrix), back out at full reverse when facing more than 45 degrees off, or close the gap.

entries.name: Mech_LoadResources
entries.description: mechsys.cpp's resource-load sequence for the mech subsystem -- the mech-side twin of Base_LoadResources (00405fac). Resets the mech-type-slot table (memset &DAT_004a9d8c, 0xff, 0x55), then streams dat\mforms (string 'mforms' at 0049a46b, joined with the shared 'dat' folder-prefix helper FUN_00492ae0): reads a 2-byte record count into DAT_004a9dec, allocates that many 28-byte vector elements (Rtl_VectorNew(..., 0x1c, count, ...) -- 7 (x,y) int16 pairs/formation, matching Formation_GetSlotOffset's stride), stores the vector pointer into _DAT_004a9df0 (g_MechFormationTable), then reads count*28 bytes straight from the file into the buffer. Afterwards loads the 7 mech texture groups (g_MechTextureGroupNames/g_MechTextureGroupSlots) via FUN_0045cdd8/FUN_00469f38, unrelated to formations. Auto-analysis does not disassemble it on its own: it sits directly after another function's RET with no call-graph edge, so it is found only by scanning for the 'mforms' string's address as a PUSH-immediate operand. Registered into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via a thunk at 00420654 (FUN_00401d64(Mech_LoadResources, 2)), so the game runs it.

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_GetIndex
entries.description: Trivial accessor, returns (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] -- a per-slot byte, 0xff sentinel meaning 'unused', otherwise the allocated dense index used by MechType_InitOne. Not independently cross-checked beyond its two callers (Mechs_InitAllTypes, MechTypeSlot_Allocate).

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate
entries.description: Assigns the next dense allocation index (DAT_004a9d8a, post-incremented) to slot param_1's (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] entry the first time it's requested; on the very first allocation overall, also caches an object-pool handle (FUN_0040feb4(1) result) into _DAT_004a9df4. Not independently cross-checked beyond call-site usage.

entries.name: MechType_InitOne
entries.description: Per-mech-type init, called once per valid slot (0-0x54) by Mechs_InitAllTypes. Opens the per-mech-type resource files (name built from the mech's own code string + several folder-prefix globals), reads a 0xd8-byte fixed record into the MECH_TYPE_DATA[typeIndex] struct (0x21e bytes/entry) at record offset 2, initializes hit-zone/collision/debris sub-resources, and -- the confirmed answer to 'how does DBSIM pick a mech's texture' -- for every mesh sub-component of this mech type, sets TSShapeInstance+0x26 (bound active DBA, see docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md) to '&g_MechTextureGroupSlots + typeRecord[0x96]*8'. typeRecord+0x96 is MechType_TextureGroupIndex (see that entry); the 0xd8-byte record it lives in is read directly from simvol0/dat/<MECHNAME>.DAT at record offset 2, so record offset 0x96 is file offset 148, the texture-group index.

entries.name: Mechs_InitAllTypes
entries.description: Creates the 'mechs' object pool (string xref confirmed) sized DAT_004a9d8a*0x21e (the MECH_TYPE_DATA record size), then loops mech-type slot 0..0x54 calling MechType_InitOne (004201a8) for every slot MechTypeSlot_GetIndex (0041ff00) reports as in-use (!= 0xff).

entries.name: Formation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: Returns a static 3-short {x, y, 0} formation offset: table[formationId * 0x1c + slot * 4 - 4] and the short after it. So a formation is 28 bytes = seven (x, y) short pairs, covering follower slots 1-7. The table pointer _DAT_004a9df0 is written by Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0), which reads dat\MFORMS.DAT -- 142 content bytes = count + five 28-byte formations, byte-exact.

entries.name: Mech_GetGunLayout
entries.description: GunLayout_GetBySlot(mechTypeRecord[0] + _DAT_004a9df4) -- this machine's hardpoint list. Its return value is what Mech_ConfigureLoadout hands MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts as the record array and count.

entries.name: Mech_RegisterLoader
entries.description: Thunk that registers Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0) into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via FUN_00401d64(Mech_LoadResources, 2), then separately allocates the 7-slot mech-texture-group vector (Rtl_VectorNew(&g_MechTextureGroupSlots, 8, 8, 1, ...)). Found by raw dword-scanning DBSIM.EXE for Mech_LoadResources' address used as a PUSH-immediate operand (68 B0 FD 41 00); like Mech_LoadResources itself, was never auto-disassembled by prior analysis (sits right after another function's RET, no call-graph edge into it).

entries.name: ConfigPart_GetClassTagZero
entries.description: CONFIG_PART vtable +0x00 (0049a494), kept by GUN_STATE and every weapon-mount class: returns 0, where TSPartBase answers a real class tag.

entries.name: ConfigPart_Dtor
entries.description: CONFIG_PART vtable +0x18 (0049a494, RTTI 'CONFIG_PART', 0x18 bytes; bases TSPartBase and SHAPE_INST at +0x10), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). HeapBlockOwner_Dtor(this+0x10, 0) on the SHAPE_INST, TSBase_Dtor(this, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00420730; class record at 004206c9

entries.name: Computer_PostMessage
entries.description: Posts a SYSTEM.STR message id to the cockpit computer's ticker -- the port at CockpitView+0x20b -- through its vtable slot 0, as a {short id, int subject} record with a null subject. The sibling for the pilot and squad channel is Ai_PostSquadMessage (00420a98).

entries.name: Ai_PostSquadMessage
entries.description: Posts {messageId, machine} to the pilot-and-squad message port (the object FUN_00433158 returns) through its vtable slot 0, suppressed for a destroyed machine unless the third argument forces it. Ids raised by the AI targeting path: 1 enemy sighted, 3 taking fire, 8 friendly fire.

entries.name: Mech_ReceiveSquadOrder
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x28. One machine receiving one transmitted squad order: switches on the record's verb (STRINGS0 group 0, 0-0x11) over twelve jump-table arms covering sixteen verbs (6, 9 and anything above 0x11 take the default) and installs the standing order at mech+0x23e, its destination at +0x240, its target at +0x248, its guard subject at +0x24c and its abandon tier at +0x250. Verbs 0xd/0xe write patrol and move, 0/2/0xb write engage, 0xc writes guard; 3/0xa/0xf clear the order and reinstall patrolling; 4/0x10 and 7/0x11 are the radar pair, writing mech+0xb2 and mech+0x96; 5 and 8 are the FIRE AT WILL / HOLD YOUR FIRE pair, writing mech+0xb6; 1 sets the ignore-the-player's-selection latch at mech+0x9a, which 0, 5 and 0xb clear. Returns 1 when the order was taken. Each case picks a reply id for Ai_PostSquadMessage, posted only when priorReply is 0, or 1 with an accepted order. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8], [EBP+0xc], [EBP+0x10]; the vtable call site at 0043164d pushes three and does ADD ESP,0xc.

entries.name: Flyer_GetSpeed
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x38: Q10(1000, flyer+0x233), where +0x233 is the type record's +0x04 forward speed, copied in by Flyer_Constructor and never written again. A chassis constant, not anything the aircraft is doing.

entries.name: Flyer_HandleCommandNoOp
entries.description: FLYER vtable +0x2c: loads its second argument into AX, then XOR EAX,EAX and returns 0 without acting on it -- which is why the shield bracket keys do nothing in a RAZOR.

entries.name: Flyer_Draw
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x00. Sets the shared draw-state global from DAT_004a9e48, calls Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel, clears it again.

entries.name: Flyer_Constructor
entries.description: Flyer class constructor. Installs vtable 0049a5e0, allocates the component-damage header at flyer+0x200 with literal counts of 1 and 1 (one main component, one dependent -- exactly what SKIMMER.DMG ships), and links the type record at flyer+0x1fa plus its .DMG and .COL pointers via Component_LinkMaxRefData.

entries.name: Flyer_DispatchMove
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x14. Calls the installed behaviour descriptor's +0x24 move triple (the descriptor pointer is at flyer+0x4d). The flyer twin of the mech dispatchers; Mech_AiTick (00411cec) is what reaches it.

entries.name: Flyer_DispatchThink
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x18. Calls the installed behaviour descriptor's +0x18 think triple.

entries.name: Flyer_DispatchReassess
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x1c. Calls the installed behaviour descriptor's +0x30 reassess triple, which for every flyer state is Flyer_AiSelectBehaviour (00422d00).

entries.name: Flyer_MovementTick
entries.description: The flyer's per-tick move, the +0x24 slot of the four behaviour states that have one. Adds the world velocity at flyer+0x24f to the position RAW -- three plain ADDs at 0042190a, with no Math_IntegrateRateOverTick, so a flyer's world velocity is a per-tick step where Razor_MovementTick's is a rate. Then four terrain probes (two wingtips at (+/-1000,-420,-300) that roll the airframe away, a nose point at (0,1000,0) and a look-ahead at (0,15000,-1500) that pitch it up), a clamp of the origin to terrain+500, and the flyby loop (sound 0x31) started or released at 30000 units from the view object. No damage, no object sweep, and no gate on being wrecked.

entries.name: Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x74. Thin wrapper over Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade on the header at flyer+0x200: destroying component 0 loses the aircraft -- sets flyer+0x99, credits the kill through the attacker's +0x60, fires the mission action at flyer+0x1b6, and writes -100000 to flyer+0x2e so it falls.

entries.name: Flyer_DirectFireHitTest
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x20. Coarse reject on SimObject_GetShapeRadius (shape+8), then Mech_SelectStruckComponent against the type's col/<NAME>.COL model (flyerTypeRec+0x32) with the per-component alive flags at obj+0x208. Damage through vtable +0x74; spawns the shot's armour impact effect, or a fixed effect id 10 once the flyer is destroyed. No shields and no collision volume -- the simplest of the three hit tests.

entries.name: Flyer_GetOverallDamage
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x40: Component_ReadOverallDamage on the health header at flyer+0x200.

entries.name: Flyer_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x78. No-ops for member index 0 (the flight leader); otherwise reads the three-int16 station offset FlyerFormation_GetSlotOffset (00423044) resolves out of dat/FFORMS.DAT and hands it to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset (00411d64), which rotates it by the GROUP LEADER's heading and adds it to the caller's point. Unlike a mech's or a base's, the offset carries a Z, which is what stacks a flight vertically.

entries.name: Flyer_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Attaches a flyer to its mission group: stores the group at flyer+0x45 and the member index at +0x49; with flyer+0x0c holding the -0x8000 sentinel takes the group's heading and zeroes pitch and roll; with the Z position holding the sentinel takes the group's own point (group+0x18, else route waypoint 0), applies the formation offset through vtable +0x78, and finally substitutes 5000 for a Z that came out zero.

entries.name: SimObject_SetRunInto
entries.description: Vtable +0x68 in ALL EIGHT SimObject-shaped tables -- base, mech, flyer and the five structure classes -- with no override anywhere. Two instructions: obj+0xb1 = 1, "something ran into me". TWO call sites through the slot, both collision sweeps calling it on whatever object blocked the move, whatever class that object is: Mech_CollisionTest (0041903a) and FUN_0046a510 (0046a581), the sweep inside StructureGroundVehicleVtable's +0x18 tick slot FUN_0046a5d0. Mech_BehaviourRamTick is the byte's only reader, and NOTHING clears it. Both the write and the read rebase (ADD reg, 0x92) and use displacement 0x1f, so a scalar search for 0xb1 finds neither -- search byte ptr [reg + 0x1f] instead.

entries.name: Flyer_PitchCommand
