entries.description: Elevator command that holds a pitch attitude: Q16(desiredPitch - flyer.pitch, 1500), resolved through cos(roll) at Q14, less Q16(pitchRate, 8000).

entries.name: Flyer_PitchToAltitude
entries.description: Elevator command that flies the aircraft to a world Z: Math_Atan2Guarded(targetZ - flyer.z, 10000) into Flyer_PitchCommand. The 10000 is a fixed horizontal run, so the demanded angle depends on the height error alone. Its other arm, gated on flyer+0xae and reading flyer+0x23c, belongs to the walking machine's obstacle avoidance and leg placement and is not known to fire on a flyer: the flyer pool is zero-filled and no flyer path that writes either field has been found.

entries.name: Flyer_CommandRoll
entries.description: Fills the command array's aileron element with Q16(desiredRoll - flyer.roll, 2500) + Q16(rollRate, -5000) and runs Flyer_ApplyFlightCommand. The arm Flyer_SteerAndFly takes whenever it is holding or limiting a bank rather than commanding one.

entries.name: Flyer_ApplyFlightCommand
entries.description: Hand-off into FlightModel_Step (00466a54). Squares the aileron and elevator elements with their sign kept ((v*v)>>8) and clamps them to +/-0x100, then calls the model with the flyer's flight block at +0x243, the .FM record at typeRecord+0x3a, and a stack array of four zeros as the wing-damage argument, which is why a Flyer never takes the model's lost-wing or lost-nacelle arms.

entries.name: Flyer_FormationThrottle
entries.description: Works a throttle figure out of the station error, the bearing to the leader and the two chassis' +0x233 speeds, folds it into the previous value of flyer+0x21c and clamps the sum to [0x8c,0x100]. No other reader of the field is known. The control law leaves FlightModel_Step's throttle element zero on every call, so nothing a Cybrid flyer decides changes its airspeed (the player's RAZOR THROTTLE binding can: FlightModel_Step's position branch then writes the setting to 0).

entries.name: Flyer_SteerAndFly
entries.description: The flyer's steering channel and the function every movement step (route step, station keeping, attack run) ends in. Builds a 16-bit bank command from Q16(-turn,2500) + Q16(bankTurnRate at flyer+0x287, 32000) + Q16(rollRate,-5000); holds the aircraft at +/-(typeRecord+0x0e, the maximum bank angle) with a 1500 hysteresis band when the bank would take it further over; answers a steering command under 2000 with rudder (Q16(-turn,4000)) and level wings instead of a bank, and only if the roll is already under 800. Fills the command array's fifth element with the terrain height under the aircraft, which is FlightModel_Step's ceiling reference. Its leader term reads leader+0x1f8, a field for which no writer is known (es2_fieldscan.py, decompile grep); the flyer pool is zero-filled.

entries.name: Flyer_LeadRouteStep
entries.description: The flight leader's route step. Takes the waypoint one past the group's cursor, advances the cursor when it is within 15000 ground units, else falls back to the cursor's own waypoint; holds altitude 30000 through Flyer_PitchToAltitude and steers with Q16(bearingError, 28000) through Flyer_SteerAndFly.

entries.name: Flyer_FormationStep
entries.description: A wingman's station-keeping. The station is the leader's position offset 0x2000 along the leader's heading plus this aircraft's FFORMS.DAT slot; a wingman that is ahead of its station while still aligned with the leader and inside 10000 units has its steering command mirrored (-0x8000 - err) rather than reversed. Ends in Flyer_SteerAndFly and then Flyer_FormationThrottle.

entries.name: Flyer_AttackRun
entries.description: The attack run, and the only place a Cybrid flyer shoots. A two-phase circuit on flyer+0x1fe: phase 0 extends AWAY from the target holding targetZ+10000 until the range passes 90000, phase 1 runs in and inside 65000 aims at the target itself, breaking off again when the bearing leaves +/-0x2000, the height over the target drops under 3000, or the range closes inside 10000. The aim is led along the target's heading by (range>>3)*(targetSpeed*8)/shotSpeed, where shotSpeed becomes PROJ.DAT row 2's speed once the run is close enough to shoot. Firing needs bearing and pitch both within +/-1000 and the flyer+0x21e countdown expired: the first shot of a pass inside 30000 is Rocket_Fire(0) off the (500,200,-100) muzzle and every later one is a pair of Bullet_Fire(2) off that point and its mirror, reloading the countdown with 1500.

entries.name: Flyer_FollowStep
entries.description: The movement step the three non-combat flyer thinks all open with: Flyer_LeadRouteStep for the group's first member, Flyer_FormationStep for everybody else, then flyer+0x96 (the radar mode) zeroed.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink
entries.description: search and destroy's think. Flyer_FollowStep, then for the flight leader only and when the flyer+0x5b countdown reads 0. The sweep reloads it with 10000, but Behaviour_SetState zeroes +0x5a..+0x81 at every reassess, so in practice the sweep runs on the state's first tick and after each 5000-count dwell: Ai_SelectTarget with mask 0x11 (mission target only, reject own class), checked against Group_IsOrderTarget before it is taken, then Flyer_EngageWithFlight.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourPatrolThink
entries.description: patrolling's think. The same shape as Flyer_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink with mask 0x10 and no order-target check, so a flight on patrol takes anything it can see that is not another aircraft.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourScoutThink
entries.description: scouting's think: Flyer_FollowStep and nothing else.

entries.name: Flyer_EngageWithFlight
entries.description: Puts the whole flight onto the leader's target: installs the attacking descriptor (00499d34) on itself, then for the group's first member only hands every surviving member the same target (obj+0x1a4, with the +0x1a2 counters and the +0x9d changed flag) and recurses into it. The recursion terminates because only the leader takes the loop.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourAttackThink
entries.description: attacking's think. Returns finished as soon as the target is immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99), which zeroes the dwell and sends the aircraft back through the reassess; otherwise Flyer_AttackRun for the flight leader and Flyer_FormationStep for everyone else.

entries.name: Flyer_AiSelectBehaviour
entries.description: The reassess slot of the five flyer states that have one (sleeping and dead carry a null triple): maps the group's current order verb onto a descriptor. 0 -> search and destroy (00499dac), 3 -> patrolling (00499d70), 4 -> sleeping (00499de8), 5 -> scouting (00499e24); 4 and 5 also latch flyer+0xa5, the out-of-the-fight byte. Verbs 1, 2 and 6 and an empty order slot match no case and leave ECX unwritten, so Behaviour_SetState is handed ECX as Flyer_DispatchReassess left it: the OR of the reassess triple, which is 00422d00, this function's own address.

entries.name: Flyer_LoadResources
entries.description: The flyer subsystem's loader (flyersys.cpp). Resets the 0x22-entry type-slot table at 004a9e50 to 0xff, then opens dat/fforms, reads a 2-byte record count into DAT_004a9e7c and count*0x12 bytes of formation records into the vector at DAT_004a9e80.

entries.name: FlyerType_RecordIndex
entries.description: Maps a FLYERS.NAM index to its slot in the loaded type-record array, out of the 0x22-entry table at DAT_004a9e50. 0xff means the type is not loaded.

entries.name: FlyerType_Register
entries.description: Claims a type-record slot for a FLYERS.NAM index the mission needs, if it has none yet, bumping the loaded-type count at DAT_004a9e4e.

entries.name: FlyerType_LoadResources
entries.description: Per-flyer-type resource load into a 0x70-byte type record: the dat/<NAME>.DAT stats over the record's first 0x2e bytes, the shape, the .dmg component file (+0x2e), the col/<NAME>.COL hit-sphere model via Collision_RegisterObject (+0x32, which is what the flyer's own vtable +0x20 Flyer_DirectFireHitTest passes to Mech_SelectStruckComponent), and the fm/<NAME>.FM flight model (+0x3a, 0x36 bytes) whose ceiling slope it derives into +0x48. It also binds the shape's texture bank by writing the LITERAL slot address 0x004a9e0e into TSShapeInstance+0x26 -- g_MechTextureGroupSlots + 3*8, texture group 3 (ENEMY) -- so every flyer type shares one bank rather than choosing per chassis the way MechType_InitOne does.

entries.name: FlyerTypes_LoadAll
entries.description: When the flyer type count 004a9e4e is non-zero: 004a9e74 = LoadNameList('flyers', 0x22), 004a9e78 = Rtl_VectorNew of that many 0x70-byte records (element ctor 00423098), then FlyerType_LoadResources for each of the 0x22 name indices whose FlyerType_RecordIndex is not 0xff. DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it.

entries.name: FlyerFormation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: dat/FFORMS.DAT slot lookup: DAT_004a9e80 + formationId*0x12 + slot*6 - 6. Three follower slots per formation, three int16 each (x, y, z), and the slot index is one-based: the flight leader takes no offset.

entries.name: ActionTimer_Tick
entries.description: One script.dat block-6 action timer per frame -- the second of the four ways a mission action activates. Counts the millisecond countdown at timer+0x2c down through Timer_CountDown, but only while the primary action at timer+0x00 has activated or the record names none (in which case it runs from mission start). On expiry it calls Action_Activate on each of the ten resolved action pointers at timer+0x04..+0x28 and re-arms the countdown with 30000, which through the <<11 in ActionTimer_SetDelay is about seventeen hours -- so a timer effectively activates once. This is why an action carrying no trigger area of its own is ordinary rather than dead.

entries.name: DBSim_BuildActionTimerRecord
entries.description: Small helper called once per row11 (action timer) record inside DBSim_LoadScriptDat: builds a resolved in-memory action timer from a primary-action ref + the delay short + a 10-slot ref array, all already resolved to row10-array pointers by the caller.

entries.name: Route_AdvanceCursor
entries.description: Steps a group's route cursor -- the {short index; waypoint-group ptr} pair at group+0x04 -- by one, and wraps the index back to zero when the route closes on itself (more than one waypoint, the new index is the last, and the last waypoint's point pointer is the same object as the first's). A closed route is a patrol that never ends.

entries.name: Route_NextWaypointClosesRoute
entries.description: Answers 1 when the waypoint after a route cursor is both the route's last and the same point object as its first -- the duplicate a closed patrol circuit ends on, and the one Route_AdvanceCursor would wrap straight off. Only Mech_BehaviourPlayerThink asks; it is what stops a circuit announcing its start point over and over.

entries.name: Squad_BroadcastOrder
entries.description: The MFD FLASH COMM page's transmit: sends one order to the whole of the player's group, best-suited machine first. Each pass scores every member not yet told -- verbs 0/2/5 prefer a machine whose behaviour descriptor +0x09 (committed) is clear, 1/8/0xf one where it is set, 4 and 7 one not already in the radar mode being asked for -- keeps the highest score and breaks ties on range to the issuer, then calls that machine's vtable +0x28 with the reply so far, so only the first recipient or the first to accept says anything. Verbs 0 and 2 stop at the first acceptance; the rest go round until everyone has been told. The score local is not initialised, so for a verb with no case every member carries the same leftover stack value ([EBP-0x1c]): range order when it is -1 or more, nobody told when it is below. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8], [EBP+0xc].

entries.name: TriggerArea_Resolve
entries.description: Load-time resolve of one script.dat block-4 (row #9) record into the 10-byte trigger-area record TriggerArea_ContainsPoint reads: type flag at +0, pointer to block-1 coordinate RefA at +2, and at +6 either a pointer to coordinate RefB (type 0) or the record's literal times 10 (other types).

entries.name: TriggerArea_ContainsPoint
entries.description: Tests a position against one resolved block-4 trigger area. Type flag 0: axis-aligned XY box strictly between the two block-1 coordinates the record points at, Z ignored. Non-zero type flag: distance from the single coordinate less than the stored radius (the file literal times 10).

entries.name: Action_Activate
entries.description: Activates one block-5 mission action, once: sets the action runtime activation flag at +0x0a (zeroed at load), then walks ten (counter ref, operation) pairs at +0x0c/+0x20, skipping a pair whose ref is negative and otherwise bumping (op 6) or clearing (op 5) the mission counter array DAT_004a9ef4. The queue of the mission message at +0x34 is INSIDE that loop, so an action naming five counters posts its line five times and one naming none posts it not at all.

entries.name: Action_TestTrigger
entries.description: Tests a position against one action's trigger areas. Returns 1 immediately if the action has already activated (+0x0a set); otherwise offers the position to each resolved block-4 area (count at +0x04, pointer array at +0x06) via FUN_004233a4 and calls Action_Activate on the first hit.

entries.name: Action_TestTriggerForGroup
entries.description: Action_TestTrigger applied to every member of a group in turn (member array at group+0x0c, count at group+0x10), stopping at the first that activates it.

entries.name: Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer
entries.description: Picks a clear arrival point for a deploying group or drop pod: offsets from the player position by distance at (player heading + bearing), then steps outward in 2000-unit increments until the point clears three tests in order. (1) Already-deployed objects, within their own vtable +0x7c collision radius plus 5000 -- APPLIED ONLY WHEN avoidDeployedObjects IS NONZERO, which Group_DeploymentCheck passes for the two walk-on verbs and clears for a drop pod, so a pod may come down on top of a machine. (2) Structure_GatherWalkCandidates collision volumes at radius 5000. (3) Terrain_FaceBlocksAt with a zero direction, which reduces to the steepness of the face under the point. The loop is unbounded.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer(int *outPoint, int distance, short bearing, int avoidDeployedObjects)

entries.name: Group_DeploymentCheck
entries.description: Per-frame arrival check for a mission group that has not entered the world yet, run by Sim_MainTick for exactly the groups whose record +0x14 action pointer is non-null. No-ops until that action runtime activation flag (action+0x0a) is set. Then the action verb (action+0x02) picks the arrival: 2 or 3 spawn a METEOR drop pod 150000 units from the player (bearing +-90 deg for 2, +-22.5 deg for 3) carrying the group, leaving +0x14 set for the pod to clear on landing and latching group+0x13 so only one pod is ever launched; 4 or 5 place the group leader at 90000 units behind (4) or 150000 ahead (5) facing bearing-0x8000, run every other member through vtable +0x78 for its formation offset, and clear +0x14; any other verb just clears +0x14 so the group goes live where it stands. All arrival points come from Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer.

entries.name: Group_OrderTargetObject
entries.description: The object the group's current order names -- the first member of the group it holds (+0xc == 0), or the object directly (1-3).

entries.name: Group_OrderTargetPosition
entries.description: The position the group's current order works to: the order object's +0x26 origin, falling back to the first waypoint of the group's route (**(*(group+6)+2)), read with no null check, when the slot is empty or names no subject.

entries.name: Group_IsOrderTarget
entries.description: Whether an object is what the group's current order names: for the order's +0xc == 0 the order holds a group and the test is group identity, for 1-3 it holds the object itself.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectPtr
entries.description: (group): the current order's +0x0e subject pointer -- the row-15 link at group+0x44 indexed by group+0x6c -- read without testing the slot for null. es2_xref finds no rel32 branch or stored pointer to it.

entries.name: Group_NearestLiveMember
entries.description: (group, obj): the member of group (array +0xc, count +0x10) nearest obj by Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, skipping obj itself and any member with destroyed (+0x99) or immobilised (+0xa4) set; 0 when none is nearer than 100000.

entries.name: Group_IsOrderComplete
entries.description: Whether a mission group's current order is finished, switched on the order's verb (order+0x00). Verb 0: the order subject's condition tier is 4 (destroyed). Verb 2: the order names a subject and either its tier is 4 or Group_NoRivalOrderOnSubject reports nothing hostile still assigned to it. Verbs 3, 5 and 6: the group's route cursor has no waypoint after the current index. Verbs 1 and 4 never complete and can only be ended by the order's action firing.

entries.name: Group_OrderTick
entries.description: Per-frame tick for a group that has entered the mission (the branch Sim_MainTick takes when group+0x14 is null). Runs the group's current order -- the row-15 link at group+0x44 indexed by the current-order index at group+0x6c -- and advances to the next when Group_IsOrderComplete reports it complete or its own action has activated, flagging the finished order in the byte array at group+0x70 and clearing each member's +0x52. Then ticks every member via Mech_AiTick.

entries.name: Route_WaypointAt
entries.description: Reads one waypoint out of a route cursor: null when the cursor has no waypoint group or the index is past its count, otherwise the resolved block-1 point at that index. Every 'is there a waypoint after this one' test in the AI is a call to this with index+1.

entries.name: DBSim_BuildGroupRecord
entries.description: Builds one script.dat block-11 record into a 0x7a-byte in-memory group record: discriminator (record +0x28) at group+0, formation id (+0x2a) at group+2, heading value at group+10, the resolved block-1 coordinate pointer at group+0x18, the resolved row-10 action pointer at group+0x14, and an allocated array of member object pointers at group+0xc. Then attaches every populated member by discriminator -- Mech_AttachToGroup (0/mechs), FUN_00421ee8 (1/flyers), FUN_00405c3c (2/bases) -- passing each its slot index within the group.

entries.name: MissionGroups_Allocate
entries.description: (array, count): array+4 = int16 count; array+0 = Rtl_VectorNew(0, 0x7a, count, 1, 004240e4), count 0x7a-byte group records. DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it on MissionGroups (004a9e84) with block 11's record count.

entries.name: Group_WriteStatusBlocks
entries.description: (group, stream) Per member in group order: Mech_ReadDamageReadouts into a 42-short buffer, then entries 1-13, 20-29 and 32-41 each written as ((0x100 - r) * 100) SAR 8, then the 6 bytes at mech+0x2a4 -- the member's Herc, Structure and Flyer kill tallies. 72 bytes a member; VSHELL reads the 66 over the machine's status block and the 6 as the pilot's mission counters.

entries.name: Mission_TotalSalvage
entries.description: Sums Mech_SalvageValue over every object on the other side from the player's that is destroyed (+0x99) or immobilised (+0xa4). Called once as the mission writes its results; the total is scaled by Q10(2500) into the campaign salvage pool.

entries.name: Group_ApplyOutnumberedDamage
entries.description: (group): Mech_ApplyOutnumberedDamage on each member of the group's member array (+0xc, int16 count +0x10). Sim_MainTick runs it on the player's group (player+0x45) when Mission_PollStatus answers 3, and raises status 18 instead when the player is destroyed (+0x99) afterwards.

entries.name: Group_ReportIfAllOutOfAction
entries.description: Walks a mission group's member list (group+0xc, count group+0x10) skipping one nominated member; if every other member is immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99) it runs the group's own 10 mission-variable slots (indices at group+0x1c, opcodes at group+0x30) against DAT_004a9ef4 with the opcode set Mech_ReportOutOfAction uses. It does NOT remove the member from the group: a dead machine stays in the roster and keeps being ticked, which is why the inert behaviour states exist. Resolves ai-goals.md's open question on group +0x1c and +0x30.

entries.name: Meteor_Dtor
entries.description: METEOR vtable +0x08 (004982b8), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). Debris_Dtor's body: installs TSObjVtable, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00424034; class record at 00423fe4

entries.name: MissionGroup_ElementCtor
entries.description: Rtl_VectorNew's per-element constructor for MissionGroups_Allocate's 0x7a-byte group records (its only reference is that PUSH at 00423d4b): zeroes the route cursor's index word at group+0x04 and nothing else. Ghidra has no function here; it is filed under Group_ReportIfAllOutOfAction's tail.

entries.name: Sim_DamageToPlayerDisabled
entries.description: Two-global predicate gating the very first line of Mech_ComponentDamageWrite for the locally piloted machine: if DAT_004a9ed6 is zero the answer is DAT_004a9ede == 1, otherwise DAT_004a9ee0 == 0. Reads as an invulnerability or practice setting; neither global's writer was traced.

entries.name: Mission_WriteResults
entries.description: (player) Writes data\results.dat -- int16 (Mission_EvaluateObjectives(player) == 9), int32 Q10(2500, Mission_TotalSalvage) + counter 20 * 25000, int16 count and that many {int16 weapon, int16 condition} salvage pairs from DAT_004a9ef0, then Group_WriteStatusBlocks over the player's group -- and then the 2000 bytes of mission counters DAT_004a9ef4 back over data\mission.var. Sim_Shutdown is its one caller.

entries.name: DBSim_LoadScriptDat
entries.description: DBSIM's reader for data\script.dat, called from World::ctor-equivalent init path (also opens player.mec and mission.str at nearby offsets). Reads a fixed 20-byte header into DAT_004a9ed2 and uses it twice: World_LoadTheater(&header) takes the int16 at 0 as the theater and the int16 at 18 as its variant, and Terrain_LoadZone(header[2]) takes the int16 at 2 as THE ZONE INDEX -- verified against all ten retail script.dat files, every offset-2 value is a zone that ships. It also zeroes the field at offset 4 before use. Then 13 count-prefixed blocks in exact order matching VSHELL's WriteScriptDatFile (0041ac54): row6-coords(12B), row7-heading(2B, x0xb6 degrees->BAM), row8-nested-waypoints, row9(6B), row10-action(74B read, only 1 field of the row10-referencing sub-block reused), row11-action-timer(24B, resolved via FUN_00423104), row12(134B raw, only the mech-type-ref field at rec-offset 40 kept), row13(92B raw, only rec-offset 44 field kept), row14(52B raw, only the type field kept), row15(14B, read and fully discarded), row16(156B, nested 20-entry crossref with a 3-way discriminator that marks row6/row7/row14 slots 'live' -- this is DBSIM's actual entity-activation mechanism), row17(54B, read and fully discarded), then a final flat count+array tail = row4's populated LUT-ref prefix (the mission's herc/weapon unlock package). See docs/formats/script-dat.md.

entries.name: Sim_ShutdownNoOp2
entries.description: Empty body. Sim_Shutdown's last call.

entries.name: Mission_ResolveRefByKind
entries.description: Resolves a script.dat cross-reference to a runtime pointer given its kind discriminator: 0 = the mission group record at index*0x7a, 1/2/3 = the live mech/flyer/base object for that roster slot, via the slot-to-object maps at DAT_004aa812 / DAT_004aa90c / DAT_004aa9ca. Builds the order record's subject pointer at +0x0e.

entries.name: DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects
entries.description: DBSIM's world-spawn pass and the function that actually builds a mission's objects -- the second of two reads of data\script.dat. RE-OPENS the file from the top (path built from maybe_DatFolderPrefixPtr + the string at 0049aa3e), skips blocks 1-6, then walks blocks 7-13 again. For every slot DBSim_LoadScriptDat's first pass marked live it constructs an object and reads that object's OWN record for placement: block 7 (134B) gives mech type at +0x28, weapon fit at +0x2a, position ref at +0x3e, heading ref at +0x40; block 8 (92B) gives position +0x28, heading +0x2a, flyer type +0x2c; block 9 (52B) gives base type +0x00, position +0x02, heading +0x04. Position refs resolve into the block-1 coordinate array (DAT_004a9e90, stride 0xc); heading refs into the pre-multiplied block-2 array (DAT_004a9e94). Mechs and bases get Terrain_HeightQuery plus the type's foot offset; flyers get no query. Each base also registers its footprint with Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint before that query. It then reads block 11 into MissionGroups (stride 0x7a) via DBSim_BuildGroupRecord, remapping member refs to dense object indices, and appends the player.mec lance in place of record 0's members. With the roster down it calls Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints (00471190) at 004263d9 and re-queries every base's ground height, the terrain having moved under them. Reading pass 1 (DBSim_LoadScriptDat) alone suggests script.dat carries no placement data; it is this pass that reads it.

entries.name: Sim_ShutdownNoOp1
entries.description: Empty body. Sim_Shutdown calls it after setting the exit code, before Sim_ShutdownNoOp2.

entries.name: Sim_RaycastObjectList
entries.description: Generic ray-vs-live-object-list query. Nine call sites in four functions: Rocket_TickUpdate (1), Bullet_TickUpdate (2), Bullet_FireBurst (1) and Razor_MovementTick (5, the airframe contact probes). Calls each candidate's vtable +0x20 (hit-test) and +0x50 (AI threat-tracking). The shot record's second exclusion at +0x14 is written only by Razor_MovementTick; all three weapon callers leave that stack slot uninitialised.

entries.name: Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep
entries.description: Radius-based splash-damage entry point. Sweeps the live-object list, skipping an object whose mission group still carries an action and the excluded object; distance - obj[+0x5c] < blastRadius calls that object +0x70. Note it truncates its int blastRadius to a short when handing it on. RETURNS 1 IF ANYTHING WAS IN RANGE, not if anything was damaged -- the flag is set beside the +0x70 call, before that call can decide the target shields swallowed it. Its one reader is the drop pod +0x4c latch. Exactly 3 call sites, all terminal: Meteor_Tick drop-pod landing, the Plasma-cannon bullet type 9 branch in Bullet_TickUpdate, and Mech_BehaviourRamTick. It is NOT the only way +0x70 is reached -- Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage and Mech_CollisionTest both call it directly.
entries.signature: short __cdecl Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep(int *hitPoint, int blastRadius, short damage, int *attacker, int *excluded)

entries.name: Salvage_QueueWeapon
entries.description: Appends one {int16 weapon id, int16 condition} to the salvage list at DAT_004a9ef0 (a 200-byte block, room for 50, unchecked), bumping the count at DAT_004a9eee. Two callers: Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage's mount-destruction roll on a Cybrid machine, and Mech_SalvageValue for each surviving mount of an enemy wreck. Mission_WriteResults writes the list as results.dat's salvage pairs.

entries.name: Detection_ContactScanRange
entries.description: Returns 30000 when DAT_004a9ee2, the scan-range setting, is 1 and 60000 otherwise: the range within which a held contact can still be selected. Its one caller is TargetSelect_CanTarget, and es2_xref.py finds this function as the only reference to DAT_004a9ee2. See docs/simulation/target-selection.md.

entries.name: Damage_ScaleByDifficulty
entries.description: Scales a damage figure in place by a Q10 factor from one of two four-entry tables selected by the firing side -- 0049a73c {3500, 2800, 2100, 1400} for side 0, 0049a744 {300, 600, 800, 1000} for anything else -- indexed by the mission difficulty at DAT_004a9ee0. So difficulty moves the two sides' damage in opposite directions (3.42x down to 1.37x, versus 0.29x up to 0.98x).

entries.name: ActionTimers_Tick
entries.description: Walks the whole resolved block-6 array at DAT_004a9ebc (count DAT_004a9eb8, stride 0x31) calling ActionTimer_Tick on each. Sim_MainTick calls it immediately before Actions_EvaluateTriggers and both AFTER the per-group Group_OrderTick/Group_DeploymentCheck pass, so a group waiting on an action arrives on the tick after it activates.

entries.name: Actions_EvaluateTriggers
entries.description: Per-frame mission trigger evaluator, called by Sim_MainTick with the player's mech. Walks the whole block-5 action array and, per action type (+0x00), picks whose position Action_TestTrigger is offered: 0 the player's mech, 1 every member of the player's group, 2/3 every member of every deployed group of side 0 (human) / side 1 (Cybrid), 4/5/6 every deployed mech / flyer / base group, 7/8/9 the action's own resolved target object at +0x36, 10 every member of the action's target group. Groups whose +0x14 action pointer is still set are skipped as subjects -- an undeployed group cannot trip a trigger.

entries.name: DetAnimObj_Dtor
entries.description: DET_ANIM_OBJ vtable +0x08 (004973cc): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then Mem_Delete(this) on flags bit 0.

entries.name: SimObject_Dtor
entries.description: ACTOR vtable +0x08 (0049a54c): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements (ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this) instead of a Mem_Delete.

entries.name: SimObject_OperatorDelete
entries.description: (obj): ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, obj). The class-specific operator delete in the +0x14 field of the ACTOR, MECH, FLYER, BASE, RADAR_BASE, GUN_BASE, VEHICLE and LC_BASE class records; their deleting destructors inline the same call.

entries.name: Mech_Dtor
entries.description: MECH vtable +0x08 (0049a282): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Three RTL destructor-count decrements (MECH, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: Flyer_Dtor
entries.description: FLYER vtable +0x08 (0049a5e0): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Three RTL destructor-count decrements (FLYER, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: GridShape_HeightAround
entries.description: Column height under a point of a shape's collision height field, the point already shifted by the grid origin. When (1 << (cellShift - 1)) < radius it returns the tallest cell within radius; below that it samples the single cell. Off-grid is 0, which is what makes the volume end at its own edges. Cells hold a byte code into the 256-entry int32 height table at grid+0x34.

entries.name: GridShape_HeightAt
entries.description: GridShape_HeightAround with the grid-origin shift applied for the caller (origin << cellShift, i.e. world units rather than cells). Returns 0 for a shape with no collision volume.

entries.name: GridShape_Raycast
entries.description: Marches a ray, in shape space, through a shape's collision height field. Rejects an empty grid and a ray with BOTH ends above grid+0x430 (the height table's last entry, its ceiling). Step length is (1 << cellShift) + clearance; the direction is rescaled to it by a Q16 divide truncated to 16 bits. Hits when GridShape_HeightAround returns nonzero above the ray's current Z; reports the hit point with the grid origin offset removed.

entries.name: GridShape_Construct
entries.description: ClassItem registry loadFn for classId 0x02bc0001 (dgs\bases/bhulks shape records): allocates a 0x438-byte GridShape (RTTI name, vtable 0049aaa0, base TSShape), installs the vtable, then calls vtable+0xc (GridShape_ReadFromStream). See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: GridShape_GetClassTag
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot 0: returns 0x2bc0001, GridShape_Construct's class id.

entries.name: GridShape_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +4 (shape): TSShape's stream size (00490cdc) plus columns +0x2a times rows +0x2c plus 0x40a -- the five int16 grid scalars and the 1024-byte height table GridShape_ReadFromStream reads after TSShape's fields, then one byte per cell.

entries.name: GridShape_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +8: returns 0. It does not call TSShape's slot +8 (00490d08).

entries.name: GridShape_ReadFromStream
entries.description: Field reader for a dgs\bases/bhulks shape record (vtable+0xc for classId 0x02bc0001), on top of the generic ClassItem base-class chain (TSShape_ReadFromStream). Its tail is the shape's COLLISION VOLUME, a coarse height field: int16 columns (+0x2a), rows (+0x2c), origin column (+0x2e), origin row (+0x30), cell shift (+0x32), a 256-entry int32 height table (+0x34, 1024 bytes, last entry addressed as the ceiling at +0x430), then rows*columns height codes (+0x434). The obvious reading, five undecoded scalars and an opaque block followed by sub-record count * sub-record size raw records, spans the same bytes and parses every retail record, but it is not the layout. See docs/simulation/hit-detection.md.

entries.name: GridShape_WriteToStream
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +0x10 (shape, stream): TSShape's write (00490e34), then the stream's +0x14 write of what GridShape_ReadFromStream reads, in the same order: the int16 columns +0x2a, rows +0x2c, origin column +0x2e, origin row +0x30 and cell shift +0x32, the 0x400-byte height table at +0x34, then one columns-byte row per row through the row-pointer array at +0x434.

entries.name: GridShape_Dtor
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +0x18 (shape, flags): when shape is set, decrements the live-object counter at *006cbf74, calls 00490958 (TSShape vtable 004a6331 slot +0x18) with flags 0, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: Terrain_LoadZone
entries.description: terrain.cpp zone/grid loader. Builds a 'zoneNNNN' filename, reads a grid header, allocates a HeightGrid, installs it as ActiveHeightGrid.

entries.name: Structure_WalkCollisionTest
entries.description: The walking-collision half of the structure volume test, called from FUN_00404ae4's gather. Per candidate: 2D distance from the point to the structure against shape+8, then the offset rotated into shape space by the transposed XY block of the object's rotation, then GridShape_HeightAround(volume, point, 0). Returns the first nonzero height. NOTE it does not apply the origin << cellShift that GridShape_Raycast applies, so the footprint a machine walks into is displaced from the one a shot is tested against by the grid's origin -- its centre on all 45 retail records. Not cross-checked against retail play.
entries.signature: int __cdecl Structure_WalkCollisionTest(int *point, unsigned short radius, int *candidates, short count)

entries.name: Terrain_HeightQueryActive
entries.description: (point): Terrain_HeightQuery(ActiveHeightGrid, point). Debris_TickUpdate calls it.

entries.name: RaycastShapeMinDistance_Clear
entries.description: Sets RaycastShapeMinDistance (004aab54) to 0. Sim_RaycastObjectList calls it twice, once just before Sim_RaycastTerrain.

entries.name: RaycastShapeMinDistance_Get
entries.description: Returns RaycastShapeMinDistance (004aab54) in EAX (the decompile drops the return).

entries.name: Sim_RaycastShapeVolume
entries.description: Ray versus a list of objects' collision height fields. Per object: coarse reject on shape+8 plus clearance plus ray length, then the object centre in muzzle space tested against a box on X and Y only (Z is not tested), then the ray transformed into shape space and marched by GridShape_Raycast. Writes the hit distance back into the ray record's +0x04 and returns early for a hit under 500. Two callers: Base_DirectFireHitTest (one object) and FUN_00404bc0 (a bulk line-of-sight query over the structure list).

entries.name: Sim_RaycastTerrain
entries.description: The ray-versus-terrain query Sim_RaycastObjectList runs before it tests any object. Calls maybe_Terrain_RayWalk(ActiveHeightGrid, origin, endPoint, rayRecord+8 -- the literal 200, as a radius, &hitPoint, 0); on a ground hit the caller measures the distance back to the origin and clips the ray to it. This is what stops a shot passing through a hillside. Its companion RaycastShapeMinDistance_Clear is only a counter reset (RaycastShapeMinDistance), not part of the query.

entries.name: Terrain_RayHitDistance
entries.description: (&distance, from, to, step): Terrain_RayWalk on ActiveHeightGrid from from to to; when it reports a hit, stores Math_DistanceBetweenPoints(from, hitPoint) in distance. Returns whether it hit. Detection_LineOfSight and Ai_LineOfSightBlocked call it.

entries.name: Scene_DrawTerrain
entries.description: (view): Raster_SetModelTransform(&DAT_004aab08); sets the render context's clip mode +0x208 to 1 while its clip block (+4) holds one region whose first dword is 0; Terrain_DrawVisibleCells(g_TerrainDrawGrid, view); restores +0x208. Called from Scene_DrawTerrainPass in the frame draw and from the heads-down map's terrain pass.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawTableIndex
entries.description: (a, b): returns the index recorded for the pair in the draw table at 004cf574 (three int16 per entry: a, b, index; count 004cf8f8); a new pair is appended with the next index, asserting 'ObjList::drawTable full' in objlist.cpp once 0x96 entries exist. ObjList_AddToDrawTable and ObjList_DrawCellObjects call it.

entries.name: ObjPick_Arm
entries.description: (point): copies the {x, y} pair to 004cf9b5/004cf9b9 and sets the pending flag 004cf9b4, arming the pixel pick ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain and ObjList_DrawEntryRender run. It is the only store of 1 to 004cf9b4; es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: ObjPick_GetObject
entries.description: Returns 004cf9c0: the last object whose draw changed the pick pixel during an armed pick (ObjList_DrawEntryRender), or 0, which ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain stores before the object pass. Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint hands a non-zero result to TargetSelect_SetObject.

entries.name: ObjPick_IsIdle
entries.description: Returns 004cf9b4 == 0: no pick is pending. Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint tests it, with the byte 0049be74, before ObjPick_GetObject.

entries.name: Scene_SubmitObject
entries.description: (obj): Scene_SubmitObjectWithRadius(obj, obj->vtable[+0x10]()) -- files one object into ObjList::drawTable under the terrain cell its position and its own shape radius pick. Scene_SubmitFrameObjects' submit for ground shapes (FlatObj), projectiles, ownerless explosions, debris, the 004a96f2 pool and drop pods.

entries.name: ObjList_AddToDrawTable
entries.description: Files one object into ObjList::drawTable at DAT_004aab80 (rows of 1000 bytes, row index interned per cell by ObjList_InternCellRow) or, when it resolves to no cell, into the flat DAT_004cf910 bucket that ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain draws after the terrain walk with no depth fade of its own. Asserts carry the objlist.cpp strings 'ObjList::drawTable entry full' and 'ObjList::drawTable full'.

entries.name: Scene_SubmitObjectWithRadius
entries.description: (obj, radius): HeightGrid_PickDrawCell(ActiveHeightGrid, obj->vtable[+0x04](), radius), then ObjList_AddToDrawTable(obj, cell); returns the cell record, which Scene_SubmitFrameObjects' machine walks cache at obj+0x7a/+0x1ea (0xffff when null).

entries.name: Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell
entries.description: (obj, cellXY): HeightGrid_ClaimDrawCell(ActiveHeightGrid, cellXY), then ObjList_AddToDrawTable(obj, cell); returns the cell record. Used where the cell is already known: a machine with a cached cell at +0x1e8, an explosion filed under its owner's cell (Explosion_GetOwnerDrawCell), and every fire.

entries.name: Scene_SubmitFrameObjects
entries.description: Per-frame scene assembly. Calls HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch(ActiveHeightGrid), then walks the object pools and lists in a fixed order and files each drawable object into ObjList::drawTable by terrain cell: g_FlatObjPool first (only shapes within 30000 of the view object, by Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, through Scene_SubmitObject), then the 004a9624 list, GlobalMechList and the 004a9e3d list (skipping a group whose +0x14 deployment gate is set, and caching the cell record at obj+0x7a/+0x1ea), the projectile pool 004a9746, g_ExplosionPool (Explosion_IsHiddenFromOwnerCockpit, then the owner's cell or its own), g_DebrisPool, 004a96f2, g_FirePool (Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell) and g_MeteorPool. It decides no visibility beyond the flat-shape range and the two gates.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawEntryRender
entries.description: Slot 0 of the depth-sorted render entry's vtable (stamped as PTR_FUN_0049ac38 by ObjList_DrawEntryConstruct). Reads the entry's cached position (+4/+8/+0xc) and object pointer (+0x32), calls Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance with the entry's own distance (+0x12), then calls the object's vtable slot 0 -- Bullet_Draw for a projectile. This is why every pooled effect is distance-fogged from its own range. After the draw, while the pick flag 004cf9b4 is set, a pick pixel no longer reading 1 records the object at 004cf9c0 and is reset to 1; and while 0049abbc is set and the object is the probed one (004cf9f8), ObjProbe_MarkCorners.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain
entries.description: (view): runs after the terrain walk in Sim_RenderFrame. Calls slot 0 of every object in the no-cell bucket DAT_004cf910 (count DAT_004cf9b0) that ObjList_AddToDrawTable fills. Then, when LocalPlayerMech's +0x1f2 record has a nonzero +0x50 and Cam_IsAttachedTo(view, player) is 0, Terrain_DrawCellObjects for the player's cached cell (+0x1e8/+0x1ea). Then, while the pick flag 004cf9b4 is set, points the display's source page +0x38 at +0x8c, saves the pixel under the pick point (004cf9b5) at 004cfa00, writes 1 there and clears ObjPick_GetObject's 004cf9c0; ObjList_SetViewObject(view); restores the saved pixel and clears 004cf9b4. Last, ObjProbe_TestCorners when DAT_0049abbc is set.

entries.name: ObjProbe_Arm
entries.description: (obj): projects obj's position (vtable +4) to the screen and sizes a square from its radius (vtable +0x10): half-size = radius << 006c60ac / (eye distance - radius), each step floored at 1. Stores the four corners {x-h, y-h}, {x+h, y-h}, {x+h, y+h}, {x-h, y+h} from 004cf9c4, the object at 004cf9f8, and sets 0049abbc. Each corner's occluded flag 004cf9f4[i] is set when the corner lies outside the render context's +0x210..+0x21c rect, but the loop never advances its point pointer (00428a72), so all four take the first corner's answer. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: ObjProbe_IsHidden
entries.description: Returns whether all four of ObjProbe_Arm's corner flags 004cf9f4[0..3] are set. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: ObjProbe_MarkCorners
entries.description: Records the display (006c5f54) at 004cf9fc; for each probe corner whose flag 004cf9f4[i] is clear, saves the pixel there (g_RasterRoutines_GetPixel) at 004cf9e4[i] and writes 2 (g_RasterRoutines_PutPixel). ObjList_DrawEntryRender calls it right after drawing the probed object 004cf9f8 while 0049abbc is set.

entries.name: ObjProbe_TestCorners
entries.description: Points the display's source page +0x38 at its +0x8c (through maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetSourcePage when it is the current display); for each corner with its flag clear, restores the saved pixel when it still reads 2, otherwise sets the flag -- something drawn after the probed object covered it. Clears 0049abbc. ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain's last step while 0049abbc is set.

entries.name: ObjList_SetDrawDistances
entries.description: (radius): the five object draw distances at DAT_004cfa0c, each Math_Q10Multiply(radius, factor) over the int16 table at 0049abb0 = {800, 900, 1000, 800, 1200}. Its one caller, Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion, passes the terrain draw radius in world units (grid+0x10c << cellShift), once a frame. ObjList_IsBeyondDrawDistance reads the result.

entries.name: ObjList_IsBeyondDrawDistance
entries.description: (obj, dist): picks a draw distance from DAT_004cfa0c by the object's type tag at +4 -- tag 0 entry 1, tag 8 entry 2, tag 5 entry 3, or entry 4 when SimObject_GetShapeRadius (vtable +0x10) is 7000 or more, anything else entry 0 -- and returns whether dist exceeds it. Called only by ObjList_DrawCellObjects (00428d92), which drops the object's render entry when it does.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawCellObjects
entries.description: The per-terrain-cell object draw hook (installed at HeightGrid+0x125, invoked by Terrain_DrawCellObjects). Walks the cell's ObjList::drawTable row and branches on each object's type tag at +4: tag 9 (a ground shape) is drawn immediately, in filing order, with the ramp row count DAT_004a5b1c zeroed around the draw and no fade of its own -- its solid faces fog with the one the cell's quad installed; everything else (a Bullet is tag 3, written by Bullet_Construct) is turned into a 0x36-byte render entry carrying its position, LOD short and distance, appended to the list ObjList_DrawSorted then walks. See docs/formats/terrain-drawing.md, 'Objects in the walk'.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawEntryConstruct
entries.description: Constructor for the depth-sorted render entry: three successive vtable stamps (base, derived, most-derived), the last being PTR_FUN_0049ac38 whose slot 0 is ObjList_DrawEntryRender.

entries.name: ObjList_SetViewObject
entries.description: (obj): stores its argument at DAT_0049ac3c. ObjList_DrawCellObjects and ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain pass the view object.

entries.name: ObjList_SortCompareSegment
entries.description: (node, newNode): ObjList_SortCompare's case where exactly one render entry carries a segment (entry +0x16 of 1 or 2, endpoints at +0x18 and +0x24). When the segment entry is the nearer (+0x12) the answer is plain distance order, and also when 00428f38 accepts neither the camera (0049ac3c + 4) nor the other entry's position (+4) against it. Otherwise it builds, once per entry (flag +0xc), the normal of the plane that contains the segment and faces the camera -- Vec3I_Cross(segment, Vec3I_Cross(segment, camera - start)), each vector halved until Math_FastMagnitude3D is at most 32000 -- at +0x11 with the camera's side of it (Vec3I_DotSign) at +0xd, and returns whether the other entry's position lies on the camera's side.

entries.name: ObjList_SortCompareSegments
entries.description: (node, newNode): ObjList_SortCompare's case where both render entries carry segments. Asks 0042933c for a point of one against the other, each way round; with none, plain distance order (+0x12). Otherwise it moves that entry's position (+4) to the point and its type (+0x16) to 0 for the call, compares through ObjList_SortCompareSegment with the other entry as the segment, restores both fields, and inverts the answer when the moved entry was node.

entries.name: ObjList_SortCompare
entries.description: (node, newNode): which side of node newNode's render entry (+8) goes on; non-zero is right, drawn later. When both entries' int16 +0x16 is 1 or 2 the answer is 0042937c's; when both are 0 it is whether newNode's distance (+0x12) is less than node's; otherwise 0042900c's.

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeInsert
entries.description: (node, newNode): descends right (+4) when ObjList_SortCompare(node, newNode) is non-zero and left (+0) otherwise, recursing until it finds the empty child to link newNode into.

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12
entries.description: (entries, count): for each entry whose int16 +0x16 is 1 or 2, fills the next 0x1d-byte node from 0049ac40 (entry at +8, children and byte +0xc cleared) and inserts it under the root with ObjList_SortTreeInsert (the first node is the root). Returns the next free node; the decompile drops it (MOV EAX,ESI).

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeAddOthers
entries.description: (entries, count, node): ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12's complement: every entry whose int16 +0x16 is neither 1 nor 2 gets the next node from node onwards and is inserted under the root at 0049ac40 with ObjList_SortTreeInsert, unless it is the root itself.

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeDraw
entries.description: (node): in-order walk of the sort tree: the left subtree, then slot 0 of the render entry at +8 (ObjList_DrawEntryRender), then the right subtree.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawSorted
entries.description: (entries, count): nothing for count 0. Builds a binary tree of the render entries in the 0x1d-byte node pool at 0049ac40 ({+0 left, +4 right, +8 entry}, the first node the root): ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12 adds the entries whose int16 +0x16 is 1 or 2, ObjList_SortTreeAddOthers the rest from the node it returns, both through ObjList_SortTreeInsert; then ObjList_SortTreeDraw walks it from the root. ObjList_DrawCellObjects calls it at the end of a cell with the entries it built, each of which it gave +0x16 = 0, so they order by distance alone: farthest first.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Ctor
entries.description: This 0x37-byte object is the player's own cockpit view manager (MECHVIEW.CPP): it holds the current view index at +0x14, the pending view command at +0x18, the CockpitView widget tree pointer at +0x1f, the owning mech at +0x29 and the herc model name at +0x2d, and it is what CockpitView_SetView/CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand drive. It is small because the heavy state lives in the CockpitView object it builds (see CockpitViewManager_LoadViews -> CockpitView_Ctor -> CockpitViewInstance). Also the site of CockpitPaletteSingleton's first (singleton-guarded) load of dpl\\cockpit.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Publish
entries.description: Stores its argument in CockpitViewManagerPublished (004cfa20). One call site: the tail of CockpitViewManager_LoadViews, passing the manager itself.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Published
entries.description: Returns CockpitViewManagerPublished (004cfa20) -- the cockpit view manager, or null before the cockpit is built. Sim_PollPlayerInput's HDD VIEW case tests the pointer itself rather than any field of it, which is the retail bug recorded in KNOWN_ISSUES.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_GetCockpitView
entries.description: (manager): returns manager+0x1f, the CockpitView widget tree (CockpitViewInstance). Sim_DispatchCommand calls it on CockpitViewManagerInstance twice, in the auto-track paths, and discards the result.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_LoadViews
entries.description: The whole cockpit bring-up, in order: (1) loads vue\\<herc> -- int32 viewCount then viewCount x 32-byte records {int x0,y0,x1,y1, cx, cy, canvasOriginX, canvasOriginY}, all coordinates shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift; every retail .VUE has viewCount=4; (2) allocates 4 slots for canopy bitmaps, 4 x 0x204 clip-region blocks and 4 span tables; (3) per view i, calls CockpitClipRegions_Load on ed<i>/hd<i> and ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans on the result, and (unless CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand) CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap for db<i>/hb<i>; (4) builds the CockpitView widget object (CockpitView_Ctor -> ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll, which sets CockpitViewInstance) and Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets; (5) THE PER-HERC COCKPIT COLOUR SCHEME: Palette_InstallRange(0x2a, 0x18, COCKPIT.DPL.entries + (schemeIdx*0x18 + 0x20)*4), i.e. live palette slots 42..65 are overwritten with COCKPIT.DPL entries [32 + 24*schemeIdx .. +24), where schemeIdx = mechTypeRecord+0x52 = offset 80 of simvol0/dat/<MECH>.DAT. Retail values are a 0-8 permutation: APOCA 0, COLOSSUS 1, SAMSON 2, MAVERICK 3, OGRE 4, OUTLAW 5, RAPTOR2 6, RAZOR 7, TOMAHAWK 8, so the nine 24-entry schemes fill COCKPIT.DPL entries 32..247. This matches the independently measured retail screenshots exactly (APOCA renders canopy index i as COCKPIT.DPL[i-10] => base 32; COLOSSUS as COCKPIT.DPL[i+14] => base 56) and explains why every WORLD<n>.DPL parks exactly slots 42-65 at filler green. (6) Repeats the same install with IMPACTCP.DPL into the secondary palette object DAT_0049aef8 for the damage flash.

entries.name: CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap
entries.description: MECHVIEW.CPP:0x12e. The .HB0/.HB1/.HB2 (.DB0/.DB1/.DB2) load site. No literal 'hb0' string exists because the folder name is built at runtime: it copies the global folder literal 'dba' (or 'hba' when VideoMode_PanelMode==3) into a stack buffer and overwrites index 2 with an ASCII digit via _itoa, giving db0/db1/db2 or hb0/hb1/hb2, then ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(hercName, buf) + ClassItem_LoadResource. View->file map: fileIdx = viewIdx>2 ? viewIdx-1 : viewIdx, so views 0,1,2,3 -> files 0,1,2,2 and view 4 loads nothing; after loading file 2 the same handle is also stored in slot 3, i.e. views 2 and 3 share one bitmap (view 3 is drawn horizontally mirrored, see CockpitView_SetView). Result handles land in CockpitViewManager+8[viewIdx]. The CockpitLayoutMode==1 branch increments byte 2 of the SHARED global 'dba' literal (MOV ECX,[0x4a0a28]; INC byte ptr [ECX+2]) rather than the local buffer -- verified in raw disassembly at 00429d3e; the follow-on load still uses the unmodified local buffer, so that branch loads db0 twice and corrupts the global folder name. Treat CockpitLayoutMode==1 as an unused/buggy path.

entries.name: CockpitCanopy_FreeViewBitmap
entries.description: Releases the canopy bitmap handle for one view and nulls its slot; when freeing view 2 it also nulls slot 3, which shares the same handle. Only called when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand (DAT_004d2704) is set, i.e. the low-memory mode that loads and frees canopy art per view switch instead of keeping all four resident.

entries.name: CockpitView_ApplyViewState
entries.description: Installs one view's state into the global render context (DAT_006c5ff4): copies that view's 0x204-byte clip-region block (CockpitViewManager+0xc + viewIdx*0x204, filled by CockpitClipRegions_Load) into ctx+4..ctx+0x208, points ActiveScanlineClipSpans at the view's prebuilt per-scanline span table (CockpitViewManager+0x10[viewIdx]), and copies the view's six .VUE ints into ctx[0x84..0x89]. The .VUE record's last two ints are the view's origin inside the cockpit canvas and go to DAT_004cfa24/28 (or VideoMode_X/YCoordShift-space DAT_004d25da/de in CockpitLayoutMode 2). View 4 instead installs the default full-screen clip block at DAT_004cfb1c and hides the cockpit widgets -- it is the external/no-cockpit view.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetView
entries.description: Switches the cockpit to view 0-4. Calls CockpitView_ApplyViewState, then blits the view's full-screen canopy bitmap once via Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, {0,0}, flags) with flags = 2 (horizontal mirror) for view 3 and 0 otherwise -- this is where the side view's single authored bitmap is flipped for the opposite side. Finally repaints every cockpit widget (CockpitView_InvalidateWidgets). The canopy is NOT redrawn per frame: it is blitted once per view change and the 3D scene is then rasterized over it, clipped to ActiveScanlineClipSpans. In CockpitLayoutMode 1 view 0 additionally blits slot 1 at y+0xc5.

entries.name: CockpitView_QueueViewCommand
entries.description: Latches a pending view-change command (field +0x18) from an input action, guarded by the current view (field +0x14). Consumed by CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand.

entries.name: CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand
entries.description: Executes the pending view command. Command 4 selects glance view 2, command 5 glance view 3, command 6 returns to view 0, command 2 selects view 4 (external). The -/+0x3600 yaw adds on 4/5/6 are gated on VideoMode_PanelMode == 1, which no retail mode stores, so a glance never turns the camera: it is the forward view's image plane continued sideways (docs/formats/cockpit-views.md). On the scroll-window path it first moves the image into the other half of the back buffer when a glance target would fall outside it (tests on Display_OriginX); on the -b paged path it instead holds glance commands until the draw page (+0x88) is 0 or 2 (1 under panel mode 1), and every pass past that gate and the cooldown calls Vga_WaitVerticalRetrace.

entries.name: CockpitView_StepViewTransition
entries.description: Runs a queued view change's animated slide, once per frame from Sim_EndFrame just before CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand, gated on pending != -1 and the armed flag at +0x1c. For commands 0/1 (heads-down pan) it steps the display origin y by 10 canvas rows per loop iteration over vue[dest].canvasOriginY - vue[src].canvasOriginY (237, or 474 after the coord shift), then a remainder step; commands 4/5/6 step x by 0x14. The loop has no timer, retrace poll or frame boundary, so its real-time speed is CPU-bound. On completion: +0x14 += 1 (or -1), +0x18 = -1, +0x1d = 2 (two-frame cooldown). See docs/formats/cockpit-views.md.

entries.name: CmdLine_SetCockpitOverride
entries.description: (name): the -C switch. _stricmp against the 13 names at 0049ac64 (ROADRUNNER ... TEST3); on a match stores the index in CockpitOverride_Index and the name pointer in CockpitOverride_Name. Sim_ParseCommandLine calls it with the text after -C.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetShakeBand
entries.description: Seeds the shake's vertical band: copies the resting view offset into 004cfae4/004cfae8 and sets the two limits at 004cfaec/004cfaf0 to that offset and that offset plus or minus the amplitude argument, the sign chosen by the view mode enum at FUN_00429820's +0x14. Sets CockpitViewShakeArmed. Also reached from CockpitView_StepViewTransition.

entries.name: CockpitView_StepShake
entries.description: One frame of the shake: moves the view's y offset (004cfae8) by up to the step argument toward whichever of CockpitView_SetShakeBand's two limits is farther away, so the view ping-pongs across the band rather than settling, then reinstalls the projection. Does nothing unless CockpitViewShakeArmed is set, and nothing in view mode 4.

entries.name: CockpitView_ClearShake
entries.description: Undoes CockpitView_SetShakeBand: restores the view offset from the resting copy at 004cfadc/004cfae0, reinstalls the projection and clears CockpitViewShakeArmed. No-op when that byte is clear or the view mode is 4. Called when the cockpit damage shake ends or restarts, from CockpitView_ApplyViewState, and from the two mech-death screen flashes.

entries.name: CockpitView_ForgetKickOffset
entries.description: Zeroes CockpitView_KickOffset without touching the render context.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetKickOffset
entries.description: (value): on the current render context (006c5ff4), +0x224 -= CockpitView_KickOffset, then += value & 0xffff, which it stores in CockpitView_KickOffset.

entries.name: CockpitView_ClearKickOffset
entries.description: Takes CockpitView_KickOffset back out of the current render context's +0x224 and zeroes it.

entries.name: CockpitView_GetShakeOffset
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the static pair {0, (int)(short)DAT_004cfaf4}: the hit shake's vertical offset, which CockpitView_SetShakeBand, CockpitView_StepShake and CockpitView_ClearShake write. Sim_RenderFrame adds the pair into the projection centre for the frame and takes it out after.

entries.name: ExternalView_SetRect
entries.description: (rect, offset): stores rect in ExternalView_Rect and at 004cfd28, and offset at 004cfad4/004cfad8; when CockpitViewManager_Published is in view 4, also writes them into the render context's (006c5ff4) +0x210..+0x224. PreferencesPanel_Raise calls it.

entries.name: ExternalView_ResetRect
entries.description: ExternalView_SetRect's body with ExternalView_DefaultRect as the source. PreferencesPanel_Raise calls it.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_FlushBorderFill
entries.description: (manager): View_FillOutside3dRect when the current view (+0x14) is 4, the external view; then clears +0x36. CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand calls it first when +0x36 is set.

entries.name: View_FillOutside3dRect
entries.description: Floods the four bands around the 3D rect (ExternalView_Rect/+4/+8/+0xc: left, top, right, bottom) with COLORS.DAT id 19 (DAT_004d3c26): a full-width band above it, one below it, and the left and right strips between. It installs a {0, colour} fill brush at the render context's +0x22c, zeroes the context's +0x208/+0x20c offsets for the fills and restores them, and issues one Raster_FillRect per non-empty band. Called by CockpitView_ApplyViewState for view 4, by CockpitViewManager_FlushBorderFill and twice by PreferencesPanel_Raise. See docs/simulation/external-views.md.

entries.name: ExternalView_GetRect
entries.description: Returns &ExternalView_Rect. ViewChain_DrawCaption centres the caption in it.

entries.name: CockpitView_ShowsWorld
entries.description: Returns 1 when the current view's .VUE rect bottom (record +0xc of the 0x20-byte record CockpitViewManagerPublished+0x14 indexes under +4) is at least 1, or a view transition (+0x1c) is running; 0 otherwise -- so 0 in the heads-down view, whose rect is empty on every HERC but RAZOR. Sim_RenderFrame draws the terrain only when it returns 1.

entries.name: CockpitClipRegions_Load
entries.description: Parser for the per-view .ED0-.ED3 / .HD0-.HD3 files (folder name built by overwriting index 2 of the 'edg'/'hdg' literals with a digit). Layout after the 9-byte VOL prefix: int16 rectCount, rectCount x {int16 y0, y1, x0, x1}; then int16 spanBlockCount, and per block {int16 firstRow, int16 rowCount, rowCount x {int16 xStart, int16 xEnd}}. Rects become type-0 region objects, span blocks type-2. Coordinates are shifted by the caller's (xShift,yShift) pair, which is (0,0) for the .HD* hi-res set and VideoMode_X/YCoordShift for the .DB*-era .ED* set. Output is a 0x204-byte block (int count + up to 128 region pointers). APOCA.HD0 reads cleanly: one full-width rect for rows 0-76 then a 235-row span block from row 77 whose spans narrow inward (the canopy frame). APOCA.HD1 is empty (rectCount=0, blockCount=0), which is why view 1 shows no 3D at all.

entries.name: World_LoadTheater
entries.description: World/theater setup, called by DBSim_LoadScriptDat with script.dat's 20-byte header as its argument (it copies the first 5 dwords to DAT_004cfd48). Builds the base name 'world<N>' via _itoa where N = DAT_004cfd48*2 + DAT_004cfd5a, i.e. header[0]*2 + header[18] -- five theaters, two variants each. Loads dpl\world<N>.dpl (the per-theater palette, which is what the retail WORLD0.DPL..WORLD9.DPL family is), then reads wld\world<N>.wld field-by-field (descriptor layout decoded and verified byte-exact against all ten retail .WLD files), then 'shades' via World_LoadShades, then world<N>.rmp -- the 8-bit software renderer's colour-ramp/lighting LUT. .RMP layout, byte-verified against all 10 retail files (WORLD0-9.RMP, all exactly 98312 bytes): int32 width, int32 height, then width*height*256 raw bytes (every file: width=32, height=12, 8+32*12*256=98312). width/height are read via the same generic field-reader callback used for .wld fields; the body is read in one call into ShadeRampTable (FUN_004734ac(fileHandle, width*height*256, ShadeRampTable)). Installs _DAT_004a5b18=rampTableBase and DAT_004a5b1c=DAT_004a5b20=width -- height is used locally for the allocation size and not retained in any global. TSTexture4Poly_Render (its only reader) uses the ramp-offset formula ((DAT_004a5b1c-1)*shade & 0xffffff00, i.e. (width-1)*shade rounded down to a multiple of 256), which makes width=32 the light-level-row count with 256 bytes per row (one byte per dither-table output 0-255). The 12 height slices are the depth-fog slices Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance selects. Finishes with Terrain_BindTextureBank(the 4th of the descriptor's 5 trailing strings) and FlatObj_LoadResources.

entries.name: Scene_DrawTerrainPass
entries.description: (view): sets +0x71 of the theater's horizon object g_TheaterHzline and has Terrain_ProjectFarEdgeAhead write into its +0x72; when that object exists, Hzline_Draw(it, view, &DAT_004cfa24, the view's canvas origin) paints the sky backdrop; then slot +0x34 of DAT_0049aee4 when that is non-null, Scene_DrawTerrain(view) and Palette_NoOp. Sim_RenderFrame's conditional arm.

entries.name: World_LoadShades
entries.description: (name): reads dat\<name> -- World_LoadTheater passes 'shades' -- as a count byte N, then N zeroed 5-byte records {byte count, pointer} at 004cfd64 (N at 004cfd68), then a byte K and K entries {record index byte, count byte, count two-byte pairs}, each pair list going into a new array on that record. 0042e8e8 indexes the table by an object's type tag (+4).

entries.name: Palette_ActivateImpact
entries.description: Swaps the active palette to ImpactPaletteObject through Palette_SetActive, saving the previous one at 004cfd8c/004cfd90 and latching 0049aef3. The flash half of the cockpit damage shake.

entries.name: Palette_ToggleImpact
entries.description: Swaps the saved and active palettes and flips 0049aef3, so repeated calls alternate between the theater palette and its impact palette -- unless Palette_RestoreFromImpact ran while the impact palette was active, which leaves the saved slot 004cfd8c on the theater palette, so later toggles swap it with itself. Called once per HitShakeNextToggleTick expiry while the shake runs.

entries.name: Palette_RestoreFromImpact
entries.description: Puts the palette Palette_ActivateImpact saved back. Called when the shake ends and when a new shake restarts over a running one.

entries.name: Palette_NoOp
entries.description: Returns immediately. LiftStart_DarkenPalette and Sim_InitMissionSession call it.

entries.name: Hzline_Ctor
entries.description: hzline constructor (vtable 0049afb0, RTTI name 'hzline', 0x7a bytes over TSGroup): TSGroup_Ctor, then the defaults +0x6c = 1, +0x54 = 3, +0x58 = 16, +0x5c = 1, +0x60 = 8, +0x64 = +0x68 = 1, +0x50 = 0, +0x70 = 0, +0x71 = 1. World_LoadTheater overwrites +0x54..+0x60 and +0x6c from the .WLD.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0042eb5c; RTTI via es2_classes.py; docs/formats/distance-fog-and-sky.md#the-sky--hzline

entries.name: Hzline_SetColors
entries.description: (self, zenithColor, groundColor, yOffset): +0x28 = (zenithColor + band count +0x58 - 1) & 0xffffff, the horizon colour; +0x2c = groundColor & 0xffffff; +0x30 = yOffset. World_LoadTheater passes .WLD shorts 1, 4 and 7.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Hzline_SetColors(hzline *self, int zenithColor, int groundColor, int yOffset)

entries.name: Hzline_Draw
entries.description: (self, view, canvasOrigin): Hzline_DrawWithOffset(self, view, self+0x30, canvasOrigin). Called only by Scene_DrawTerrainPass, with &DAT_004cfa24.

entries.name: Hzline_DrawWithOffset
entries.description: (self, view, yOffset, canvasOrigin): +0x34 = -view pitch (+0x10), +0x36 = view roll (+0x12); Hzline_BuildHorizon; adds yOffset >> 1 to both line ends' y; Hzline_FillSky; moves both ends down one row; Hzline_FillGround.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Hzline_DrawWithOffset(hzline *self, void *view, int yOffset, int *canvasOrigin)

entries.name: Hzline_BuildHorizon
entries.description: (self, canvasOrigin): writes the horizon line's screen ends to +0x38/+0x3c and +0x40/+0x44: (256 << coord shift) either side of a midpoint f*tan(pitch) from the projection centre (006c60b8/bc) along the rolled screen vertical, f = 2^006c60ac, plus +0x30 in y. A non-zero canvas origin lengthens it by its own length: both ends for a non-zero y, else the end on the x's side. +0x48/+0x4c = (sin roll, -cos roll), Q14, the band step direction; the test that would negate it compares the unsigned pitch with -0x4000 and is never true.

entries.name: Hzline_FillSky
entries.description: Paints the sky above the horizon line with the solid brush {0, colour} at the render context's +0x22c: +0x58 - 1 bands of +0x54 rows, the first in the horizon colour +0x28 and each next one entry lower, then the zenith colour beyond the last. Raster_FillRect rects when roll (+0x36) is 0, Raster_DrawPolygonReversed quads otherwise; the rolled bands' y offset uses one band fewer than the level fill's.

entries.name: Hzline_FillGround
entries.description: Fills from the horizon line to the bottom of the view (render context +0x21c). With +0x71 set, which Scene_DrawTerrainPass does before its only call, one fill in the horizon colour +0x28: Raster_FillRect when level, else a polygon of the line and the view-rect corners below it through Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch. The rolled branch moves the line by its midpoint's offset from Terrain_ProjectFarEdgeAhead's point (+0x72/+0x76) into polygon slots 2-3, which every path overwrites or leaves past the vertex count. With +0x71 clear it would paint +0x60 bands of +0x5c rows down from colour +0x2c + +0x60 - 1.

entries.name: Hzline_BlitHorizonStrip
entries.description: (self, bitmapSet, view, yOffset, offset): blits the frames of a bitmap set (count +4, frame list +8) one after another along the hzline's horizon line, starting from a position scrolled by the view's heading (+0x14) and wrapping the frame index; VideoMode_BlitBitmapFlags when level, VideoMode_BlitRotated by the negated roll otherwise. es2_xref.py finds no reference to it.

entries.name: Hzline_LoadBitmapBank
entries.description: (self, name): loads the named resource from the folder PTR_DAT_004a0a28 names (the 'dba' folder Terrain_BindTextureBank uses) and stores it at +0x50, which Hzline_Ctor zeroes. es2_xref.py finds no reference to it.

entries.name: Hzline_Dtor
entries.description: hzline vtable +0x18 (0049afb0, the sky backdrop Hzline_Ctor builds), the destructor its class record names: (hzline, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, TSGroup_Dtor(hzline, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0042f6d2; class record at 0042f682

entries.name: TexPoly_RandomPointOnCircle
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x24 (0049afe6), (poly, outPoint, outAngles, _, centre, radius, shift): draws a BAM angle a with Math_RandomNext, writes the Euler triple (0, 0, a) to outAngles, and outPoint = (centre.x + (Q14(radius, cos a) << shift), centre.y + (Q14(radius, cos(a - 0x4000)) << shift), poly+0x79).

entries.name: TexPoly_SetupRings
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x20 (0049afe6), (poly, rect): ring count +0xf9 = +0x6d / +0x71 (the step); for ring i the radius step * (i + 1) + step / 2 at +0x9f[i], the int16 0xffff / ((step * (i + 1) * 4) / +0x75) at +0x81[i], and a Math_RandomNext angle at +0xdb[i]; then copies the rect's +4/+8/+0xc into +0xff/+0x103/+0x107 and sets +0x22.

entries.name: TexPoly_DrawAtPoints
entries.description: TexPoly's vtable (0049afe6, RTTI 'TexPoly' at 004302aa, base TSTexture4Poly) slot +0x34, a slot TSTexture4Poly does not have; es2_xref finds the vtable entry and no call. Runs slot +0x20 (0042f970) first while +0x22 is clear; installs g_CurrentShapeDbaContext = this+0x1a, the surface base 006c697a = this+0x61 and 006c6976 = 006c60ec; Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance(0). Then for each of the +0x23 12-byte points at +0xe: when the viewer (arg+4) has moved since the last call (+0xff/+0x103), a point not flagged in the byte array at +0x16 and farther than +0x6d + +0x7d is reflected through the midpoint of the old and new viewer positions and flagged, and a flagged point nearer than +0x6d - +0x7d is unflagged; each point below index +0xfd gets slot +0x28 with its distance, Raster_SetModelTransform at its position and slot +0x2c (TexPoly_Render). Stores the viewer position at +0xff..+0x107.

entries.name: TexPoly_Render
entries.description: TexPoly's vtable (0049afe6) slot +0x2c, which TexPoly_DrawAtPoints calls once per point. Normally builds the poly's quad from the frame descriptor g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] + surface*0x14 (surface base 006c697a, index this+0xc) and hands it to Raster_SetupTexturedSpan, as TSTexture4Poly_Render does; while g_TexturedPolyUseBitmapBrush is set it takes the bitmap of the surface's +0 field when Raster_FrontFacing on the points this+4/+6 is positive and of its +8 field otherwise, and draws through Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices and PolyFill_FillThenOutline, calling slot +0x30 when the projection reports a vertex behind the near plane.

entries.name: TexPoly_ClipPolygon
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x30 (0049afe6), (poly, pairsIn, pairsOut): walks the current polygon's DAT_006c6968 vertices (indices at DAT_006c6976 + DAT_006c696a*2) edge by edge against the per-vertex code at DAT_006c697e, keeping a vertex coded 2 and, on an edge with one end coded 2, inserting the crossing at depth DAT_006c60b0 -- position interpolated with Math_Mul32To64/Math_DivMod64 and offset by DAT_006c60b8/DAT_006c60bc into 006cbb86/006cbb8a, and the vertex's 8-byte pair from pairsIn interpolated the same way into pairsOut. Returns the output count, also left in DAT_006cbc86.

entries.name: TexPoly_Dtor
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x18 (0049afe6, RTTI 'TexPoly', 0x10b bytes, derived from TSTexture4Poly), the destructor its class record names: (poly, flags). Five RTL destructor-count decrements, TSBase_Dtor(poly, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004302fa; class record at 004302aa

entries.name: TexPoly_Slot28NoOp
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x28 (0049afe6): an empty body.

entries.name: Palette_LoadAndActivate
entries.description: Loads a .DPL by path and makes it THE active palette object (ActivePaletteObject / DAT_0049b020). World_LoadTheater calls it with dpl\\world<N>, so the live 256-slot palette IS the theater palette in its entirety -- it is not a merge of COCKPIT.DPL and WORLD<N>.DPL. The only cockpit-owned slots are 42..65, overwritten afterwards by the per-herc scheme install in CockpitViewManager_LoadViews.

entries.name: Palette_SetActive
entries.description: Swaps ActivePaletteObject and returns the previous one. Used to temporarily retarget Palette_InstallRange at the secondary impact palette (DAT_0049aef8) without disturbing the live one.

entries.name: Palette_InstallRange
entries.description: Palette_InstallRange(baseIndex, count, srcRgbaArray): copies count RGBA/RGB entries from srcRgbaArray into the global active display palette (*(DAT_0049b020+8) + baseIndex*4), then tracks the min/max dirty index range (DAT_0049b028/DAT_0049b02c) for a batched hardware palette update -- classic indexed-display-mode palette management. Used by the cockpit-view constructor to install the small IMPACTCP.DPL flash palette into a 24-entry sub-range (base 0x2a) of the shared 256-slot palette, distinct from CockpitPaletteSingleton's own local RGB array.

entries.name: Palette_ReadRange
entries.description: (start, count, out): copies count dword entries from the active palette (ActivePaletteObject+8) from index start into out. The read-back of Palette_InstallRange.

entries.name: Palette_GetEntry
entries.description: (index): returns the active palette's dword entry at index (ActivePaletteObject+8).

entries.name: Palette_FlushDirtyRange
entries.description: Pushes the accumulated dirty index range to the display and clears it; if the active palette object changed since the last flush it uploads the whole palette instead.

entries.name: PaletteCycle_Register
entries.description: (record): stores record in the first empty slot of the five at 004cfde8, its due time (Time_GetCoarseTicks + record's int16 +4) at 004cfdfc and 0 at 004cfe10, returning 1; 0 when all five are taken. Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges walks the slots. World_LoadTheater registers each record of the theater's cyc file, reading three int16s per record but stepping 12 bytes through a count*6-byte buffer; no .CYC entry is in any retail VOL (name scan of the eleven, which finds the .WLD/.RMP entries).

entries.name: PaletteCycle_Unregister
entries.description: (record): clears the first of PaletteCycle_Register's five slots (004cfde8) holding record.

entries.name: Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges
entries.description: Per-frame animated palette cycling. Walks 5 fixed slots (DAT_004cfde8 descriptors, DAT_004cfdfc next-due times, DAT_004cfe10 rotation offsets); when a slot's due time passes it rotates that slot's palette sub-range by one entry and reinstalls it via Palette_InstallRange. Keyed off Time_GetCoarseTicks. Blinking cockpit/console lights.

entries.name: Palette_InterpolateColours
entries.description: Colour-space sibling of Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges: interpolates rampCount colour pairs across `levels` steps, emitting 0x01RRGGBB-style entries. Distinct from the index-range remapper used for terrain shading.

entries.name: Palette_BeginCrossFade
entries.description: Palette_BeginCrossFade(fromPalette, toPalette, durationCoarseTicks): precomputes per-channel 8.8 deltas (to - from) / duration into DAT_004cfe28/004d0028/004d0228 over the from object's entry count, and disarms the step timer (0049b03c). Either endpoint may be null, meaning fade to/from black. Callers: Sim_DeathFlash and LiftStart_DarkenPalette.

entries.name: Palette_StepCrossFade
entries.description: Steps the Palette_BeginCrossFade fade by wall clock, not by call: the first call arms an end time of now + duration in Time_GetCoarseTicks units, and each call writes from + delta * elapsed >> 8 into the live palette from entry DAT_004cfe20 (never written, so 0) and extends the dirty range. Returns the coarse ticks remaining; once past the end it returns 0 without writing, so the last value written is the one from the last call before the end, not the destination.

entries.name: Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges
entries.description: Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges(from, to, rampCount, levels, out): linearly interpolates palette index RANGES, not colours. Each of from/to/out is an array of (int16 start, int16 count) pairs; for each of rampCount ramps it emits `levels` interpolated ranges in 8.8 fixed point, with the final step forced exactly to the `to` endpoint. Called twice by maybe_World_LoadTheater with endpoint tables read from WORLD<n>.WLD. WORLD0 expands to 11 ramps x 16 levels, all ranges within indices 96-239 (terrain shading only; no cockpit equivalent found).

entries.name: Palette_ShadeRampLookup
entries.description: Palette_ShadeRampLookup(value, shade): idx = value & 0xff, clamped to 0 when >= ActivePaletteObject+0x0c (the ramp count); reads ActivePaletteObject+0x10 as an array of 8-byte {int16* indices, int32 length} shade ramps and returns ramp[idx].indices[ Math_Q8Multiply(shade, length) ], stepping back one when that lands on the end. So a value here is a RAMP NUMBER, not a colour: the ramps are per-material brightness sequences of palette indices. They live in the tail of each .DPL, after the 256 colour entries. Sole consumer found: TSShadedPoly_Render.

entries.name: Cockpit_CreateCanvasContext
entries.description: Allocates the cockpit widget layer's own 0x239-byte render context, sets clip mode 1 (single rect) at +0x208 and the caller's rect at +0x210..+0x21c, and stores it in DAT_004d042c. Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets passes the whole cockpit canvas and keeps the result at CockpitViewInstance+4.

entries.name: Panel_LoadWrapper
entries.description: Trivial wrapper funneling .DFN/.HFN panel loads into ClassItem_LoadResource with the panel's filename.

entries.name: Cursor_LoadWrapper
entries.description: Trivial wrapper funneling .DCI cursor loads into ClassItem_LoadResource with the cursor's filename.

entries.name: CockpitView_Ctor
entries.description: (view, mech): the 0x288-byte cockpit widget tree.
