entries.description: Paint shared by gunsight children 7 and 8. The +0x45 flag picks the subject: set, NavMarker_Position and colour id 15; clear, the waypoint after the player group's route cursor with colour table entry 0, or -- on a branch gated by DAT_004d2af0, with no writer found by es2_xref.py -- the player's selected target. Takes the ground range with Vec2_DistanceBetween and the bearing as Math_Atan2Guarded(dx, dy) - 0x4000, then draws the error (mech.heading - bearing) as a filled diamond on the tape within +/-0xe38 and as a filled arrow past the rect's right or left end beyond it. Child 8 also composes 'WAYPOINT ' + cursor+1 + ': ' + Hud_WorldUnitsToMetres(range) + ' M.' into its label.

entries.name: Gau_RovingGunsightWidget
entries.description: Large composite 'roving gunsight' HUD-overlay container (matches HUDRovingGunsightGadget/HUDLockingGunsight/HUDPipper class names). Contains the confirmed HTorsoTwist (child rect at 1104, loads bitmap 'hudhtick') and a target-speed text-readout anchor (offsets 1120/1124/1132, format string '000 K/H'). NAVBAR is confirmed NOT here.

entries.name: Gunsight_AddChild
entries.description: Appends a child pointer to the roving-gunsight complex's array at widget+0xd7 (count at +0xff), so construction order is child index. Gunsight_Paint (0043d5c8) walks that array calling each child's slot 0.

entries.name: Gunsight_Paint
entries.description: Paints the front-window HUD: every child of the array at widget+0xd7 in order, then the mission-name label and the speed readout.

entries.name: Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint
entries.description: The roving gunsight's vtable +8, called once a frame from Sim_RenderFrame. Copies CockpitView+0x26c..+0x27e (target, world aim point, pod present flag) into the widget's state block at +0xb7..+0xc9, adds the target's heading (+0xc7), its shape radius from vtable +0x10 (+0xcd) and a literal 2000 (+0xd1), drives child 1, the heading tape, with the NEGATED viewing object's heading -- the sign that makes the compass strip run the same way the simulation's own bearings do -- then runs every child's slot +4 and repaints the whole complex. While the armed byte +0x8c is set and the done byte +0x8d clear, child 1 is given the power-up wind-up ramp (coarseTicks - +0x90) * 0x32 as a ushort instead: climbing from zero for a heading <= 0x8000, counting down from zero above it, latching +0x8d the frame it reaches the heading.

entries.name: Gunsight_SetValues
entries.description: Called once a frame by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate with the machine's heading (mech+0x10), turret twist (+0x298) and turret pitch (+0x29a). Caches them at widget+0xb1/+0xb3/+0xb5 and forwards each one's delta to a child's AddDelta slot (+0xc): heading -> child 7 as (new - old), twist -> child 2 (the rotation indicator) as (old - new), pitch -> child 3 as (old - new).

entries.name: Gunsight_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Returns the roving gunsight's 38-byte target/angle state block, widget+0xb1. Callers are Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate and the three TargetSelect_* entry points, which set byte 36 to 1 to arm the target indicator.

entries.name: Hud_UpdateSpeedReadout
entries.description: Formats the HUD speed text: itoa(Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph(LocalPlayerMech)) followed by the literal ' K/H' (0049c112). The gadget it writes into is DAT_004d185c, built in Gau_RovingGunsightWidget against the width template '000 K/H'.

entries.name: HudClock_Tick
entries.description: The front window's TIME: clock: when Time_GetCoarseTicks passes the deadline at 004d1888, pushes it to now + 0x3c and carries the ASCII digits MM at 004d1860 and SS at 004d1863 by one second, wrapping 99:59 to 00:00, then rebuilds 'MM:SS' at 004d1868. Gunsight_Paint and Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint call it.

entries.name: Gunsight_PaintAltitudeScale
entries.description: (gunsight): only for a flyer (type record +0x50): from the point at +0x113 draws a scale 0x24 << YCoordShift tall out of Hud_BitmapBank frames 15-18 -- frame 15 at the point and 16 at the foot, a narrow column at frame 15's right edge filled in palette 0x4b up to the terrain height under the machine and edged in 0x49 above it, frame 17 at the machine's height (mech+0x2e), and frame 18 twice as a tape scrolled by height / 50, clipped to its own strip. Heights map from grid+0x110 at the foot to grid+0x114 + 5000 at the top, clamped. Gunsight_Paint and Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint call it.

entries.name: Gunsight_PaintHudScanner
entries.description: One line: HudScanner_Paint(scannerScreen, gunsight+0x10b). The gunsight complex's only reference to the MFD's scanner screen.

entries.name: GauRovingGunsight_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (block): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the twelve x/y pairs at +0x10..+0x34 and +0x3c..+0x70 by VideoMode_XCoordShift / VideoMode_YCoordShift; the int at +0x38 is left alone. Gau_RovingGunsightWrapper runs it on the .GAU block at +1088 (0x440), as Gau_ThrottleWidget does GauThrottle_ApplyCoordShift.

entries.name: Gunsight_ReticleRepaint
entries.description: HUDCrosshairGunsight vtable +0x04 (0049c124): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Gunsight_ReticlePaint.

entries.name: HudWaypointIndicator_Repaint
entries.description: HNavGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c154): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator.

entries.name: Gunsight_UnusedChild_Repaint
entries.description: HUDPipper vtable +0x04 (0049c174): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Gunsight_UnusedChild_Paint.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickGadget_PaintNoOp
entries.description: HUDRovingGunsightGadget vtable +0x00 (0049c188): an empty body.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickGadget_InvalidateNoOp
entries.description: HUDRovingGunsightGadget vtable +0x04 (0049c188): an empty body.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickSurface_Repaint
entries.description: HUDRovingGunsight vtable +0x04 (0049c1b0): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Gunsight_ClickSurface_Paint.

entries.name: Gunsight_TargetIndicatorRepaint
entries.description: HUDLockingGunsight vtable +0x04 (0049c1c4): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Gunsight_TargetIndicatorPaint.

entries.name: HudSlideBarHidden_Repaint
entries.description: VFixRotationGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c20c): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, which for this class is HudSlideBarHidden_PaintNoOp.

entries.name: HudRotationIndicator_Repaint
entries.description: HFixRotationGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c22c): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, HudRotationIndicator_Paint.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's SCANNER screen (mode 3), the largest of the six at 0x524 bytes. Builds the plot geometry (dish at inset+(0x26,1), centre at inset+(0x41,0x1c), plot radius 0x19 GAU), the 100-entry contact vector at +0x68 and the four corner readouts. Binds MFD bank frames 14 (dish) and 15 (turret wedge). Range comes from MfdScannerRanges 004d1cf4 = 50000/100000/200000 world units (300/600/1200 m at 1000 units = 6 m) indexed by the zoom field at MfdDisplay+0xc5, default 2. The `radar` bank's 10-frame sweep is NOT this screen's -- MfdDisplay_Update plays it over the same dish on a switch to mode 3. See docs/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Update
entries.description: Rebuilds the SCANNER screen's contact list from the live object list: skips the viewing machine, anything dead (+0x99/+0xa4), a group still awaiting deployment (group+0x14), an invulnerable structure type (class 1 with BASES.DAT +0x1e), a Cybrid not currently radar-visible (+0x95), and anything past the current display range on the ground plane. Survivors are rotated by Math_BuildRotation2D(-heading) and stored as (x, -y) with a colour id per class and side, so the plot is hull-relative nose-up. Also mirrors mech+0x96 into +0x34 and re-presses PASS or ACTIVE when it changed. Its hostile branch's blinking obj+0x1aa last-known-position marker is DEAD CODE: every constructor sets obj+0xa7 = 1 and nothing clears it. See docs/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_UpdateAndPaint
entries.description: MFDRadar vtable +0x04 (0049c328), the MFD screen's per-frame slot: MfdRadarScreen_Update, then the screen's own slot +0x00, MfdRadarScreen_Paint.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Paint
entries.description: Paints the SCANNER screen: floods the dish rect with raw palette index 0x11, blits MFD frame 15 rotated about its own corner at the plot centre by turretTwist - 0x6000, covers it with frame 14, draws the passive-range ring (ellipse outline, colour id 11) only when passive and 140000 < range, then frame 17 (reference line), frame 18 (player marker), each contact as a 2x2 fill, frame 16 over the selected target, and the four RNG:/TRG: readouts as right-aligned zero-padded four-character fields. See docs/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: HudScanner_Paint
entries.description: The front window's floating scanner repeater. Belongs to the GUNSIGHT complex, not the MFD: Gunsight_Paint and Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint reach it through the one-line FUN_0043e0ec after the child loop. Takes the SCANNER screen object (CockpitView+0x1ed's +0xd9) and the widget's own point at +0x10b (.GAU offset 1196), calls MfdRadarScreen_Update to rebuild the shared contact list, and RETURNS IMMEDIATELY when that screen is the display's current one -- so it and the F4 screen are never on screen together. Draws a 0x2e-unit red circle outline (colour id 9), the turret arc as two lines at twist +/- 0x2000, MFD frame 18 at the centre, each contact as a radius-2 black disc with a radius-1 coloured core, and MFD frame 16 over the selection. Its plot scale divides by the half-size (46 device px), not by the screen's 0x19. See docs/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's FLASH COMM screen (mode 1). Builds six order rows: rect inset+(2,0xd)-(0x60,0x3a) GAU with both corners nudged in by 1<<XCoordShift, stepping 7<<YCoordShift per row. Font ColorSchemePanels[1] CPGREEN with [2] CPRED as the alternate at +0x21, background colour id 0x11, text margin 2<<XCoordShift. The six rows are positions over STRINGS0.STR group 0's orders: rows 4 and 5 switch to verbs 7 and 8 when their state byte's bit 1 is set (MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb). See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_Paint
entries.description: MFDFlashComm vtable +0x00 (0049c36c): floods the screen rect (+0x39) with colour 0x11 through a temporary brush, copies the current selection (*(+8)) into +0x32, then for each of the six rows sets its label's frame -- 0049b0c4 when the row's flag byte (+0x2c+i) has bit 0, 0049b0b8 for the selected row, 0049b0b0 otherwise -- and its text and hotkey from the tables at 004d132c/004d1374 (index +3 when the flag has bit 1), and draws the selected row's plate with MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate.

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_Update
entries.description: MFDFlashComm vtable +0x04 (0049c36c): when the selection (*(+8)) differs from +0x32, the force byte +0x36 is set, or a row is pending in +0x37: repaints the old row (+0x37 if set, else +0x32) unselected, makes the new selection current and repaints it selected, each with MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate, Label_SetTextWithHotkey and Widget_DrawToCockpit; then clears +0x36 and sets +0x37 to -1.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb
entries.description: The STRINGS0 group 0 verb the FLASH COMM page's selected row names: the row index at screen+0x32, plus 3 when that row's own state byte at screen+0x2c+row has bit 1 set. Only rows 4 and 5 ever have that bit set (MfdFlashComm_ToggleRowVariant refuses any other row), so the page sends verbs 0-5, 7 and 8. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] only.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_SetScreenRow
entries.description: (screen, row) copies screen +0x32 into the previous-row word +0x37, then stores row at +0x32. Seven calls from MfdFlashComm_HandleAltKey.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_ToggleRowVariant
entries.description: (screen): for selected row (+0x32) 4 or 5 only, flips bit 1 of that row's state byte at screen+0x2c+row and sets +0x36; any other row is left alone. MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb adds 3 to the verb of a row with that bit set. MfdFlashComm_Transmit calls it.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_ResetRow
entries.description: (screen, row) ANDs the row state byte +0x2c+row with 1 (clears the second-verb bit 1, keeps bit 0) and restores the row label's hotkey font +0x21 to ColorSchemePanels[2] CPRED (0049b0b4). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_DisableRow
entries.description: (screen, row) ORs bit 0 into the row state byte +0x2c+row and sets the row label's hotkey font +0x21 to ColorSchemePanels[6] CPOFF (0049b0c4). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate
entries.description: (screen, row, erase): blits the selected-row plate at the top-left of row label row (rows past 6 map to row - 3) from the MFD bitmap bank at 0049cbcc, through VideoMode_BlitBitmap: frame 13 when erase is set, otherwise 11 plus the press byte (+0x1b) of the widget at the MFD's +0x40. 0043f7a4, 0043f878 and MfdButton_SetCaption call it.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's MISSILE CAM screen (mode 5), matching the MFDMissileView class name in DBSIM's string table. Like the nav map it gets no background chrome from MfdDisplay_Repaint, filling the screen with its own camera image. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_Paint
entries.description: The MISSILE CAM screen's draw: the code pointer stored first in the vtable at 0049c449 that MfdMissileViewScreen_Ctor installs. A nonzero DAT_0049c398 starts a flash: when it differs from the screen's copy at +0x45 it stamps a deadline 0x1e coarse ticks ahead at +0x46, and until then each paint toggles the byte at +0x20 and fills the screen rect (DAT_004d1ac8) with COLORS.DAT id 16 (DAT_004d3c20) or id 19 (DAT_004d3c26) alternately and returns; at the deadline it clears the copy and DAT_0049c398. With DAT_0049c394 set it walks the effect pool (Pool_Prev) for that round: gone, it clears DAT_0049c394; found, the camera takes the round's position (+0x26/+0x2a/+0x2e) plus Q14(500, cos h) in x and Q14(500, cos(h - 0x4000)) in y, h being the heading at +0x10 -- 500 units along the round's own X axis, to its right, not along its heading -- and the round's euler triple (+0xc/+0x10), and the world is drawn from there into the screen's own render context: fill id 16 one column short of the rect's right edge, Scene_SubmitFrameObjects with ViewObjectPtr swapped to the camera, Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion and Scene_DrawTerrain with TerrainTexturingEnabled forced 0 and shade mode 004aab30 forced 1, then two Raster_DrawLine calls through the centre (full width, full height) and a ring-mode Raster_DrawEllipse of radius half the centre's y, all in id 19, with the cockpit shake offset taken out of the context rect for the pass. With DAT_0049c394 clear it fills the rect with palette index 0x11 and sets the labels from STRINGS0 group 35: NONE in label 1 when CockpitView_SumLauncherCounts is 0, else READY TO and LAUNCH in labels 0 and 1; LOCK in label 3, in ColorSchemePanels[0] on id 4 while the gunsight's +0xd6 (mech+0x9b, lock) is clear, else in [3] on id 19 or id 9 by coarse-tick bit 0x20. See docs/formats/mfd.md, 'MFDMissileView -- mode 5'.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_Update
entries.description: MFDMissileView vtable +0x04 (0049c449): raises the repaint counter +0x43 to 2 when DAT_0049c394, +0x1c, or the cockpit view's +0x1f5 object's +0xd6 byte is set; at 2 runs the screen's own slot +0x00 (MfdMissileViewScreen_Paint), at 1 Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, 004d1ac8), decrementing the counter either way.

entries.name: CockpitView_SumLauncherCounts
entries.description: Over CockpitViewInstance's weapon gauges (+0x70 array, count +0x98), sums the int16 each mount (gauge+0xbd) writes through its vtable +0x60 when that call returns a subtype other than 5, not a launcher; returns the sum. MfdMissileViewScreen_Paint shows the label 004d16f4 when it is 0.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_BlinkLockLabel
entries.description: (screen): flips the MISSILE CAM screen's +0x44 with coarse-tick bit 0x20 and, on each flip, re-fonts label 3 (+0x3f) in ColorSchemePanels[3] on a plate of COLORS.DAT id 9 (bit set) or id 19 (bit clear), returning 1; 0 when nothing changed. The same blink MfdMissileViewScreen_Paint applies to the LOCK label, latched in a byte. es2_xref.py finds no branch to it and no stored pointer.

entries.name: MfdMapScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's NAV MAP screen (mode 2). Copies the inset rect into this+0x18..0x24, allocates a 0x239-byte offscreen render target (this+0x10) centred at -((x1-x0)>>1), -((y1-y0)>>1), and a 0x22-byte view (this+0x14, View_Ctor) with perspective shift 8. No labels, no aux buttons.

entries.name: MfdMapScreen_PaintNoOp
entries.description: MFDNavMap vtable +0x00 (0049c4be): an empty body. The map draws from its per-frame slot +0x04, MfdMapScreen_Paint.

entries.name: MfdMapScreen_Paint
entries.description: NAV MAP paint, vtable slot 1; runs every frame the screen is up. Floods the inset with COLORS.DAT id 19, centres the map projection on the viewing machine (obj+0x26/+0x2a) at a fixed scale of 200000 (8.8 world units per pixel), calls HddMap_DrawTerrain(obj+0x10) so the map turns heading-up, then draws a cross in id 16 through the centre with two Raster_DrawLine calls, (-1,0)-(1,0) and (0,-1)-(0,1) shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift. No grid, border or markers.

entries.name: WeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for a weapon hardpoint gauge. Lazily loads the `pweapons` (DAT_0049c4d0) and `wpn_dmg` (DAT_0049c4d4) sprite banks, folder selected off DAT_004d25f0, builds the two-sequence WPN_DMG frame table (frames 1-9 and 9-1, one tick each) into _DAT_004d1adc, gives the gauge its own sequencer over it at +0x6c, and sets the sensor-dropout ranges to 120-360 dark and 180-1800 shown.

entries.name: WeaponGauge_MountProjectileType
entries.description: (gauge): the Type (int16 +0) of the PROJ.DAT record the gauge's mount (+0xbd) holds at +0x20, or -1 with no mount or no record. MfdDisplay_SyncMissileCamMode tests it for 0, Rocket.

entries.name: WeaponGauge_MountProjectileSubtype
entries.description: (gauge): the subtype id (int16 +2) of the PROJ.DAT record the gauge's mount (+0xbd) holds at +0x20, or -1 with no mount or no record. MfdDisplay_SyncMissileCamMode tests it for 3, the electro-optical missile.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The weapon-row gauge class for energy mounts (vtable 0049c91c), built via CockpitView_CreateEnergyWeaponGauge. Builds the charge bar (WeaponSliderGadget_Ctor) over the same value field the ammunition class puts its number in (x0+36..x0+53, y0..y0+5).

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_Paint
entries.description: EnergyWeaponGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c91c): while +0x8c is set, paints the row's two children (+0x18, +0x1c) through slot +0x00 of their tables at +0x17. AmmoWeaponGauge_Paint is the ammunition row's.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_Update
entries.description: Energy weapon row's per-frame update. While armed: runs the power-up fill until done, then the sensor dropout -- Player_DependentCondition(2) into +0x74 and PanelGauge_TickDropout when nonzero -- and on the dark-to-shown transition repaints both children (select gadget, charge bar).

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState
entries.description: EnergyWeaponGauge vtable +0x10 (gauge, block), the write-back twin of EnergyWeaponGauge_GetState over the 0x17-byte state block at +0xc2. Block[1], the charge bar's slider position, when it differs from +0xc6: stored there and set on the slider (child +0x1c) through its slot +0x14, SliderWidget_SetValueH, which commits back through EnergyWeaponGauge_OnChildClick. Block[0], the bar's fill, when it differs from +0xc2: stored there and at the bar's +0x7a, and at +0xdb unless the power-up fill is running (+0x8d). The destroyed byte (+0x11) puts both children's state (+0x1b) to 2 or back to 0, deferred through +0xc1 while CockpitView_GetShakeOffset reports a shake. Bytes +0x14..+0x16 go to +0xd6..+0xd8. Repaints whichever children changed.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_GetState
entries.description: Returns gauge+0xc2, the 0x17-byte display state block that WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState and 0040e0e0 copy into a local.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_PowerUpFill
entries.description: An energy weapon row's power-up fill: the charge bar shows min(elapsed * 0x19, live) against the coarse ticks since the row was armed, then the live value (+0xdb) and done from elapsed >= 0x33. Repaints both children.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_OnChildClick
entries.description: The energy weapon row's vtable slot 0, which its children forward to. Searches the child table at +0x18 (count +0x68): child 0 is the select gadget, and it chains the row via WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember when bit 1 of the click value (the mouse-button word 0049db6c) is set and arms it via CockpitView_ArmWeaponByGauge otherwise; child 1 is the charge bar (WeaponSliderGadget, which no press reaches in retail), whose committed slider position is clamped to 0..0x400 and stored at +0xc6 -- block[1] of the state block WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState reads back as the charge target.
entries.signature: void __cdecl EnergyWeaponGauge_OnChildClick(int gauge, int child, uint value)

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The weapon-row gauge class for ammunition mounts (vtable 0049c8fc), built via CockpitView_CreateAmmoWeaponGauge. Adds a left-aligned numeric label over the value field at x0+36..x0+53, y0..y0+5 of the .GAU hardpoint rect; FUN_004411b4 fills it with itoa(rounds) in ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE when the mount is selected and [11] GRAY otherwise.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_Paint
entries.description: Ammunition row's paint: the select gadget, then itoa(rounds) into the value label in WHITE (selected) or GRAY, skipped while the row is dark or mid-wipe.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_Update
entries.description: Ammunition row's per-frame update. Marks the power-up done at once, runs the sensor dropout as EnergyWeaponGauge_Update does, and refreshes the round-count label only while the row is neither dark nor mid-wipe (+0x76 clear and the +0x6c sequencer idle).

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_SetState
entries.description: ProjectileWeaponGauge vtable +0x10 (0049c8fc), (gauge, block): EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState's ammunition twin. A new dword 0 (the round count) goes to +0xc2 and marks the row dirty (+0xb0 = 2). A new byte +0x11 goes to +0xd3 and sets the select gadget's (+0x18) state +0x1b to 2 or 0. New bytes +0x14/+0x15/+0x16 go to +0xd6/+0xd7/+0xd8. Any of the byte changes also invalidates the select gadget (its slot +0x04) and marks the row dirty.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_GetState
entries.description: Returns gauge+0xc2, the display state block WeaponMount_PushAmmoGaugeState copies into a local from the mount's +0x77 gauge. The ammunition twin of EnergyWeaponGauge_GetState.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_OnChildClick
entries.description: The ammunition weapon row's vtable slot 0, the twin of EnergyWeaponGauge_OnChildClick: child 0 chains the row on the right-button bit of the click value and arms it otherwise, then marks the row for repaint at +0xb0. It is also the PodGauge vtable's +0x2c entry.
entries.signature: uint __cdecl AmmoWeaponGauge_OnChildClick(int gauge, int child, uint value)

entries.name: PodGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The weapon-row gauge class for equipment pods (vtable 0049c8d0), built via FUN_004321d4. Has no state box and no value field: its name label spans x0+11..x0+53 of the .GAU hardpoint rect, and its 11-char name buffer is seeded with a literal space, then the mount name, then STRINGS0.STR group 3 (' POD') appended into whatever room is left -- 'SHIELD' becomes ' SHIELD POD'.

entries.name: PodGauge_Paint
entries.description: PodGauge vtable +4, shared by all three pod gauge classes. Picks the name label's font and ink from the two state bytes: the destroyed byte at +0xc3 wins and prints the offline text across the widened label while hiding the row's select gadget (state 2), and failing that the button byte at +0xc2 selects the gray font 0049b0d8 with ink 0x2e when off and the dark font 0049b0dc with HudColorTable id 12 when on. That re-fonting is the only feedback a pod row gives, since it has no state box.

entries.name: PodGauge_Update
entries.description: Pod row's per-frame update: the power-up slot, then the sensor dropout, then the name label's repaint, held back while the row is dark or mid-wipe.

entries.name: PodGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: PodGauge vtable +0x14. Writes the caller's 8 bytes over gauge+0xc2 and marks the widget dirty, but only when the destroyed byte at +0xc3 has changed -- the button byte at +0xc2 cannot make this class repaint. TogglePodGauge_SetStateBlock compares both bytes.

entries.name: PodGauge_GetStateBlock
entries.description: PodGauge vtable +0x18, shared by every pod gauge class: returns gauge+0xc2, an 8-byte block whose byte 0 is the button and byte 1 the mount's destroyed flag.

entries.name: PodGauge_OnClick
entries.description: PodGauge vtable slot 0 (0049c8d0), reached the usual way -- the row's WeaponSelectGadget child forwards its click to the owner's slot 0, after sounding Widget_ClickSound. It sets the repaint byte at +0xb0 and returns. A Shield, Targeting or Energy pod row therefore clicks and sounds but holds no on/off state; TogglePodGauge_OnClick is the ECM/Turbo override that does.

entries.name: TogglePodGauge_Ctor
entries.description: PodGauge_Ctor followed by the vtable 0049c8a4 -- the pod gauge row that carries an on/off state. Built for the ECM pod directly and for the Turbo pod through TurboPodGauge_Ctor; no other pod gets it.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl TogglePodGauge_Ctor(void *gauge, int *rect, int cockpitView, short hardpoint, void *pod)

entries.name: TogglePodGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: TogglePodGauge vtable +0x14: PodGauge_SetStateBlock's override, repainting when either the button byte at +0xc2 or the destroyed byte at +0xc3 has changed rather than the destroyed byte alone.

entries.name: TogglePodGauge_OnClick
entries.description: TogglePodGauge vtable slot 0 -- structurally identical to ShieldsGauge_OnClick: searches its own child table at +0x18 (count at +0x68) for the widget that was clicked and, for child 0, XORs the button byte at +0xc2 and marks the row dirty. This is the whole of a pod's on/off toggle, and only the ECM and Turbo rows have it.

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_Ctor
entries.description: TogglePodGauge_Ctor followed by the vtable 0049c878 and one extra child widget -- the Turbo pod's charge bar over pod+0x7d.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl TurboPodGauge_Ctor(void *gauge, int *rect, int cockpitView, short hardpoint, void *pod)

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: EnergyPodGauge (the Turbo Pod row, TurboPodGauge_Ctor) vtable +0x14, (gauge, block): when the button byte, the destroyed byte or the charge dword (block+4) differs from +0xc2/+0xc3/+0xc6, copies the block's first two dwords to +0xc2/+0xc6, also stores the charge in +0xe2 while the power-up fill is not done (+0x8d clear), and marks the row dirty (+0xb0 = 2).

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_OnClick
entries.description: EnergyPodGauge vtable +0x00, (gauge, child): when child is the row's first child (+0x18), XORs the button byte +0xc2 and marks the row dirty -- TogglePodGauge_OnClick's toggle.

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_Paint
entries.description: EnergyPodGauge vtable +0x04: while +0x8c is set, paints the select gadget (+0x18) and, unless +0x76 is set, the sprite sequence at +0x6c is running (SpriteSequence_State), the label's rect is off screen or the gadget is hidden (+0x1b == 2), sets the label (+0xca): a destroyed pod (+0xc3) gets the text at DAT_004d13c8 and hides the gadget; otherwise the frame and colour for the button's state (+0xc2). A live pod also paints its charge bar (+0xde) to +0xc6.

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_Update
entries.description: EnergyPodGauge vtable +0x08: PodGauge_Update(gauge).

entries.name: TurboPodGauge_PowerUpFill
entries.description: The Turbo Pod row's power-up fill, the same ramp as EnergyWeaponGauge_PowerUpFill over the pod's raw charge (+0xe2 into +0xc6): min(elapsed * 0x19, live) until elapsed > 0x32, then the live value and done. On a 2500-unit bar it climbs to 1250 and then jumps.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_Ctor
entries.description: The console button panel under the weapon rows, from .GAU offset 468. Builds FOUR WeaponRangeSelectGadget children from the rects at 484/500/516/532 and registers each with Widget_RegisterClickable in index order -- the chain selector, LINK, TRACK, and a fourth whose rect is zero in every retail .GAU and which therefore never takes a click. Installs ConsoleButtons_OnChildClick as slot 0, and hides child 2 (TRACK) outright when the piloted machine is a flyer.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetChainNumber
entries.description: (panel, chain): stores the int16 chain number at panel+0xb1 and does nothing else; the caption is repainted elsewhere. WeaponMounts_SetChain, Gau_WeaponButtonsWidget, ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock and ConsoleButtons_OnChildClick call it.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_ToggleAutoTrack
entries.description: The console buttons manager's auto-track toggle, reached from ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock and from Sim_DispatchCommand's command 0x14 (and forced off by command 0xe). Flips the manager's +0xb3, pushes the new state into the tracking object at +0x20 and repaints it, then withdraws both 0x26 AUTO TRACKING ENGAGED and 0x27 AUTO TRACKING DISABLED from the computer's message port and posts the one the mode just became -- the same shape as Mech_ToggleRadarMode. Refuses outright when the tracking object's +0x1b is 2.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch
entries.description: Stores the LINK button's latch byte at panel+0xb4 and calls WeaponMounts_ToggleLink. Called from the button's own click handler and again from ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock when the manager writes the byte back cleared -- two of the three toggles one press produces.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_Paint
entries.description: WeaponRangeGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c85c), the console-button row: paints its four children (+0x18..+0x24) through slot +0x00 of each child's table at +0x17.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_Update
entries.description: WeaponRangeGauge vtable +0x08 (0049c85c): runs each of its four children's slot +0x0c (FlushDeferredPaint).

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock
entries.description: The write-back half of ConsoleButtons_GetStateBlock: applies each of the three fields that differs from the panel's own copy. The manager clears the LINK byte before writing back, so this sees a change and calls ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch again -- the third of the three toggles one LINK press produces.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Copies the console panel's three live fields -- chain number (+0xb1, short), auto-track latch (+0xb3) and LINK latch (+0xb4) -- into the scratch block at 004d1ae0 for WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate to read.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_OnChildClick
entries.description: The console button panel's child-click slot, switching on the child index: 0 advances the chain number at panel+0xb1 (wrapping at 3) and repaints the caption, 1 calls ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch, 2 toggles auto-track. Reached identically by a mouse click and by a key, since ConsoleButtons_HandleCommand presses the same children.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_HandleCommand
entries.description: The console button panel's command slot: scancode 0x26 (L) presses child 1, the LINK button; 0x29 (backquote) presses child 0, the chain button. The pair of literals is what identifies the whole command-code space as PC set-1 scancodes.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for WeaponSelectGadget (object size 0x46), the weapon-row leaf without chain membership. Called directly only by PodGauge_Ctor -- a pod row cannot join a fire chain -- and as the base constructor of ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_Ctor. Class name from the descriptor record at 00443283.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_PaintUnderlay
entries.description: Blits WPN_DMG frame 0 (112x14, the row background) at the gadget's .GAU rect and prints the slot number, unless the owning gauge is dark or mid-wipe or not yet armed.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: WeaponSelectGadgetVtable +0x0c: the same body as MFDStateGadget_FlushDeferredPaint -- at pending-paint count +0x1f 1, Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, gadget, 0); at 2, slot 0 of the vtable at +0x17; decrementing it either way.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_OnClick
entries.description: WeaponSelectGadgetVtable +0x08 (gadget, flags): unconditionally calls the owner's (+0x24) vtable slot 0 with (owner, gadget, flags), then slot 1 of the vtable at +0x17 and slot 2 of the sub-object at +0x20.

entries.name: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for ChainedWeaponSelectGadget (object size 0x67), the clickable weapon row EnergyWeaponGauge_Ctor and AmmoWeaponGauge_Ctor build. Derives from WeaponSelectGadget, whose constructor it calls first; the extra level is what carries fire-chain membership, which is why PodGauge_Ctor builds the plain base class instead. Also builds the row's hardpoint state box and weapon-name label. Class name from the descriptor record at 0044333b.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_Paint
entries.description: Paints one weapon row: the row plate from PWEAPONS frame 0 (selected) or 1 (not) at the .GAU rect minus one device pixel on both axes, the hardpoint state box from PWEAPONS frames 4/5/6 by state, the weapon name from the gauge's own 12-char buffer (+0xb1), and the round count. Text colour is the font: ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE / [11] GRAY for the name, [13] GREEN / [11] GRAY for the count; the label's field 0x1d is the background colour it paints first (0x2e here).

entries.name: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget's FlushDeferredPaint slot +0xc (vtable 0049c7dc), also reached by the jump at 004433ea. Counter +0x1f at 1: Widget_DrawToCockpit(0) on the gadget and on its second rect at +0x56; at 2: WeaponSelectGadget_PaintUnderlay and the Paint slot. Either way it decrements the counter.

entries.name: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_OnClick
entries.description: ChainedWeaponSelectGadgetVtable +0x08: the same body as WeaponSelectGadget_OnClick.

entries.name: WeaponSliderGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for WeaponSliderGadget (object size 0x7e; class name from the descriptor record at 004432df), a PanelHSliderGadget leaf: the energy weapon row's charge bar, child 1 of EnergyWeaponGauge_Ctor's gauge. Its last vtable stores are WeaponSliderGadgetVtable at +0x17 and WeaponSliderGadget_PanelSliderGadgetVtable at +0x3e. Built on SliderWidget_CtorBase, so it is a horizontal slider over 0..0x400 carrying the +0x1d drag flag, but no press reaches it: the row's ChainedWeaponSelectGadget is registered first and its hit rect, the whole .GAU hardpoint rect, contains the bar in every retail file. Drops the value field's top edge by one GAU unit, builds an LEDBarGraph over range 0x400 at +0x46, and then, when the byte it is handed is zero (as it is in every retail .GAU, where it lands in confirmed-zero padding), overwrites its three colour fields with raw palette indices 0x20 (even columns), 0x22 (odd) and 0x2e (remainder) -- not COLORS.DAT ids, which is why a capacitor bar is blue where the Master Energy Pool's meter is grey.

entries.name: WeaponSliderGadget_Paint
entries.description: WeaponSliderGadgetVtable +0x00, the energy row charge bar's paint: the LEDBarGraph at +0x46 to the value at +0x7a, skipped while the owning gauge (+0x42) is dark or mid-wipe or not yet armed.

entries.name: WeaponSliderGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: WeaponSliderGadgetVtable +0x0c: calls slot 0 of the vtable at +0x17 when the pending-paint count +0x1f is 2, and does nothing at 1 and never decrements it.

entries.name: WeaponRangeSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for WeaponRangeSelectGadget (object size 0x41), the weapon-range gauge's button; derives from PanelStateGadget, so it latches. Built by FUN_00441dd0. Class name from the descriptor record at 00443223.

entries.name: ConsoleButton_Paint
entries.description: Paints the chain/link/auto-track console buttons: plate from PWEAPONS frames 2 + state (frame 2 unlit, solid palette index 34 = the retail blue at RGB (77,77,182); frame 3 lit, index 14 green) blitted at the widget's own rect, then the caption. The chain button's caption comes from the three-entry Roman-numeral table at 0049c71c ('I', 'II', 'III'), a literal .rdata table unrelated to the string file. LINK and TRACK are not fixed the same way: both read ConsoleButtonCaptions (004d13d0) indexed by the widget's own kind field (param_1[10]: 1=LINK, 2=TRACK), which SimStrings_LoadAll fills from STRINGS0.STR group 4. Caption font is ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE when unlit, [12] DARK when lit.

entries.name: WeaponRangeSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: WeaponRangeSelectGadgetVtable +0x0c: the same body as WeaponSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint.

entries.name: WeaponRangeSelectGadget_OnClick
entries.description: WeaponRangeSelectGadgetVtable +0x08 (gadget, flags): when flags bit 0 is set, slot 2 of the sub-object at +0x20, then the owner's (+0x24) slot 0 with (owner, gadget, flags). No +0x17 repaint call and no state toggle.

entries.name: Gau_ShiftRects2
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the next 16-byte rect by VideoMode_XCoordShift / VideoMode_YCoordShift -- the same body as GauEnergyMeter_ApplyCoordShift. Gau_ShiftRects3, Gau_ShiftRects3Point and Gau_ShiftRects5 start with it.

entries.name: Gau_ShiftRects3
entries.description: (rects): Gau_ShiftRects2, then shifts the third rect (+0x20). Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets runs it on CockpitGauRecord+0x2d.

entries.name: Gau_ShiftRects3Point
entries.description: (rects): Gau_ShiftRects2, then shifts the third rect (+0x20) and the x0/y0 pair at +0x30. Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets runs it on CockpitGauRecord+0x41.

entries.name: Gau_ShiftRects5
entries.description: (rects): Gau_ShiftRects2, then shifts the three rects after it (+0x20, +0x30, +0x40). Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets runs it on CockpitGauRecord+0x59.

entries.name: GauWeaponButtons_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the four 16-byte rects after it left by VideoMode_XCoordShift (x) and VideoMode_YCoordShift (y). Gau_WeaponButtonsWidget runs it on the .GAU block at +0x1d4 (the panel and its four buttons).

entries.name: WeaponGauge_SetStateNoOp
entries.description: WeaponGauge vtable +0x10 (0049c95c), kept by ChainedWeaponGauge, PodWeaponGauge, TogglePodGauge and EnergyPodGauge: an empty body. EnergyWeaponGauge installs EnergyWeaponGauge_SetState.

entries.name: PodGauge_PowerUpFillDone
entries.description: PodWeaponGauge and TogglePodGauge vtable +0x1c, the power-up fill slot: sets the done byte +0x8d at once, so a plain or toggle pod row has no ramp. EnergyPodGauge installs TurboPodGauge_PowerUpFill.

entries.name: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_Dtor
entries.description: ChainedWeaponSelectGadget's destructor (class record 0044333b): (gadget, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, PanelSelectGadget_Dtor(gadget, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0044342b; class record at 0044333b

entries.description: WeaponRangeSelectGadget's destructor (class record 00443223): (gadget, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, PanelSelectGadget_Dtor(gadget, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The real shield meter, called only by Gau_ShieldDisplayWidget (00432454) with .GAU offset 0x268=616. NOT an LED bar -- it loads no sprite bank and instead builds a 0x40-byte child per shield facing via FUN_00444aec plus a text label via FUN_004387ac/FUN_00438884 (the same generic label constructors the .DFN font consumers use). That matches retail: nested green concentric boxes with a numeric readout above and below. The .GAU block at 616 is a zero header rect followed by four 16-byte rects at 632/648/664/680, all shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift in ShieldsGauge_ApplyCoordShift. Distinct from EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor (00444d5c), which the earlier maybe_ShieldsGauge_Ctor name wrongly claimed was this widget.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Paint
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's vtable+4 slot. Unconditionally calls ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette and ShieldsGauge_UpdateReadouts.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Update
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's per-frame update slot (vtable+8, called from the general HUD paint pass, not the click pipeline). Gated on visibility and a 'shields present' flag; when the dirty flag ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock set (+0xb0==2) is pending, refreshes the ring palette and readouts and clears it. This is the bridge between Shield_BalanceInputRead's once-per-frame gameplay update and the HUD paint pass -- the click sets a flag, the gameplay tick consumes it into real sim state and a dirty bit, and this slot is what actually repaints from that bit.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_PowerUpFill
entries.description: The shield meter's power-up fill, called by ShieldsGauge_Update while armed and not done: each displayed facing (+0xb5, +0xb9) is the lesser of the coarse ticks since arming and the live value ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock parked at +0xcc/+0xd0; sets done (+0x8d) once both match, and marks the gauge dirty.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_OnClick
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's own vtable slot 0 (per the same *param_1=&PTR_thisFunction ctor-assignment evidence used for MfdButton_OnClick). Searches its own +0x18/+0x68 child-pointer table (populated identically to MfdDisplay's, by ShieldsGauge_Ctor) for the clicked facing widget; index 0 (front) sets state byte +0xc2=1 clearing +0xc3, index 1 (rear) the reverse. Consumed once per frame by Shield_BalanceInputRead, not painted directly.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: Write-back counterpart to ShieldsGauge_GetStateBlock: overwrites the 15-byte state block at param_1+0xb5 from param_2 (called by Shield_BalanceInputRead with the freshly computed front/rear percentages and a cleared click-flag pair), and sets the dirty flag at +0xb0=2 if the values actually changed. Also zeroes the front/rear fields when the gauge's +0x8d 'shields down' flag is set.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Trivial accessor: returns param_1+0xb5, the start of ShieldsGauge's 15-byte live state block (front charge, rear charge, balance, then the two click flags ShieldsGauge_OnClick sets). Shield_BalanceInputRead copies out of this pointer directly rather than through a richer accessor.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette
entries.description: Computes the shield meter's six ring colours and installs them at palette index 0x42 (66-71). Per facing (charge at +0xb5 and +0xb9) three rings light in turn: ring 1 from 0, ring 2 from 0x100 at twice the rate, ring 3 from 0x180 at four times, each as base * t >> 10 in Q10. Above 0x400 the same three tracks run again over base + (bright - base) * t. Colour immediates at 0049c9cb..0049c9d0: base RGB6 (25,59,23), bright (59,59,23). Install order is the stack layout, so 66-68 are the first facing outermost-first and 69-71 the second. At the nominal half charge all six resolve to RGB (48,116,44), matching the retail screenshot's meter.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_UpdateReadouts
entries.description: Fills ShieldsGauge's two numeric labels (object +0xc4 and +0xc8) from the fore/aft balance at +0xbd: itoa(balance * 200 >> 10) and its complement out of 200. An even split reads 100 and 100, which is what retail shows.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_FacingCtor
entries.description: Builds one 0x40-byte shield-facing child for ShieldsGauge_Ctor, one per facing, over the .GAU rects at 632 and 648. Draws no geometry: its paint slot (FUN_00444b5c) only tests visibility. The nested concentric rings the retail meter shows are painted into the herc's own canopy art in palette indices 66-71; the gauge animates them by rewriting those six palette slots (ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette).

entries.name: ShieldFacing_Paint
entries.description: A shield-facing child's Paint slot. Draws no geometry -- only a visibility test (FUN_00431410) -- because the concentric rings retail shows are palette-animated into the herc's own canopy art, not drawn by this widget (see ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette in docs/formats/cockpit-hud-widgets.md).

entries.name: ShieldFacing_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: The shield facing's vtable slot +0xc, the per-frame deferred-paint flush every cockpit widget class implements. Counter at +0x1f: 2 decrements without repainting (a facing has no content to rebuild, its rings being palette-animated), 1 calls Widget_DrawToCockpit and decrements. The counter is set to 2 by Widget_InvalidateDeferred, which Widget_Repaint calls on every press and release.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the four 16-byte rects after it left by VideoMode_XCoordShift (x) and VideoMode_YCoordShift (y). Gau_ShieldDisplayWidget runs it on the .GAU block at +0x268 before ShieldsGauge_Ctor.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_FacingDtor
entries.description: ShieldsSelectGadget's destructor (class record 00444cb2), ShieldsGauge_FacingCtor's object: (gadget, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, PanelSelectGadget_Dtor(gadget, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00444d2c; class record at 00444cb2

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor
entries.description: This is the Master Energy Pool meter (reactor charge), not the shield meter. Called only by Gau_EnergyMeterWidget (004323e0) with .GAU offset 0x224=548, whose child rect is at 564 -- in OUTLAW.GAU that rect is (91,198)-(115,205), directly under the TRACK button, which is where retail draws the blue pinstripe bar. Builds an LED bar with value range 0x400, writing HudColorTable ids 6 and 5 into the pinstripe colour fields 0x2c/0x30 and id 19 into the remainder colour 0x24; those resolve to palette indices 98/97/16 = (0,116,204), (0,40,160), (0,0,0), i.e. blue. Class identity is from the binary's own class-name table, which pairs 'EnergyPoolGauge' immediately with 'LEDBarGraphV' (file offset 280429) and 'ShieldsGauge' with 'ShieldsSelectGadget' (279148): the LED bar class is EnergyPoolGauge, and ShieldsGauge is a different class entirely (see ShieldsGauge_Ctor).

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_Paint
entries.description: EnergyPoolGauge vtable +0x04 (0049cabc): when the bar's (+0xb5) rect is on screen, installs the gauge's own render context (+0xbf, given the current one's clip and origin) when it has one, paints the bar to the value at +0xb1 through its slot +0x00, and reinstalls the previous context.

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_Update
entries.description: EnergyPoolGauge vtable +0x08: EnergyPoolGauge_Paint's body gated on the dirty byte +0xb0 == 2, followed by Widget_DrawToCockpit(1, gauge+4) and +0xb0 = 0.

entries.name: EnergyMeter_SetValue
entries.description: (meter, &value): stores value at meter+0xb1 and, when it differs from the previous one, sets the paint count +0xb0 to 2. Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate passes CockpitViewInstance+0x1e5 and energyPool << 10 / 10000 (0..0x400, the range of the LEDBarGraphV 00444edc builds).

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_OnChildClickNoOp
entries.description: EnergyPoolGauge vtable +0x00 (0049cabc): an empty body.

entries.name: GauEnergyMeter_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the one rect after it by VideoMode_XCoordShift / VideoMode_YCoordShift. Gau_EnergyMeterWidget runs it on the .GAU block at +0x224 (the panel and its one child).

entries.name: MFDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: MFDisplay constructor (vtable 0049cfbc, RTTI name 'MFDisplay', 0x10 bytes): stores its argument at +4 and clears +0xc. The five MFD screen constructors (MfdStatusScreen_Ctor, MfdRadarScreen_Ctor, MfdFlashCommScreen_Ctor, MfdMissileViewScreen_Ctor, MfdMapScreen_Ctor) start with it.

entries.name: Cockpit_GetMfd_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Cockpit_GetMfd and returns its result (the decompile drops it). MfdRadarScreen_Update and MfdFlashCommScreen_DrawRowPlate use it.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the multi-function display. Lazily loads three sprite banks -- `mfd` (DAT_0049cbcc), `mfd_dmg` (DAT_0049cbd4) and `radar` -- each selecting folder "hba"/"dba" off DAT_004d25f0.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Repaint
entries.description: Full MFD repaint, in order: mode buttons 0-5, the screen background, all visible buttons 0-12, the current screen's paint slot, then the title from DAT_004d13e0[mode]. Background frame is a bare switch on the mode over the `mfd` bank's frame-pointer array: modes 0/1/4 take element 1, mode 3 element 2, modes 2/5 take literal 0 and skip the blit. Frame 0 is never used as a background. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Update
entries.description: MFD per-frame update. While the power-up is armed and not done (+0x8c/+0x8d) on the scanner (mode 3) it starts, then steps, the dish animation's SpriteSequence at +0x331 and returns; the pass after it ends sets done, and the next frees the sequencer and the radar bank. On another screen done comes once the coarse tick passes +0x345. Then dispatches the current screen's update slot via +0xcd + mode*4, refreshes the title for modes 2 and 5, and when a transmission is active draws the speaking pilot's frames at inset+(0x14,0) and fills the message label at +0x329. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButton_OnClick
entries.description: MFD button dispatch: finds the clicked button's index in the +0x18 array, then switches on it. Indices 0-5 call MfdDisplay_SetMode(i) -- this is what makes mode index = F-key - 1. Index 11 (PASS) and 12 (ACTIVE) set the radar-mode flag at CockpitViewInstance+0x203's +0x96 to 0/1 and swap which of the two lights. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_KeyDispatch
entries.description: MFDGauge vtable +0x0c (0049cfa0), (display, key): returns 0 while the display's rect (+0xeb) is off screen. Keys 0x20, 0x2d, 0x213 and 0x214 press children 7, 10, 8 and 9 when the current page's row of the table at 0049cbdf (13 bytes a page) enables them -- 0x213 cycles the scanner range with MfdDisplay_CycleScannerRange where it does not; on page 1, 0x34 and 0x33 run 00447014 and 00447048 and 0x1e/0x22/0x23/0x18/0x12 or 0x2e/0x21 pick rows 0-5 with MfdFlashComm_SelectRow. Returns 1 for a key it handled, 0 otherwise. HddDisplay_KeyDispatch is the Heads-Down Display's.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_HandleAltKey
entries.description: (mfd, code): FLASH COMM's [Alt] order keys, offered every code before the MFD's own command slot. For 0x21e, 0x222, 0x223, 0x218, 0x221 ([Alt]+A G H O F) it selects row 0, 1, 2, 3 or 5 through 0043f9b8 on the comm screen (+0xd1), transmits (MfdFlashComm_Transmit) and selects the row again (MfdFlashComm_SelectRow); 0x22e and 0x212 ([Alt]+C, E) select row 4 and transmit only when MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb is 4 or 7 respectively. Returns 1 for those seven codes, 0 for any other. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetDropoutRanges
entries.description: Picks the MFD's sensor-dropout set by condition ([0,1,2,2,2] at 0049cb34): sequencer 004d1d0c[set], sequences set*2 and set*2+1, and the spell ranges from 0049cb94/cba0/cbac/cbb8. Each sequencer's set holds one sequence, so SpriteSequence_Select refuses both numbers for sets 1 and 2 and the sequencer plays the one it was built with both ways.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_CycleMode
entries.description: (mfd): MfdDisplay_SetMode(mfd, (+0xc1 + 1) wrapped at 6). Sim_PollPlayerInput's command 0xe calls it on CockpitViewInstance+0x1ed.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetMode
entries.description: Switches the MFD to a screen (0-5, = F-key - 1). Lights button `mode` and unlights the previous via their +0x40 flag, stores the mode at +0xc1, then walks the 6x13 visibility table at 0049cbd8 for buttons 6-12 showing/hiding each. Gau_MfdPanelWidget calls it with 3 (SCANNER) at build time, which is what a cockpit powers up on. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: Cockpit_CycleTarget
entries.description: TargetSelect_Cycle(CockpitViewInstance). MfdButton_OnClick's SELECT/TARGET case calls it in every mode but 0.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_StepStatusSubject
entries.description: (mfd): increments the status screen's subject cursor +0x318, wrapping to 0 at the count +0x31c. MfdButton_OnClick's SELECT/TARGET case calls it in mode 0.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_CycleScannerRange
entries.description: The SCANNER screen's RANGE button: steps MfdDisplay+0xc5 and wraps at 3, then MfdDisplay_SetScannerRange installs MfdScannerRanges[index] at MfdDisplay+0xbd. Stepping outwards from the default index 2 means the first press goes from 1200 m to 300 m.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetScannerRange
entries.description: (mfd, index): when index differs from +0xc5, stores it there and MfdScannerRanges[index] at +0xbd. MfdDisplay_CycleScannerRange calls it.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_NextAvailableRow
entries.description: (display) steps display+0xb1 forward with wrap 5->0, skipping rows whose state byte has bit 0, then MfdDisplay_SetSharedRow. The . key (0x34) via MfdDisplay_KeyDispatch.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_PrevAvailableRow
entries.description: (display) as MfdFlashComm_NextAvailableRow but backwards, wrapping 0->5. The , key (0x33) via MfdDisplay_KeyDispatch.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetSharedRow
entries.description: (display, row): stores row at display+0xb1, the first int of the screen-shared state block, when it differs from what is there. Direct callers: MfdFlashComm_SelectRow, MfdFlashComm_HandleListClick, 00447014 and 00447048.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_HandleListClick
entries.description: Resolves a click on the MFD's screen area to a FLASH COMM row. Returns at once unless the display is on mode 1, then walks the six row label rects in index order -- inclusive on all four edges -- and stops at the first hit. Rows are built top..top+14 and stepped by 14, so adjacent rows share a line and the first-match walk gives it to the upper one. A hit on the row already selected presses XMIT and transmits; any other row is selected.

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_SelectRow
entries.description: (display, widget, row): only when widget is the display's base panel widget (+0xfb) and the current mode (+0xc1) is 1, FLASH COMM, stores row as the display's shared selected row through MfdDisplay_SetSharedRow and sets the byte at +0xe6, FLASH COMM's entry in the per-screen byte array at +0xe5 + mode. Both keyboard handlers pass the display's own +0xfb, so the mode test is the one that can refuse: 004469c0 for the plain hotkeys and 00446c10 for the [Alt] ones after it has transmitted. See docs/formats/mfd.md#keyboard.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 00447130; docs/formats/mfd.md#keyboard

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SyncMissileCamMode
entries.description: (mfd): switches the MFD to mode 5 (MISSILE CAM) and back while an electro-optical launcher is armed: the condition is that CockpitView_FindArmedMountGauge(CockpitViewInstance) returns a gauge for which WeaponGauge_MountProjectileType is 0 (Rocket) and WeaponGauge_MountProjectileSubtype is 3. When it holds and g_MfdMissileCamMode is -1: with g_MfdMissileCamArmed set it saves the current mode (+0xc1) in g_MfdMissileCamSavedMode and MfdDisplay_SetMode(5); either way g_MfdMissileCamMode becomes 5 and the flag is set. When it no longer holds and g_MfdMissileCamMode is not -1, MfdDisplay_SetMode(saved mode) and the flag is set. MfdDisplay_SetMode clears both whenever it changes the mode with g_MfdMissileCamMode not -1, so a mode chosen by hand while the condition holds stays until the condition ends, when the saved mode is restored over it; a saved mode equal to the current one changes nothing and leaves the switch held. MfdDisplay_Update calls it, and while g_MfdMissileCamMode is not -1 draws no transmission. See docs/formats/mfd.md, 'Modes'.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00447164 and MfdDisplay_SetMode's writes at 00446e8e-00446e98

entries.name: MfdFlashComm_Transmit
entries.description: The FLASH COMM page's XMIT widget: resolves the selected row to a verb through MfdFlashComm_SelectedVerb, writes it into the shared order record at DAT_004d0458 and broadcasts it through Squad_BroadcastOrderFromCockpit. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] only.

entries.name: MFDSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for MFDSelectGadget, the MFD's momentary leaf button (object size 0x40, indices 7-10). Three levels over Widget_CtorRect ending at vtable 0049cf60, whose slot 0 is MfdButton_SetCaption; leaves slot +8 as the inherited Widget_ForwardClickToOwner, so it has no lit flag and shows only the shared press state. The class name is its own, from the descriptor record at 00447a6f. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButton_SetCaption
entries.description: Sets one MFD button's caption from its index at +0x28: for index < 6 it composes "F1"-"F6" on the stack from the two-byte literal at 0049cea3 ("Fx") with '1'+index written over the second byte -- the six mode captions are not stored as strings. For index >= 6 it takes DAT_004d13e0[index] from STRINGS0.STR group 5. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MFDSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: MFDSelectGadgetVtable +0x0c: the same body as MFDStateGadget_FlushDeferredPaint.

entries.name: MFDStateGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for MFDStateGadget, the MFD's latching leaf button (object size 0x41, indices 0-5, 11 and 12, plus 6 by falling through the ctor switch). Four levels over Widget_CtorRect ending at vtable 0049cf20, whose slot 0 is MfdButton_Repaint; overrides slot +8 with 004474a8, which refuses a press while the +0x40 lit flag is already set, sets it, forwards to the owner, repaints and sounds the click. The class name is its own, from the descriptor record at 00447a17. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MFDStateGadget_OnClick
entries.description: MFDStateGadgetVtable +0x08 (gadget, flags): PanelStateGadget_OnClick's body, but only while the state byte +0x40 is 0, so a click latches it on and never off.

entries.name: MfdButton_Repaint
entries.description: Repaints one MFD button and re-fonts its caption: buttons 0-5 and 11-12 take ColorSchemePanels[12] DARK when the +0x40 lit flag is set and [10] WHITE when clear, which is why the selected F-key reads dark-on-green. Caption text is resolved the same way as MfdButton_SetCaption. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MFDStateGadget_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: MFDStateGadgetVtable +0x0c: steps the pending-paint count at +0x1f -- at 1, Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, gadget, 0); at 2, slot 0 of the vtable at +0x17 -- decrementing it either way.

entries.name: MFDListGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for MFDListGadget (object size 0x28), the MFD's screen-content click region, registered by MfdDisplay_Ctor after the 13 buttons. Derives from PanelListGadget. Class name from the descriptor record at 004479d3.

entries.name: MFDListGadget_OnClick
entries.description: The MFD screen-area gadget's vtable +8. Left button only; calls MfdFlashComm_HandleListClick(owner, self, &DAT_004d1e67), the owner taken from the gadget's own +0x24. The mirror of HDDListGadget_OnClick.
entries.signature: void __cdecl MFDListGadget_OnClick(int gadget, unsigned char buttonFlags)

entries.name: MfdGau_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: Coordinate-shifts the MFD's .GAU block at offset 728 in place before MfdDisplay_Ctor reads it: 13 consecutive rects from int index 4 (file offset 744), then the panel rect at int index 0x38 (file offset 952). The 13 rects are zero in all nine retail .GAU files and no constructor reads them; only the panel rect is live. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: Cockpit_GetMfd
entries.description: Returns CockpitViewInstance+0x1ed, the cockpit's MFD widget.

entries.name: MFDSelectGadget_Dtor
entries.description: MFDSelectGadget's destructor (class record 00447a6f): (gadget, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, PanelSelectGadget_Dtor(gadget, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00447b21; class record at 00447a6f

entries.name: MFDStateGadget_Dtor
entries.description: MFDStateGadget's destructor (class record 00447a17): (gadget, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, PanelSelectGadget_Dtor(gadget, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00447b4e; class record at 00447a17

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the throttle slider gauge. Lazily loads the `throttle` sprite bank into DAT_0049cfc4, folder selected by DAT_004d25bb == 3 choosing "hba" over "dba". Reads CockpitViewInstance and its own .GAU track rect. Bank frame 0 is a 2px tick, frame 1 the knob.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_Paint
entries.description: ThrottleGauge vtable +0x04 (0049d1e0): paints its child (+0x18, the slider) through slot +0x00 of its table at +0x17, then Bitmap_Blit(**(DAT_0049cfc4+8), gauge+0xc2, 0).

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_Update
entries.description: ThrottleGauge vtable +0x08 (0049d1e0): runs its child's slot +0x0c (FlushDeferredPaint).

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_SetValues
entries.description: Writes the gauge's live value pair at +0xb1 from a caller struct of two ints: [0] speed as a Q10 fraction of max, [1] throttle Q10 +/-0x400. Pushes the throttle down to the slider child's set-value slot (+0x14) when it changed, and marks the child dirty (+0x1f = 2) when the speed fraction changed. Called once a frame by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_GetValues
entries.description: Returns gauge + 0xb1, the speedFraction/throttle int pair. Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate reads [1] (gauge+0xb5) into mech+0x290 unless the mech+0x93 dirty flag says input moved the throttle this frame, in which case it pushes the other way. That arbitration is the whole of the two-way binding between the slider and the keyboard.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_OnChildValue
entries.description: Gauge slot 0: a child reporting a value. Finds the child in the gauge's array (+0x18, count +0x68); index 0 is the slider, and its value is negated when the gauge's +0xc1 is 0 (the vertical variant) before being stored to +0xb5. That negation cancels SliderWidget_GetValueV's own inversion, leaving positive = forward = knob up.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_CtorV
entries.description: The throttle's vertical slider child, built when .GAU offset 1064 (SLIDE_DIR) == 1 -- the case all 9 retail .GAU files use. Knob spans the track's full width with its height from throttle bank frame 1 (28x12), limits +/-0x400 at +0x24/+0x26, and an initial position centred on the track (knobBottom = trackBottom - (trackHeight - knobHeight)/2), which is the manual's centred-is-stopped detent. Also constructs the two LED fill bars from .GAU ints [8..11] and [12..15] into private fields +0x7e and +0x82 -- it never registers them as children, and nothing ever paints them (see LedBarGraph_CtorV).

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_DrawKnobV
entries.description: ThrottleVSliderGadget vtable +0x00 (0049d12c): when the slider is on screen, places the knob rect from the knob position (+0x28/+0x2c), points the raster source page at the draw page, saves the screen under the knob (offset by the canvas origin) into +0x52 with Region_Save, blits the knob bitmap (+0x4e) mirrored (flag 2) when the knob sits right of 160 << XCoordShift, and records the knob rect at +0x6e/+0x72. ThrottleSlider_PaintV is the table's +0x0c.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_PaintV
entries.description: Vertical throttle slider paint. Copies the gauge's +0xb1 speed fraction into +0x7a/+0x4a and does nothing further with it, reads the two LED fill bars' rects only to widen the invalidated region handed to FUN_0043122c, then blits the knob at its current height. It never draws either bar -- see LedBarGraph_CtorV.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_OnValue
entries.description: Throttle slider commit slot (vtable +8). Notifies the parent gauge via VSliderGadget_OnClick (which dispatches the owner's slot 0 = ThrottleGauge_OnChildValue, then repaints), then sets ThrottleLeverMode (0049a06e) from the sign of the committed value -- but gated on a joystick throttle control being configured AND assigned to THROTTLE in preferences, so it is inert on a keyboard/mouse setup.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_CtorFixed
entries.description: The SLIDE_DIR != 1 throttle slider variant: a fixed 12px-wide knob centred horizontally and spanning the track's full height. No retail .GAU selects it (all 9 hold 1 at offset 1064), so this branch is never exercised by retail data and its behaviour is unverified.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_PaintH
entries.description: Slot 0 (Paint) of ThrottleHSliderGadgetVtable, the class ThrottleSlider_CtorFixed builds and no retail .GAU selects. When CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes: sets the knob's x span +0x2e/+0x36 from the int16 position +0x28 and width +0x2c, points the current display's draw page (+0x38) at its visible page (+0x3c), records the knob rect offset by the render context's +0x220/+0x224 in the region at +0x5a and saves the pixels under it into +0x52 (Region_Save), Bitmap_Blit's the knob bitmap +0x4e at +0x2e and keeps that position at +0x6e/+0x72.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_FlushPaintH
entries.description: Slot 0xc (FlushDeferredPaint) of ThrottleHSliderGadgetVtable. At +0x1f == 2 and when CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes: Region_Restore's the pixels saved under the knob's previous position (+0x6e), copies the gauge's +0xb1 into +0x7a/+0x4a, repaints the knob as ThrottleSlider_PaintH does, then Widget_DrawToCockpit(1, rect) over the union of the knob's old and new rects and the two LED bars' rects (+0x7e, +0x82), and clears +0x1f.

entries.name: GauThrottle_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the three 16-byte rects after it by VideoMode_XCoordShift / VideoMode_YCoordShift. Gau_ThrottleWidget runs it on the .GAU block at +1000.

entries.name: VSliderGadget_InvalidateDeferred
entries.description: PanelVSliderGadget vtable +0x04 (0049d19c), kept by ThrottleVSliderGadget: this->[0x1f] = 2, the vertical slider's copy of Widget_InvalidateDeferred. HSliderGadget_InvalidateDeferred is the horizontal one.

entries.name: PanelVSliderGadget_Dtor
entries.description: PanelVSliderGadget's destructor (class record 00448b9a): (slider, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, PanelSliderGadget_Dtor(slider+0x3e, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00448c0c; class record at 00448b9a

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_DtorV
entries.description: ThrottleVSliderGadget's destructor (class record 00448ab2), ThrottleSlider_CtorV's object: (slider, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, PanelSliderGadget_Dtor(slider+0x3e, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00448c3c; class record at 00448ab2

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_DtorFixed
entries.description: ThrottleHSliderGadget's destructor (class record 00448a52), ThrottleSlider_CtorFixed's object: (slider, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, PanelSliderGadget_Dtor(slider+0x3e, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00448c74; class record at 00448a52

entries.name: HDDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: HDDisplay constructor (vtable 0049d668, RTTI name 'HDDisplay', 0x10 bytes): stores its two arguments at +4 and +8. HddCommandScreen_Ctor and HddDamageScreen_Ctor run it first.

entries.name: HddDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: HDDisplay constructor, .GAU offset 1212 (PHDD.CPP). Reads the block's origin, four region rects (+0xc1 screen, +0xe1 order column, +0xd1 damage column, +0xf1 title indicator), 15 widget rects and 3 comm-box marker rects; loads the 'static' and 'hdd' sprite banks and the 'hddclip' clip region; builds both page objects (+0x101 command display, +0x105 damage detail), the title label (+0x51b) and three 0x14e-byte comm gauges; ends with HddDisplay_SetPage(obj, 0).

entries.name: HddDisplay_Repaint
entries.description: Whole-display paint: every visible widget, then the current page object's paint, then the title indicator rect (+0xf1, colour id 13 or -- while +0x51f is set, which the constructor does -- id 15), then HddDisplay_SetTitle, then the three comm gauges. A gauge slot with no squadmate in it is flooded with colour id 19 inset one device pixel instead.

entries.name: HddDisplay_Update
entries.description: Heads-Down Display per-frame update: records the selected target for the damage page, runs HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress, then (outside the external view) the sensor dropout with the PanelGauge_Ctor default ranges and no sequencer, flagging the current page for a full repaint when +0x76 changes, then the widgets' and the page's updates. It also sets the comms-out latch (gauge +0x147) of every destroyed squadmate while the view manager's transition flag +0x1c is set and its view +0x14 is 4, and forces every destroyed, latched comm box to state 1.

entries.name: HddDisplay_RepaintPage
entries.description: (display): saves the render context, sets the current page object's +0xc to the signed byte display+0xb0, runs the page's slot 0 (its Repaint -- HddCommandScreen_Repaint on the command page), decrements display+0xb0 and restores the context. HddDisplay_Repaint runs it after the page's Show, and HddDisplay_Update before HddDisplay_SetTitle.

entries.name: HddDisplay_PaintCurrentScreen
entries.description: (hdd): saves the current render context (006c5ff4, 0x81 dwords plus +0x208), hands the current screen (+0x101 array at index +0x109) the paint countdown +0xb0 at its +0xc, calls its vtable slot 1, decrements +0xb0, and restores the context. HddDisplay_Update calls it.

entries.name: HddDisplay_KeyDispatch
entries.description: Heads-Down Display key handler. The arrows, [-]/[=] and keypad -/+, and [1]-[3] press widgets 2-7 and 10-12 through Widget_PressChild, so they share the buttons' dark-state hold; [S]/[I]/[W] set the damage page directly; anything else goes to the current page's own dispatch (vtable +0x10).

entries.name: HddDisplay_OnChildClick
entries.description: HDDGauge vtable +0x00 (0049d64c), (display, child): finds child among the +0x68 children listed from +0x18 and stores its index in the byte +0x528.

entries.name: HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress
entries.description: The heads-down display's widget-press dispatch, switched on the pressed-widget index at display+0x528 and clearing it to 0xff on the way out. Cases 0-1 pick the page, 2-7 the four map pans and the two zooms on page 0 and the damage screen's subject and category steps on page 1, 10-12 select a comm box, 13 is XMIT -- HddCommandScreen_CommitPick, HddCommandScreen_FillOrderRecord, Squad_SendOrderToSlot -- and 14 is CANCEL. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] only.

entries.name: HddDisplay_SetPage
entries.description: Switches the display between its two pages (0 = command display [F7], 1 = damage detail [F8]): unlights the old page button, hides the old page object, shows the new one, lights its button, then applies the 2x15 widget visibility table at HddPageWidgetVisibility -- a 0 moves a widget at state 0 to 2, the value HddButton_Paint refuses to draw at, and a 1 moves one at state 2 back to 0.

entries.name: HddDisplay_SetTitle
entries.description: Fills the title label (+0x51b) from STRINGS0 group 11 entry 0 ('MAP') on page 0, or group 12 indexed by the damage screen's current category (' STRUCT DAMAGE' / ' INTERN DAMAGE' / ' WEAPON DAMAGE') on page 1.

entries.name: HddDisplay_SelectPilot
entries.description: Selects one of the three squad comm boxes (widgets 10-12): unlights the previous, records it at +0x52b, stores the new index at +0x517, lights its widget, sends the pilot a select message, and tells the command screen.

entries.name: HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames
entries.description: HDDGauge frame loader (PHDD.CPP). Builds the resource name `pilot<n>` with _itoa, loads its .OFS animation-offset table (27 entries), then loads the matching sprite bank from folder "dba". Emits the literal errors "HDDGauge::Couldn't load anim offset" / "...bitmap array".

entries.name: HddGauge_ConditionIndex
entries.description: Averages a mech's 19 structural damage bytes into a 0-100 integrity percentage and buckets it into the five STRINGS0 group 28 conditions at 90 / 74 / 51 / 1 -- OK, SHIELDS DN, INT DAMAGE, CRITICAL, DESTROYED.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintIdle
entries.description: Paints one squad comm box while its pilot is not broadcasting: floods the video area with colour id 19 and fills five labels -- the pilot's name, 'STATUS:', the condition from STRINGS0 group 28, 'OBJECTIVE:', and the pilot's current order from group 40. Matches the manual's 'their video box remains darkened, displaying only their name, their status, and their current orders'. Defers to HddGauge_PaintStatic when the pilot's comms are out.

entries.name: CommBox_BeginMessage
entries.description: Builds the two filenames for one comm message and acquires a speech slot. suffix = '_' + 2-digit message id + 3-digit variant; the wav is 'P' + voiceBank + suffix in simvoice/simvoicf/simvoicg, the script 'P' + ('A' + squadSlot) + suffix in snc/. voiceBank is (slot >> 2) + 1 with 3 remapped to 4, so twelve squad slots share three recorded voices P1_/P2_/P4_ -- the same grouping as str\\PILOT0/1/2/4.STR.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame
entries.description: Draws one frame of a talking pilot into a comm box: floods it with colour id 19, blits the requested frame of the pilot<n> bank at that frame's own .OFS offset pair, and refreshes the name label.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintScream
entries.description: The comm box's picture for message 0x25 (the death scream), in place of the .SNC frames: portrait frame 0x1b until the deadline +0x143 passes, then HddGauge_PaintStatic until it passes again, flipping the phase byte +0x148; each flip sets a new deadline max(5, Math_RandomBelow(0x14)) coarse ticks on. +0x149 holds the previous phase.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintStatic
entries.description: Draws the next of the 'static' bank's five frames into a comm box and advances the cycle -- the manual's 'the video box goes to static and you can send them no messages'.

entries.name: CommBox_OnMessageBegin
entries.description: The pilot/squad port's begin callback, installed through MessagePort_AddBeginCallback. Starts that speaker's .wav and .SNC portrait and plays the whitenz static under it.

entries.name: CommBox_OnMessageEnd
entries.description: The matching end hook for CommBox_OnMessageBegin.

entries.name: HddDisplay_ServiceCommBoxes
entries.description: (hdd): Snc_ServiceQueue, then the state machine of each of the three comm boxes (stride 0x14e from +0x12d), and drops the MFD's published block (+0x766 of 0049d230) when its box is idle or comms-out. Called by HddDisplay_Update each frame and by CommBox_OnMessageBegin. See docs/formats/heads-down-display.md.

entries.name: CommBox_PushVideoClip
entries.description: Pushes a render context clipped to a comm box's video rect (box+0x1d..+0x29), translated out of the current context's origin and the heads-down pan, so a portrait taller than its box is cut off at the bezel. CommBox_PopVideoClip takes it back off.

entries.name: CommBox_PopVideoClip
entries.description: Pops the render context CommBox_PushVideoClip installed.

entries.name: HddGauge_Name
entries.description: Returns comm-box gauge `slot`'s name pointer (+0x137), the one HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames filled by walking PILOTS.STR to the machine's pilot index. The display argument is ignored: the gauge vector is reached through the global at 0049d230 instead.

entries.name: HddDisplay_NextSubject
entries.description: Steps the damage detail's subject selector (display+0x55c, a short) forward: 5 wraps to 0, and a slot whose machine pointer in the +0x534 array is null is skipped by recursing, except slot 4 (the target), which is a stop empty or not. Returns the new slot's machine. Reached from HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress's arrow-right (5) case on page 1, which stores the result at +0x524.

entries.name: HddDisplay_PrevSubject
entries.description: Steps the damage detail's subject selector (display+0x55c) back: below 0 wraps to 4 (the target) without testing it; otherwise a slot whose machine pointer in the +0x534 array is null is skipped by recursing. Returns the new slot's machine. Reached from HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress's arrow-left (4) case on page 1, which stores the result at +0x524.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_SetSubjectCaption
entries.description: Sets the damage screen's subject caption from the display's five-entry name array at +0x548 (the player's 'YOU', three squadmate names, then 'TARGET') indexed by the subject selector at +0x55c. The player draws in ColorSchemePanels[3] on colour id 6, a squadmate in [2] on HudColorTable_Get(slot) (ids 12, 15, 26), and the target in [2] on id 15.

entries.name: Sim_SetCommBox0PilotOverride
entries.description: (n): stores CommBox0PilotOverride (0049d248). Sim_ParseCommandLine passes the _atol of the -t argument.

entries.name: HddButton_Ctor
entries.description: One HDDisplay sub-widget: rect at [0..3], owning display at param_1[9], index at param_1[10], label at param_1[0xb], unlit/lit frames at param_1[0xc]/[0xd], visibility state at +0x1b (2 = hidden), lit flag at +0x40.

entries.name: HddButton_Paint
entries.description: Paints one HDDisplay sub-widget, gated on state +0x1b < 2. The frame index differs by case, which is what makes some of these buttons latching and others momentary: indices 0/1 (the F7/F8 page buttons) take the frame from the object's own selection flag +0x40 and caption themselves 'F7'/'F8' from the shared 'Fx' literal at 0049d4f5 in ColorSchemePanels[12] selected / [10] not -- they have no pressed state; 2-7 (four arrows, two map magnifiers) take the frame from the shared press byte +0x1b and so light only while held; 10-12 fill the selected comm box's marker rect; 13/14 blit the plate and caption XMIT/CANCEL from STRINGS0 group 9, both frame and font indexed by that same press byte (ColorSchemePanels[4 + pressed]).

entries.name: HddButton_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: HDDSelectGadget vtable +0x0c (0049d60c): while the button is on screen, at stage 2 (+0x1f) repaints it through its own slot +0x00; at stage 1 repaints buttons 10-12 (index +0x28) the same way and copies any other to the cockpit with Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, button); decrements the stage either way.

entries.name: HddButton_OnClick
entries.description: HDDSelectGadget vtable +0x08 (0049d60c), (button, value): unless the button is lit (+0x40) and is button 0 or 1 (+0x28), toggles the lit byte, calls the owning display's (+0x24) slot +0x00 with (display, button, value), invalidates itself (slot +0x04) and runs its PanelGadget mixin's (+0x20) slot +0x08, the click sound. So buttons 0 and 1 latch on.
