Of keys 8-13 only the first held key counts, into the second pair at 004d244d/004d2451. Each entry comes from the table at 0049eb6d, shifted left 7 (+/-0x80). That table is filled at startup by the static initialiser at 0045b888. The pairs are sources, not destinations: Input_BuildSourceTable registers them alongside the joystick axes in the source-pointer table at 004d2394, and the binding config chooses which source each game axis reads.

entries.name: Input_BuildSourceTable
entries.description: Input-system init. Populates the source-pointer table at 004d2394 with the address of every available input value -- the two keyboard axis pairs Input_BuildKeyboardAxes writes, the four joystick axes at DAT_004d2414+0x0d/0x11/0x15/0x19, and the buttons -- so that a key or axis binding is a choice of pointer rather than a hardcoded path. This indirection is why Sim_PollPlayerInput reads some axes through a pointer-to-pointer.

entries.name: Input_BuildPlayerDevice
entries.description: The per-frame input build: reads the twelve controls-block bytes at ControlsOptionBase and routes the joystick's four normalised axes, hat and eight buttons into the device struct at DAT_004d234a that Sim_PollPlayerInput consumes. Each axis row's byte selects a DESTINATION pair (0 unassigned, 1 the movement pair, 2 the turret pair), not a source; a control whose destination is taken falls to a second rank that wins when both have moved, and the keyboard pairs are the last fallback. Also: pulls the first FIRE-bound button of the walker's block out to +0x0d and zeroes its byte (using a hardcoded 0x11 rather than ControlsOptionBase+4, so a RAZOR finds its trigger through the walker's block), applies the press-once button latch Input_LatchButton sets, writes the hat over the turret pair at 0xc0 under HAT=2, and applies keyjoy.cfg's Backturn and Rudder reversals. It also owns the command queue at DAT_004d2148: it drains each code through Sim_DispatchCommand after masking with DAT_0049eae0 = 0x47ff (which discards the Shift bank, folding a shifted key onto the plain one) and then resets the count. It is the input-tape record and playback point too -- see docs/formats/tap-input-tape.md.

entries.name: SimInput_SetEnabled
entries.description: Toggles the simulator's keyboard input on and off. Turning it on registers two subscribers with KeyListener_Register: Input_KeyjoyAxisKey against the 30-byte list at 0049eb33 and SimCommandQueue_Push against the 7-byte list at 0049eb5d. Turning it off clears the three 15-byte key-state blocks at DAT_004d2418.

entries.name: Input_LatchButton
entries.description: Marks one of the eight joystick buttons as acted on: sets DAT_004d237a[i] and stores the state to suppress at DAT_004d2382[i]. FUN_0045a7f4 then forces that button's byte to zero on every following tick until the player releases it, which is the whole of the press-once rule. Sim_PollPlayerInput calls it for every button whose action it dispatches.

entries.name: Input_GetCursorPos
entries.description: Returns &Input_CursorPos (004d238a). Cockpit_PickEdgeCursor reads the cursor from it during TapePlayback.

entries.name: Mouse_FitBoundsToDisplay
entries.description: Reads the bounds of the driver 0045c23c returns, sets x1 and y1 to the current display's width and height (GLDisplay_GetAttribute 0 and 1) less one, and writes them back with MouseDriver_SetBounds. Does nothing when 0045c23c returns 0.

entries.name: Keyjoy_LoadConfig
entries.description: Reads data\keyjoy.cfg once at input init: four GetPrivateProfileStringA calls against section [Keyjoy] for Tilt, Backturn, Missile and Rudder, each a case-insensitive compare against the word Reverse setting DAT_0049eab8/eabc/eac0/eac4. Anything else, the shipped Default included, leaves the flag clear. DBSIM's only profile import is GetPrivateProfileStringA.

entries.name: Input_InitKeyboardAxisTable
entries.description: Static initialiser (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b64, priority 0x20) that writes the 28-byte (dx,dy) table KeyboardAxisDeltas (0049eb6d) read by Input_BuildKeyboardAxes. Ghidra has no function here (gap 0045b888-0045ba8c).

entries.name: Input_PollDeviceBlock
entries.description: Zeroes the 0x29-byte device block at 004d247a and refills it from each registered device: the keyboard (kind 1) through Input_ReadKeyboardCommand into the head word, bits 12 and 13 then cleared; the joystick (kind 3) through 0045c528 and 0045bbf4 into +0x0d..+0x28; the mouse (kind 2) through Input_ReadMouseState into the two ints at +2 and +6 and the bytes +0xa/+0xb/+0xc from button bits 0/1/2. Returns the block. Input_BuildSourceTable stores the pointer at 004d2414.

entries.name: Input_ReadKeyboardCommand
entries.description: (out, kind): for kind 1 with the keyboard device enabled, stores Input_ReadDeviceEvent's next code at out; returns 0 only when the device is disabled. Any other kind writes nothing and returns 1. Input_PollDeviceBlock fills the device block's head word with it, and Input_BuildPlayerDevice calls it.

entries.name: Input_ReadJoystickState
entries.description: (out, kind): for kind 3 or 4, takes the device in Input_DeviceTable[kind] less 0x1f; when it is enabled and its vtable (+0x24) slot 1 returns a record, copies 0x1d bytes of it into out. Returns 0 when the device is disabled or gives no record, 1 otherwise (other kinds write nothing). Input_PollDeviceBlock reads the joystick (kind in 004d2528) through it. The shape of Input_ReadMouseState.

entries.name: Input_ReadMouseState
entries.description: (out, kind): for kind 2 with the mouse device enabled, copies the {int, int, int16 buttons} record 0045c22c returns into out and caches it at 004d24a3; when 0045c22c returns null it copies the cached record instead. Returns 0 only when the device is disabled; for any other kind it writes nothing and returns 1.

entries.name: Input_EnableDevice
entries.description: (device): finds device among the nine entries of Input_DeviceTable and runs InputDevice_Enable on it; 0 when it is not registered.

entries.name: Input_DisableDevice
entries.description: (device): finds device among the nine entries of Input_DeviceTable and runs InputDevice_Disable on it.

entries.name: Input_GetKeyboardDevice_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Input_GetKeyboardDevice and returns its result (the decompile drops it). SimInput_SetEnabled tests it for nonzero.

entries.name: Input_GetMouseDevice_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Input_GetMouseDevice and returns its result. CockpitMouse_Init registers its listener on the device it returns; Gau_RovingGunsightWidget, AlertPanel_SetFocus and 00459cd8 test it for nonzero.

entries.name: InputDevice_Register
entries.description: (device, kind, slot): the input-device base: stores kind at device+1, slot in Input_DeviceTable[kind] (004d24ec) and clears the kind's enabled byte (004d2510 + kind). Kind 0 and 1 store the kind at 004d251c and 004d2520. Kind 2 (mouse) and 3 (joystick) first disable whichever device of that kind is already registered, then store the kind at 004d2524 or 004d2528 -- the nonzero 'one is registered' tests Input_GetMouseDevice and the device poll make. Returns device.

entries.name: InputDevice_Enable
entries.description: (device): for kind 2 or 3, disables the registered device of that kind when there is one and re-records the kind at 004d2524/004d2528; then sets device+0 = 1 and the kind's enabled byte at 004d2510. Input_BuildSourceTable enables the keyboard and mouse devices through it, Joystick_InitAndSeedBindings the joystick.

entries.name: InputDevice_Disable
entries.description: (device): clears device+0 and the kind's enabled byte at 004d2510 + device+1.

entries.name: InputDevice_IsEnabled
entries.description: (device): returns the enabled byte at device+0.

entries.name: Input_DeviceSlot
entries.description: (index): returns the input device pointer at Input_DeviceTable + index * 4. Input_GetDevice reads the table through it.

entries.name: Input_GetKeyboardDevice
entries.description: Returns Input_DeviceTable[the keyboard's kind at 004d2520] less 4, or 0 when 004d2520 says none is registered. The keyboard twin of Input_GetMouseDevice.

entries.name: Input_GetMouseDevice
entries.description: Returns the registered mouse device -- Input_DeviceTable[2] less 0x3a, the offset of its InputDevice sub-object -- or 0 when 004d2524 says none is registered. AlertPanel_Leave calls it directly.

entries.name: Input_IsKindEnabled
entries.description: (kind): returns the enabled byte at 004d2510 + kind.

entries.name: KeyboardInputDevice_Ctor
entries.description: (this, arg): runs KeyboardDriver_Ctor(this, arg), registers the InputDevice sub-object at this+4 as kind 1, stores arg at +9 and clears +0xd. Input_BuildSourceTable constructs it with 0x10000.

entries.name: Input_ReadDeviceEvent
entries.description: Pops one code from the unclaimed-key ring at 006bb734 for a keyboard device, draining the rest when the device asks for it. This is the route a code takes when no Key_WndProcHook subscriber claimed it.

entries.name: MouseInputDevice_Ctor
entries.description: (this): runs MouseDriver_Ctor, then registers the InputDevice sub-object at this+0x3a as kind 2 with InputDevice_Register. Input_BuildSourceTable constructs it.

entries.name: MouseInputDevice_Dtor
entries.description: (this, flags): clears the enabled byte of the kind at this+0x3b, clears 004d2524 when that kind is the registered mouse, runs MouseDriver_Dtor and frees the object when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: MouseInputDevice_GetState
entries.description: (device): MouseDriver_GetState(); device is passed on and not read. Input_ReadMouseState copies the record it returns.

entries.name: Input_GetMouseDeviceUnchecked
entries.description: Input_DeviceTable[2] less 0x3a, or 0 when the slot is empty -- Input_GetMouseDevice without its 004d2524 registration test. Mouse_FitBoundsToDisplay calls it.

entries.name: JoystickDevice_Ctor
entries.description: Constructs the joystick input device: base ctor JoystickDevice_CtorBase (which enumerates and sets the resolution field +0x16 to 7), registers it in the device table as kind 3, installs vtable PTR_FUN_0049ec9c at +0x24 and stores the response-curve selector at +0x28. Its one caller FUN_00459dd4 passes (3, 0x201, 0xf, 1).

entries.name: JoystickDevice_Dtor
entries.description: IMJoystick vtable +0x00 (0049ec9c, the table at +0x24 of the joystick device JoystickDevice_Ctor builds), the destructor its class record names: (device, flags). Reinstalls that table, clears its slot in the device table DAT_004d2510 (index +0x20) and DAT_004d2528 when that holds the same index, runs DVJoystick's destructor (00477524) with flags 0, and Mem_Deletes on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0045c2c4; class record at 0045c537

entries.name: Joystick_ReadWithResponse
entries.description: The joystick device object's vtable +4: normalises, applies the deadzone and the response curve selected by the object's +0x28, then expands the button mask and hat bits into the 0x1d-byte block at DAT_004d24b0. A joystick is always built with mode 1 (FUN_00459dd4 passes it to FUN_0045c27c), the SQUARED curve: deadzone 0x19 SUBTRACTED to give +/-103, then |x|^2 scaled by 1/((103*103)>>8), so full deflection is 103*103/41 = 258, just over the 0x100 the control laws clamp at. Mode 0 is linear; mode 2 reads through Joystick_ReadAxisSigns, whose -1/0/+1 axes the deadzone then zeroes. Neither is used by the joystick; reading the deadzone as mode 0's linear rescale puts full deflection on 0x80 and halves every downstream response.

entries.name: Input_GetDevice
entries.description: Returns the registered input device of the given kind from the table at Input_DeviceTable, offset back to the object base, or 0 for none. Kind 3 is the joystick, and FUN_0045c508(3) is the presence test the CONTROLS panel gates on -- Input_QueryCapabilities' +0 is 1 or 2 and never 0, so it cannot answer that question.

entries.name: JoystickDevice_Poll
entries.description: (device): Joystick_Poll(device). Input_PollDeviceBlock calls it on Input_GetDevice(3).

entries.name: Vga_WaitVerticalRetrace
entries.description: MOV DX,0x3da / IN AL,DX / TEST AL,8 / JZ: spins until the VGA input-status register reports vertical retrace. One caller, CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand (0042a726), on the -b paged path only. A user-mode IN faults on NT-family Windows.

entries.name: VideoMode_BlitBitmap
entries.description: (block, bitmap, point): draws a bitmap at point less block+0x9a/+0x9e (004d25da/004d25de). Does nothing for a null bitmap. With the panel mode (+0x7b) 3 and the hi-res-banks flag (+0xb0) clear it calls 004816bc with a size of the bitmap's column count (+6) and row count (+4) shifted left by the X and Y coordinate shifts (+0x7e, +0x80), stored at 004d275c/004d2760; otherwise Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, point, 0). All 39 call sites pass the video-mode block 004d2540.

entries.name: VideoMode_BlitBitmapFlags
entries.description: (block, bitmap, point, flags): VideoMode_BlitBitmap with a flags argument passed through: Bitmap_BlitScaled at the bitmap's size doubled by the coordinate shifts in panel mode 3 without hi-res banks, else Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, point, flags).

entries.name: VideoMode_BlitBitmapSized
entries.description: (block, bitmap, point, flags, size): Bitmap_BlitScaled at an explicit size, with the size shifted left by the coordinate shifts (+0x7e, +0x80) first in panel mode 3 without hi-res banks. The point is offset by block+0x9a/+0x9e as in VideoMode_BlitBitmap.

entries.name: VideoMode_BlitRotated
entries.description: (block, bitmap, point, a, b, c): does nothing for a null bitmap; otherwise Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked(bitmap, point less block+0x9a/+0x9e, a, b, c). All callers pass the video-mode block 004d2540.

entries.name: Main_StaticInit
entries.description: MAIN.CPP's C++ static initialiser: the priority-0x20 entry at 004a7b70 in Borland's _INIT_ table (00 20 d8 ca 45 00), with no direct caller. Loads the video-mode/sim-globals block base 004d2540 into EBX, constructs the member object at 004d2603 (FUN_00481460), memsets the 0xc3-byte block to zero and fills its defaults through EBX: among them VideoMode_PanelMode (+0x7b) and maybe_CockpitLayoutMode (+0x7c) = 0, the 320-wide mode-0 geometry, Display_UseScrollWindow (+0xaa, 004d25ea) = 1, PilotingRazor = 0 and ControlsOptionBase = 0xd. Ends by seeding the two Math_RandomNext state blocks at 004d261d and 004d268f. The only write of +0x7c anywhere, and the only writer of +0x7b besides VideoMode_Configure.

entries.name: Tape_PackFile
entries.description: Writes one bundle block into an open tape: a uint32 size then the named file's bytes in 500-byte chunks. A source file it cannot open writes size 0, which is why data\object.str is empty in every retail tape.

entries.name: Tape_UnpackFile
entries.description: Reads one bundle block out of an open tape and writes it to the named path, in 500-byte chunks. A null destination consumes the block and discards it.

entries.name: Resource_Load
entries.description: Resource_Load(path): wraps a folder\name string into a temporary object and calls ClassItem_LoadResource(obj, 0), returning the loaded resource handle. The single entry point every HUD sprite bank, panel and cursor load goes through after ResourcePath_BuildFolderName builds the path.

entries.name: DemoTape_PickRandom
entries.description: Loads group 0x14 of tapes\demolist.str and returns entry time() % count, or entry 0 when the table holds one name. The retail table holds DEMO1, DEMO2 and DEMO3.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_Raise
entries.description: What commands 0x58 ([F12]) and 0x219 ([Alt+P]) reach: builds prf_alrt (PreferencesPanel_Ctor, 004566c4 -- NOT ctl_alrt, which is 00457d1c), raises DAT_004d2576 to stop the simulation while it is up and restores whatever it was on the way out, and snapshots the view object's whole settings block before the panel opens to write back afterwards. The modal loop itself is PreferencesPanel_Run (00456d4c).

entries.name: ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting
entries.description: Applies the HERC DETAIL preference (DAT_004d1fc5, 0-4) to three globals through three key/value table pairs: g_ShapeDetailSizeScaleQ10 (2000 in every slot), g_ShapeDetailBias {4,3,2,1,0} and g_TSDetailBiasFromHercDetail {2,2,1,1,0}. Called from Sim_RenderFrame when the byte changes and unconditionally at mission bring-up (00461ddc); both sites push the preference byte itself, with nothing in between.

entries.name: StructureDetail_ApplySetting
entries.description: The STRUCTURE DETAIL counterpart of ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting, called with DAT_004d1fc6 from the same two sites. Walks g_StructureDetailKeys and writes the matching g_StructureDetailValues entry into both g_TSDetailBiasFromStructureDetail -- which Structure_DrawWithDetailBias pushes into the TSDetailPart bias -- and DAT_004a9e48, whose consumer is not traced.

entries.name: LiftStart_DarkenPalette
entries.description: The lift start's darkening, left over from Metaltech: Earthsiege's elevator-lift mission start: called from Sim_InitMissionSession at 00461cec when block +0x54 is set. Builds two GLPalette objects whose headers copy ActivePaletteObject's, each over its own copy of the live entries (004d27c8 over 004d27d0, 004d27cc over 004d27d4), sets 0049aef6 to 8 and calls Palette_NoOp, rewrites entries 32-47 and 64-79 of the first as (G>>1, R>>1, B>>1) -- red and green swapped as well as halved -- installs those two spans live, and starts a 0x78-coarse-tick Palette_BeginCrossFade from the darkened object to the copy. Clears 0049aef4. LiftStart_Rise steps the fade and frees all four allocations.

entries.name: LiftStart_Rise
entries.description: The lift start's ride, left over from Metaltech: Earthsiege: called from Sim_InitMissionSession at 00461e28 when block +0x54 is set. Loads dba\intro (absent from every retail VOL) and uses its frame 0 unchecked. Raises the player machine from placed z - 4000 to placed z, 35 units a frame, with sound 0x21 running; each frame projects view-space (0, 1000, -camera z) -- world height 0, 1000 units ahead -- to a screen row, renders the scene with the viewport bottom cut to that row, blits intro from the row down and fills colour id 19 (DAT_004d3c26) below it, and steps the cross-fade while the row is below -200 and LiftStart_FadeRemaining is nonzero, then Sim_EndFrame. Sim_MainTick does not run. At the top: stops 0x21, plays 0x29, CockpitView_SetShakeBand(5) and one CockpitView_StepShake((next & 0xffff) % 5) on 0x4d268f per Sim_RenderFrame for 0x1e coarse ticks, with no Sim_EndFrame, so none of those frames is presented. Then clears the shake, frees the palettes and sets 0049aef4.

entries.name: Sim_DeathFlash
entries.description: Loads the death1/death2/world0 palettes, mutes effects, plays 0x26, fades death1 -> death2 -> black over 0x78 ticks each while shaking the view (band 10, Math_RandomBelow(0x4d268f, 10)) for the first 0x1e ticks, then installs world0 and runs a StatusAlertPanel of kind 2. es2_xref finds nothing reaching it, and the death1 and death2 palettes it loads are in no shipped VOL or install file. The player's death plays ViewChain_PlayerDeathCamera instead.

entries.name: ViewChain_Apply
entries.description: Once a tick from Sim_MainTick. While the view manager's step flag (+0x1c) is up, moves DAT_004d2572 to the pending view 004d259e and sets the camera up for it (views 1-4: free, cockpit, outside, chase); otherwise, in the outside view on the player, copies the preference 004d259c into InputDrivesCamera. Draws the caption while 004d25a4 counts.

entries.name: ViewChain_ViewObject
entries.description: Moves ViewObjectPtr onto the squad camera (004d270c) already viewing the object, or a free one seeded from the current camera and attached afresh, or the spare at 004d27d8. Stores the object in 004d2708 and sets InputDrivesCamera to 1, or to 004d259c for the player.

entries.name: ViewChain_DrawCaption
entries.description: The external view's caption: 'VIEW: ' + YOU / the squad pilot's name at x 50 and 'CONTROL: ' + CAMERA / HERC at x 215, STRINGS0.STR groups 36 and 17, in the green 6x8 font, centred in the band below the view-4 3D rect.

entries.name: VideoMode_Configure
entries.description: Sets the whole video-mode global block from a mode byte read out of the prefs file. Mode 0: VideoMode_PanelMode=0, UseHiResBanks=0, viewport 320x240, canvas 320x480, back buffer 640x480, coord shifts 0. Mode 1: UseHiResPanels=3, UseHiResBanks=0, viewport 640x480, canvas 640x960, back buffer 1280x960, shifts 1. Mode 2: as mode 1 but UseHiResBanks=1. So UseHiResPanels==3 selects .HFN/.HBA/.HB<n> art while UseHiResBanks separately selects the hi-res HUD sprite banks -- which is why the two idioms documented in cockpit-views.md differ. All three branches also set Display_UseScrollWindow (004d25ea) to 1, the scroll-window display path; Sim_ParseCommandLine runs later and its -b case clears it, selecting the paged path. None of them writes maybe_CockpitLayoutMode (004d25bc), which no code in the image can write at all.

entries.name: Sim_ParseCommandLine
entries.description: DBSIM's own argument parser. Owns the input-tape switches -r (record to <name>.tap), -p (play it back) and -D (play a tape DemoTape_PickRandom chooses, with the demo abort armed), plus -eggplant, the language and video switches and the -d dmp log.

entries.name: Cam_AttachTo
entries.description: Asks the object's vtable +0x30 for its eye and orbit-centre points, then Cam_AttachEye and Cam_AttachOrbit on ViewObjectPtr -- so an attach always ends in mode 1, directly behind at the least distance.

entries.name: View_GetActiveObject
entries.description: Returns ViewObjectPtr. HddMap_DrawTerrain reads the map projection's +4 triple through it: centre x, centre y, scale.

entries.name: Path_PrefixBaseDir
entries.description: Returns 004d28e0, a static buffer holding the directory string at 004d2840 followed by the given path with any drive letter ('X:') removed. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Path_PrefixBaseDir; DBSim_LoadScriptDat, DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects, DemoTape_PickRandom and Keyjoy_LoadConfig build paths with it.

entries.name: DriveCfg_PrefixPath
entries.description: (path): copies the directory at 004d2890 -- DriveCfg_Directory, which Sim_Run fills from data\drive.cfg -- into 004d2930, appends path less a leading drive 'X:' when path[1] is ':', and returns 004d2930. OnlineManual_Raise resolves es2guide.hlp through it and PilotMessagePort_Paint the training voice clips.

entries.name: Config_BuildPath
entries.description: (name): 'data\' + name, or 'tapes\' + name while TapePlayback is set, built in the static buffer 004d2980, which it returns. prefs.cfg and keyjoy.cfg are opened through it.

entries.name: Language_StringFilePath
entries.description: (name, extension): builds 'st<letter>\<name>.<extension>' in the static buffer 004d29a0, the letter being the language letter 004d25ba patched into the 'str' literal at 0049f27d (so 'str' for the default r). The name and extension go through Path_WithExtension. ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll, the alert panel constructors and the sound catalog build their .STR paths with it.

entries.name: Voice_ArchiveName
entries.description: Returns the voice archive name, patching the last character of the literal 'simvoice' with the language byte at 004d25ba: SIMVOICE / SIMVOICF / SIMVOICG.

entries.name: Voice_FilePath
entries.description: (name, extension): builds '<Voice_ArchiveName()>\<name>.<extension>' in the static buffer 004d29be, the name and extension going through Path_WithExtension. The message ports and CommBox_BeginMessage find their speech files with it.

entries.name: Language_GetFolderName
entries.description: Reads the first byte of data\language.cfg and returns the matching resource folder name: 'F' -> FRENCH, 'G' -> GERMAN, 'S' -> SPANISH, anything else ENGLISH. The retail CD ships the first three.

entries.name: OnlineManual_Raise
entries.description: Command 0x35's handler: composes <Language_GetFolderName()>\es2guide.hlp into the buffer at 004d29dc, resolves it to a full path through DriveCfg_PrefixPath and returns that path -- the caller passes it to Help_Show. Two callers, Sim_DispatchCommand's `?` case and SystemButtons_OnChildClick's child 0, so the key and the right-hand system button are one path. This is the manual's 'On-Line Manual' MISC. entry -- a Windows help file, not a game screen.

entries.name: Sim_Suspend
entries.description: Sets DAT_004d25f6, which holds Sim_Run's loop in its sleep-and-pump branch, suspends every sound and pauses the cockpit's two message ports. The pair to Sim_Resume, on the window losing and regaining focus.

entries.name: Sim_Resume
entries.description: Clears DAT_004d25f6, resumes every sound and resumes the cockpit's two message ports. The main window's WM_SETFOCUS calls it.

entries.name: Cockpit_RepaintShieldGauge
entries.description: When CockpitViewInstance and its shield gauge (+0x1e9) are set, calls the gauge's vtable slot 1. Video_ToggleFullscreen calls it.

entries.name: Sim_Run
entries.description: WinMain's body: reads data\drive.cfg, parses the command line, refuses without -eggplant, then runs subsystem phases 0, 1, Sim_InitMissionSession and phase 3, and loops phase 4, Sim_MainTick, the camera, Sim_RenderFrame, Sim_EndFrame and phase 6 until DemoAbort, the quit flag 004d2582, a non-zero Sim_MainTick or WM_QUIT; then stops the music and sound, saves option 6 if the full-screen state changed, and calls Sim_Shutdown.

entries.name: Sim_MainTick
entries.description: DBSIM's per-frame simulation tick. Updates SimTickDelta from a hardware/timer source, iterates every global object list, and calls Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate once per live mech in GlobalMechList.

entries.name: ViewChain_PlayerDeathCamera
entries.description: Sim_MainTick calls it once a tick in place of Mission_PollStatus while the player's machine is destroyed (+0x99) and the simulation is not frozen (DAT_004d2576); a nonzero return makes Sim_MainTick raise the status alert for 2 and end the mission whatever the answer. First call, latched by DeathCamera_Started: arms DeathCamera_Countdown from its class table, makes the player ViewChain_Chosen, enters the outside view on the player (from the cockpit by view command 2 and pending view 3, otherwise ViewChain_ViewObject and ViewChain_CaptionFrames = 2), sets InputDrivesCamera, runs CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand and ViewChain_Apply itself, and unless the camera is locked writes the orbit pitch, roll 0, heading and distance. Every call: clears the camera lock +0x4a, Cam_Steer with the class's constant steer, throttle and trigger, sets the lock, and returns Timer_CountDown(DeathCamera_Countdown) == 0. Every table is indexed by the type record's +0x50, 0 walker and 1 RAZOR. Holds the 004d2540 block base in ESI throughout.

entries.name: Sim_EndFrame
entries.description: Per-frame tail. Scroll-window path (Display_UseScrollWindow != 0): CockpitView_StepViewTransition, Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges, Palette_FlushDirtyRange, Display_Present, CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand, with the +0xac render target selected around them under VideoMode_PanelMode 1. Paged path (-b): the same calls without Display_Present, plus a page flip -- the render target's +0x8c becomes the visible page (+0x34, g_RasterRoutines slot 18), +0x88 the draw page (+0x3c, slot 17), and the two swap. Driver 3 fills both slots with empty stubs, so under -b nothing here reaches the screen.

entries.name: Sim_RenderFrame
entries.description: The whole frame draw; 13 callers -- Sim_Run once a frame, and the redraws in PreferencesPanel_Raise, LiftStart_Rise, Sim_DeathFlash, DemoTape_PickRandom and Sim_InitMissionSession. Order: Subsystem_RunPhase(5); ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting when option byte 004d1fc5 has changed and StructureDetail_ApplySetting when 004d1fc6 has; adds CockpitView_GetShakeOffset's pair into the ints at Sim_RenderContext +0x220/+0x224 for the frame; Raster_InstallViewProjection, Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion(ActiveHeightGrid, view, 0), CockpitView_PerFrameUpdate, Scene_SubmitFrameObjects; then, when CockpitView_ShowsWorld, Raster_InstallViewProjection, LightManager_SetCameraPosition, Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion again, Raster_SetModelTransform(0), Scene_DrawTerrainPass and ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain; then Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate, slot +8 of CockpitViewInstance+0x1f5, slot +0x10 of CockpitView_GetSquadMessagePort's port and of CockpitViewInstance+0x20b; takes the shake offset back out; and ends with SystemButtons_PaintForPointer(CockpitViewInstance, &DAT_004d234c).

entries.name: ViewChain_ToggleCameraControl
entries.description: [Enter]/[Tab] in view 4: flips 004d259c, and redraws the caption when the camera is on the player.

entries.name: Sim_HandleWindowKey
entries.description: (code): 0x21c ([Alt+Enter]) runs Video_ToggleFullscreen unless a tape is playing back with 004d25b0 set; 0x430 ([Ctrl+B]) calls __break (INT3) when 004d25b0 is set. Returns 1 for either code, 0 otherwise. Input_BuildPlayerDevice and Sim_DispatchCommand call it.

entries.name: Sim_DispatchCommand
entries.description: The simulator's command dispatcher: every queued command code passes through here, and Sim_PollPlayerInput also calls it directly (passing 0x14 for one of the MFD cases). Offers the code to the cockpit widget tree (CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand), then to FUN_0045fd60, then its own switch, and finally to the player mech's vtable +0x2c. Codes are PC set-1 scancodes with 0x200 added for Alt -- 0x26 is L, 0x29 is backquote, 0x11/0x211 are W and Alt+W, 0x02-0x0b and 0x202-0x20b the two number-key banks. Case 0x0e/0x14 latch g_CenterTurretMode and clear g_CenterBodyMode; case 0x2b does the reverse and caches g_CenterBodyTargetHeading. Both also clear the auto-turret-tracking flag at mech+0x202 -> +0x14.

entries.name: Sim_PollPlayerInput
entries.description: Reads the input device struct (axes at +0x0e steer, +0x10 throttle, +0x12 torso twist, +0x14 torso pitch) and dispatches player control: Mech_ApplyThrottleInput, Mech_TorsoTwistTick, Mech_TorsoPitchTick. Also hosts the keyboard command switch.

entries.name: Cockpit_GetConsoleButtons
entries.description: Returns CockpitViewInstance+0x1e1, the weapon console panel: WeaponMounts_SetChain hands it to ConsoleButtons_SetChainNumber, Sim_DispatchCommand to ConsoleButtons_ToggleAutoTrack and reads its auto-track latch +0xb3.

entries.name: PausePanel_Dtor
entries.description: GeneralSmallAlert's destructor (class record 0046107d), PausePanel_Ctor's object: (panel, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, GeneralAlert_Dtor(panel, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004610d9; class record at 0046107d

entries.name: Sim_CreateRenderContext
entries.description: Allocates 0x239 bytes, runs GLViewport_Ctor on them, stores the result in Sim_RenderContext (004d2552), sets its int at +0x208 to 1 and installs it with Raster_InstallRenderContext. Sim_InitMissionSession calls it.

entries.name: Light_CreateMissionSun
entries.description: Called exactly once per mission, unconditionally, from Sim_InitMissionSession (FUN_004614fc) right after the light-system reset (FUN_0048dbfc) and before DBSim_LoadScriptDat -- creates the ONE directional 'sun' light every mission gets. Direction is NOT read from any mission/theater file: it's built from two HARDCODED constant vectors, local_38=(0,0x1000,0) and local_40=(-6000,0,21000), combined via FUN_0047eaac (looks like a normalize/transform) then FUN_0047ffb4 (looks like it derives a direction from a target-point + up-vector pair, output stored as the light's direction field). Intensity is set via vtable+4 call with literal 0x100 (256). The created light is registered via Light_Register (FUN_0048bd44) AND pushed onto a persistent list (Light_PersistentList) via Light_AddPersistent, so it survives a later Light_ReregisterPersistent (Light_ReregisterPersistent) call. No separate ambient (type=0) light creation was found anywhere in the binary -- Light_ComputeShadeForFace's type-0 branch may be genuinely unused by real missions, meaning faces angled away from the sun likely render fully unlit (shade=0), not floor-lit. FUN_0047eaac/FUN_0047ffb4/FUN_0048d99b (the actual per-face dot-product math) are not decoded; the lighting is a single fixed sun direction and intensity with no mission-specific lighting data.

entries.name: Sim_ShowLoadingScreen
entries.description: (name): builds the bitmap's path with ResourcePath_BuildFolderName under the folder at PTR_DAT_004a0a28 (PTR_DAT_004a0a40 when VideoMode_PanelMode is 3), loads it with Resource_Load, blits frame 0 at (0, 0), Display_Present, and frees the array with GLBitmapArray_Dtor. Sim_InitMissionSession shows the mission loading screen with it.

entries.name: Sim_ReadLoadingScreenChoice
entries.description: (theaterOut, isRazorOut): reads the 0x14-byte header of data\script (with the dat extension) and stores its first int16 -- the theater World_LoadTheater doubles -- in theaterOut; then reads the first five int16s of data\player.mec and sets isRazorOut when the fifth, the player entry's mech type, is 8 (RAZOR in MECHS.NAM). Asserts (INIT.CPP lines 0xde, 0xe4, severity 5) that each file opens. Sim_InitMissionSession builds the loading screen's name from them: 'flyrX' for the Razor, else 'hercX', X = theater + 1.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 004613b4; strings at 0049f879 and 0049f88e; MECHS.NAM

entries.name: Sim_InitMissionSession
entries.description: Per-mission session setup: resets the light system (FUN_0048dbfc), creates the mission's one hardcoded sun light (Light_CreateMissionSun), then calls DBSim_LoadScriptDat and DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects. Confirms lighting setup happens once per mission load, independent of which script.dat/theater is loaded. Also picks the FOCAL SHIFT -- 9 when DAT_004d30c4 >= 0x4b1 and 8 otherwise -- and passes it as the third argument of the view constructor FUN_0048bc98, which stores it at view+0x1a. That is the whole of the field of view; see docs/formats/cockpit-views.md.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE; docs/formats/cockpit-views.md for the focal shift

entries.name: Sim_Shutdown
entries.description: The simulator's exit path, run by Sim_Run however the main loop ends: closes the tape files, Mission_WriteResults(LocalPlayerMech), then the exit code at 004d283c -- 6 under DemoMode, 0 with the quit flag 004d2582, else 4 when the player's +0x99 is set and MissionModeFlag (004a9ed6) is, else 3 -- then Sim_ShutdownNoOp1 and Sim_ShutdownNoOp2.

entries.name: TSSunLight_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSSunLight_Dtor (00427e3d).
entries.source: ES2DecompileContainingBatch DBSIM 00462003 / VSHELL 00427e3d: identical after normalisation; RTTI TSSunLight vtable 0049f8d8 slot +0x00

entries.name: TSLight_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSLight_Dtor (00427e02).
entries.source: ES2DecompileContainingBatch DBSIM 0046209e / VSHELL 00427e02: identical after normalisation; RTTI TSLight vtable 0049f8ec slot +0x00

entries.name: Cam_Dtor
entries.description: CAM vtable +0x00 (0049f900, RTTI 'CAM', 0x4e bytes, derived from TSCamera), the destructor its class record names: (cam, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, TSContext_Dtor(cam, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00462150; class record at 00462104

entries.name: Sound_ResolveSamplePath
entries.description: Prefixes a catalog filename with 'HMI\\', or 'HMX\\' when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set. SIMSOUND.VOL carries both banks, hmx being the same content at half the sample rate; EXPLO5.WAV is in hmi only.

entries.name: sfxWndProc
entries.description: MainWndProc filter registered by Sound_Init (see WndProcHook_Register). Two messages only: WM_TIMER (0x113) pumps the SOS/MME service routine, and MM_MCINOTIFY (0x3b9) with MCI_NOTIFY_SUCCESSFUL re-issues Music_PlayTrack, which is what loops the CD track.

entries.name: Sound_Init
entries.description: (enable). Registers sfxWndProc as a MainWndProc hook, allocates the five-slot speech channel pool (5 x 0x42-byte records plus a 5 x 100-byte script buffer at 004d2df4), then allocates and initialises the SFX manager with a cache cap of 2,000,000 bytes -- 1,000,000 when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set -- 60 resource slots and 90 voice slots, and loads the sound catalog.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Load
entries.description: Loads str\\SOUNDS.STR -- one .STR group of 57 entries, each a filename plus a 7-byte attribute blob -- into three parallel arrays: names (004d2b0c), attribute pointers (004d2bfc) and voice handles (004d2cfc), count in 004d2dec. Per entry: resolve the path through Sound_ResolveSamplePath, Sfx_Open as a sample, priority 5, Sfx_SetLooping to attribute byte 0, Sfx_SetVolume to Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000), Sfx_Cache if byte 2 is set, then default byte 4 to 5 and byte 5 to 100 where they are 0xff and set byte 8 to 100. The code reads a TEN-byte blob: bytes 7-9 are runtime scratch (resume flag, category volume, throttle counter) that the file does not supply.

entries.name: Sound_Preload
entries.description: Caches one catalog id's sample without playing it.

entries.name: Sound_Shutdown
entries.description: Stops the CD, unregisters sfxWndProc, tears the SFX manager down and clears SfxManager.

entries.name: Sound_IsCategoryEnabled
entries.description: Splits the catalog at id 10: below 10 answers to the music enable flag (0049f90c), 10 and up to the effects flag (0049f910). This is why every data-driven table plays its sound id + 10.

entries.name: Sound_ConsumeRequest
entries.description: (catalogId) -> may play. interval = (2 - detailSetting 004d1fc7) * attribute byte 3; interval 0 always plays, otherwise attribute byte 9 counts up (wrapping at 0x0f) and only every interval-th call passes. Keeps a sound fired by many objects at once from playing once per object. Dead code in the shipped binary: no CALL to it exists anywhere in the code section and its address is stored nowhere, so the authored divisors in attribute byte 3 never take effect.

entries.name: Sound_Play
entries.description: (catalogId). Non-positional. Rolls the variation count (attribute byte 6) to displace the id, sets volume to Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000) * byte 8 / 100 -- or 0 when the category is muted -- and plays.

entries.name: Sound_PlayAt
entries.description: (catalogId, worldPoint). Positional. Rolls the variation count, then Sound_Place computes volume and pan; plays only if the result is audible. One entry point covers every data-driven sound in the sim (PROJ.DAT, ROCKETS.DAT, EXPLOS.DAT, the alerts).

entries.name: Voice_PlayNamed
entries.description: (wavName, volume). Acquires a speech slot for the name with no .SNC script, sets its volume and starts it.

entries.name: Sound_UpdatePosition
entries.description: Re-runs Sound_Place for a sound already playing, without starting it.

entries.name: Sound_Place
entries.description: (catalogId, worldPoint) -> audible. Resets the model transform and pushes the point through the current camera transform, so the listener is the camera. With d = Math_FastMagnitude3D(view): beyond attribute byte 5 * 1024 the volume is 0 and nothing plays; at or past byte 4 * 1024 it is (max - d) * vol / max -- the divisor is max, not max - min, so a sound at exactly min is already attenuated. Final volume is scaled by attribute byte 8 / 100. Pan is (-2a) & 0xffff for a = Math_Atan2Bam(viewX, viewY) below 0x8000, and 2a & 0xffff above.

entries.name: Sound_Stop
entries.description: Stops one catalog id's voice.

entries.name: Sound_IsPlaying
entries.description: Returns whether one catalog id's voice is still playing.

entries.name: Voice_EvictLru
entries.description: Picks the speech slot with the oldest last-use tick (+0x37), closes whatever voice it held and returns it.

entries.name: Voice_Acquire
entries.description: (wavName, sncPath) -> slot. Looks the name up across the five speech slots; a miss evicts the least recently used (Voice_EvictLru), copies the name in, opens an SFX voice at priority 0xff so catalog voices can never evict it, caches it, and loads the .SNC script. Gated on Sound_SpeechEnabled.

entries.name: Sound_SetMusicEnabled
entries.description: Stores the music enable flag when it differs from the current value. No side effect of its own; the caller mutes or unmutes.

entries.name: Sound_SetEffectsEnabled
entries.description: Stores the effects enable flag when it differs from the current value. No side effect of its own; the caller mutes or unmutes.

entries.name: Sound_MuteMusic
entries.description: Zeroes the volume of catalog ids 0-9 and clears the music enable flag; when a CD track is set, saves the position and stops the CD instead.

entries.name: Sound_MuteEffects
entries.description: Zeroes the volume of catalog ids 10 and up and clears the effects enable flag.

entries.name: Sound_MuteOne
entries.description: (id): zeroes one catalog id's volume and clears both the music and effects flags. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sound_UnmuteMusic
entries.description: Restores ids 0-9 to Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000) * byte 8 / 100, or resumes the CD from the saved position, and sets the music enable flag.

entries.name: Sound_UnmuteEffects
entries.description: Restores ids 10 and up to their own volumes and sets the effects enable flag.

entries.name: Sound_UnmuteOne
entries.description: (id): the counterpart of Sound_MuteOne -- restores the id's attribute volume and raises both the music and effects flags. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_EffectiveVolume
entries.description: (id): 0 when there is no SfxManager, else SoundCatalog_Attributes[id] byte 1 (volume) times byte 8 (category volume percent) / 100. CockpitView_StepViewTransition stores sound 0x2d's into 004cfd38.

entries.name: Sound_SetBaseVolume
entries.description: Overwrites attribute byte 1 (the authored 0-100 volume) and re-applies it.

entries.name: Sound_SetCategoryVolume
entries.description: Writes attribute byte 8, the per-sound category scale every volume computation multiplies through, and re-applies the resulting volume.

entries.name: Sound_ShiftMusicSet
entries.description: (delta, charIndex). Offsets one character of each of the ten music filenames by delta and re-opens them -- how a different music set would have been selected. All ten name battle1.wav, which ships in no archive.

entries.name: Sound_SetPitch
entries.description: Sets one catalog id's playback rate through Sfx_SetPitch, as the original's 16.16 ratio (0x10000 = 1.0). Cockpit_PowerUpSound is the only caller found, dropping the engine hum to 42000.

entries.name: Sound_StartMissionMusic
entries.description: Plays Music_CdTrack when the SFX manager is up, a track is set and Sound_MusicEnabled is up. Sim_InitMissionSession's own music start, called immediately after it writes the track and the enable byte.

entries.name: Sound_SuspendAll
entries.description: Sets attribute byte 7 for each catalog voice that loops forever (record +0x18 == 0) and is playing (flag 0x100), clearing it for the rest; saves the CD position into 0049f91c when music is on; stops the CD, every voice (Sfx_StopAll) and releases the driver (Sfx_ReleaseDriver). Paired with Sound_ResumeAll.

entries.name: Sound_ResumeAll
entries.description: Replays exactly the catalog voices whose attribute byte 7 was set by Sound_SuspendAll, and resumes the CD from the saved TMSF position.

entries.name: Snc_ServiceQueue
entries.description: Drains the global .SNC event queue (004d2efa, 8-byte {time, slot} entries, count 0049f97c) of everything now due, calling each slot's Snc_Advance.

entries.name: Sim_InitMissionSessionNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Sim_InitMissionSession calls it after Sound_Init, before Light_ResetSystem.

entries.name: Snc_Load
entries.description: (slot, sncPath, voiceHandle). Reads the .SNC file into the slot's 100-byte buffer: an int32 length followed by that many bytes of {int8 frame, int8 deltaTicks} pairs, then appends the 0xff terminator itself -- the terminator is NOT in the file. With no path the buffer is just 0xff and the voice plays with the portrait held.

entries.name: Snc_Start
entries.description: Points the slot's cursor at the start of its script; an immediately-0xff script sets the frame to 1 and plays without animation, otherwise stamps the start time and runs Snc_Advance. Then plays the voice.

entries.name: Snc_Advance_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Snc_Advance with the same argument. Snc_ServiceQueue calls it.

entries.name: Snc_Advance
entries.description: Reads {frame, delta} pairs, accumulating delta into the slot's next-event time until it passes now, publishes the frame at slot+0x08, and re-inserts the slot into the global event queue. Reaching 0xff sets the frame to -1, which is what tells HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame the message is over.

entries.name: Snc_GetFrame
entries.description: Returns the slot's current portrait frame (slot+0x08); -1 once the script has ended.

entries.name: SfxHandle_SetVolume
entries.description: (handle*, volume): Sfx_SetVolume(SfxManager, *handle, volume) when the manager exists and *handle is not -1. Voice_PlayNamed calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_Init
entries.description: (manager, memoryCap, resourceSlots, voiceSlots). Called as (cap, 60, 90). Allocates the resource table at +0x34 (stride 0x21c) and the voice table at +0x38 (stride 0x28), fills every slot's handle with -1, then brings the backend up with the config block at +0x24.

entries.name: Sfx_ReadConfig
entries.description: Reads DATA\\SOUND.CFG with GetPrivateProfileString into the manager's config block at +0x24: Driver (MME=1 / DirectSound=2) at +0x2a, Buffers (1-64, else 5) at +0x30, Rate (11 gives 0x10, else 0x20) at +0x24, Width (Mono gives 4, else 8) at +0x28. +0x26 is fixed at 1 and +0x32 at 0x200.

entries.name: SfxManager_Dtor
entries.description: (manager, flags): Sos_Shutdown, Mem_Delete on the arrays at +0x34 and +0x38 (clearing both), then Mem_Delete(manager) when flags bit 0 is set. Sound_Shutdown runs it on SfxManager with 3.

entries.name: Sfx_ReleaseDriver
entries.description: Sos_ReleaseDigiDriver. Sound_SuspendAll's last step after Sfx_StopAll.

entries.name: Sfx_AcquireDriver
entries.description: Returns Sos_AcquireDigiDriver's answer. Sound_ResumeAll's first step.

entries.name: Sfx_ServiceTimer
entries.description: (manager, hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam): Sos_Service(hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam). sfxWndProc's WM_TIMER arm.

entries.name: Sfx_Open
entries.description: (manager, name, type, userValue, loadState) -> voice handle, or -1. Handles are generation<<16|slotIndex, the generation coming from the manager's counter at +0x20; every accessor re-reads the slot's own copy and rejects a mismatch. Takes a free voice slot and defaults it (priority 5, volume 100, loop 1, pan 0x8000, pitch 0x10000), then binds a resource: an existing resource with the same name is shared and its refcount bumped, otherwise a free resource slot takes the name. type 0 = .hmp MIDI song (flag 0x1), 1 = digital sample, 2 = the streamed path (flag 0x1000).

entries.name: Sfx_Close
entries.description: Releases one voice slot and drops its resource's refcount.

entries.name: Sfx_Cache
entries.description: (manager, voiceHandle, in). Loads or unloads the voice's resource. Loading stats the file for its byte size into record+0x210, and if cached+size would exceed the manager's cap at +0x18 runs Sfx_EvictUntilFree first; on success sets record+0x20c and adds the size to the cached total at +0x1c. Unloading refuses while the resource refcount (+0x208) is 2 or more.

entries.name: Sfx_Play
entries.description: (manager, voiceHandle). Caches the resource on demand, starts it through Sos_StartVoice, sets the playing flag 0x100 and bumps the manager's playing-sample (+0x3c) or playing-song (+0x40) count. It does NOT test the 0x100 flag first: playing a voice that is already sounding starts a second concurrent copy on another SOS channel rather than restarting or being ignored, and the voice record keeps only the newest handle (+0x24), so Sfx_Stop can no longer reach the older copies.

entries.name: Sfx_Stop
entries.description: Stops one voice and clears its playing flag.

entries.name: Sfx_IsDone
entries.description: Returns nonzero when the voice is not playing; when the backend reports it finished, calls Sfx_Stop to clear the state.

entries.name: Sfx_Service
entries.description: Sos_Service(0, 0, 0, 0): the library service call with no window message. AlertPanel_Present calls it while SfxManager is set.

entries.name: Sfx_PickEvictionVictim
entries.description: Scores every live voice and returns the lowest: (resource cached ? 100 : 0) + priority + (playing ? 1000 : 0) + (playing && looping ? 10000 : 0). An idle, uncached, low-priority voice is taken first and a looping playing one last.

entries.name: Sfx_EvictUntilFree
entries.description: Frees cached resources by repeatedly taking Sfx_PickEvictionVictim's choice until the requested number of bytes fits under the manager's cap.

entries.name: Sfx_SetCallback
entries.description: Writes voice+0x10, handed to the backend sample object when the voice starts.

entries.name: Sfx_SetVolume
entries.description: Writes voice+0x14 (0-100) and re-applies it to the backend if the voice is live.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPitch
entries.description: Writes voice+0x20 as 16.16; 0x10000 is 1.0 and clears flag 0x400, anything else sets it.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPan
entries.description: Writes voice+0x1c; 0x8000 is centre and clears flag 0x800, anything else sets it.

entries.name: Sfx_SetLooping
entries.description: Writes voice+0x18 as a repeat COUNT, not a boolean: 0 = forever, 1 = once, n = n times. Sets flag 0x80 for any value other than 1.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPriority
entries.description: Writes voice+0x0c. The sound catalog uses 5; the speech channel uses 0xff so catalog voices can never evict it.

entries.name: Sfx_PlayMusicTrack
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_PlayTrack. Music does not go through SOS, so the manager reaches MCI through four thunks of this kind rather than through its own backend.

entries.name: Sfx_StopMusic
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_Stop.

entries.name: Sfx_IsMusicIdle
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_IsIdle.

entries.name: Sfx_GetVoiceRecord
entries.description: Validates a voice handle and returns a pointer to its record+4, or 0.

entries.name: Sfx_StopAll
entries.description: (manager). Sfx_Stop's body over every voice with the 0x100 playing flag and a live resource: Sos_StopVoice (which returns 1 unconditionally), decrement the playing-song (+0x40) or playing-sample (+0x3c) count, clear 0x100. The loop is bounded by +0x10, the resource slot count (60), not the voice count +0x14 (90). Only caller: Sound_SuspendAll (0046311c).

entries.name: Sfx_GetMusicPosition
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_GetPosition.

entries.name: Sfx_ResumeMusicAt
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_ResumeAt.

entries.name: Str_FormatStatic
entries.description: (format, ...): _vsprintf into the static buffer 004d2f74 and returns it.

entries.name: Display_SetOrigin
entries.description: Driver 3's g_RasterRoutines slot 15 target, reached through the stub 00489802. Moves the viewport window over the back buffer to point param_2: sets the render target descriptor's pixel pointer and row-table base to base + y*width + x and stores the point in Display_OriginX/Y. Ignores param_1, the page.

entries.name: Display_Present
entries.description: Screen_PresentFrame(&Display_OriginX, &Display_ScreenRect): puts the viewport window at the display origin on screen. 29 call sites (es2_xref): 25 on the scroll-window path only, 21 in CockpitView_StepViewTransition and one each in AlertPanel_Present, AlertPanel_Leave, Sim_EndFrame and Sim_InitMissionSession; the mission loading screen Sim_ShowLoadingScreen, the preferences panel's per-pass PreferencesPanel_Present, and MainWndProc's WM_PAINT (windowed) and 0x812 handlers unconditionally.

entries.name: Display_PresentRect
entries.description: Presents one rect {x0,y0,x1,y1} of the view: offsets it by the render context's origin (+0x210/+0x214 minus +0x220/+0x224) when the context's +0x20c is set, then calls Screen_PresentFrame with that rect offset by Display_OriginX/Y as the source and by Display_ScreenRect as the destination. es2_xref finds no rel32 caller and no stored pointer.

entries.name: Window_CentreRect
entries.description: (left, top, right, bottom, flags, out): SetRect(out, x, y, width, height) for a rect of the given size centred on the desktop -- y is kept as top when flags bit 1 is set. The last two fields are the size, not the far corner. MainWindow_Create passes its adjusted window rect and 004d3750.

entries.name: Win_SetPumpCursor
entries.description: (cursor): stores Win_PumpCursor (004d37a4). Sim_Run and 00465288 call it with a non-null HCURSOR.

entries.name: Win_PumpMessages
entries.description: Drains the thread's message queue with PeekMessageA(PM_REMOVE), translating and dispatching each message. Returns 1 at WM_QUIT (0x12); otherwise, once the queue is empty, restores the cursor 004d37a4 (SetCursor, when set) and returns 0.

entries.name: Screen_ResetBackBufferGlobals
entries.description: Clears the back-buffer globals (the bitmap header 004d30a4, the display 004d30a8, BackBuffer_Pixels, the memory DC 004d30b8 and its DIB 004d30bc, the palette flag 004d30b0, the timer id 004d368c), takes the size from VideoMode_BackBufferWidth/Height into 004d30c4/c8, and resets the BITMAPINFOHEADER at 004d30d0 to size 0x28, one plane, 8 bits. MainWindow_Create runs it before creating the window.

entries.name: Screen_CreateBackBuffer
entries.description: Builds the back buffer: a memory DC (004d30b8), the system palette read into 004d30f8 with red and blue swapped, an 8-bit top-down DIB section of 004d30c4 x 004d30c8 whose pixels are BackBuffer_Pixels, a 0xe-byte bitmap header over it at 004d30a4, and a 0xa0-byte display named 'BMP_8' at 004d30a8 (GLDisplay_Ctor, GLDisplay_Open) made current with Raster_SelectRenderTarget, draw page 1 and visible page 0, and its four page origins zeroed: they are set 0/200/400/600 rows apart only for a display named 'VGA_8' (004a085f). Ends with GLDisplay_SetAttribute(display, 9, 0). MainWindow_Create runs it once the window exists.

entries.name: Assert_Stub
entries.description: Returns immediately. Assert_Report calls it.

entries.name: MainWindow_KillTimer
entries.description: KillTimer(MainWindow_Handle, the timer id at 004d368c) when that id is nonzero. Sim_Run runs it before Sim_Shutdown; MainWndProc, Video_ToggleFullscreen and Assert_Report run it before PostQuitMessage, and MainWindow_Create when CreateWindowExA fails.

entries.name: MainWindow_Create
entries.description: (hInstance, nCmdShow): creates the 'EarthSiege II' window sized from the display size at 004d25c2/c6 and centred on the desktop -- or, with the fullscreen flag 004d25e2 set, sized to the whole desktop and made topmost with SetWindowPos -- and stores it in MainWindow_Handle. On failure runs MainWindow_KillTimer; on success Screen_CreateBackBuffer, ShowWindow and UpdateWindow. Returns whether the window exists.

entries.name: Screen_ClearToBlack
entries.description: Clears the screen to palette index 0. Windowed (004d25e2 clear): zeroes BackBuffer_Pixels and StretchBlts a 10x10 corner of the zeroed DIB over the whole client rect inside BeginPaint/EndPaint, realizing the palette when 004d30b0 is set. Fullscreen: restores the DirectDraw surface 004d3798 when IsLost reports DDERR_SURFACELOST, locks it -- or 004d379c below 640 wide -- zeroes each row, unlocks, and below 640 wide flips 004d3798. Sim_InitMissionSession and Sim_Run call it.

entries.name: Screen_SetSoftwareCursor
entries.description: (bitmap): stores Screen_SoftwareCursor (004d37a8), the sprite Screen_PresentFrame draws at the pointer in fullscreen. Its one caller, Sim_InitMissionSession, passes the 'lo_curs' resource when the display is narrower than 640.

entries.name: Screen_PresentFrame
entries.description: Screen_PresentFrame(int *srcPoint, int *dstRect): copies the back buffer's rect at srcPoint (BackBuffer_Pixels, row stride VideoMode_BackBufferWidth) to dstRect on screen. Fullscreen (_DAT_004d25e2 != 0): restores a lost surface, locks the DirectDraw primary (004d3798), or below 640 wide the back surface (004d379c), copies row by row, blits the software cursor bitmap (Screen_SoftwareCursor) at GetCursorPos() colour-keyed on byte 1, unlocks, and below 640 wide flips. Windowed: StretchBlt from the DIB's DC (004d30b8) inside BeginPaint/EndPaint. Its only callers are Display_Present and Display_PresentRect.

entries.name: Palette_CreateForDisplay
entries.description: (quads, count): builds the 256-entry LOGPALETTE at 004d37ac from RGBQUADs and returns CreatePalette's handle. With the system palette in SYSPAL_NOSTATIC use, it copies count entries flagged 1 (PC_RESERVED), clears the rest, and forces entry 0 to black and 255 to white, both flagged 0. Otherwise it keeps the NUMRESERVED/2 system colours at each end (flags 0) and copies the middle entries flagged 5 (PC_RESERVED | PC_NOCOLLAPSE), moving the blue of any that matches a static colour by 3 (down from 0xfc and up, up otherwise). Screen_SetPalette calls it.

entries.name: Palette_ClearSystemPalette
entries.description: Creates a palette from the LOGPALETTE header at 004a041c with all 256 entries black and flagged 5 (PC_RESERVED | PC_NOCOLLAPSE), selects and realizes it on the screen DC, then selects the old palette back and deletes it. Screen_SetPalette runs it before realizing a new palette.

entries.name: Palette_SetDisplayEntries
entries.description: (palette): builds 256 PALETTEENTRYs: the NUMRESERVED/2 system colours at each end flagged 0, the rest from the palette's 6-bit entries at +8 shifted left 2 and flagged 5. Windowed (004d25e2 clear) it sets them as the back buffer DIB's colour table (SetDIBColorTable on 004d30b8) and AnimatePalettes the screen palette 004d30b0; full screen it hands them to the DirectDraw palette 004d37a0 (slot +0x18, SetEntries(0, 0, 256, entries)). Palette_FlushDirtyRange calls it.

entries.name: Screen_SetPalette
entries.description: (palette): nothing for null. Stores palette at 004d3bb0 and converts its 256 four-byte entries (+8; R, G, B, flags) to RGBQUADs: flags bit 0 means 6-bit components, shifted left 2; otherwise an entry is copied only when flags bit 1 is set. Runs 00465b3c, makes 00465920(quads, 256)'s result the palette 004d30b0, selects and realizes it on the screen DC and SetDIBColorTable's the back-buffer memory DC 004d30b8. In full screen (004d25e2) it also copies the quads to a PALETTEENTRY array at 004d37b0 with peFlags 1 and calls 004d3794's vtable +0x14 (IDirectDraw::CreatePalette, flags 0x4c) into 004d37a0, and on success 004d3798's vtable +0x7c (IDirectDrawSurface::SetPalette) with it.

entries.name: ClassItem_LoadFromFile
entries.description: (path): opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, loads one class item from it with ClassItem_LoadResource, destroys the stream and returns the item. Palette_LoadAndActivate and Sim_InitMissionSession call it.

entries.name: WndProcHook_Register
entries.description: Appends a raw (hwnd,msg,wParam,lParam)-shaped filter function to the first free slot (of 10) in the table at DAT_004d3bb4 that MainWndProc tries, in order, before its own message switch -- any hook returning nonzero short-circuits MainWndProc entirely. Mouse_WndProcHook is one of four registered hooks found; the others are sound/movie-playback related.

entries.name: WndProcHook_Unregister
entries.description: Removes a hook previously added by WndProcHook_Register from the DAT_004d3bb4 table.

entries.name: Video_CreateDirectDrawExclusive
entries.description: DirectDrawCreate into 004d3794, then IDirectDraw::SetCooperativeLevel (vtable +0x50) with MainWindow_Handle and flags 0x57 (FULLSCREEN | ALLOWREBOOT | NOWINDOWCHANGES | EXCLUSIVE | ALLOWMODEX). Returns 1 when both succeed, else 0. Video_ToggleFullscreen calls it. VSHELL's Display_CreateDirectDrawExclusive is the same without ALLOWMODEX.

entries.name: DDraw_SetModeAndCreateSurfaces
entries.description: (width, height, bpp): IDirectDraw::SetDisplayMode on 004d3794 (slot +0x54); on success releases the back surface 004d379c, the primary 004d3798 and the palette 004d37a0, and creates the primary (slot +0x18) into 004d3798: below a display width (004d25c2) of 640 a ModeX flip chain with one back buffer (caps 0x204218) whose back surface it fetches into 004d379c (GetAttachedSurface, slot +0x30), otherwise a single primary (caps 0x4200). A failed create is retried once without DDSCAPS_VIDEOMEMORY (0x4000). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. Video_ToggleFullscreen calls it.

entries.name: DDraw_Release
entries.description: Clears the screen (Screen_ClearToBlack) when a DirectDraw object exists, releases the back surface 004d379c, the primary 004d3798, the palette 004d37a0 and the DirectDraw object 004d3794 (slot +8 each, nulling the globals), and ClipCursors the pointer to the whole screen. Video_ToggleFullscreen calls it on the way back to a window, and 00465288 once its message loop ends.

entries.name: Video_ToggleFullscreen
entries.description: Fullscreen/windowed switch on the flag at 004d25e2. Going fullscreen: saves the window rect to 004d3750, takes the window topmost at the game resolution via AdjustWindowRectEx + SetWindowPos, ClipCursors the pointer into it, centres it and hides the software cursor; failure posts WM_QUIT. Coming back: restores the saved rect. Reached from the left system button and from Help_Show, which runs it first so raising the on-line manual leaves fullscreen.

entries.name: Video_LeaveFullscreen
entries.description: Video_ToggleFullscreen when the full-screen flag 004d25e2 is set, otherwise nothing. Key_WndProcHook calls it for [Alt+Tab] (0x20f), [Ctrl+Esc] (0x401) and [Alt+Esc] (0x201) instead of passing those codes on.

entries.name: Help_Show
entries.description: WinHelpA(mainWindow, path, HELP_CONTENTS, 0), after Video_ToggleFullscreen drops the game back to a window when 004d25e2 says it is fullscreen.

entries.name: Math_MeanVec3Short
entries.description: Component-wise (a + b) >> 1 of two 3-short vectors into the static at 004d3bdc, whose address it returns. Its one caller is FlightModel_Step, averaging this tick's angular rates with last tick's before integrating the attitude.

entries.name: Math_IntegrateVec3IntOverTick
entries.description: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick over a 3-int vector, in place, returning it. It reads each component as a SHORT and writes back an int, so a component past 0x7fff is truncated before integration.

entries.name: Math_IntegrateVec3ShortOverTick
entries.description: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick over a 3-short vector, in place, returning it. The short-stride twin of Math_IntegrateVec3IntOverTick.

entries.name: FlightModel_Step
entries.description: The flight model. Settles, in order: the throttle setting at state+0x1e, the airspeed it demands (throttle interpolated across the type's minimum..maximum airspeed, biased by pitch attitude at Q10 250 nose-down against 62 nose-up), sideslip drag, the three angular rates, the new attitude, and the velocity vector in that attitude. It moves nothing -- it produces the world velocity Razor_MovementTick integrates. Turning is bank-driven: the heading rate is -roll >> fm[30] and is applied on top of the integrated attitude. Attitude is integrated as a rotation MATRIX from the mean of this tick's rates and last tick's, with the eulers read back out, so a vertical climb does not gimbal. The fifth argument, a literal 1 at both call sites (Razor_ApplyFlightInput, Flyer_ApplyFlightCommand), is never read.
entries.signature: void __cdecl FlightModel_Step(int *input, int *state, short *flightModel, int *wingDestroyed, int unused)

entries.name: Time_GetCoarseTicks
entries.description: (GetTickCount() - startTick) >> 4, i.e. elapsed time in 16 ms units (62.5 Hz). The mission clock gadget (HudClock_Tick) advances one displayed second per 0x3c=60 of these units, so the original's clock runs ~4% fast. This is the coarse UI/event timebase and is NOT the same thing as SimTickDelta, which Sim_MainTick reads from a separate per-frame timing struct.

entries.name: Time_AdvanceCoarseTick
entries.description: Subtracts 0x10 from Time_GetCoarseTicks' start tick (004d3bfc), moving the 16 ms clock on by one tick. Ghidra had no function here. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Time_AdvanceCoarseTick (00465a2c).

entries.name: Time_InitSimClock
entries.description: SimTickDelta = 0x100 and 004d3bea = 0x100, 004d3bf4 = 1000, 004d3bec/004d3bee/004d3bf0/004d3bf6 = 0x7d, and 004d3bf8/004d3bfc = GetTickCount(). Sim_InitMissionSession calls it after Light_CreateMissionSun, before DBSim_LoadScriptDat.

entries.name: Time_ElapsedToQ8Clamped
entries.description: (unit, elapsed): (elapsed << 8) / unit clamped to [0x40, 0x1c2], returned in AX (the decompile drops the return). Time_BeginSimTick computes SimTickDelta with unit 004d3bec and 004d3bea with unit 004d3bee through it.

entries.name: Time_BeginSimTick
entries.description: Spins until 40 ms have elapsed (25 Hz frame cap), then sets SimTickDelta = clamp((elapsedMs << 8) / 125, 0x40, 0x1c2). SimTickDelta is Q8 with 1.0 = 125 ms, so rate units are per-125 ms.

entries.name: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick
entries.description: Q8mul(SimTickDelta, rate), clamped to signed 16-bit range. Core 'apply a per-unit-time rate as this tick's delta' primitive.

entries.name: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick2
entries.description: (rate): Math_Q8Multiply(004d3bea, rate) clamped to +/-0x7fff: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick with the second Q8 delta, the one Time_BeginSimTick computes with unit 004d3bee. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_IntegrateRateOverTick2 (00465b50).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00467858; compared with VSHELL 00465b50

entries.name: Math_RateFromTickDelta
entries.description: (delta): (delta << 8) / SimTickDelta, the inverse of Math_IntegrateRateOverTick: the per-unit rate that yields delta this tick. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_RateFromTickDelta (00465b84).

entries.name: Math_IntegrateRateWithRemainder
entries.description: (value, remainder): value = clamp(value * SimTickDelta >> 8, +/-0x7fff) in place, and remainder = the low 8 bits of |value * SimTickDelta| shifted left 2, or 0x3ff when the product overflows, with value's sign. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_IntegrateRateWithRemainder (00465ba4).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004678a8; compared with VSHELL 00465ba4

entries.name: Math_MulTickDelta64
entries.description: (x): (int64)x * SimTickDelta. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_MulTickDelta64 (00465c08).

entries.name: Math_CountupTimerTick
entries.description: (rec): the short at rec+1 += SimTickDelta; returns it. Math_CountdownTimerTick's mirror. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_CountupTimerTick (00465c1c).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0046792c; es2_naming.py match against VSHELL 00465c1c

entries.name: Math_CountdownTimerTick
entries.description: Countdown-timer tick over a 3-byte packed record. THE COUNTER IS THE SHORT AT +1 FROM THE PASSED POINTER, NOT AT +0: rec[+1] -= SimTickDelta, clamped at 0, returns the new value in AX. Verified across all 40 call sites -- each passes a base whose sibling code reads or writes the short one byte higher (mech+0x258 with the word at +0x259, mount+0x30 with the refire counter at +0x31, rocket+0x5c with the counter at +0x5d). Records sit in stride-3 runs: mech+0x258/0x25b/0x25e and +0x264/0x267/0x26a, globals 0x4a9ee6/0x4a9ee9. The leading byte is untouched by this function, and for all four global instances (0x4a9be8, 0x4a9bec, 0x4a9ee6, 0x4a9ee9) is never read or written anywhere in DBSIM -- only ever address-taken -- so its meaning is still OPEN, not settled as padding. Rocket_TickUpdate's use reloads the counter from ROCKETS.DAT +0x08, which is the exhaust-flame cell-anim and NOT a seeker target-reacquire.
entries.source: docs/simulation/dbsim-physics-notes.md; disassembly of 00467944 + all 40 call sites

entries.name: Timer_SetShort
entries.description: (rec, value): the short at rec+1 = value * 004d3bf6 * 0x100. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Timer_SetShort (00465c5c).

entries.name: Timer_CountUp
entries.description: (rec): the int at rec+1 += SimTickDelta; returns it. Timer_CountDown's mirror. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Timer_CountUp (00465c84).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0046798c; es2_naming.py match against VSHELL 00465c84

entries.name: Timer_CountDown
entries.description: Generic countdown step in the simulation's timer unit (about 0.49 ms per count, not a millisecond): subtracts SimTickDelta from the int at p+1, clamps at 0, returns it. Taking p+1 rather than p is why the AI behaviour block's dwell countdown sits at an unaligned +0x05 with a spare byte at +0x04. Mech_AiTick passes &block+0x04, so descriptor+0x04 is a dwell time in timer units.

entries.name: ActionTimer_SetDelay
entries.description: (timer, value): stores value << 11 at timer+1, converting the file's delay into the simulation's timer counts. DBSim_BuildActionTimerRecord and ActionTimer_Tick call it.

entries.name: Math_RateLimitedMoveToward
entries.description: Generic per-tick turn/slew-rate limiter: moves current toward target by at most step, returns remaining error. Used by rocket guidance and the shield recharge tick.
entries.signature: short __cdecl Math_RateLimitedMoveToward(short *current, short target, short step)

entries.name: Math_RateLimitedMoveTowardInt
entries.description: 32-bit twin of Math_RateLimitedMoveToward (004679d8), the same operation on a short. Steps *current toward target by step without overshooting and returns the remaining gap, or 0 on arrival. The flight model uses it for airspeed, which is an int where every rate a walker slews is a short.
entries.signature: int __cdecl Math_RateLimitedMoveTowardInt(int *current, int target, int step)

entries.name: VolumeGroup_Ctor
entries.description: (group, a, b, c, d): clears the 0x1e volume pointers and the count byte +0x78, sets VolumeGroup_BufferSize to 0x400, then VolumeGroup_SetGroup(group, a, b, c, d) -- what VolRStream_SetGroup runs on an existing group. VolRStream_SetGroup builds g_VolumeGroup with it.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize
entries.description: (size): stores max(size, 0x80) in VolumeGroup_BufferSize. Sim_Run calls it with 0x200 immediately before the only VolRStream_SetGroup call; when that call creates the group, VolumeGroup_Ctor stores 0x400 over it before any volume is loaded. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize.

entries.name: Path_JoinSkipDrive
entries.description: (dir, name): copies dir, or the empty string at 004a08a8 when it is null, into the static buffer 004d3c38, appends name without a leading 'X:' drive prefix and returns the buffer. VolumeGroup_SetGroup builds each volume's path with it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Path_JoinSkipDrive.

entries.name: Path_SkipDrive
entries.description: (path): returns path + 2 when path[1] is ':', else path. VolumeGroup_SetGroup compares loaded volume names through it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Path_SkipDrive.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_SetGroup
entries.description: (group, mask, extension, dir, dirFirst): the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_SetGroup without its assert: removes the volumes whose flags +0x20 share no bit with mask, returns when the group holds 0x1e volumes, then scans 'vol\*<extension>' with findfirst/findnext twice, once under dir and once without it (dirFirst nonzero puts the dir pass first), adding each file whose 'vol\<name>' matches no loaded volume's name (+8, compared through Path_SkipDrive) with VolumeGroup_AddVolume(group, Path_JoinSkipDrive(dir, name), mask). Sim_Run's call passes extension '.vol'.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00467bd4; strings at 004a08a9 and 0049f4b6

entries.name: VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume
entries.description: (group, index): Volume_Dtor(volume, 3) on the volume at index, shifts the later pointers down one, decrements the count byte +0x78 and clears the freed last slot. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume without its asserts.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_AddVolume
entries.description: (group, path, mask): Volume_LoadVolume(path, mask, VolumeGroup_BufferSize) and, when it loads, inserts the volume so the list stays in descending order of the byte at volume +0x1c (read from the volume header), then increments the count byte +0x78. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_AddVolume.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_LoadVolume
entries.description: (group, path): returns 0 for a null path or a full group (0x1e volumes); otherwise, unless a loaded volume's name (+8) equals path, VolumeGroup_AddVolume(group, path, 0xffffffff); returns 1. VolRStream_LoadVolume calls it on g_VolumeGroup. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_LoadVolume without its assert.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_FindEntry
entries.description: Tries Volume_FindEntry (0047ccec) on each volume in a VolumeGroup (volume pointers from +0, count byte at +0x78) in order and returns 1 at the first hit. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_FindEntry.

entries.name: Raster_SetShadeRampDimensions
entries.description: Raster_SetShadeRampDimensions(shadeLevels, depthSlices) -> DAT_004d3d38 / DAT_004d3d3c, plus a 1/n reciprocal table. Sole caller is World_LoadTheater, which passes the world<N>.rmp header's own two int32s (32 and 12 in every retail file) straight through -- which is what fixes Raster_ShadeRampRow's row arithmetic.

entries.name: Raster_SetVisibilityRange
entries.description: Sets DAT_004a08c4, the far limit Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance measures against. Sole caller is Terrain_DrawCellQuad, per cell, with grid[+0x10c] << grid[+0x108] -- the HeightGrid's view radius in cells scaled to world units. Retail zones land on 40960, 81920 or 163840 world units (246 m, 492 m, 983 m).

entries.name: Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance
entries.description: Sets DAT_004a08c8, the depth-slice byte offset Raster_ShadeRampRow adds: zero for anything inside half the visibility range (DAT_004a08c4), otherwise Math_Q16Multiply(t, depthSlices - 1) * shadeLevels * 256. That is the original's distance fog, and it is what the world<N>.rmp's 12 height slices are for. Called per drawn object (FUN_0042876c, with the object's own distance), per terrain cell (Terrain_DrawCellQuad), and with zero from TexPoly_DrawAtPoints.

entries.name: Raster_ShadeRampRow
entries.description: Raster_ShadeRampRow(shade) = ((shade * (DAT_004d3d38 - 1) + DAT_004a08c8) & 0xffffff00) + ShadeRampTable -- the base of one 256-byte row of the theater's world<N>.rmp, indexable directly by palette index. DAT_004d3d38 is the ramp's shade-level count (32 in every retail file) and DAT_004a08c8 a whole number of 8192-byte depth slices set from the drawn object's distance by Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance. Both flat poly renderers call it with a literal 0x80, which with 32 levels is row 15.

entries.name: Raster_SetupTexturedSpan
entries.description: Per-vertex setup for the textured/Gouraud span fills. In its param_6 == 2 (Gouraud) branch it computes each vertex's ramp row as shade * (DAT_004d3d38 - 1) + DAT_004a08c8 << 8 -- the same arithmetic as Raster_ShadeRampRow, depth bias included. Together with Raster_DrawPolygon's mode-1 branch this is why the Gouraud and textured paths fog by the same rule as the flat ones, even though neither renderer calls Raster_ShadeRampRow itself. Its param_1 (positions, stride 3 int32) and param_2 (UV corners, stride 2 int32) are both walked one entry per vertex for param_3 vertices, and param_3 is the poly's own vertex count (poly+8). That is why a 3-vertex TSTexture4Poly is textured from the first three of the four corners its caller always writes -- see docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md, 'Three-vertex texture polys'.

entries.name: Raster_DrawPolygon
entries.description: Polygon submit: (vertexCount, vertices, mode, atlasPage, shadeLevelPtr, transparencyFlag). Clips, builds edges, then walks scanlines calling the span routine the mode selects -- 0 Raster_SpanTextured (u,v only), 1 Raster_SpanTexturedShaded (u,v plus a shade level taken from param_5), 2 Raster_SpanTexturedGouraud (u,v plus a third interpolant, which Raster_DrawPolygon reads from slot +0x14 of its edge records; it sits at +0x18 in the vertex record Raster_SetupTexturedSpan fills). param_4 goes to DAT_004a09b4 as the atlas page; param_6 to DAT_004a09ac, which selects the span routine's transparent half. In mode 1 it turns *param_5 into a ramp row in place -- shade * (DAT_004d3d38 - 1) + DAT_004a08c8, the depth bias included -- so this path fogs by the same rule as Raster_ShadeRampRow without calling it. See Raster_SetupTexturedSpan for the mode-2 equivalent.

entries.name: Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear
entries.description: (verts, uvs, vertexCount, bitmapHandle, shades, shadeMode, worldSpaceFlag, transparency): the perspective-correct textured polygon fill, DBSIM's counterpart of VSHELL's TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB. Terrain_DrawCellQuad uses it for cells inside twice the near-distance threshold (DAT_0049aad0) and Raster_SetupTexturedSpan, which maps affinely, for the rest. Per vertex it stores 1/z (1 << DAT_006c60ac over the view depth) at +0x14 and u and v << 16 times 1/z; clips (Raster_ClipPolygonX/Y) and builds edges (Raster_BuildEdgeTables, flags 0xb, 0xf in shade mode 2). Each row is drawn in runs of 2^k pixels: k = 10 when the row's ends have equal 1/z, else 4, 5, 6 or 7 as |delta 1/z| >> 12 is over 3000, over 1000, over 300 or less; at each run's end u and v are recovered with Int64Pair_Q16Divide and the run is filled affinely by Raster_SpanTexturedShaded, or Raster_SpanTexturedShadedClipped through a run list. With DAT_0049f278 set, the row's start and its last partial run's end take Raster_BuildEdgeTables' quadratic fit instead of a divide. shadeMode is DAT_004aab30: mode 1 turns shades[0] into one ramp row for the polygon, DAT_004a09c4 = (shade * (shadeLevels-1) + depthBias) << 8, the Raster_ShadeRampRow formula; mode 2 builds that row per vertex and interpolates it along the edges, but no span reads it. Terrain only ever fills shades[0] (from the cell's baked byte), so retail terrain is flat-shaded per triangle, mode 1.

entries.name: Raster_ClipEdgeCrossX
entries.description: (x, a, b, out, flags): writes the vertex where edge a-b crosses the vertical line x into out and returns 1; returns 0 and writes nothing when either endpoint lies exactly on the line. Interpolates from the endpoint with the smaller x by t = (x - lo.x) / (hi.x - lo.x) (Q16): y always, and by flags as in Raster_BuildEdgeTables -- 8 depth (+8), 1 u and v (+0xc, +0x10), 1 with 2 w (+0x14), 4 shade (+0x18). Raster_ClipPolygonX's crossing routine.

entries.name: Raster_ClipPolygonX
entries.description: (count, in, out, flags): one Sutherland-Hodgman pass of a ring of 7-dword vertices against x in [ctx+0x210, ctx+0x218 + 1] of the installed render context (006c5ff4). An inside vertex is copied; an edge that crosses a bound gets the crossing from 00469790 (passed the bound, both vertices, the output slot and flags), kept when that returns non-zero. Returns the output count. The first stage of Raster_DrawPolygon and Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear.

entries.name: Raster_ClipEdgeCrossY
entries.description: Raster_ClipEdgeCrossX for a horizontal line y, interpolating x from the endpoint with the smaller y. Raster_ClipPolygonY's crossing routine.

entries.name: Raster_ClipPolygonY
