entries.name: Heap_InitInBuffer
entries.description: (heap, size, block): heap+0 and +8 = block, +4 = size, +0xc and +0x10 = size & ~7; the block's first dword 0, second size & ~7, and the tag 'KLBF' (0x46424c4b) at block+8. Sim_Run sets up 006bb37c over the 0xb0000 bytes at 00604f88 with it when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set.

entries.name: Memory_IsAllocatedBlock
entries.description: Returns 1 when ptr (header at ptr-8) lies inside the pool's [base, base+size) and its header holds 'KLBA' (0x41424c4b). The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_IsAllocatedBlock.

entries.name: Memory_LargestFreeBlock
entries.description: Returns the size of the largest block on the pool's free list minus 0x6c, clamped to 0. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_LargestFreeBlock.

entries.name: Memory_Alloc
entries.description: First-fit allocation from a src\mymem.cpp pool (pool, size, trackLow): the same algorithm and 'KLBA'/'KLBF' block tags as VSHELL's Memory_Alloc, with the asserts compiled out. Mem_New and Mem_NewArray use it on the pool at 006bb37c.

entries.name: Memory_Free
entries.description: Returns a block to a src\mymem.cpp pool, tagging it 'KLBF' and coalescing it with its free neighbours: VSHELL's Memory_Free without the asserts. Mem_Delete calls it.

entries.name: Mem_HeapAlloc
entries.description: calloc(1, size), adding the block's own recorded size to the heap byte count at 006bb390, which Mem_Delete subtracts from. The large-request path of Mem_New and Mem_NewArray, and what Arena_Push allocates an arena with. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_HeapAlloc; returns the calloc pointer in EAX (the decompile drops it).

entries.name: Mem_New
entries.description: The global operator new, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_New. A size below the pool's free byte count (006bb388, pool 006bb37c + 0xc) and no larger than the pool's largest free block less 0x6c (00476dd0) is carved from the pool by Memory_Alloc; anything else goes to Mem_HeapAlloc. Both paths hand back zeroed memory, which is what settles what an uninitialised object field holds at construction. Mem_Delete is its pair; Mem_NewArray is the same with 8 bytes added.

entries.name: Mem_NewArray
entries.description: The global array operator new, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_NewArray: Mem_New with 8 bytes added to the size. It returns the block start, so the 8 bytes are unused slack, not a header. Rtl_VectorNew allocates through it and callers pass count * element size; Mem_DeleteArray is its pair. Also the fallback Arena_Alloc drops to when there is no arena or the arena is full.

entries.name: Mem_Delete
entries.description: The global operator delete, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_Delete: a pointer for which Memory_IsAllocatedBlock holds on the pool at 006bb37c goes back to it through Memory_Free; anything else is _free'd and its size at p[-1] subtracted from the heap byte count at 006bb390. Pairs with Mem_New.

entries.name: Mem_DeleteArray
entries.description: The global array operator delete, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_DeleteArray: body identical to Mem_Delete (a tagged block in the pool at 006bb37c goes back through Memory_Free, anything else is _free'd and its size at p[-1] subtracted from the heap byte count at 006bb390). Rtl_VectorDelete frees through it.

entries.name: JoystickDevice_CtorBase
entries.description: (this, kind, ...): GL_ClaimGlobal(this, kind, this); when this is the instance claimed for kind (006c5f38[kind]), Joystick_Enumerate(this, kind); then sets the resolution field +0x16 to 7. JoystickDevice_Ctor runs it.

entries.name: Joystick_Enumerate
entries.description: joyGetDevCapsA over joystick ids 0 and 1 only, into JOYCAPS blocks at DAT_006bb3fc (stride 0x194), stamping each MMRESULT at DAT_006bb724; then one joyGetPosEx per device. Sets each JOYINFOEX's dwSize to 0x34 and dwFlags to 0xccf -- X, Y, Z, R, POV, BUTTONS, CENTERED, USEDEADZONE. U and V are never requested.

entries.name: Joystick_Poll
entries.description: Polls both sticks with joyGetPosEx and packs the 0x12-byte device reading. Stick 0's X and Y always; its Z as the throttle and R as the rudder when JOYCAPS_HASZ/HASR, else stick 1's X and Y. dwPOV is matched against exactly 0/18000/27000/9000 into bits 0-3 of one byte -- no diagonal matches. Stick 1's button mask is OR'd in shifted left by stick 0's wMaxButtons.

entries.name: Joystick_NormaliseAxes
entries.description: Maps each of the four raw joyGetPosEx axes onto a signed byte: (raw << 8) / 0xffff - 0x80, giving -0x80..+0x80. Joystick_ReadWithResponse takes the width as 1 << the resolution field +0x16, which JoystickDevice_CtorBase sets to 7. No JOYCAPS min/max is consulted -- the game leans entirely on Windows' own calibration.

entries.name: Joystick_ReadAxisSigns
entries.description: (device, out): returns 0 when bit 0 of the device's first byte is clear. Otherwise Joystick_NormaliseAxes into the device's four axes (+4..+0x10), replaces each with its sign (-1, 0 or +1), copies the four axes and the int16 at +0x14 to out and returns 1. Joystick_ReadWithResponse reads response mode 2 through it, and its deadzone step then zeroes every axis.

entries.name: Input_QueryCapabilities
entries.description: Rebuilds the eight-byte joystick capability block at 006bb72c on every call and returns it: +0 is 2 when stick 1 enumerated (DAT_006bb728 zero), otherwise 1, never 0, +2 the button count (DAT_006bb438 + DAT_006bb5cc clamped to 8), and +4/+5/+6 whether a throttle, rudder and hat are present, from the device flag word's bits 0, 1 and 4. The controls panel greys its rows against it, and Input_SetThrottleLeverMode reads +4.

entries.name: KeyboardDriver_Ctor
entries.description: (this, arg): GL_ClaimGlobal(this, 1, this); when this is the claimed keyboard instance (006c5f3c) runs 00477940 and, if that succeeds, registers atexit 00477890, Assert hook 00477894 and a KeyListener_Register subscription with callback 00477970. KeyboardInputDevice_Ctor runs it.

entries.name: KeyboardDriver_Init
entries.description: (this): WndProcHook_Register(00477ae0), then returns bit 0 of this+0. KeyboardDriver_Ctor runs it for the claimed keyboard instance and goes on only when it returns non-zero.

entries.name: Keyboard_FlushKeys
entries.description: (keyboard): empties KeyEventRing (read index 006bb938 = write index 006bb934) and clears bit 1 (keys pending) of the keyboard object's flags. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Keyboard_FlushKeys.

entries.name: Keyboard_PopKey
entries.description: (keyboard): pops the next 16-bit code off KeyEventRing (read index 006bb938, write index 006bb934) and returns it, 0 when the ring is empty; clears bit 1 (keys pending) of the keyboard object's flags when it empties the ring. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Keyboard_PopKey.

entries.name: KeyListener_Register
entries.description: Appends to the ten-slot {enabled, wantedCodes, callback} keyboard subscriber table at 006bb93c that Key_WndProcHook walks. wantedCodes is a NUL-terminated list of the low bytes (scancodes) that subscriber wants; the first callback to return 1 consumes the code.

entries.name: KeyListener_RegisterCopy
entries.description: A byte-identical copy of KeyListener_Register (00477a0c) at a different address: appends {1, wantedCodes, callback} to KeyListenerTable. Input_BuildSourceTable registers callback 00477970 with wanted codes 0049eae4 through it.

entries.name: Key_WndProcHook
entries.description: The keyboard filter in the same ten-slot table ahead of MainWndProc as Mouse_WndProcHook. Catches WM_KEYDOWN/UP (0x100/0x101) and WM_SYSKEYDOWN/UP (0x104/0x105), translates the virtual key through the 223-entry scancode table at 004a1104, ORs in 0x800 for Shift, 0x200 for Alt, 0x400 for Ctrl and 0x80 for a key-up, then offers the code to the ten subscribers at 006bb93c; whatever none of them claims goes into the 256-entry ring at 006bb734.

entries.name: Raster_BuildEdgeTables
entries.description: (count, vertices, flags): turns a clipped ring of 7-dword screen vertices {x, y, depth, u, v, w, shade} into per-row edge entries. Drops repeated points (fewer than 3 left gives 0 rows); walks forward from the top vertex (smallest y, rightmost) into the right-edge table at 006bbe14 and backward from the top-leftmost one into the left-edge table at 006c0914, until each reaches the bottom y. Each 10-dword row entry: +0 x, +4 depth (flag 8), +8/+0xc u and v (flag 1), +0x14 shade (flag 4); flag 2 makes u and v 64-bit (high dwords at +0x20/+0x24, shifted by 10 instead of 8) and adds w at +0x10 and a quadratic fit of u/w and v/w through the edge's ends and middle at +0x18/+0x1c. Returns 006c5414 = {first row (clamped to ctx+0x214), row count, left table, right table}.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00477c3c; table roles from Raster_DrawPolygon's use (+8 start x, +0xc end x)

entries.name: ObjectPool_QueueForDelete
entries.description: Appends an object to a deferred-delete queue (pointer array at queue+0, int16 count at queue+4), used with g_FlatObjDeleteQueue and the other pools' queues. Nothing is destructed here, and the append does not test the capacity at queue+6.

entries.name: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue
entries.description: Drains the queue ObjectPool_QueueForDelete fills: destructs each entry through its vtable +0x08, returns it to the pool, then zeroes the count.

entries.name: Stub_ReturnZero
entries.description: Returns 0. Vtable +0x0c of every simulation-object, projectile, effect and FlatObj table, and of the table at 00498064; what the slot is for is not established.

entries.name: Drawable_GetRadiusZero
entries.description: DRAWABLE vtable +0x10, kept by MAT_OBJ, REG_OBJ, TINY_OBJ, their TS_ variants, LightSource, SMOKE and DummyDrawable: returns 0. TS_OBJ and everything below it install SimObject_GetShapeRadius in the slot.

entries.name: Drawable_Dtor
entries.description: DRAWABLE vtable +0x08 (004a14bc, RTTI 'DRAWABLE', 0xc bytes): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, reinstalls DRAWABLE's table, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0.

entries.name: ANSequence_NextFrame
entries.description: Plain ANSequence vtable +0x20: frame >= frameCount-1 ? frame : frame+1, i.e. CLAMPS rather than wrapping. That clamp is the only way a one-shot's end is observable, because the end-of-sequence test everywhere is frame == nextFrame. Every retail chassis carries exactly one non-cyclic sequence and its chassis record's death-animation id names it. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] sequence, [EBP+0xc] frame.

entries.name: ANSequence_PrevFrame
entries.description: Plain ANSequence vtable +0x24: frame != 0 ? frame-1 : 0, i.e. holds at the first frame. Args derived from disassembly: only [EBP+0xc] is read, the sequence pointer being unused on this arm.

entries.name: ANSequence_FrameShortOfTarget
entries.description: ANSequence vtable +0x28 (004a6864), (seq, frame, target, flag): 1 when frame < target, or frame == target and flag is 0; otherwise 0. AnimThread_FindTransition asks it of a transition's destination sequence, for forward play, with the thread's +0x1c as the flag. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 0046301c.

entries.name: ANSequence_FrameShortOfTargetBackward
entries.description: ANSequence vtable +0x2c (004a6864), ANSequence_FrameShortOfTarget's mirror for backward play: 1 when frame > target, or frame == target and flag is 0. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 00463048.

entries.name: ANCyclicSequence_NextFrame
entries.description: ANCyclicSequence vtable +0x20: frame < frameCount-1 ? frame+1 : 0, i.e. wraps. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] sequence, [EBP+0xc] frame, plain RET.

entries.name: ANCyclicSequence_PrevFrame
entries.description: ANCyclicSequence vtable +0x24: frame != 0 ? frame-1 : frameCount-1, i.e. wraps. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] sequence, [EBP+0xc] frame.

entries.name: ANCyclicSequence_FrameShortOfTarget_Always
entries.description: ANCyclicSequence vtable +0x28 (004a6828): returns 1 in AX. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 004630b0.

entries.name: ANCyclicSequence_FrameShortOfTargetBackward_Always
entries.description: ANCyclicSequence vtable +0x2c (004a6828): returns 1 in AX. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 004630bc.

entries.name: ShapeInst_Construct
entries.description: TSShapeInstance constructor. Reads the node count from shape->animList+0x16 into shapeInst+0xc, then allocates the three per-node arrays ONCE: dirty flags at +0xe, local transforms at +0x12 (stride 0xc) and world transforms at +0x16 (stride 0x20). Seeds the locals from the anim list's default transforms and calls ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms. Nothing reallocates these, so an instance stays sized and numbered by the shape it was built with -- root 0 for a machine -- whatever root Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel later swaps in.

entries.name: ANShapeInstance_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ANShapeInstance_Dtor (004631bc).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00478850 VSHELL 004631bc: differs only in callee labels and decompiler typing; RTTI ANShapeInstance vtable slot

entries.name: ShapeInst_CountThreads
entries.description: (shapeInst): returns how many of the ten thread slots from shapeInst+0x1a are filled, counting up to the first null.

entries.name: ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority
entries.description: (shapeInst): bubble-sorts the thread slots at shapeInst+0x1a ascending by AnimThread_SequencePriority, swapping only on strictly greater, so equal priorities keep registration order. ShapeInst_RegisterThread runs it on every registration and AnimThread_StepAll after every advance; since ShapeInst_EvalAllNodeLocals runs last-to-first, the lowest priority wins a node two threads cover.

entries.name: ShapeInst_RegisterThread
entries.description: (shapeInst, thread): stores thread in the first empty of the ten slots at shapeInst+0x1a and re-sorts them with ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority; returns 1, or 0 when all ten are taken. ShapeInst_AddThread registers through it.

entries.name: ShapeInst_RemoveThread
entries.description: (shapeInst, thread): finds thread in the ten slots at shapeInst+0x1a that ShapeInst_RegisterThread fills, shifts the slots after it down by one and zeroes the tenth; returns 1, or 0 when thread is not registered. Does not free the thread.

entries.name: AnimThread_StepAll
entries.description: Advances every thread on the shape instance by the timestep (AnimThread_Advance, 00479614), last slot first over ShapeInst_CountThreads slots, then re-sorts the slots with ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority. Then, if a first thread exists, writes its ramped root transform (AnimThread_ReadRootTransform, 00478fa8) into the leading slot of the world-transform array at shapeInst+0x16 -- the first thread after the sort, which is not always the one ShapeInst_SeedRootTransform seeded before the advance.

entries.name: ShapeInst_EvalAllNodeLocals
entries.description: Runs AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals (004799a4) over every thread the shape instance holds (thread pointers from shapeInst+0x1a upward), passing the local-transform array (shapeInst+0x12) and the dirty-flag array (shapeInst+0xe). The loop runs last-to-first and AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals overwrites each covered node's local transform unconditionally, so the first slot's write is the one left standing for a node several threads cover -- and the slots are kept in ascending sequence priority by ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority. See docs/formats/dts-node-posing.md, 'Several threads on one shape'.

entries.name: ShapeInst_ReadRootTransform
entries.description: (shapeInst, out): AnimThread_ReadRootTransform of the first thread into out, or the identity transform (0x4000 on the diagonal) when the instance has none.

entries.name: ShapeInst_SeedRootTransform
entries.description: (shapeInst, transform): when the instance has a thread, AnimThread_WriteRootTransform(first thread, transform) and copies the 0x20-byte transform into world slot 0 (shapeInst+0x16). The first thread is the first after ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority. SimObject_ApplyRootMotion seeds identity through it before stepping.

entries.name: ShapeInst_ComposeChildTransform
entries.description: Same expansion as ShapeInst_ExpandRootTransform, then concatenates the result onto the parent's world transform (FUN_0047f914) into the destination slot.

entries.name: ShapeInst_ExpandRootTransform
entries.description: Expands one 12-byte local transform into a 0x20-byte world transform with no parent: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 over the three leading shorts, and the trailing three shorts widened to the ints at +0x14/+0x18/+0x1c. Confirms the 0xc-byte local record layout is [eulerX, eulerY, eulerZ, x, y, z] as shorts.

entries.name: ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms
entries.description: Composes the per-node WORLD transform array (shapeInst+0x16, stride 0x20, indexed by transform id) that everything else reads -- e.g. Mech_TargetRelativeToPilot (0041ef14) and the cockpit eye. Walks the relation list (pairs of shorts at animList+0xc, count at animList+10): parent == -1 goes through ShapeInst_ExpandRootTransform (00478b10), otherwise ShapeInst_ComposeChildTransform (00478ab8) against the parent's already-built world transform. Dirty-flag driven off shapeInst+0xe (bit 0 = local changed, bit 1 = world rebuilt, so children follow), and memsets the flag array when done.

entries.name: ShapeInstance_StepAnimation
entries.description: Advance threads, evaluate keyframes into per-node local transforms, rebuild world transforms. In call order: AnimThread_StepAll (004789a0) then ShapeInst_EvalAllNodeLocals (004789f4, which runs AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals per thread) then ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms (00478b58). The keyframe interpolation is the middle step, so poses are re-blended every time this is called. Cadence: the sole caller is SimObject_ApplyRootMotion (0040250c), which Mech_IntegrateMotion runs once per sim tick -- poses are evaluated per TICK, not per rendered frame. DBSIM has no separate render rate to be per-frame at: FUN_004677bc spin-waits the whole loop to 40 ms (25 Hz), so tick and frame are the same thing in the original. A port with a fixed 25 Hz tick matches vanilla pose cadence exactly, however fast it renders.

entries.name: ShapeInst_PushModelTransform
entries.description: (shapeInst, scratch, root): saves g_ModelTransformPtr, Transform_Concat(root, saved, scratch), installs scratch with Raster_SetModelTransform and returns the saved pointer. ANShapeInstance_Render brackets TSShapeInstance_Render with it and ShapeInst_PopModelTransform. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ShapeInst_PushModelTransform (004635a4).

entries.name: ShapeInst_PopModelTransform
entries.description: (shapeInst, saved): Raster_SetModelTransform(saved) when saved is non-null. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ShapeInst_PopModelTransform (004635d0).

entries.name: ANShapeInstance_Render
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ANShapeInstance_Render (004635e4). It differs from VSHELL's: VSHELL runs Transform_Ctor on the local transform first and reads the shape through TSShapeInstance_GetShape; DBSIM's makes no Transform_Ctor call and reads the shape at instance +4 inline.
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00478c98 VSHELL 004635e4: differs as described; RTTI ANShapeInstance vtable slot

entries.name: ANShape_Render
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ANShape_Render (00463630).

entries.name: AnimThread_Ctor
entries.description: (thread, animList): stores animList at +0, AnimThread_SetSequence(thread, 0, 0, 0), zeroes the 0x20 bytes at +0x2e and stores 0x4000 in the int16s at +0x2e, +0x34 and +0x3e. Returns thread. ShapeInst_AddThread builds each 0x52-byte thread with it.

entries.name: AnimThread_SequencePriority
entries.description: (thread): returns the int16 at +6 of the sequence the thread is playing (shape->sequences[thread+4]) -- the field after the tick count and before the ground-movement flag at +8, the file's 'priority'.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00478d80; ANSequence file layout

entries.name: AnimThread_LoadFrameGroundMovement
entries.description: Called on every animation frame advance. If the sequence ground-movement flag is set, loads Transforms[transformIndices[frame * numParts]] -- part index 0, the root node -- into the thread ground translation (+0x22/24/26) and rotation (+0x28/2a/2c) and sets the ground-move flag at +0x20.

entries.name: AnimThread_CommitGroundMovement
entries.description: On frame exit, folds the completed frame full ground transform into the thread stored transform.

entries.name: AnimThread_UncommitGroundMovement
entries.description: Inverse of AnimThread_CommitGroundMovement, for backward playback.

entries.name: AnimThread_ReadRootTransform
entries.description: Returns scale(groundTransform, thread[0x1c]/thread[0x1e]) composed onto the thread stored transform, where the fraction is intra-frame accumulator over frame duration. Inverse of AnimThread_WriteRootTransform.

entries.name: AnimThread_WriteRootTransform
entries.description: Stores inverse(scale(groundTransform, frac)) composed with the incoming transform. Paired with AnimThread_ReadRootTransform so that seeding identity and reading back yields the exact per-tick root-motion delta.

entries.name: AnimThread_SetSequence
entries.description: (thread, sequence, frame, offset): cuts a thread straight to a sequence and frame, abandoning any target. Stores the sequence at +4 and +8 and the frame at +6, the sequence's vtable +0x20 answer for the frame at +0xa, the intra-frame offset at +0x1c and the frame's duration from the sequence's 6-byte frame table (+0xc) at +0x1e, loads the frame's ground movement (AnimThread_LoadFrameGroundMovement), then clears the target (+0x16 and +0x18 = -1, +0x1a = 0), sets +0xc to -1 and +0x50 to 1. AnimThread_SeekToPosition, ShapeInst_AddThread and the locomotion ticks call it.

entries.name: AnimThread_SeekToPosition
entries.description: Parks a thread at a Q14 fraction of a sequence instead of playing through it: sums the sequence's frame durations, scales the position by Q14 x (total - 1) (FUN_0047dfb4), walks the frames subtracting durations, and installs the resulting frame + intra-frame offset with AnimThread_SetSequence (004791a0). The only caller pair is the two torso ticks, which pass (unsigned)angle >> 2 -- this is how a turret angle becomes a pose. See docs/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: AnimThread_FindTransition
entries.description: (thread): walks the current sequence's (+4) frames from the current frame (+6) when playing backward (rate +0x4e < 0) or the next frame (+0xa) otherwise, stepping with the sequence's vtable +0x24 (previous) or +0x20 (next) until it laps, and scans each frame's transitions (8-byte records at anim +0x1e, a frame's first index and count in the sequence's 6-byte per-frame table at +0xc) for one whose destination (+2) is the target sequence (+0x16). A match is armed: duration (+0) to +0x12, the target to +0xe, destination frame (+4) to +0x10, transform index (+6) to +0x14. With no target frame (+0x18 == -1) that is final; otherwise the destination sequence's vtable +0x2c (backward) or +0x28 (forward) is asked, with (destination frame, target frame, +0x1c), whether it lands on the near side of the target, and the scan continues when it does not. Leaves the scan frame (+0xc) at -1 when nothing qualifies. AnimThread_SetTarget calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004792c8; ported as AnimationThread.FindTransition

entries.name: AnimThread_SetTarget
entries.description: Asks playback to reach a sequence via whatever transition leads there rather than snapping to it: writes thread+0x16/+0x18/+0x1a, clears the at-target bit and runs AnimThread_FindTransition to find the transition. frame -1 means any frame will do; flags bit 0 stops playback dead on arrival. This, not AnimThread_SetSequence, is how the death fall is started, so sweeping the latter's call sites alone does not enumerate what plays a sequence. Args derived from disassembly: four pushes with ADD ESP,0x10 at 00416db5.
entries.signature: void __cdecl AnimThread_SetTarget(void *thread, short sequence, short frame, short flags)

entries.name: AnimThread_SetPlaybackRate
entries.description: Writes the playback rate to thread+0x4e; restarts the sequence when the sign flips.

entries.name: AnimThread_Advance
entries.description: Advances one animation thread by dt * thread[0x4e] >> 8, crossing frames forward or backward and driving the ground-movement load and commit hooks.

entries.name: AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals
entries.description: The keyframe interpolator. For each animated column of the playing sequence, reads the transform-pool index at (sequence, frame) and at (nextSequence, nextFrame); if the two indices match, copies the 12-byte local transform straight; otherwise calls Anim_BlendKeyframeTransforms (00492600) with a Q10 interpolant of ((frameAccumulator * 0x400 + frameDuration/2) / frameDuration) -- the SAME elapsed-frame fraction AnimThread_ReadRootScaled already ramps root motion by. Writes into the shape instance's per-node local array (shapeInst+0x12, stride 0xc, indexed by transform id) and sets that node's dirty byte in shapeInst+0xe. Columns whose part id is 0 are skipped entirely, so transform 0 keeps its default and never takes an animated pose. Thread field offsets confirmed here: +4 sequence, +6 frame, +8 nextSequence, +10 nextFrame, +0x1c frameAccumulator, +0x1e frameDuration.

entries.name: Assert_Ctor
entries.description: (assert): Assert_Emit(0, 1, 0, 0, 0), counts the object live and returns it. The static initialiser 00479c40 builds the assert logger 006c574c with it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_Ctor (0044de50).

entries.name: Assert_RunHooks
entries.description: Calls each hook on the list at 006c575c with the severity. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_RunHooks.

entries.name: Assert_Report
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_Report: (logger, severity, condition, file, line, message). Severities 4-6 run the hooks (Assert_RunHooks), emit (Assert_Emit), call Assert_Emit again with severity 1 (which has no case and prints nothing), call 00464fc8 and MainWindow_KillTimer, PostQuitMessage(0) and _exit(1); lower severities only emit.

entries.name: Assert_AddHook
entries.description: Pushes a callback onto the assert hook list at 006c575c; aborts with an assert_abort_notify message if the allocation fails. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_AddHook.

entries.name: Assert_Format
entries.description: (buffer, severity, file, line, message): formats 'Assert::<severity name>: Line <line> in "<file>"' with the severity-name table at 004a160c, then appends ': <message>' when there is one. Assert_Emit builds its line with it.

entries.name: Assert_SetLogDir
entries.description: (dir): copies dir into 006c5760, the directory Assert_LogPath puts in front of the log name, and returns that buffer. Sim_Run calls it with 004d2840.

entries.name: Assert_LogPath
entries.description: Builds the assert log's path in 006c5860: the directory string at 006c5760 followed by the log name. Returns it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_LogPath.

entries.name: Assert_AppendToLog
entries.description: (text): opens Assert_LogPath() with _open(0x901, 0x180) = O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_APPEND, aborting on failure; while 004a1628 is set it first writes an 80-byte line of dashes and clears the flag; then writes the text and CR LF and closes. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_AppendToLog.

entries.name: Assert_Emit
entries.description: Formats and outputs one assert by severity (the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_Emit): 2 prints the message, 3 counts (006c58b0) and shows the formatted line in a MessageBoxA titled 'Error', 4 prints it and shows the box, 5 prefixes 'Internal Error: Please call Sierra...' and shows the box, 6 prints the break notice. 3-5 call 004668b0 first.

entries.name: ClassItem_RegisterBucket
entries.description: (entries, count): appends an {entries, count} bucket to the registry ClassItem_FindHandler searches (006c58b8, count 004a16a8), unless count is 0. Light_ResetSystem registers g_TSObjectTypeRegistry with it; GL_RegisterClassItems and AN_RegisterClassItems register the tables at GL_ClassItemTable and AN_ClassItemTable.

entries.name: ClassItem_LoadResource
entries.description: Generic polymorphic resource loader entry point (stream, mode). Reads an 8-byte type tag via ClassItem_ReadTypeTag, looks up a handler via ClassItem_FindHandler, calls its loadFn.

entries.name: Arena_AllocDup
entries.description: Second emitted copy of Arena_Alloc (0047a1bc), same code: (size, arena) bump-allocates from {base, limit, cursor}, falling back to Mem_NewArray with no arena or no room. The 3Space shape readers call this copy (GridShape_ReadFromStream, TSShape_ReadFromStream, TSPartList_ReadFromStream, ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames), as VSHELL's shape constructors call its Arena_Alloc (00403dc4).

entries.name: Arena_Alloc
entries.description: Bump-allocates from the {base, limit, cursor} arena it is handed: advances the cursor and returns base + old cursor, with NO zeroing of its own. A null or exhausted arena falls back to Mem_NewArray. Every weapon mount comes from here, out of the arena MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts pushes -- and that arena is calloc'd, so a mount block is zero however it was served.

entries.name: ClassItem_PeekTypeTag
entries.description: (stream, tag[2]): saves the stream position (vtable +4), reads the 8-byte class type tag into tag (-1, 0 beforehand), and when no handler is registered for it (ClassItem_FindHandler) and 004a16ac is set, copies it to 006c59a8 and reads the rest of the header into 006c59b0 (ClassItem_TryEveryLoader). Seeks back to the saved position unless the status is 2 (end of data), then runs 0047a768 on the stream.

entries.name: ClassItem_Skip
entries.description: (stream): reads a class item's 8-byte type tag and seeks past its body, the size in the tag's second dword rounded up to an even length, then runs 0047a768 on the stream. Shape_LoadAllRoots and BaseType_ResolveShape skip items with it.

entries.name: ArenaStack_Push
entries.description: (a, b, c): increments the depth 004a16d8, stores the three dwords in the 12-byte entry at 006c59ec + depth*12 and points the current-arena pointer 006c58b4 at it. Arena_Push calls it.

entries.name: ArenaStack_Pop
entries.description: Decrements the depth 004a16d8 and points 006c58b4 back at the entry below. Arena_Pop calls it.

entries.name: ClassItem_FindHandler
entries.description: Searches a registry of (idArray, count) bucket pairs for a matching type tag, returns a 12-byte {id, loadFn, extra} descriptor.

entries.name: ClassItem_TryEveryLoader
entries.description: (stream, tag): walks the 004a16ac registry buckets at 006c5958 ({entries, count}) and calls each 12-byte {id, loadFn, extra} entry's loadFn with (006c59a8, tag, stream), returning 1 at the first that returns nonzero and 0 when none does. ClassItem_PeekTypeTag and ClassItem_ReadTypeTag fall back to it for a tag no handler is registered for.

entries.name: ClassItem_TagTotalSize
entries.description: (tag): an item's total length from its 8-byte class type tag: the size dword at +4 as it is when the high nibble of byte 3 is set, else size + 8 (the tag itself) rounded up to an even length. WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks steps through chunks with it.

entries.name: ClassItem_DebugPrintType
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VshellClassItem_DebugPrintType (00404120).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 0047a488 VSHELL 00404120: differs only in callee labels and decompiler typing; RTTI GLRegion vtable slot

entries.name: ClassItem_ReadTypeTag
entries.description: Reads the 8-byte type tag from a resource stream, called by ClassItem_LoadResource.

entries.name: ClassItem_CloseItem
entries.description: (stream): reads one byte at a time with Stream_ReadByte until the stream position (vtable +4) reaches the end offset (+8) of the item frame ClassItem_CurrentFrame points at, or the stream status goes non-zero. ClassItem_LoadResource runs it after the item's loader, so an item whose loader read short still leaves the stream at its end. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ClassItem_CloseItem (ClassItem::closeItem) without its assert and overrun report.

Returns 0 when the status is nonzero; _reads count bytes when count is nonzero, a failure going to FileRWStream_SetIoError and a short read setting status 2 and returning 0; returns 1. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's FileRWStream_Read.

entries.description: (s): cuts s after its last character above a space (code > 0x20), dropping trailing blanks and control characters; returns s. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Str_TrimRight (00450428).

entries.name: Path_Split
entries.description: (path, drive, dir, name, ext): the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Path_Split (0045045c).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0047d08c, diffed against VSHELL 0045045c

entries.name: Str_Concat4
entries.description: (a, b, c, d, out): concatenates the non-null strings a to d into out, or into the static buffer 006c5e2f when out is null, and returns it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Str_Concat4.

entries.name: Math_Atan2Bam
entries.description: atan2 in binary angles, arguments (x, y): 0 is +x and +y is a quarter turn, so in screen space 0 is right and a quarter turn is down. The result is masked to 14 bits and shifted left 2.

entries.name: Vec2_DistanceBetween
entries.description: Copies a 2D point, subtracts another (Vec2_Subtract) and returns the approximate magnitude (Vec2_Magnitude) -- the distance primitive the HUD waypoint indicator uses.

entries.name: Point3I_DistanceBetween
entries.description: (a, b): copies a, subtracts b (Vec3_Subtract) and returns Point3I_Magnitude of the difference. LightManager_SelectLightsForObject and LightManager_SelectLightsUnconditional measure light distances with it.

entries.name: Math_AsinBam
entries.description: Arcsine of a Q14 sine as a binary angle. Takes the magnitude (restoring the sign at the end), rounds it to a multiple of 4, and below 0xe00 * 4 (about 0.875) reads the coarse table at 004a1e54 at a further 8x step; above it reads the fine table at 004a05d4 (entry 0x1000, for 1.0, is 0x4000, a quarter turn).

entries.name: Vec3I_Cross
entries.description: (a, b, out): out = a x b on int32 triples (x = a.y*b.z - a.z*b.y, y = a.z*b.x - a.x*b.z, z = a.x*b.y - a.y*b.x), 32-bit products; returns out. ObjList_SortCompareSegment builds its plane normal with it.

entries.name: Math_Dot2S
entries.description: (a, b): a.x*b.x + a.y*b.y on int16 pairs, as an int. Mech_ApplyTerrainSlopeToSpeed calls it.

entries.name: DotProductVec3Short
entries.description: Literal 3-component dot product on two three-short vector pointers: a.x*b.x+a.y*b.y+a.z*b.z, no scaling/clamping. Called (via the Light_ComputeShadeForFace accessor wrapper FUN_0048d99b) with the poly's Normal-index point and a directional light's own direction vector -- confirms the type-1 (directional) lighting term in Light_ComputeShadeForFace is a plain dot product, i.e. the poly's 'Normal' auxiliary point genuinely holds a normal-like vector (not a position), consistent with TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest's use of them: the normal and centre are auxiliary vertex-index fields used for facing math, not literal mesh geometry.

entries.name: DotProductVec3Int
entries.description: Same as DotProductVec3Short but on int (not short) components -- used by Light_ComputeShadeForFace's type-2 (point light) branch after converting the light-to-face displacement into ints.

entries.name: Vec3I_DotSign
entries.description: (a, b): the sign of the dot product of two int32 triples, summed in 64 bits: 1 when it is zero or more, -1 when negative. ObjList_SortCompareSegment tests plane sides with it.

entries.name: Math_DivMod64
entries.description: (out{quotient, remainder}, int64 *n, d): stores n / d and n % d as two int32s and returns out.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude2D
entries.description: Sqrt-free 2D magnitude approximation: max(|dx|,|dy|) + min(|dx|,|dy|)/2 -- the octagonal estimate, exact on axis and up to ~11.8% high on a diagonal. The 2D counterpart of Math_FastMagnitude3D. This is the distance both HUD distance readouts display, so the original's own on-screen ranges carry that error.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude3D
entries.description: Sqrt-free 3D magnitude approximation: L + M*0.34375 + S*0.25 (sorted |dx|,|dy|,|dz|). Verified via raw disassembly (three CMP/XCHG sort pairs, SAR+ADD coefficient chains). Direction-dependent error: about 8% low on the body diagonal, up to about 8.7% high elsewhere. Reused for collision bounding-sphere radius, sound placement, LOD size and the rocket's proximity beep (round to camera, not a fuze).

entries.name: Math_TransposeRotation2D
entries.description: Swaps the two off-diagonal shorts of a Q14 2D rotation matrix, which for a rotation is its inverse. Ai_KeepFormation uses it to take the delta from a formation post into the group leader's own frame.

entries.name: Transform_TransposeRotation
entries.description: Transposes a transform's rotation in place (swaps +2/+4, +8/+0xc, +0xa/+0xe), which inverts a pure rotation; the rank byte is left alone.

entries.name: Math_MapRange
entries.description: Five-argument linear remap of a value from one range onto another, with a rounding bias of one less than the input span, signed to match the output's direction. Its one caller is the flyer branch of Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph, which maps airspeed from 0..AirSpeedMax onto 0..typeRec+0xc2 -- a flyer's record does not describe the walker top speed the other branch divides by.

entries.name: Math_Mul32To64
entries.description: (out int64, a, b): stores the 64-bit product a * b and returns out.

entries.name: Math_ISqrt
entries.description: (n) -> floor(sqrt(n)) for unsigned n, bit by bit: BSR for the top bit, then trial additions of halving powers of two against the running square. 0 for 0.

entries.name: Math_CosBam
entries.description: Cosine of a 16-bit binary angle in Q14: rounds the angle to a 16-BAM step ((a >> 4) + bit 3), takes its magnitude, and reads the quarter-turn table at 004a25dc (indices 0-0x400, 16384 at 0, 11585 at 0x200, 0 at 0x400) directly below a quarter turn and negated as table[0x800 - i] above it.

entries.name: Math_Q16Divide
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point divide: ((int64)a << 16) / b.

entries.name: Math_Q16Multiply2
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point multiply, (int64)a*b >> 16: a second copy of Math_Q16Multiply with an identical body.

entries.name: Math_Q16Multiply
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 16. Used by MechType_InitOne to rescale a mech type's speed fields by a Q16 ratio built with Math_Q16Divide.

entries.name: Math_Q8Multiply
entries.description: Q8 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 8. Verified via raw disassembly (SHRD EAX,EDX,0x8) matching the decompiler's >>8 exactly.

entries.name: Math_Q10Multiply
entries.description: Q10 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 10. Used in the shield-balance code; also builds the HUD's speed-display scale factor in MechType_InitOne.

entries.name: Math_Q14Multiply
entries.description: (int a, int16 b): Q14 fixed-point multiply, (int64)a*b >> 14. The scale of the Q14 sine/cosine table at 004a25dc.

entries.name: Plane_FromPointNormal
entries.description: (plane, point, normal): scales normal to length 0x800 component by component through Math_Mul32To64 and Math_DivMod64 by its magnitude -- Point3I_ExactMagnitude when every component lies strictly within +/-15001 (0x3a99), Point3I_Magnitude otherwise -- and sets plane.d = -(point . normal').

entries.name: Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect
entries.description: (plane{nx,ny,nz,d}, segment{start[3],end[3]}, out[3]) -> bool. Denominator = dot(n, end-start), numerator = -(dot(n, start) + d); rejects a parameter outside the segment by comparing the pair with the sign of the denominator rather than dividing first, then applies it per component through a 64-bit multiply (0047de78) and divide (0047dd21).

entries.name: Poly_SplitByPlane
entries.description: (plane, poly, front, back) -> bool, each polygon {count, int32 {x, y, z} points*} with the output point buffers supplied by the caller. Walks the edges from the last vertex, classifying each with Plane_ClassifyPoint: a front vertex (1) goes to front, a back vertex (-1) to back, one on the plane (0) to both, and an edge that crosses from one side to the other adds its Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect point to both before the vertex. A side left with fewer than 3 points is emptied. When each side either ends that way or received no vertex strictly on its own side (a polygon lying in the plane), front becomes a copy of the whole input. Returns 1 only when both sides are non-empty, and empties both for an input of fewer than 3 points. Its two callers, 00494ba8 and 00494d4c, each call it at six sites, keeping front each time and swapping the in and out lists with Dword_Swap.

entries.name: Point3I_ExactMagnitude
entries.description: (p): Math_ISqrt of x*x + y*y + z*z, summed in 32 bits.

entries.name: Math_ISqrt_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Math_ISqrt.

entries.name: Math_Mul32To64_Thunk
entries.description: Forwarder to Math_Mul32To64 that returns its out pointer.

entries.name: Math_DivMod64_Thunk
entries.description: Forwarder to Math_DivMod64 that returns its out pointer.

entries.name: Point3IPair_Ctor
entries.description: (p): runs maybe_Point3I_Ctor on p and p+0xc. Poly_SplitByPlane calls it on a local. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Point3IPair_Ctor (004514ab).

entries.name: Plane_ClassifyPoint
entries.description: (plane{nx,ny,nz,d}, point[3]) -> int: 1 when dot(n, point) > -d, 0 when equal, -1 when less, the dot product through DotProductVec3Int_Thunk. Poly_SplitByPlane sorts vertices with it.

entries.name: Math_BuildRotation2D
entries.description: Builds a 2x2 Q14 rotation matrix for a binary angle into a short[4] -- {cos, sin, -sin, cos}, both looked up in the quarter-turn table at 004a25dc.

entries.name: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14
entries.description: Builds a 3x3 rotation matrix (9 Q14 fixed-point shorts + 1 mode byte, 10 shorts total output) from three short Euler angles (param_1), using a sin/cos lookup table at DAT_004a25dc (1024-entry quarter-wave table, angle unit = 0x10000 per full circle, i.e. raw/65536*360 = degrees). Has a fast-path when the X and Y angle components are both zero (2-axis-only case, cos/sin of Z alone); otherwise builds the general 3-axis matrix via the standard trig-table-driven approach (the same trig-table technique as the simulation's other rotation math). Called by Light_CreateMissionSun with angles (-6000, 0, 21000) -- confirms the sun's direction is computed, not stored as a literal vector.

entries.name: Rotation_Concat
entries.description: (a, b, out): composes two 20-byte rotations (nine Q14 int16 entries, rank byte at +0x12) into out, with +0x2000 rounding and the rank fast paths of Transform_Concat but no translation. A rank below 1 on either side copies the other; two rank-1 (Z-only) operands give a rank-1 result with entries 4-7 zeroed and entry 8 = 0x4000; any other mix gives rank 2. Debris_Throw composes a piece's yaw onto the spawn attitude with it; FlightModel_Step also calls it.

entries.name: Transform_RotationToEuler
entries.description: (rotation short[9] Q14, out ushort[3]): out[0] = Math_AsinBam(m[5]). At a quarter turn either way (gimbal lock) out[1] = 0 and out[2] = Math_Atan2Bam(m[0], m[1]); otherwise out[1] = Math_Atan2Bam(m[8], -m[4]) and out[2] = Math_Atan2Bam(m[3], -m[2]). Returns out.

entries.name: Transform_Concat
entries.description: Composes two 32-byte transforms (9 Q14 int16 matrix entries, a rank byte at +0x12, three int32 translations at +0x14/+0x18/+0x1c) into a third. Branches on both operands' rank bytes -- translation only, Z-rotation only, or full 3x3 -- as an optimisation, not a behavioural difference. Every hit test builds its object-to-muzzle frame with this.

entries.name: Transform_RotateVector2D
entries.description: (vec2, transform, out): rotates an int16 2D vector by the transform's XY block alone (terms +0..+6), Q14 with +0x2000 rounding, into int16 out.

entries.name: Math_Rotate2DPoint
entries.description: Rotates an {int x, int y} point by a Math_BuildRotation2D matrix, rounding at Q14.

entries.name: Transform2D_ApplyToPoint
entries.description: (point int[2], xf, out int[2]): out = the point through the 2x2 Q14 matrix at xf (Math_BuildRotation2D's short[4] layout, rounded by +0x2000 >> 14) plus the int translation at xf+8/+0xc.

entries.name: RotateVectorByMatrixQ14
entries.description: Matrix-vector multiply: rotates param_1 (three shorts) by the 3x3 Q14 matrix param_2 (as built by BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14), writing the result to param_3. Has fast-paths for the matrix's degenerate mode byte (param_2[9]) similar to the matrix builder's own fast path. Called by Light_CreateMissionSun as rotate((0,0x1000,0), sunRotationMatrix) -- i.e. the sun's direction is 'straight up' rotated by the fixed Euler angles, not an arbitrary hand-authored vector.

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToShortPoint
entries.description: Transforms an int16 point by a 32-byte transform into an int32 result, Q14 with round-to-nearest (+0x2000 before the >>14). Same math as Transform_ApplyToPoint, narrower input; used for collision sphere centres.

entries.name: Transform_RotatePoint
entries.description: (point, transform, out): Transform_ApplyToPoint without the translation -- the rotation alone on an int32 point, Q14 with +0x2000 rounding and 64-bit intermediates, with the rank-byte fast paths. The rigid-inverse idiom rotates the negated translation through a transposed copy with it.

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToPoint
entries.description: Transforms an int32 point by a 32-byte transform, Q14 with round-to-nearest and 64-bit intermediates. The int-width counterpart of Transform_ApplyToShortPoint.

entries.name: GL_ClaimGlobal
entries.description: (this, index, instance): clears this+0 and stores instance at GL global index (006c5f38 + index*4, the table GL_GetGlobal reads) when that slot is still empty, so the first object constructed for an index becomes GL_GetGlobal(index)'s and is the one its own init runs for. MouseDriver_Ctor passes 2, KeyboardDriver_Ctor 1, InputDriverKind0_Ctor 0, GLDisplay_Ctor 7 (the current display).

entries.name: GL_SetGlobal
entries.description: (index, value): stores value at 006c5f38 + index*4 and returns 0, unless value is non-null and the slot already holds one, when it stores nothing and returns 1.

entries.name: MouseDriver_Ctor
entries.description: (this): GL_ClaimGlobal(this, 2, this), constructs the fields at +4, +0xe, +0x16, +0x24 and +0x2c, and when 004809d8 returns this runs Mouse_Init and, if that succeeds, registers 004806f8 with Assert_AddHook. MouseInputDevice_Ctor runs it.

entries.name: MouseDriver_Dtor
entries.description: (this, flags): when GL_GetGlobal2 returns non-zero, Mouse_Shutdown(this) and GL_ClearGlobal(this, 2); Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. MouseInputDevice_Dtor runs it. The InputDriverKind0_Dtor shape.

entries.name: Mouse_Init
entries.description: Registers Mouse_WndProcHook into the WndProc filter chain and, when bit 0 of the driver's first dword is set, runs the empty Mouse_InitNoOp, saves the bounds rect to +0x24 (MouseDriver_GetBounds) and sets it to {0, 0, 0x140, 400} with MouseDriver_SetBounds. Returns that bit.

entries.name: Mouse_Shutdown
entries.description: (driver): Mouse_Init's inverse. When bit 0 of the driver's first dword is set: WndProcHook_Unregister(Mouse_WndProcHook), clears that dword and restores the bounds Mouse_Init saved at +0x24 with MouseDriver_SetBounds; returns 1. Returns 0 otherwise. MouseDriver_Dtor runs it.

entries.name: MouseDriver_GetBounds
entries.description: (driver, out): copies the pointer's bounds rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at driver+0xe..+0x1a into out.

entries.name: MouseDriver_SetBounds
entries.description: (driver, record): sets the bounds rect at driver+0xe..+0x1a from the record's first four ints and the shorts at driver+0x1e/+0x20/+0x22 from its +0x10/+0x12/+0x14.

entries.name: Mouse_InitNoOp
entries.description: An empty function (PUSH EBP; MOV EBP,ESP; POP EBP; RET). Mouse_Init calls it when bit 0 of the driver's first dword is set.

entries.name: MouseDriver_GetState
entries.description: Returns 006c5fd4, the mouse driver's {int x, int y, int16 buttons} record.

entries.name: Stub_ReturnZeroCopy
entries.description: Returns 0 -- a second copy of Stub_ReturnZero. Gau_RovingGunsightWidget calls it and ignores the result.

entries.name: MouseListener_Register
entries.description: Appends {enabled=1, eventMask, callback} to the first free slot (of 10) in the mouse-listener table at DAT_006c5f5c that Mouse_DispatchEvent fans events out to. Returns the slot index or -1 if full. Same {enabled,mask,fn}-triple-array idiom as WndProcHook_Register's table and the keyboard-binding table read by FUN_00477ae0 -- DBSIM reuses this shape for at least three unrelated subscriber lists.

entries.name: MouseListener_Unregister
entries.description: Clears slot param_2's enabled flag in the mouse-listener table at DAT_006c5f5c.

entries.name: Mouse_RecomputeScale
entries.description: Recomputes DAT_004a2de4/DAT_004a2de8, the 16.15 fixed-point (gameSize<<0xf)/clientSize factors Mouse_DispatchEvent uses to rescale window-client mouse coordinates into game space. Reads the window's current client rect, so it must be re-run on resize.

entries.name: Mouse_WarpCursorToPoint
entries.description: Rescales a game-space point to client coordinates (inverse of Mouse_RecomputeScale's factor), ClientToScreens it and calls SetCursorPos. Three callers, all gated on a live mouse device: Gau_RovingGunsightWidget centres the pointer on the gunsight as the cockpit is built, AlertPanel_SetFocus puts it on the focused widget's centre, AlertPanel_Leave restores the position the panel saved at its own +0x302.

entries.name: Mouse_DispatchEvent
entries.description: Rescales a raw window-client-space (x,y) from Mouse_WndProcHook into the game's internal coordinate space via a fixed-point factor (Mouse_RecomputeScale), packs the current L/R button-held bitmask into DAT_006c5fdc, and calls every enabled entry of the 10-slot mouse-listener table (DAT_006c5f5c, registered via MouseListener_Register) whose event mask has the event kind's bit set.

entries.name: Mouse_WndProcHook
entries.description: Registered into the MainWndProc filter chain (see WndProcHook_Register). Catches WM_MOUSEMOVE(0x200)/WM_LBUTTONDOWN(0x201)/WM_LBUTTONUP(0x202)/WM_RBUTTONDOWN(0x204)/WM_RBUTTONUP(0x205) -- none of which MainWndProc's own switch handles -- and forwards each to Mouse_DispatchEvent with a kind id (0=move,1=ldown,2=lup,3=rdown,4=rup) and a button-held bitmask built from wParam.

entries.name: GL_GetGlobal2
entries.description: Returns GL_GetGlobal(2) in EAX (the decompile drops the return). MouseDriver_Ctor and MouseDriver_Dtor compare their object with it.

entries.name: InputDriverKind0_Ctor
entries.description: (this, word): GL_ClaimGlobal(this, 0, this); when this is GL_GetGlobal0's instance, InputDriverKind0_Init(this, word) and, if that returns non-zero, Assert_AddHook(00480ab7, an empty function). Returns this. Sim_InitMissionSession builds a 6-byte one with 0x26d3 into 004d258e; 0045bfcc runs it before InputDevice_Register(this+6, kind 0). The MouseDriver_Ctor shape.

entries.name: InputDriverKind0_Dtor
entries.description: (this, flags): when GL_GetGlobal0 returns non-zero, the empty InputDriverKind0_DtorNoOp and GL_ClearGlobal(this, 0); Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. 00461e74 runs it on 004d258e with 3.

entries.name: InputDriverKind0_Init
entries.description: (this, word): stores the int16 at this+4 and returns this+0 & 1. GL_ClaimGlobal has just cleared this+0, so from InputDriverKind0_Ctor it returns 0 and the assert hook is never added.

entries.name: GL_ClearGlobal
entries.description: (unused, index): stores 0 at 006c5f38 + index*4.

entries.name: GL_GetGlobal0
entries.description: GL_GetGlobal(0), the kind-0 input driver's slot of 006c5f38; returns it in EAX (the decompile drops it).

entries.name: InputDriverKind0_DtorNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. InputDriverKind0_Dtor calls it before GL_ClearGlobal.

entries.name: GLViewport_Ctor
entries.description: GLViewport constructor (vtable 004a2e28, RTTI name 'GLViewport', 0x239 bytes, over GLBase 004a3380): constructs the rect at +0x210 (RectI_Ctor) and +0x220, then copies the viewport held at GL_GetGlobal7()+0x40 (0x81 dwords from +4, then +0x208..+0x22c) and clears +0x230, +0x231 and +0x235. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLViewport_Ctor.

entries.name: Raster_InstallRenderContext
entries.description: Installs a render context: DAT_006c5ff4 = ctx, and PTR_DAT_004a362c = ctx+4, its clip block. The block's mode sits at ctx+0x208 -- 0 none, 1 the single rect at ctx+0x210, 2 the region list the block holds -- and CockpitView_ApplyViewState is what puts a view's context into mode 2 with the herc's .HD/.ED canopy regions. THE ctx+4 OFFSET IS LOAD-BEARING for reading brush code: the fill brush Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch reads at clipBlock+0x228 is the field callers write as ctx+0x22c, and the line brush at clipBlock+0x224 is ctx+0x228.

entries.name: GLViewport_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLViewport_Dtor (00452943).
entries.source: ES2DecompileContainingBatch DBSIM 00480cc3 / VSHELL 00452943: identical after normalisation; RTTI GLViewport vtable 004a2e28 slot +0x18

entries.name: GL_GetPtr40
entries.description: Returns the dword at +0x40 of its argument. GLViewport_Ctor calls it on GL_GetGlobal7's object to find the viewport it copies. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GL_GetPtr40.

entries.name: GLDisplay_SetClipBlock
entries.description: (display, block): stores block at display+0x44 and, when display is GLDisplay_GetCurrent's, installs it with Raster_SetClipBlock. Raster_InstallRenderContext calls it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLDisplay_SetClipBlock (00452993).

entries.name: GL_RegisterClassItems
entries.description: ClassItem_RegisterBucket(GL_ClassItemTable, 9): makes the nine GL resource classes loadable by ClassItem_LoadResource. Screen_CreateBackBuffer calls it, as does the undisassembled code at 00480ad4 (a function from 00480ac4 that then builds a 0x48-byte object with GLDisplay_CtorAndOpen).

entries.name: GLBase_GetClassTag
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLBase_GetClassTag (004529cc).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00480dfc VSHELL 004529cc: identical after normalisation; RTTI GLBase vtable slot

entries.name: GLBase_GetStreamSize
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLBase_GetStreamSize (004529d4).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00480e04 VSHELL 004529d4: identical after normalisation; RTTI GLRegion vtable slot

entries.name: GLBase_GetMemorySize
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLBase_GetMemorySize (004529dc).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00480e0c VSHELL 004529dc: identical after normalisation; RTTI GLRegion vtable slot

entries.name: GLBase_ReadFromStream
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLBase_ReadFromStream (004529e4).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00480e14 VSHELL 004529e4: identical after normalisation; RTTI GLPrimitive vtable slot

entries.name: GLBase_WriteToStream
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's GLBase_WriteToStream (004529ec).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00480e1c VSHELL 004529ec: identical after normalisation; RTTI GLBase vtable slot

entries.name: GLDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: (display, kindName): GL_ClaimGlobal(display, 7, display), so the first display built becomes GL_GetGlobal7's current one; registers an assert hook and an atexit handler, clears the flags dword +0 and stores GLDisplay_DriverIdFromName(kindName) at +0x30, the driver id Raster_SelectRenderTarget installs. Does not open the display. Screen_CreateBackBuffer and HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster build 0xa0-byte 'BMP_8' displays with it, then GLDisplay_Open.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00480e4c; name table at 004a2ea0

entries.name: GLDisplay_CtorAndOpen
entries.description: (display, kindName, bitmapHeader): GLDisplay_Ctor's body followed by GLDisplay_Open(display, bitmapHeader).

entries.name: GLDisplay_Dtor
entries.description: (display, flags): GLDisplay_Close(display), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster destroys its BMP_8 display with it.

entries.name: GLDisplay_Open
entries.description: (display, bitmapHeader): when flags +0 is still zero: the first call ever (counter 004a2e44) runs GLDisplay_FirstOpenNoOp; then RasterDriver_OpenDisplay(driver id +0x30, bitmapHeader, display+4). On success allocates two 0x22c-byte clip blocks (RectI at +0x20c), initialises the first for the display's width and height (+8, +0xc) with ClipBlock_Init and copies it into the second, stores them at +0x40 and +0x44 (the block GLDisplay_SetClipBlock replaces), zeroes +0x34..+0x3c, sets flags bit 0 and returns 1. Returns 0 when already open or when RasterDriver_OpenDisplay fails.

entries.name: GLDisplay_Close
entries.description: (display): GLDisplay_Open's inverse. When open (flags bit 0): Mem_Delete of the clip block +0x40 (the one at +0x44 is not freed), clears the flags, RasterDriver_CloseDisplay(driver id +0x30, display+4), and decrements the open count 004a2e44, running GLDisplay_LastCloseNoOp when it reaches 0. Returns 0.

entries.name: Raster_SelectRenderTarget
entries.description: (display): makes display the current GL display (global 7) and installs it into the rasterizer. GLDisplay_ClearCurrent always returns 0, so the early return of 1 when a display is already current never runs: the current display is cleared and replaced. Then RasterDriver_InstallRoutines(display+0x30); copies display +0x4..+0x2c to 004a366a.. (004a366a is the row-pointer table Raster_SpanBitmap writes through); calls g_RasterRoutines' SetVisiblePage, SetSourcePage and SetDrawPage slots with +0x34, +0x38, +0x3c; Raster_InstallViewport(+0x40); stores +0x44 at 004a362c; returns 0. Called by HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster, Sim_EndFrame and Screen_CreateBackBuffer.

entries.name: GLDisplay_DriverIdFromName
entries.description: (display, name): looks name up in the three-entry table at 004a2ea0 ('VGA_8', 'VGA_4', 'BMP_8') and returns the matching raster driver id from 004a2eac: 1, 0 or 3; an unknown name returns the terminator 4. display is not read. The decompile drops the return; it is MOV EAX,[EBP+EDI*4-0x10].
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004811e4; tables at 004a2ea0 and 004a2eac

entries.name: GLDisplay_GetAttribute

entries.name: Bitmap_Blit
entries.description: Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, {int x, int y}, flags) -- the engine-wide sprite/background blit. flags bit 1 (value 2) mirrors horizontally, bit 0 (value 1) flips vertically, 3 does both; confirmed at the reticle corner-bracket draw (0044401d..0044403a) which draws one corner sprite four times with flags 0/2/1/3, offsetting x by the bitmap's width field (+6) for flag 2 and y by its height field (+4) for flag 1. Used with flags=2 to produce the cockpit's opposite side view from the single authored side bitmap.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitScaled
entries.description: (bitmap, point, flags, size{w, h}): Bitmap_Blit's scaled twin. Hands the bitmap at +4 to GL_BlitScaled with GL_GetGlobal7; a packed bitmap (+0x12 nonzero) is first unpacked by Bitmap_UnpackToScratch into the buffer at 006c5ffc, which stands in for the data pointer (+0xe) and size (+0xa) for the call and is freed afterwards unless 006c5ff8 is set. VideoMode_BlitBitmap's scaled branch calls it.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked
entries.description: Rotated blit of a bitmap object. When the object's packing type (+0x12) is non-zero, Bitmap_UnpackToScratch unpacks it into DAT_006c5ffc, the object's size (+0xa) and data pointer (+0xe) are swapped to the scratch copy for the blit and restored after, and the scratch is freed unless DAT_006c5ff8 is set. Then Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaledThunk with the object's +4 rows,cols pair.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked(void *bitmap, int *position, int flip, int *size, short angle)

entries.name: Bitmap_UnpackToScratch
entries.description: Unpacks a bitmap object's data (+0xe, length +0xa) into a fresh DAT_006c5ffc buffer sized by the packed data's first dword, through one of two decoder classes chosen by packing type +0x12: 1 (vtable 004a17c8) or 3 (vtable 004a1820). Returns the unpacked size; returns 0 without unpacking for any other type, or when DAT_006c5ff8 is set.

entries.name: HudFont_GlyphWidth
entries.description: One glyph's advance width: the fixed width at font+0xc when that is not -1, otherwise the per-glyph width byte at font+0x2a indexed by char - firstCharCode. Every retail font stores -1 and is therefore proportional.

entries.name: HudFont_MeasureString
entries.description: Sums HudFont_GlyphWidth over a NUL-terminated run. Callers that align a run subtract 1<<XCoordShift from the result to drop the trailing advance past the last glyph.

entries.name: HudFont_CellHeight
entries.description: Returns font+0xa, the glyph cell height (file offset 0x0e; 13 for .HFN, 10 for .DFN). This is the glyph art's height, not the ink height at font+0x16 that labels centre by.

entries.name: HudFont_DrawGlyph
entries.description: Blits one glyph: height from font+0xa (file 0x0e cellHeight), width from HudFont_GlyphWidth, bit depth from font+0x12 (file 0x16, 8 in every retail file), pixels from the pool at font+0x22 indexed through the per-glyph offset array at font+0x26. Draws with its top row at y - font+0x16 (file 0x1a, the ink height), which is the other half of Label_SetRect's vertical rule.

entries.name: HudFont_DrawString
entries.description: Draws a NUL-terminated run with a .DFN/.HFN font at a caller-supplied top-left, advancing the pen by each glyph's own width. A display-wide alignment override at renderContext+0x231 (1 = right, 2 = centre against the field width at +0x235) shifts the whole run first; it is 0 in the cockpit.

entries.name: Raster_DrawLine
entries.description: Draws a line between two {x,y} points in the installed render context, in the pen at clip block +0x224 (mode 0 flat colour, or mode 2), offset by the context's origin when its +0x208 flag is set and clipped against its clip regions.

entries.name: Line_ClipToRect
entries.description: (a, b, rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}): clips the segment a-b in place against the inclusive rect, against y0, x0, y1 and x1 in that order, each time moving the outside endpoint to the crossing computed from it in 64 bits (truncating). Returns 0, leaving the points as they were, when both endpoints lie beyond the same bound; otherwise 1. Raster_DrawLine clips through it for clip mode 1 and for each rect of a clip list.

entries.name: Line_ScanConvertToSpanRegion
entries.description: (a, b, out): writes the int16 span region of a one-pixel line: top row min(y), count |dy| + 1, then an {x0, x1} pair per row -- {x, x} on each row of a vertical line, one row {xmin, xmax} for a horizontal one, and otherwise the run of x a Bresenham walk from the smaller-x end puts on each row. Raster_DrawLine fills the result with the pen's span routine.

entries.name: Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch
entries.description: Generic polygon draw, dispatching on the mode of the brush at *(int*)(clipBlock + 0x228), a {mode, colour} pair. Mode 4 is the line-loop/outline path (edge pairs plus the closing edge); mode 0 resolves the span routine DAT_004a57c4 and calls it as (scanlineList, colour) -- a FLAT FILL of that palette index when the colour's top byte is zero, with a tag-4 lookup when it is 4; mode 6 calls slot 1 of g_RasterRoutines, mode 1 Raster_FillContourPolygon, and modes 5 and 7 Raster_FillBitmapPolygon through slot 33 (004a5848). Raster_DrawPolygonReversed reverses an anticlockwise outline before calling it.

entries.name: Raster_DrawPolygonReversed
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Gfx_FillPolygonReversed (00455b02), identical but for the rel32 call, which goes to Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch.

entries.name: Raster_DrawPolygonEitherWinding
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Gfx_FillPolygonEitherWinding (00455b9b), byte-identical: hands a zero-or-negative shoelace sum to Raster_DrawPolygonReversed, anything else to Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch. PolyFill_Fill fills through it.
