entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ScanConvertToSpanRegion (00456000), byte-identical but for its two absolute addresses (the stack-save slot and the vertical-edge store table at 004865e4).

entries.name: Raster_FillRect
entries.description: Fills a rect through the installed clip block: mode 0 direct, mode 1 intersected with ctx+0x210, otherwise walked against each region in the block's list (rect regions intersected, span regions clipped through FUN_00486af4). Used by the MFD status screen's label backgrounds and its component highlight.

entries.name: Rect_Intersect
entries.description: (a, b, out): intersects two rects {x0, y0, x1, y1} (inclusive) into out and returns out, or 0 when they do not overlap. Raster_FillRect and Region_CopyRectBetweenPages clip with it.

entries.name: SpanList_FromRect
entries.description: (rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}, out): int16 y0 at out+0, the row count y1 - y0 + 1 at out+2, then one int16 pair {x0, x1} per row. Raster_FillRect calls it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's SpanList_FromRect (00457634).

entries.name: Raster_FillSpanList
entries.description: (spans, origin): copies a span list {int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row} to PTR_DAT_004a36a9 translated by origin -- plus (clipBlock+0x20c - +0x21c, +0x210 - +0x220) when clipBlock+0x208 is set -- and fills it with the brush at clipBlock+0x228: mode 0 through g_RasterRoutines slot 0 with the brush colour (a type-4 colour resolved through the table at 004a4fbd), mode 6 through the routine at 004a57c8; other modes return. Clips per the clip mode at clipBlock+0x204: 0 none, 1 the rect at +0x20c (SpanList_ClipToRect), otherwise each region in the block's list.

entries.name: SpanRegion_Intersect
entries.description: (a, b, out): intersects two span regions ({int16 top row, int16 row count, then an {x0, x1} int16 pair per row}) row by row into out; returns out, or 0 when no row overlaps. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's SpanRegion_Intersect. Raster_DrawLine, Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch and Raster_FillRect clip against span regions with it.

entries.name: SpanList_ClipToRect
entries.description: (rect, spans, out): clips a span list {int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row} to rect {x0, y0, x1, y1}: rows outside the rect's rows and leading rows that miss its columns are dropped, x ranges are clamped, and a row that misses after the first hit becomes the empty span {1, 0}; the count ends at the last hit. Writes to out and returns it, or 0 when no row survives. Raster_FillSpanList and Region_CopyRectBetweenPages clip with it.

entries.name: maybe_Cursor_SetImage
entries.description: Empty: returns at once. The cockpit cursor-slot functions call it with a .DCI cursor's bitmap (+4) and hotspot (+8) on the paged path, where they call maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage on the scroll-window path; the name is inferred from those arguments.

entries.name: Cursor_SyncPosition
entries.description: Stores the pointer position in param_1: to DAT_004a3638/3c when DAT_004a365e is set, bracketed by g_RasterRoutines slots 31 and 30 (maybe_ hide/show cursor) when DAT_004a3634 is set; otherwise to DAT_004a3662/66. Driver 3 fills both slots with empty stubs. Driver3_SyncCursorPosition is driver 3's copy of the same routine.

entries.name: Cursor_GetPosition
entries.description: (out): copies the pointer position at 004a3638/004a363c -- the slot Cursor_SyncPosition writes when 004a365e is set -- into out. Gunsight_ClickSurface_Paint, HddCommandScreen_SynthesizeListClick and Input_BuildPlayerDevice read it.

entries.name: Raster_FillContourTriangle
entries.description: Fills a triangle of three {x,y} vertices by interpolating its three palette indices in contour bands: it cuts the triangle at every whole index between the highest and lowest corner and flat-fills each band (Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch, writing the band's upper index into the installed brush's colour) with that index, so a point takes the ceiling of its interpolated index. Equal corners fill flat; a degenerate triangle draws nothing.

entries.name: Raster_FillContourPolygon
entries.description: Brush mode 1 of Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch, (count, points): a polygon shaded per vertex. Maps each vertex's ushort shade from the brush's list at +0xc to a palette index through the ramp the brush colour's low word names (8-byte records at 004a4fbd: +0 entry array, +4 int16 length; entry (shade * length) >> 8), fans triangles from vertex 0 and fills each with Raster_FillContourTriangle, with the brush switched to mode 0 meanwhile. Restores the brush's colour and mode 1 after.

entries.name: Region_CopyRectBetweenPages
entries.description: (region, point): offsets the region's rect by point (and the drawing context's translation), then copies it through g_RasterRoutines_CopyRect: unclipped for clip mode 0, clipped to the context rect (00486890) for mode 1, and per clip-list entry for mode 2 (rects through 00486890, span regions through SpanList_ClipToRect and the routine 004a5810).

entries.name: Region_CopySpansBetweenPages
entries.description: (region, point): Region_CopyBetweenPages for a type-2 region: copies its span list translated by point (and the drawing context's translation when +0x208 is set) into the scratch span buffer 004a36a9 and hands it to the page-copy routine 004a5810 as (spans, point): unclipped for clip mode 0, through SpanList_ClipToRect against the context rect for mode 1, and for mode 2 per clip-list entry (rects through SpanList_ClipToRect, span regions through SpanRegion_Intersect).

entries.name: Region_CopyBetweenPages
entries.description: (region, point): copies the area a region covers from the raster source page to the draw page: 00487ad0 for a type-0 rect, 00487c01 for a type-2 span list. MessagePort_CopyBoxBetweenPages calls it with the raster source and draw pages swapped. A region is {int type; ...}: type 0 carries a rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +4, type 2 a pointer to a span list ({int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row}) at +4.

entries.name: Region_SaveRect
entries.description: (region, buffer): wraps buffer in a stack bitmap header the size of the region's rect (translated by the drawing context's offset when +0x208 is set) and grabs the screen into it with Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch(header, rect, 0).

entries.name: SpanRegion_PixelCount
entries.description: (spans): sums x1 - x0 + 1 over a span list's rows into EAX. Its bytes end at MOV EAX,EDX with no POP, LEAVE or RET, so execution runs on into 00487e5e.

entries.name: Region_SaveSpans
entries.description: (region, buffer), hand-written: Region_Save for a type-2 region. Copies each row of its span list from the screen into buffer through the raster routine 004a5818 (buffer, row, x0, x1), advancing buffer by x1 - x0 + 1. When the drawing context's +0x208 is set it first translates the list into 004a36a9, adding CX + ctx+0x210 - ctx+0x220 to the top row and DX + ctx+0x20c - ctx+0x21c to each x, with ECX and EDX as the caller left them: Region_Save has the region pointer in both.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00487e5e and its call in Region_Save (00487f2d); Region_Save's callers load EDX with the region they push

entries.name: Region_Save
entries.description: (region, buffer): copies the screen pixels a region covers into buffer: Region_SaveRect for a type-0 rect, Region_SaveSpans for a type-2 span list, called with the region in ECX. The message ports, AlertPanel_Enter and CockpitView_SetShakeBand save screen areas with it, each pushing (region, buffer). A region is {int type; ...}: type 0 carries a rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +4, type 2 a pointer to a span list ({int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row}) at +4.

entries.name: Region_PixelCount
entries.description: Returns the number of pixels a region covers: Rect_PixelCount for type 0, 00487e3c for type 2 (span list), 0 otherwise. The message ports size their two save-under buffers with it. A region is {int type; ...}: type 0 carries a rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +4, type 2 a pointer to a span list ({int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row}) at +4.

entries.name: Region_RestoreRect
entries.description: (region, point, buffer): wraps buffer in a stack bitmap header the size of the region's rect (format 8, flags 0x10) and draws it at point with Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch.

entries.name: SpanRegion_Restore
entries.description: (region, point, buffer): for each row of the region's span list, offset by point (and the drawing context's translation when +0x208 is set), hands the row's slice of buffer to the span routine 004a5820 as (src, y, x0, x1), advancing through buffer by each span's width.

entries.name: Region_Restore
entries.description: (region, point, buffer): puts saved pixels back: 00487f6c for a type-0 rect, 00487fb0 for a type-2 span list. The counterpart of Region_Save. A region is {int type; ...}: type 0 carries a rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +4, type 2 a pointer to a span list ({int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row}) at +4.

entries.name: Raster_DrawEllipse
entries.description: (rect): rasterizes the ellipse inscribed in rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} with a midpoint algorithm into a span list at PTR_DAT_004a36ad and fills it with Raster_FillSpanList about the rect's centre. The brush at clipBlock+0x228 decides the shape: mode 0 fills the ellipse; mode 4 draws a one-pixel ring as two span passes with the mode switched to 0 between them and restored after; any other mode draws nothing. A zero half-width or half-height draws a vertical or horizontal line through Raster_DrawLine instead.

entries.name: Math_AbsInt
entries.description: Returns |x| of an int32 by the sign-mask idiom (x ^ (x >> 31)) - (x >> 31).

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch
entries.description: (bitmap, position, flags): applies the installed clip block to a blit. Offsets the destination by the context's translation when ctx+0x20c is 1; then hands a type-1 (transparent) bitmap (byte +5 low nibble) to Bitmap_BlitTransparent, which clips it itself; otherwise dispatches on the clip mode at ctx+0x208 -- mode 0 unclipped through the routine at 004a582c, mode 1 rect-clipped to ctx+0x210 through 004a5834, and mode 2 the same rect clip, but only when the block holds at least one region (ctx+4 non-zero), and nothing otherwise.

entries.name: Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch
entries.description: (bitmap, point, flags): the reverse of Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch: zeroes the bitmap's data (+0xa, size +6), clears the low nibble of +5, sets the format byte +4 to 8 when it does not match the display depth 004a367a (8 or 4), offsets the point by the context's translation when +0x208 is 1, and reads the screen into it through the routine pointer 004a5830 -- unclipped for clip mode (+0x204) 0, clipped to the rect +0x20c for mode 1, and once per rect entry of the clip list for mode 2.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitScaledClipDispatch
entries.description: (bitmapData, point, flags, size{w, h}): offsets the point by the current context's translation when its +0x208 is 1, then calls the scaled blit routine pointer at 004a5838 as (bitmapData, w, h, &point, clip, flags) with clip 0 for clip mode (+0x204) 0 and the context's rect at +0x20c for modes 1 and 2 (mode 2 only when the region count at +0 is positive). Unlike Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch it has no transparent-bitmap branch.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled
entries.description: Draws a bitmap into a rotated, arbitrarily-sized destination quad through brush mode 5, installing the brush {5, 4, &sourceQuad, dimensions}; mode 5 skips palette index 0 (Raster_SpanBitmap). Its first argument points at the bitmap's rows,cols pair (the bitmap object's +4/+6); the source quad is (0,0),(cols-1,0),(cols-1,rows-1),(0,rows-1). flip bit 2 mirrors it in x, bit 1 in y. The destination quad is (0,0),(w,0),(w,h),(0,h) from the size pair, each corner rotated by the binary angle and then translated by the position -- so that position is the rotated quad's top-left, not its centre.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled(short *dimensions, int *position, unsigned char flip, int *size, short angle)

entries.name: Math_BuildRotation2DInto
entries.description: (out, angle): Math_BuildRotation2D(angle, out) -- the same call with the arguments the other way round. Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled calls it.

entries.name: Math_Rotate2DPoint_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Math_Rotate2DPoint with the same arguments.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitTransparent
entries.description: The transparent/RLE sprite blitter. Rejects against the context's clip rect (ctx+0x210..+0x21c), then sets a per-call flag from whether the clip mode is 2 and sends every pixel run it emits either to the plain span writer (DAT_004a581c/DAT_004a5824) or to the region-clipped one (DAT_004a5820/DAT_004a5828). That flag is why a sprite drawn through a mode-2 context is cut to the canopy cutout scanline by scanline rather than to a rectangle. (bitmap, position, flags): the bitmap's int16 height +0 and width +2, and its data +0xa: a 0x10-byte colour table, then the code stream (SpriteCode_*): a code with bit 7 set is a run of code & 0x3f pixels, packed 4-bit indices into the colour table when bit 6 is clear (Raster_SpanCopy), one colour from the following byte when it is set (Raster_SpanFill); a code with the top two bits clear ends the row; 0x40 ends the sprite; any other 0x4x code skips transparent pixels. flags bit 0 flips the sprite vertically, bit 1 horizontally.

entries.name: SpriteCode_Count
entries.description: (code): code & 0x3f, the pixel count of a transparent-sprite code. Bitmap_BlitTransparent decodes every code with it.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsRun
entries.description: (code): code & 0x80. Bitmap_BlitTransparent draws a run of SpriteCode_Count pixels for a code with it set.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsLiteralRun
entries.description: (code): whether bit 6 (0x40) of a run code is clear. Bitmap_BlitTransparent then reads the run's pixels as packed 4-bit indices, (count + 1) / 2 bytes; with bit 6 set the run is one colour from the single byte that follows.

entries.name: Raster_SpanFillRegion
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, colour): calls the region-clipped raster routine at 004a5828 with (colour, y, x0, x1). Bitmap_BlitTransparent emits a one-colour run through it in clip mode 2.

entries.name: Raster_SpanFill
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, colour): calls the raster routine at 004a5824 with (colour, y, x0, x1). Bitmap_BlitTransparent emits a one-colour run through it when the clip mode is not 2.

entries.name: Raster_SpanCopyRegion
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, pixels): calls the region-clipped raster routine at 004a5820 with (pixels, y, x0, x1). Bitmap_BlitTransparent emits a literal run through it in clip mode 2.

entries.name: Raster_SpanCopy
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, pixels): calls the raster routine at 004a581c with (pixels, y, x0, x1). Bitmap_BlitTransparent emits a literal run through it when the clip mode is not 2.

entries.name: Math_NegateIf
entries.description: (flag, value): returns -value when flag is nonzero, else value. Bitmap_BlitTransparent calls it.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsRowEnd
entries.description: (code): whether the top two bits (0xc0) of a code are clear. Bitmap_BlitTransparent then steps to the next row and moves x back by SpriteCode_Count, extended by SpriteCode_IsRowEndExtension's byte.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsRowEndExtension
entries.description: (byte): 1 when the byte after a row-end code is non-zero with its top two bits clear, else 0. Bitmap_BlitTransparent then consumes it and moves x back by byte * 0x40 + count instead of count. The decompile drops the return.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsEnd
entries.description: (code): whether code is 0x40, the end of a transparent sprite. Any other code with bit 6 set and bit 7 clear skips SpriteCode_Count transparent pixels.

entries.name: RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable
entries.description: Register convention: driver id in EAX, result in EAX. Walks g_RasterDriverTable's {int id, void **table} pairs and returns the matching table pointer, or the terminator's id (-1) when none matches. A matching entry with a null table returns 0.

entries.name: RasterDriver_InstallRoutines
entries.description: Looks the driver id up with RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable and copies g_RasterRoutineCount (36) dwords from the result into g_RasterRoutines with REP MOVSD. Returns 1, or 0 when the id is unknown. It does not test for a null table, which drivers 0 and 1 carry, so every install that returns has copied driver 3's.

entries.name: GLDisplay_FirstOpenNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. GLDisplay_Open calls it on the first open ever (open count 004a2e44 still 0).

entries.name: GLDisplay_LastCloseNoOp
entries.description: Empty body (pushes and pops EDI, EBX, ESI). GLDisplay_Close calls it when the open count 004a2e44 returns to 0.

entries.name: RasterDriver_OpenDisplay
entries.description: (driverId, bitmapHeader, info): calls into the driver's own routine table (RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable, looked up afresh for each call): slot 8 (bitmapHeader) and then slot 9 () must each return 0, else it returns 0; then slot 10 (), slot 11 (bitmapHeader, info) and slot 7 (info+0x24, info), and returns 1. GLDisplay_Open passes display+4 as info. Ghidra's fastcall prototype is wrong; all three arguments are on the stack.

entries.name: RasterDriver_CloseDisplay
entries.description: (driverId, info): calls slot 12 of the driver's own routine table (RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable) with info. GLDisplay_Close passes display+4.

entries.name: Raster_InstallViewport
entries.description: (viewport): copies the viewport's first 0x81 dwords to 004a33f0 and its dwords 0x81-0x8a to 004a35f4..004a3618. Raster_SelectRenderTarget passes the display's +0x40.

entries.name: Raster_SetClipBlock
entries.description: (block): stores the clip block pointer PTR_DAT_004a362c that the raster routines read. Raster_InstallRenderContext passes ctx+4; Raster_SelectRenderTarget calls it too.

entries.name: ClipBlock_Init
entries.description: (block, width, height): zeroes the region area +0..+0x200 and +0x204..+0x210 (clip mode +0x204 0, so unclipped), sets the rect's far corner +0x214/+0x218 to width-1/height-1, zeroes +0x21c/+0x220, and points the pen +0x224 at 004a361c and the fill brush +0x228 at 004a3624. GLDisplay_Open initialises a display's clip block with it.

entries.name: Gfx_PlotPixel
entries.description: Plots one pixel at an {x, y} pair through the current drawing context (004a362c), clipped to its rect or clip-region list. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Gfx_PlotPixel.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot30NoOp
entries.description: Slot 30 of raster driver 3's routine table (004a5884): pushes and pops EBX, EDX, ESI, EDI and ES and returns. Cursor_SyncPosition calls slot 30 after storing the pointer position; Driver3_SyncCursorPosition calls this directly.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot31NoOp
entries.description: Slot 31 of raster driver 3's routine table (004a5884): pushes and pops EBX, EDX, ESI, EDI and ES and returns. Cursor_SyncPosition and Driver3_SyncCursorPosition call slot 31 before storing the pointer position.

entries.name: maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage
entries.description: Empty: returns at once. Sits beside Driver3_SyncCursorPosition, driver 3's copy of Cursor_SyncPosition; the cockpit cursor-slot functions call it with a .DCI cursor's bitmap and hotspot when Display_UseScrollWindow is set, as they call maybe_Cursor_SetImage otherwise.

entries.name: Driver3_SyncCursorPosition
entries.description: Raster driver 3's copy of Cursor_SyncPosition: the same stores, with the routine-table slot 31 call before them, but it calls 004897c8 (driver 3's slot 30, Driver3_Slot30NoOp) directly where Cursor_SyncPosition calls slot 30 through g_RasterRoutines. AlertPanel_Leave calls it.

entries.name: Driver3_BlitClipped
entries.description: Slot 26 of raster driver 3's routine table, the blit Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch calls: (bitmap, point, clipRect, flags) clips the bitmap at point to clipRect {x0, y0, x1, y1} inclusive, or to the surface when clipRect is null, then copies it in one of four orientations by flags bits 0-1: opaque when the bitmap's byte +5 has bit 0x10, otherwise skipping colour 0.

entries.name: Driver3_OpenDisplay
entries.description: Slot 11 of raster driver 3's routine table (g_RasterRoutines_Driver3), which RasterDriver_OpenDisplay calls with (bitmapHeader, info): allocates the surface's row-offset table into info+0, takes the width and height from the one-shot overrides when they are not negative (resetting them to -1) or else from the header, fills the rest of info and sets Display_ScreenRect and the origin to 0. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Driver3_OpenDisplay (004281fb).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0048a0c8; es2_naming.py diff against VSHELL 004281fb

entries.name: Driver3_Slot7NoOp
entries.description: Slot 7 of raster driver 3's routine table (g_RasterRoutines_Driver3): returns at once. RasterDriver_OpenDisplay and GLDisplay_SetAttribute call slot 7.

entries.name: Driver3_CloseDisplay
entries.description: Slot 12 of raster driver 3's routine table, which RasterDriver_CloseDisplay calls: (info) frees the row-offset table at info+0 that Driver3_OpenDisplay allocated.

entries.name: Raster_GetPixel
entries.description: Driver 3's g_RasterRoutines slot 4: (point) returns the byte at the draw surface 004a366a: rowTable[point.y] (+4 + y*4) + point.x + base (+0).
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0048a234; driver-3 table at 004a5894

entries.name: Raster_PutPixel
entries.description: Driver 3's g_RasterRoutines slot 5: (point, value) stores the byte at the address Raster_GetPixel reads.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0048a255; driver-3 table at 004a5898

entries.name: Driver3_SpanCopy
entries.description: Slot 22 of raster driver 3's routine table, Raster_SpanCopy's: (pixels, y, x0, x1) copies x1 - x0 + 1 bytes from pixels into row y at x0 through the surface's row-offset table, dwords then bytes; nothing when x0 > x1.

entries.name: Driver3_SpanFill
entries.description: Slot 24 of raster driver 3's routine table, Raster_SpanFill's: (colour, y, x0, x1) fills x0..x1 of row y with the colour byte, dwords then bytes; nothing when x0 > x1.

entries.name: Raster_FillBitmapPolygon
entries.description: g_RasterRoutines slot 33, which Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch calls for brush modes 5 and 7. Reads the brush at clipBlock+0x228: +8 the source quad, +0xc the bitmap dimensions pointer, and +0x10 a remap table only when the mode is 7 (otherwise it passes 0). Finds the top and bottom vertices, walks the two edges with Raster_BitmapEdgeSetup/Raster_BitmapEdgeStep and calls Raster_SpanBitmap per scanline within the clip rows. Reached only through the driver-3 table, so Ghidra auto-analysis had no function here.

entries.name: Raster_BitmapEdgeStep
entries.description: Steps an edge one row: decrements its row count and, at zero, moves to the next edge with Raster_BitmapEdgeSetup (returning 0 when none is left); otherwise adds the u, v and x steps. Returns 1 while the edge continues.

entries.name: Raster_BitmapEdgeSetup
entries.description: Advances an edge of Raster_FillBitmapPolygon from vertexIndex to the next vertex in the edge's direction (edge[0], +1 or -1, wrapping), storing its row count, the source-quad u,v at the start in 16.16 and their per-row steps (Math_Q16Divide), and the destination x start and step. Skips zero-height edges. Returns 0 when the walk reaches the bottom vertex.

entries.name: Raster_SpanBitmap
entries.description: Fills one scanline between two edges of Raster_FillBitmapPolygon, sampling the nearest texel through dimensions+2 (cols, the stride) and dimensions+0xa (the data pointer), clipped by the render context's clip mode. With remap null (brush mode 5) a texel of palette index 0 is not stored (OR AL,AL / JE at 0048ae87); with remap set (mode 7) every texel, index 0 included, is stored as remap[texel].
entries.signature: void __cdecl Raster_SpanBitmap(int *leftEdge, int *rightEdge, short *dimensions, unsigned char *remap)

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedClipped
entries.description: Draws the span at x DAT_004a5958, length DAT_004a0984, through the visible-run list at DAT_004a5954 ({x, length} pairs, DAT_004a5950 of them): for each run that overlaps it, advances the destination DAT_004a0980 and the u/v accumulators past the hidden pixels, trims the length at the run's end and calls Raster_SpanTextured. Returns at the first run that starts at or past the span's end. Raster_DrawPolygon uses it in mode 0 when ActiveScanlineClipSpans is set and either the context clip mode (+0x208) is 2 or maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled is set; the run list is then the row's clip spans, or with the depth buffer the runs Raster_DepthTestSpan leaves.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedShadedClipped
entries.description: Raster_SpanTexturedClipped for mode 1: the same visible-run walk, calling Raster_SpanTexturedShaded.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudClipped
entries.description: Raster_SpanTexturedClipped for mode 2: the same visible-run walk, also advancing the ramp-row accumulator DAT_004a09c4 by DAT_004a09c8 per skipped pixel, calling Raster_SpanTexturedGouraud.

entries.name: Raster_DepthTestSpan
entries.description: Per-pixel depth test and write for one span: walks DAT_004a5b00 dwords of the buffer from DAT_004a5af4 with a value starting at DAT_004a5af8 and stepped by DAT_004a5afc per pixel; where the stored dword is greater it writes the value and the pixel is visible. Collects the visible pixels as {x, length} runs at 004a595c (x = index + DAT_004a5af0), sets DAT_004a5950 to the run count and DAT_004a5954 to 004a595c, the list the ...Clipped span routines walk. Raster_DrawPolygon calls it per row when maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled is set, with the buffer at _DAT_006c6014 + (row * stride + x) * 4 and the value the edge's interpolated view depth ORed with (row + DAT_004a5b04) << 24.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0048b748 and its call site in Raster_DrawPolygon (004684fb)

entries.name: ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans
entries.description: Flattens a loaded region list (rects + span blocks from CockpitClipRegions_Load) into a per-scanline span table of `rowCount` rows (0xf0 << VideoMode_YCoordShift, i.e. 240 or 480). Each row is {int spanCount, ptr to spanCount x {int start, int length}}, sorted by start. Stores the result in ActiveScanlineClipSpans. This -- not any colour key -- is the cockpit's 3D-viewport cutout mechanism.

entries.name: TSContext_Ctor
entries.description: TSContext constructor (vtable 004a5b51, RTTI name 'TSContext', 0x16 bytes): constructs the point at +4 (maybe_Point3I_Ctor) and the int16 triple at +0x10 (maybe_Point3S_Ctor). TSCamera_Ctor and the light constructors run it first.

entries.name: View_CtorBase
entries.description: Base view constructor (vtable 004a5b51): copies an int[3] position to +4..+0xc and a short[3] angle triple to +0x10..+0x14. The +4 triple is what View_GetActiveObject's readers take as the camera position.

entries.name: TSContext_Dtor
entries.description: TSContext destructor (vtable 004a5b51, RTTI name 'TSContext', 0x16 bytes): restores the vtable and frees the object when flag & 1.

entries.name: maybe_TSLight_SetIntensity
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's maybe_TSLight_SetIntensity (0045da4c).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 0048bbe0 VSHELL 0045da4c: identical after normalisation; RTTI TSLight vtable slot

entries.description: Transforms a light's world position (+0x04) and direction (+0x10) by the given transform into the model-space copies at +0x22 and +0x2e. Those copies, NOT the world fields, are what Light_ComputeShadeForFace and Light_ComputeShadeForNormal read. Driven per composed node by Raster_SetModelTransform, gated on DAT_006cbc88.

entries.name: Light_Register
entries.description: Adds a light object pointer to the active light list (DAT_006c6130, 10-slot max, dedups by pointer identity). Four call sites found by es2_xref: FUN_00407388/FUN_00407444 (pooled directional/point light getters, see their own entries), Light_ReregisterPersistent (re-registers a persistent light list Light_PersistentList into the active manager), and Light_CreateMissionSun (00461240).

entries.name: Light_Unregister
entries.description: Swap-removes a light pointer from the active light list DAT_006c6130 and decrements DAT_006c612c. The inverse of Light_Register.

entries.name: Light_ComputeShadeForFace
entries.description: The per-face 'shade byte' (0-255, clamped) calculation feeding TSShadedPoly_Render (0047542c). TSSolidPoly_Render does NOT call it -- a solid poly carries no light term at all. NOT a simple angle calc -- a real light-accumulation loop over the active light list (DAT_006c6130, max 10 slots, count DAT_006c612c), dispatching per-entry on a type tag from FUN_0048d94b: type 0 = ambient (adds a flat intensity from FUN_0048d956 unconditionally -- not populated by a retail mission, see Light_AddDirectional/PointHelper's entries), type 1 = directional (dot-product-like test via FUN_0048d99b against the face's Normal point (param_1), only contributes when the result crosses a fixed threshold, i.e. face-vs-light-direction test), type 2 = point light (distance-attenuated: displacement from the light's position (FUN_0048d961) to the face's Center point (param_2) combined with the Normal via FUN_0048d86e, divided by distance/range fields FUN_0048d973/FUN_0048d97e). Params: param_1 = the poly's normal point (three shorts), param_2 = its centre point (same two pointers TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest receives). Sibling functions FUN_0048bdcc/FUN_0048c060 are near-identical variants (different param shapes) used elsewhere for the same shade calc, likely per-vertex vs. per-face evaluation.

entries.name: Light_ComputeShadeForNormal
entries.description: The per-normal sibling of Light_ComputeShadeForFace (0048bdcc/0048c060 were flagged as near-identical variants; this is the one the terrain uses). Takes (short* normal, int* centre) and walks the same active light list, returning a shade byte clamped to 255. Directional (type 1) branch, which is the only one a retail mission populates: dot = DotProductVec3Short(normal, lightDir); if (dot < 0) shade -= (intensity * dot) >> 22. Normals arrive normalised to length 0x800 and the mission sun's direction vector is length 0x1000 at intensity 0x100, so the whole expression is shade = min(255, 512 * cos) -- IT SATURATES AT cos 0.5, i.e. every surface within 60 degrees of facing the sun gets the ramp's top row rather than a falloff. Flat ground sits at cos 0.544 and is pinned at 255. Called by Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade once per cell triangle at zone load.

entries.name: Raster_InstallViewProjection
entries.description: Installs a view's projection state into the rasterizer globals: perspective shift from view+0x1a (DAT_006c60ac), near plane from +0x1e (DAT_006c60b0), orthographic divisor from +0x22 (DAT_006c60b4), and from the render target at view+0x16 the clip rect +0x210..+0x21c. The projection centre DAT_006c60b8/bc starts as that rect's top-left and then has the target's +0x220 pair subtracted -- that pair being the .VUE projection centre plus the view's canvas origin, installed by CockpitView_ApplyViewState.

entries.name: Raster_SetViewTransform
entries.description: (viewTransform): Raster_SetModelTransform's twin for the view side. Installs viewTransform (the identity at 006c6080 for null) at 006c6078, rebuilds g_ModelToView = Transform_Concat(g_ModelTransformPtr, view), its inverse g_ViewToModel (Transform_InvertRigid) and g_EyeInModelSpace (the origin through that inverse). Raster_InstallViewProjection calls it.

entries.name: Raster_SetModelTransform
entries.description: Installs a transform as the renderer's current model transform (null means the identity at 006c6080); the pointer goes to g_ModelTransformPtr. Builds g_ModelToView = Transform_Concat(model, [006c6078]), its inverse g_ViewToModel (Transform_InvertRigid), and g_EyeInModelSpace (the origin through that inverse). When 006cbc88 is set it moves every registered light (list 006c6130, count 006c612c) into the model's space with Light_TransformToModelSpace, using the inverse of the model transform. Same code as VSHELL's Raster_SetModelTransform (0045e198).

entries.name: Raster_ModelToView
entries.description: (point, out): Transform_ApplyToPoint_Thunk by the current model-to-view transform g_ModelToView. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Raster_ModelToView.

entries.name: Raster_PerspectiveScale
entries.description: Scales a world-space extent to pixels at a given depth: (extent << DAT_006c60ac) / z, or (extent << 8) / DAT_006c60b4 in the orthographic mode. The beam draw uses it for half-width, flooring the result at 2.

entries.name: Raster_PerspectiveDivide
entries.description: The perspective divide, ahead of Raster_ProjectToScreen's centring: screenOut[0] = (viewPoint[0] << DAT_006c60ac) / viewPoint[1], screenOut[1] = (viewPoint[2] << DAT_006c60ac) / viewPoint[1], or both over DAT_006c60b4 with a shift of 0 (the orthographic mode). Returns screenOut. Dividing components 0 and 2 by component 1 is what fixes the view-space axis order as (across, DEPTH, up) -- the fact that says which component Terrain_DrawCellQuad's fog distance is. DAT_006c60ac is the focal shift installed from view+0x1a.

entries.name: Raster_ProjectToScreen
entries.description: Final projection step: screenX = x + DAT_006c60b8, screenY = DAT_006c60bc - y. That centre is the .VUE projection centre, not the middle of the viewport rect, and is where the gunsight reticle sits -- anything running parallel to the view axis vanishes there. APOCA's is 95 rows down a 240-row view.

entries.name: TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest
entries.description: (normal, centre), both three-short points: with the focal shift 006c60ac at 0, rotates the normal into view space through g_ModelToView and returns 1 when its depth component is negative; otherwise returns dot(normal, g_EyeInModelSpace - centre). Called from all three flat poly renderers (TSSolidPoly_Render 00474db4, TSShadedPoly_Render 0047542c, TSTexture4Poly_Render 00474e9c) to pick the front or back surface colour. The same code as VSHELL's TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest (0045e480).

entries.name: Raster_FrontFacing
entries.description: (normal, point): with no perspective (006c60ac zero) rotates the int16 normal by g_ModelToView's matrix and returns 1 when the result's second component (y) is negative, else 0; otherwise returns the dot product of the normal with g_EyeInModelSpace - point (positive when the face looks at the eye). TexPoly_Render picks the surface's front bitmap (+0) when it is positive and the back (+8) otherwise.

entries.name: Poly_ProjectShapeVertices
entries.description: The .DTS renderers' sibling of Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices: projects the current face's vertices (count 006c6968, index list 006c6976 from 006c696a) into the screen-point list 006cbb86 and sets its count 006cbc86. With 006c60ac zero it transforms each untouched vertex by g_ModelToView (0048da87) and projects it with a constant divisor (x << 8 / 006c60b4 + 006c60b8, -z << 8 / 006c60b4 + 006c60bc), memoising it as 2 in the state bytes 006c697e, and returns 0; otherwise it returns Poly_ProjectShapeVerticesPerspective's result. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ProjectShapeVertices. TSShadedPoly_Render, TSSolidPoly_Render and TSTexture4Poly_Render call it.

entries.name: Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices
entries.description: Projects the vertices the current face names -- DAT_006c6968 of them from DAT_006c696a into the index list DAT_006c6976, indexing the point array DAT_006c6970 -- into the screen-point list DAT_006cbb86 / count DAT_006cbc86. Memoises per point in the state byte array DAT_006c697e: 0 untouched, 1 behind the near plane, 2 already projected, so a shared vertex is transformed once per shape. Takes no arguments. Returns non-zero when any vertex fell behind the near plane, which is the caller's signal to run Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane. Reads 12-byte int32 points. Two callers: BeamTracer_Draw (the ELF/ELF2 quad branch) and TexPoly_Render (0042fc34). The .DTS poly renderers (TSSolidPoly_Render, TSShadedPoly_Render, TSTexture4Poly_Render) use the sibling Poly_ProjectShapeVertices (0048c848) over 6-byte int16 point triples instead.

entries.name: Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane
entries.description: Clips the current face's vertex ring against the near plane DAT_006c60b0 in view space, rebuilding the screen-point list DAT_006cbb86 and returning the new count DAT_006cbc86. Walks consecutive index pairs: both projected emits the second, exactly one projected emits the crossing point (linear in view-space depth, plus the projection centre) and then the second if it is the projected one. Takes no arguments. Run only when Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices returns non-zero.

entries.name: Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithUV
entries.description: (uvIn, uvOut): Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane carrying a per-vertex {u, v} int pair along. Walks the current face's index ring (count DAT_006c6968, indices from DAT_006c6976 + DAT_006c696a * 2): an edge with both ends projected (state byte 2) emits the end's screen point and copies its pair; an edge with one projected end emits the crossing of the near plane DAT_006c60b0 (view x and -y linear in depth, plus the centre DAT_006c60b8) with the pair interpolated by the same fraction, then the end if it is the projected one. Returns the new count DAT_006cbc86 (points at DAT_006cbb86). TSTexture4Poly_Render's g_TexturedPolyUseBitmapBrush branch calls it when Poly_ProjectShapeVertices returns 1.

entries.name: PolyFill_Fill
entries.description: Fills the screen polygon left in the point-list globals by Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices / Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane, through Raster_DrawPolygonEitherWinding -> Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch, then runs PolyFill_FillThenOutline's same outline pass without its mode-5 guard. Winding-agnostic: Raster_DrawPolygonEitherWinding measures the signed area and hands the other winding to Raster_DrawPolygonReversed. Takes no arguments -- everything is globals. Called by BeamTracer_Draw for each ELF chain quad, where the outline pass is inert because the beam installed its own brush.

entries.name: PolyFill_FillThenOutline
entries.description: The polygon fill both flat poly renderers hand their two resolved colours to. Fills in DAT_006c60dc, then when DAT_006c60d4 (the line colour) differs and the mode is not 5, sets the fill colour to the line colour, sets mode DAT_006c60d8 = 4 and re-draws the SAME polygon -- an outline pass, not a second fill. Mode 4 is confirmed at Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch's iVar11 == 4 branch, which walks consecutive vertex pairs and closes back to the first vertex. Callers ramp both colours before this runs, so the != test is on ramped bytes, not raw surface values. DAT_006c60d8/DAT_006c60dc are one brush {mode, colour} and are the DEFAULT one: the fill dispatches on whatever clipBlock+0x228 points at, normally this pair, so a caller that installs a brush of its own there (BeamTracer_Draw) leaves these writes inert. PolyFill_Fill (0048d4b4) is the sibling without the mode-5 guard.

entries.name: Raster_SaveState
entries.description: Saves the renderer's current model state into a slot: g_ModelToView (0x20 bytes), the model transform pointer 006c607c, the view transform pointer 006c6078, g_EyeInModelSpace, and, when 006cbc88 is set, a 0x16-byte model-space copy per registered light from +0x34. Its light loop steps the save slot but reads the light from the fixed address [006c6130] every pass, so only the first registered light's model-space copy is saved or restored. ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform saves each freshly composed node with it; ShapeInst_BindNodeTransformArray saves the object's base state.

entries.name: Raster_RestoreState
entries.description: Reinstates a Raster_SaveState slot: the model and view transform pointers, g_ModelToView, a recomputed g_ViewToModel (Transform_InvertRigid), g_EyeInModelSpace and the lights' model-space copies (Light_RestoreModelSpace). Its light loop steps the save slot but reads the light from the fixed address [006c6130] every pass, so only the first registered light's model-space copy is saved or restored. ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform uses it for a node already composed and to return to the object's base state.

entries.name: TSGroup_ReadFromStream
entries.description: TSGroup's vtable +0x0c load method (group struct is 0x28 bytes, built by the type registry's tag-0x00140014 ctor 0048e7a4). Reads four int16 counts into +0x20 indexes / +0x22 points / +0x24 surfaces / +0x26 polys, allocates +0x10 / +0x14 / +0x18 / +0x1c for each, then streams them. The surface array at +0x18 is surfaceCount int32s read RAW -- no conversion of any kind -- so the value a poly renderer indexes really is the file's own {int16 colour, int16 flag} pair packed into one int32.

entries.name: TSPartBase_ReadFromStream
entries.description: TSPartBase vtable 004a6268 slot +0xc (part, stream): reads three int16 head fields, the transform +4, the id +6 and the radius +8, then the 6-byte centre into +0xa: the head every part chunk carries (TSBasePart in the format docs). The derived parts' reads call it first, and dgs\bases/bhulks shape records reach it through GridShape's read. The radius is the shape's bounding radius: SimObject_GetShapeRadius and the LOD selector 004033e4 both read it as one, and it tracks BASES.DAT +0x2a within about a fifth across all 45 records.

entries.name: Anim_BlendKeyframeTransforms
entries.description: Blends two 12-byte ANAnimList transform records (3 euler shorts then 3 translation shorts) by a Q10 factor (0x400 == fully the second). Rotation components take the SHORTEST ARC: the difference is biased by 0x10000 when it would go negative, subtracted, then folded back by 0x10000 when it exceeds 0x7fff -- the shortest signed 16-bit difference -- before the Q10 multiply and arithmetic >>10. Translation components are a plain truncating lerp on the 16-bit difference. All fixed point; no float anywhere.

entries.name: Math_NormalizeVec3ToLength
entries.description: Rescales an int Vec3 in place to the requested length and returns it. Zeroes all three when the magnitude is zero; otherwise scales each by Math_Q16Divide(length << 16, magnitude) NARROWED TO A SIGNED 16-BIT VALUE before the multiply, so a step over a short delta comes out shorter than asked for. Distinct from Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength (0046c138), which is the three-short form and halves until the magnitude fits first.

entries.name: Math_DistanceBetweenPoints
entries.description: Distance between two int Vec3s: copies a to a stack temp, subtracts b, and returns FUN_00492971 -- the Vec3 form of Math_FastMagnitude3D -- so it carries that function's direction-dependent error (about 8% low to 8.7% high). The MFD TARGET range readout and BeamTracer_Ctor's chain node count both go through it.

entries.name: Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints
entries.description: Ground-plane distance between two int Vec3s: Vec2_Subtract then Vec2_Magnitude, returned in EAX, Z dropped entirely. Every range an AI steering decision is made on is this; the 3D Math_DistanceBetweenPoints gates only obstacle avoidance's machine sweep and following's standoff -- a waypoint on a hilltop is as near as one at its foot.

entries.name: Math_Atan2Guarded
entries.description: atan2 as a BAM angle, with the degenerate pair nudged onto an axis. ARGUMENT ORDER IS (x, y), NOT (y, x): it forwards to Math_Atan2Bam_Thunk(p1, p2) and sets p1 -- the X -- to 1 when both are zero. Both Math_HeadingToward and Math_EulerToward call it as (dx, dy). Getting this backwards mirrors a bearing about the 45-degree line and turns an elevation into a polar angle from +Z.

entries.name: Math_HeadingToward
entries.description: Ground-plane bearing from one position to another as a BAM angle: atan2(to.y - from.y, to.x - from.x) via FUN_00492800, minus a quarter turn, because the sim's forward axis is model Y and not model X. Call sites pass the destination first. DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects uses it to face a group along the first leg of its route when the group's block-11 record carries no heading ref.

entries.name: Math_ElevationAngle
entries.description: (a, b): Math_Atan2Guarded(Math_FastMagnitude2D_Thunk(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y), a.z - b.z) on int32 triples, returned in AX. Flyer_AttackRun passes its aim point and the flyer's position (+0x26) and feeds the result to Flyer_PitchCommand.

entries.name: Math_EulerToward
entries.description: Math_EulerToward(out, from, to), d = from - to: euler[2] = Math_Atan2Guarded(dx, dy) - 0x4000, euler[1] = 0, euler[0] = Math_Atan2Guarded(Math_FastMagnitude2D(dx, dy), dz). Math_Atan2Guarded takes (x, y), so euler[2] is the ground bearing and euler[0] is an ELEVATION above the horizon, not a polar angle from +Z. The quarter-turn subtraction is because the simulation's forward axis is model Y. Same helper and same argument order as Math_HeadingToward.

entries.name: Math_OffsetPointByBearing
entries.description: Offsets an int Vec3's x and y by a distance along a BAM bearing, the bearing quarter-turned back because the sim's forward axis is model Y. The skirting state's circling step.

entries.name: Vec2_Subtract
entries.description: In-place 2D vector subtract: a->x -= b->x, a->y -= b->y. Confirms the HUD's waypoint/contact distances are ground-plane distances, Z ignored.

entries.name: Vec2_Magnitude
entries.description: Thin wrapper: Math_FastMagnitude2D(v->x, v->y) via Math_FastMagnitude2D_Thunk.

entries.name: Vec3_Subtract
entries.description: (a, b): subtracts b from a in place, z first and then x and y through Vec2_Subtract; returns a.

entries.name: Point3I_Magnitude
entries.description: Returns Math_FastMagnitude3D of an int32 point's three components (through Math_FastMagnitude3D_Thunk; the decompile drops the return value).

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude2D_Thunk
entries.description: Forwards (dx, dy) to Math_FastMagnitude2D and returns its result. Vec2_Magnitude and Math_EulerToward call it.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude3D_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Math_FastMagnitude3D(x, y, z).

entries.name: Math_Atan2Bam_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Math_Atan2Bam with the same arguments. Math_Atan2Guarded calls it.

entries.name: Math_CosBam_Thunk
entries.description: (angle): Math_CosBam(angle), returned in AX.

entries.name: Math_Q14Multiply_Thunk
entries.description: (a, b): Math_Q14Multiply(a, b) on int16 arguments, returned in AX.

entries.name: Math_DivInt
entries.description: (a, b): a / b, signed. Math_NormalizeVec3ToLength calls it.

entries.name: Math_ScaleByCos
entries.description: (length, angle): Math_Q14Multiply_Thunk(length, Math_CosBam_Thunk(angle)) as a sign-extended int16. Math_OffsetPointByBearing calls it.

entries.name: Math_ScaleBySin
entries.description: (length, angle): Math_Q14Multiply_Thunk(length, Math_SinBam(angle)) as a sign-extended int16. Math_OffsetPointByBearing calls it.

entries.name: Math_SinBam
entries.description: (angle): Math_CosBam(angle - 0x4000), i.e. the sine in Q14, returned in AX.

entries.name: Str_ReplaceFirst
entries.description: (s, find, replace): replaces the first occurrence of the character find in s with replace (strchr) and returns s.

entries.name: Path_WithExtension
entries.description: (path, extension): copies path into the static buffer 006cbc90, cuts it at the first '.' (Str_ReplaceFirst), then appends '.' and the extension.

entries.name: ResourcePath_BuildFolderName
entries.description: The shared folder\name resource-path builder: ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(name, folder) writes 'folder\\name' into a shared static buffer (&DAT_006cbcae) via FUN_00492a84(name) + strcat('\\') + strcat(folder). Confirmed by tracing its two operands against known-good results (e.g. ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(hercName, "vue") and the folder-name pointer table at CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames).

entries.name: NameList_Split
entries.description: (buffer, out): walks the NUL-terminated names in buffer until one starts with a '\n' byte, storing each name's address in out when out is non-null, and returns the count (EAX = EDI; the decompile drops it). LoadNameList splits the .NAM file with it.

entries.name: VolFile_GetSize
entries.description: (path): opens path as a VolRStream (loose file or volume entry) and returns VolRStream_GetSize, or 0 when the open fails. LoadNameList sizes the .NAM file with it.

entries.name: LoadNameList
entries.description: Loads a nam\<name>.NAM list -- a flat run of NUL-terminated ASCII names indexed by type number -- with a capacity bound as the second argument. Called with ('mechs', 0x55) into the mech name table DAT_004a9de4 that MechType_InitOne indexes, and with ('flyers', 0x22) into DAT_004a9e74. These are the tables that turn script.dat block 7's and block 8's type numbers into resource base names; MECHS.NAM ships 21 names and FLYERS.NAM 3.

entries.name: Math_RandomSeed
entries.description: Seeds one Math_RandomNext state block: the cursors at +0x70/+0x71 to the literals 0x18 and 0x37, then a memmove of 112 bytes (56 int16) from the static table at 004a6958. The function it calls afterwards, 00492e3c, is an empty stub -- no clock and no entropy reaches the generator. Called for both 0x4d261d and 0x4d268f from Main_StaticInit (0045cad8), and by Math_RandomSeedAndSkip.

entries.name: Math_RandomSeedAndSkip
entries.description: (state, count). Seeds the given generator block with Math_RandomSeed, calls the empty stub 00492e41, then draws and discards count values with Math_RandomNext; count is a signed 16-bit value, so a count of zero or less discards none. es2_xref.py finds no reference to it anywhere in the image. See docs/simulation/random-generator.md.

entries.name: Math_RandomNext
entries.description: The game's pseudo-random generator: an additive lagged Fibonacci generator over a 56-entry (0x38) table of shorts with two rotating byte cursors at state+0x70 and state+0x71. Each call does table[i] += table[j]; returns the new table[i] in the low 16 bits; then advances both cursors modulo 56. Callers pass the state block address (0x4d261d) and mask the result -- & 0xfff for the terrain material roll in TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap and for the explosion's ~51% per-component roll in FUN_004187d0. Seeded only by Math_RandomSeed (00492d7c), from a static table; there is no entropy input anywhere, so DBSIM's simulation replays identically on every run.

entries.name: Math_RandomBelow
entries.description: A draw in [0, bound): (Math_RandomNext() & 0x7fff) % bound. The mask drops the sign bit rather than taking an absolute value, so the distribution is the low fifteen bits'. Used by Component_SpillIntoDependents' weighted pick.

entries.name: Math_RandomSeedNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Math_RandomSeed's last call.

entries.name: Math_RandomSeedAndSkipNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Math_RandomSeedAndSkip calls it after Math_RandomSeed, before the discarded draws.

entries.name: Ovl_ReadFile
entries.description: (dst, size, count, path): opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, asserting (OVL.CPP line 0x15) on a bad stream status, reads size * count bytes into dst with VolRStream_Read, asserting (line 0x17) when that fails, and closes it. MechType_InitOne reads the 0xd8-byte type record and the 0x36-byte block with it; FlyerType_LoadResources its 0x2e-byte stats.

entries.name: ViewFrustum_Ctor
entries.description: (frustum, far, margin): constructs the position at +0xc and the six 0x10-byte planes from +0x18 (Plane_Ctor), stores far at +4, margin at +0 and -1 (every plane enabled) at +8. Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion builds one with far = grid+0x10c << cellShift and margin = 1.5 cells.

entries.name: ViewFrustum_Build
entries.description: (frustum, view, far, margin): the six planes of the view's frustum, each built in view axes (across, depth, up), rotated by the view's euler matrix and handed to Plane_FromPointNormal. With F = far, M = margin, s = the view's perspective shift (+0x1a), and from the render context (+0x16) the rect +0x210..+0x21c (w, h) and the pair +0x220/+0x224 (-cx, -cy): near (+0x18) through (0,-M,0), normal (0,F,0); far (+0x28) through (0,F,0), normal -(0,F,0); top (+0x38) through (0,0,M), normal (0, cy*F>>s, -F); bottom (+0x48) through -(0,0,M), normal (0,(h-cy)*F>>s, F); left (+0x58) through -(M,0,0), normal (F, cx*F>>s, 0); right (+0x68) through (M,0,0), normal (-F,(w-cx)*F>>s, 0). The position (+0xc) is the view's.

entries.name: ViewFrustum_ClipPolygon
entries.description: (frustum, poly, out) -> bool: ViewFrustum_ClipGroundPolygon without the Z shift, with the planes as built.

entries.name: ViewFrustum_ClipGroundPolygon
entries.description: (frustum, poly, lowZ, highZ, out) -> bool: copies the six planes, shifting each non-vertical one (Plane_IsVertical) along Z by lowZ when its Z component is <= 0 and by -highZ when positive (Plane_ShiftAlongZ); moves poly to the eye (Poly3_SubtractOffset), cuts it with Poly_SplitByPlane keeping the front against the enabled planes in the order left, right, top, bottom, far, near, and moves the result back (Poly3_AddOffset). Returns whether any points are left. Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion clips the draw square with it, passing grid+0x110 and grid+0x114.

entries.name: Poly3_SubtractOffset
entries.description: (in, offset, out): out = in with offset subtracted from each int32 {x, y, z} point; count copied.

entries.name: Poly3_AddOffset
entries.description: (in, offset, out): out = in with offset added to each int32 {x, y, z} point; count copied.

entries.name: Transform_Ctor
entries.description: Constructs a transform: Transform_CtorRotation on it (which returns its argument) and maybe_Point3I_Ctor on its translation at +0x14. Returns it.

entries.name: Rtl_ReturnArgCopy2
entries.description: Returns its argument unchanged (MOV EAX,[EBP+8]; the decompile drops it) -- a third copy of Rtl_ReturnArg. Transform_Ctor and Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled call it.

entries.name: View_GetPosition
entries.description: (view) -> view + 4, the view's int32 position.

entries.name: View_GetPerspectiveShift
entries.description: (view) -> the dword at view + 0x1a, the perspective shift.

entries.name: View_GetRenderContext
entries.description: (view) -> the dword at view + 0x16, the view's render context.

entries.name: View_BuildTransform
entries.description: (view, out): Transform_SetEulerAndTranslation(out, view + 0x10, view + 4).

entries.name: Transform_CtorRotation
entries.description: (transform): returns Rtl_ReturnArgCopy2(transform), its argument; constructs nothing. Transform_Ctor runs it on the transform before constructing the translation at +0x14.

entries.name: Transform_SetEulerAndTranslation
entries.description: (out, euler, position): writes position into the transform's translation (+0x14..+0x1c) and builds the rotation from the euler triple with BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14.

entries.name: Point3I_Negate
entries.description: (p): negates Z, then X and Y through Point3I_NegateXY.

entries.name: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14_Thunk
entries.description: (matrix, euler): BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14(euler, matrix), the arguments exchanged.

entries.name: Point3I_NegateXY
entries.description: (p): negates X and Y.

entries.name: Plane_Ctor
entries.description: maybe_Point3I_Ctor on the plane's normal, which it starts with; returns it. ViewFrustum_Ctor and ViewFrustum_ClipGroundPolygon build their six planes with it.

entries.name: Dword_Swap
entries.description: (a, b): exchanges the dwords at a and b. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Dword_Swap; every direct caller swaps the in and out point-list pointers after a Poly_SplitByPlane pass.

entries.name: Plane_IsVertical
entries.description: (plane) -> 1 when the normal's Z is 0 and X, Y are not both 0; 0 otherwise.

entries.name: Plane_ShiftAlongZ
entries.description: (plane, v): plane.d -= v * plane.nz.

entries.name: HeightOffsetTable_Ctor
entries.description: VectorTable constructor (vtables ClassItem 004a6a08, TSBase 004a6a2c, then VectorTable 004a6a58; RTTI name 'VectorTable', 0x1c bytes): (table, count) stores count at +0xc, base 0 at +8 and step 100 at +4, a count-byte computed-flag array at +0x10, count int32 triples at +0x14 and eight at +0x18. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's HeightOffsetTable_Ctor; HeightGrid_Constructor's table at +0xd0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0049515c; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: HeightOffsetTable_SetScale
entries.description: (table, base, step): stores base at table+8 and step at table+4. TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap, TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap and Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion call it on HeightGrid+0xd0 with the grid's height base (+0x110) and height scale (+0x118).

entries.name: HeightOffsetTable_Reset
entries.description: (table): memsets the per-height computed flags (table+0x10, length table+0xc) to 0 and writes the view-space image of the up vector (0, 0, 0x10000) under g_ModelToView into the vector table+0x18 points at, via Transform_RotatePoint_Thunk. Called on HeightGrid+0xd0 after each HeightOffsetTable_SetScale.

entries.name: HeightOffsetTable_Get
entries.description: (table, rawHeight): returns the 12-byte view-space offset of a raw height byte at table+0x14 + rawHeight*12. Filled on first use after HeightOffsetTable_Reset (flag byte table+0x10[rawHeight]): each component of the up vector at *(table+0x18) times rawHeight*step(+4) + base(+8), through Math_Q16Multiply. Terrain_DrawCellQuad adds it to each corner.

entries.name: maybe_Point3I_Ctor
entries.description: Rtl_ReturnArg(p), then returns p: the same shape as VSHELL's maybe_Point3I_Ctor, called on int32[3] locals before they are filled (Light_ComputeShadeForFace, Light_TransformToModelSpace, Math_DistanceBetweenPoints). The name is inferred from those call sites.

entries.name: Rtl_ReturnArg
entries.description: Returns its argument unchanged. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Rtl_ReturnArg.

entries.name: VectorTable_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VectorTable_Dtor (00468103).
entries.source: ES2DecompileContainingBatch DBSIM 004953ab / VSHELL 00468103: identical after normalisation; RTTI VectorTable vtable 004a6a58 slot +0x18

entries.name: Transform_RotatePoint_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Transform_RotatePoint with the same arguments.

entries.name: MonoDevice_Ctor
entries.description: (dev): dev+0 = CreateFileA("\\.\DARKMONO.VXD", 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x4000000 FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE, 0), the developer monochrome-monitor driver that does not ship, so the handle is INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE in retail. Returns dev.

entries.description: (dev, flags): CloseHandle(dev+0) when MonoDevice_IsOpen; Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Mono_SetFlag
entries.description: (on): MonoDevice_SetFlag on the global device 006cbcd4 when on is 1, MonoDevice_ClearFlag otherwise.

entries.name: maybe_Mono_Clear
entries.description: MonoDevice_Ioctl5(006cbcd4, 0x20): control code 5 with a space as its one byte, read as a clear-screen fill character. Sim_InitMissionSession calls it when the -m flag 004d2701 is set, and 0045c630 before it lists the view names.

entries.name: Mono_WriteText

entries.name: Mono_Printf

entries.name: Mono_Ioctl4

entries.name: MonoDevice_StaticInit

entries.name: MonoDevice_IsOpen
entries.description: (dev): dev+0 != -1. Every MonoDevice ioctl wrapper tests it first.

entries.name: MonoDevice_GetFlag
entries.description: (dev): returns the dword at dev+4, which MonoDevice_SetFlag and MonoDevice_ClearFlag write.

entries.name: MonoDevice_SetFlag
entries.description: (dev): dev+4 = 1.

entries.name: MonoDevice_ClearFlag
entries.description: (dev): dev+4 = 0.

entries.name: MonoDevice_Ioctl5
entries.description: (dev, byte): when open, DeviceIoControl(dev+0, 5, &byte, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0).

entries.name: MonoDevice_WriteChar
entries.description: (dev, a, b, ch): when open, DeviceIoControl(dev+0, 6) with the 6-byte {int16 a, int16 b, int16 ch}.

entries.name: MonoDevice_WriteText
entries.description: (dev, a, b, text): when open, DeviceIoControl(dev+0, 7) with the 0x58-byte {int16 a, int16 b, int16 length, char[82]}, the text cut to 0x50 characters.

entries.name: MonoDevice_Ioctl4
entries.description: (dev, byte): when open, DeviceIoControl(dev+0, 4, &byte, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0).

entries.name: MonoDevice_Ioctl2
entries.description: (dev): when open, DeviceIoControl(dev+0, 2) with no buffers.

entries.name: MonoDevice_Ioctl3
entries.description: (dev): when open, DeviceIoControl(dev+0, 3) with no buffers.

entries.name: Sos_BindLibrary
entries.description: Loads the HMI SOS DLL -- sos9503.dll on Windows NT-family, sos32s03.dll otherwise -- and fills the 100-entry thunk pointer table by walking the descriptor array at 004a6ab4 (stride 0x24: void** destinationSlot, then the export name inline as char[0x20]) and calling GetProcAddress for each. Refcounted through 004a6ab0.

entries.name: Eh_InitExceptBlock
entries.description: Borland C++ exception-frame prologue, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Eh_InitExceptBlock (0046b234): builds the frame's registration record (handler 0049672c, the frame descriptor passed in EAX, the live-destructor count from [006cbf74]) and links it into the FS:[0] SEH chain. Functions that construct objects with destructors call it first, which is why it has 258 call sites.

entries.name: Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount
entries.description: Borland RTL helper, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount: (object, vptrOffset) returns the destructor count in the dynamic type's typeinfo (+0x20), found through vptr[-4] and the typeinfo pointer at vptr-0xc; 0 for a null object. Every polymorphic delete adds it to [006cbf74] before calling the virtual destructor with flag 3.

entries.name: Rtl_VectorDelete
entries.description: Borland RTL _vector_delete_ (named by its own error string 'Illegal mode in _vector_delete_' at 004a79fc), the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Rtl_VectorDelete: (array, elemSize, count, mode, dtor). Takes the count from array[-1] when mode & 0x10, runs dtor(elem, 2) on each element from last to first under the mode & 7 calling convention, then frees the block with Mem_DeleteArray when mode & 8 and returns 0; otherwise returns the block start.

entries.name: Rtl_VectorNew
entries.description: Borland RTL _vector_new_ (named by its own error string 'Illegal mode in _vector_new_' at 004a7a1c), the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Rtl_VectorNew: when passed no memory, allocates elemSize*count bytes with Mem_NewArray (plus a 4-byte count prefix when mode bit 0x10 is set), then runs the element constructor once per element at elemSize stride. Worth having named because it appears in the middle of data-structure loaders -- e.g. the HeightGrid cell array allocation in TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap -- where it can otherwise be mistaken for domain logic.

entries.name: Rtl_PureVirtualCalled
entries.description: Borland's pure-virtual handler: pushes "Pure virtual function called" (004a7a3c) and calls __ErrorExit (import thunk 004966a8). Fills every abstract slot -- 24 vtables in DBSIM hold it.

entries.name: g_ShapeDetailSizeScaleQ10
entries.description: Q10 factor the projected size is scaled by before the threshold comparison in Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel. Written by ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting from g_HercDetailScaleValues, which holds 2000 for all five settings; the image's own initialiser leaves it at Q10 one (1024).

entries.name: g_ShapeDetailBias
entries.description: Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel's starting root index -- the floor on how fine any machine is drawn. Written by ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting from g_HercDetailBiasValues {4,3,2,1,0} indexed by the HERC DETAIL preference byte DAT_004d1fc5, so setting 0 is the crudest and 4 the finest. Zero in the image; the runtime value is the load-bearing one.

entries.name: g_BaseDeathStageCount
entries.description: How many stages each of the four structure death sequences runs: 8, 6, 6, 2. The last of five parallel four-entry tables indexed by a BASES.DAT component record's +4; the others are the collapse explosion type (004973fc), the hold after it (00497404), whether that explosion goes off at the object's origin (0049740c), and the smoke explosion type (00497414).

entries.name: Light_PersistentCount
entries.description: Entry count of Light_PersistentList (004a9690).

entries.name: BeamQuadIndexOffsets
entries.description: Four INT16s {1, 0, 1, 2}, the per-corner offsets Beam_LoadResourceTables adds when building BeamQuadIndexTable. Element size is set by the builder's own 'word ptr [ECX*2 + 0x498640]'; read as bytes the quads collapse to a degenerate edge.

entries.name: CollisionTable_Count
entries.description: int16: the number of 6-byte collision model entries CollisionTable_Reserve has handed out.

entries.name: DmgTable_Count
entries.description: int16: the number of 12-byte .DMG component tables DmgTable_Reserve has handed out, one per mech and flyer type.

entries.name: maybe_ComponentDependencyList
entries.description: Dependency list walked by Component_DestroyAndCascade to find and destroy dependent components.

entries.name: MissileAmmoNameTable
entries.description: 4 char* indexed by a PROJ.DAT Missile record's subtype id: SARH, ARH, ARM, EO. Read only by WeaponMount_GetDisplayName, with no bounds check -- MISSL (id 21, subtype 4) reads one past the end.

entries.name: WeaponMountNameTable
entries.description: 33 char* in weapon-id order -- the simulator's own weapon names, walked by Weapons_LoadResourceTables into each WeaponMountTemplate's +0x52. NOT the SHELL0/GAM/WEAPONS.DAT catalog's names: id 7 is 'EMP' here and 'EMPC' there, id 30 'SHIELD' vs 'SHLD'. Ids 13-16 hold bare round counts ('6','8','10','24') because a launcher never prints this name.

entries.name: ElfMountVtable
entries.description: The ELF/ELF2 weapon-mount vtable. MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts's case for weapon ids 6 and 22 runs WeaponMount_CtorEnergy and then overwrites the object's vtable pointer with this, so an ELF is an energy mount with five slots replaced: +0x28 ElfMount_FireDispatch, +0x2c ElfMount_CanFire, +0x30 ElfMount_TriggerHeld, +0x34 ElfMount_SpinUpAndChargeTick, +0x5c WeaponMount_EnergyIsSpent. The charge, power-level, wake, priority and gauge slots are NOT replaced, so an ELF carries and charges an ordinary capacitor and prints an ordinary bar.

entries.name: BehaviourStateTable
entries.description: The 22 AI behaviour state descriptors, 0x3e stride, zero-filled in the image and built at startup as C++ statics from BehaviourSlotBlocks. Descriptor layout: +0x00 name pointer into BehaviourStateNames, +0x04 a dwell time in MILLISECONDS before the state reassesses (50000 for combat states, 10 -- under one tick -- for the rest), +0x08 sixteen one-byte flags expanded from a 16-bit mask by Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits, bit 0 suppressing the dwell countdown, +0x18/+0x24/+0x30 the think/move/reassess triples, +0x3c a short of 0 or 3. 004993a4 + 22*0x3e lands exactly on BehaviourSlotBlocks, which is what fixes the count at 22. States 0/1/2 are 'deciding'/'player'/'player fly', the three Mech_Constructor installs.

entries.name: BehaviourSlotBlocks
entries.description: 22 unmarked 0x24-stride blocks of pointer-to-member-function triples {func, thisDelta, vtableIndex}, the source the AI behaviour state descriptors at BehaviourStateTable are built from at startup. Slot +0x00 is the state's think function, +0x0c its move, +0x18 its reassess; the static initialiser at 00413ed4 copies them to descriptor +0x18/+0x24/+0x30 respectively. 18 of the 22 move slots hold Mech_MovementTick (0041a360) -- those are the 18 states sharing the walk move, not one entry per mech type; 00499928 is block 1's move slot, and the blocks start at 004998f8. Full layout in docs/simulation/ai-dispatch.md.

entries.name: FlyerBehaviourSlots
entries.description: The flyer behaviour class' three pointer-to-member-function triples, each {func, thisDelta, vtableIndex}: +0x00 the slot the dispatcher at 00415b38 reads (0041c194), +0x0c the per-tick move (Razor_MovementTick), +0x18 empty. The walker set is the identically shaped block at 0049991c, whose move slot is Mech_MovementTick. Mech_Constructor picks between three behaviour instances by (is this the local player, does the type record set the flyer flag), so Razor_MovementTick runs for the player's RAZOR alone.

entries.name: BehaviourStateNames
entries.description: 22 packed NUL-terminated AI behaviour state names, the game's own, in table order: deciding, player, player fly, attacking, flanking, facing off, attacking base, attacking flyer, patrolling, travelling, following, bulldog travel, search/destroy, sleeping, skirting, guarding, driving off en, ramming, fleeing, in limbo, dead, disabled. Each descriptor's +0x00 points at its entry. No xrefs -- reached as base + offset by the static initialiser.

entries.name: FlyerBehaviourStateTable
entries.description: The Flyer class' seven behaviour descriptors, stride 0x3c. Zero-filled in the image and built by Flyer_BuildStateTable (00414c65). Two bytes shorter than the mech table's 0x3e because a flyer descriptor carries no OBJECTIVE: string index. Order: deciding, attacking, patrolling, search and destroy, sleeping, scouting, dead.

entries.name: FlyerBehaviourSlotBlocks
entries.description: Seven 0x24-byte source blocks, one per flyer behaviour state, holding the think/move/reassess member-function triples Flyer_BuildStateTable copies into each descriptor's +0x18..+0x3b.

entries.name: FlyerBehaviourStateNames
entries.description: Seven packed NUL-terminated names for the flyer behaviour states, the game's own: deciding, attacking, patrolling, search and destroy, sleeping, scouting, dead.

entries.name: SlideDamageScaleByDifficulty
entries.description: short[4] {400, 800, 1200, 1600} -- scale on the damage Mech_CollisionTest deals the player for a long downhill slide, indexed by MissionDifficulty.

entries.name: TargetingPodComponentRotation
entries.description: The seven component slots [Tab] cycles a HERC target through: 0, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10. Read only by Mech_NextTargetableComponent, twice. Seven of the machine's twenty-nine slots, across both the chassis band and the systems band of Mech_AiSelectAimComponent's table.

entries.name: ThrottleLeverMode
entries.description: Joystick throttle-lever mode: 0 = no lever (keyboard/plain stick), +1 = lever present, -1 = lever present with its sense inverted. Set by FUN_00459d20, which writes 1 only when the input config reports a throttle control AND the preferences page assigns it to THROTTLE rather than TURRET, and 0 otherwise; the key command (Sim_PollPlayerInput case 5) and the cockpit slider commit (FUN_00448378) only flip between +1 and -1 and are gated on that same pair. Not a forward/reverse gear selector, which is the obvious reading of the +1/-1 values: DBSIM has no gear. In Mech_ApplyThrottleInput it gates two things: the absolute-lever read (|axis-0x100|*2, deadbanded below 100) and the throttle clamp, which spans the full +/-0x400 at 0 and closes to one side of zero otherwise. That is why holding the keyboard throttle down walks a HERC through zero into reverse.

entries.name: AirframeContactImpactFx
entries.description: A PROJ.DAT-shaped 12-entry ImpactFX table held in the image rather than in a file, used for airframe contacts alone: shield {11,11,11,11}, ground and armour both {0,1,4,5}. Statically initialised, and pointed at by AirframeContactShot+0x0a.

entries.name: AirframeContactShot
entries.description: The shot record Razor_MovementTick reuses for every airframe contact, refilled per probe. +0x00 pointer to a stack ray {transform*, length = airspeed, clearance}, +0x04 armour damage (Q10 of airspeed for a ground contact, a flat 1000 or 5000 for an object one), +0x06 shield damage, always 8000, +0x08 splash 0, +0x0a AirframeContactImpactFx, +0x0e attacker = NULL so a collision is nobody's kill, +0x14 the aircraft itself, which is Sim_RaycastObjectList's second exclusion.

entries.name: LockTone_PhaseSounded
entries.description: Mech_LockTonePlay's blink latch: set once the lock tone has sounded for the current phase of the 0x40-coarse-tick cadence, cleared when that bit goes low, so the tone plays once per phase rather than every tick.

entries.name: LockTone_WasLocked
entries.description: Mech_LockTonePlay's edge latch: set while a lock is held, so that losing it plays trgunloc (0x16) exactly once. The branch that consumes it returns before the target-changed test, which is why switching target while locked plays the loss tone and not the acquisition blip.

entries.name: FlatObj_Vtable
entries.description: Vtable of class FlatObj (Borland RTTI at 0041bcf6: 'FlatObj', 0x41 bytes). Five slots: FlatObj_Draw, SimObject_GetPosition, FlatObj_Destruct, Stub_ReturnZero, SimObject_GetShapeRadius -- no tick, so a FlatObj is static unless its owner moves it. Every spawner writes type 9 at obj+0x04, the tag ObjList_DrawCellObjects draws on the spot with the ramp row count zeroed.

entries.name: AiAimScatterByDifficulty
entries.description: short[4] {1000, 800, 400, 200} -- how far Ai_FireAtPoint throws a Cybrid machine's aim off, indexed by MissionDifficulty.

entries.name: g_ShapeDetailThresholds
entries.description: The LOD root threshold table, seven int32s {75, 60, 45, 25, 18, 12, 6} in projected pixels. MechType_InitOne writes this one address into EVERY mech type record's detail struct at +0xe2, so it is a single global table and not per-chassis data. Descending, so Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel advances while the shape is SMALLER than the entry -- the opposite sense to TSDetailPart_Render's ascending per-part table.

entries.name: g_MechTextureGroupNames
entries.description: 7-entry array of pointers to the literal strings 'light'/'medium'/'heavy'/'enemy'/'apocatex'/'razortex'/'newhercs' (the strings themselves start at 0049a437, 0x0049a37c holds an 8th unrelated pointer -- not part of this array, unresearched). Confirmed dead in DBSIM.EXE's own code (zero xrefs to the array base or any individual string, checked both via ReferenceManager and a full-binary decompiled-text scan) -- DBSIM does NOT read this table at runtime to pick a mech's DBA. The real runtime mechanism is MechType_TextureGroupIndex (see that entry) feeding g_MechTextureGroupSlots directly; this string table is very likely leftover linked-in rodata from the same shared ThreeSpace source file, present in the binary but never actually executed. Byte-verified against the 7-name set in docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: s_mforms_0049a46b
entries.description: String literal 'mforms', mechsys.cpp's dat\MFORMS.DAT resource name (joined with the 'dat' folder prefix by FUN_00492ae0 in Mech_LoadResources). Sits in a literal pool alongside other mechsys.cpp string constants (difficulty names, texture-bank names) immediately followed by the source-file name 'mechsys.cpp' itself -- typical MSVC layout for a translation unit's string constants. No Reference object existed to this address before Mech_LoadResources was manually disassembled, because that function itself was never auto-analyzed; found by raw byte-scanning every initialized memory block for the literal ASCII bytes.

entries.name: DamageScaleBySide0Difficulty
entries.description: short[4] {3500, 2800, 2100, 1400} -- Q10 damage factor Damage_ScaleByDifficulty applies to a shot fired by side 0, indexed by MissionDifficulty.

entries.name: DamageScaleByCybridDifficulty
entries.description: short[4] {300, 600, 800, 1000} -- the same factor for a shot fired by any other side.

entries.name: g_TerrainDrawGrid
entries.description: The zone's HeightGrid as Terrain_LoadZone constructs it (the HeightGrid_Constructor result stored through ESI at 004279ec). Scene_DrawTerrain passes it to Terrain_DrawVisibleCells.

CellWalk_Polygon's second walk-direction flag: 1 in the image, which with maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled == 0 selects the far-to-near walk. es2_xref finds one reference, the read in CellWalk_Polygon. VSHELL's counterpart is 00471884.

entries.name: g_UnusedTerrainTypeNames
entries.description: A 3-entry pointer table to the literal strings 'urban', 'waste', 'ruins' (at 0049ab82/0049ab88/0049ab8e); the 4th slot is not a pointer, so the table is exactly 3 long. Found via string xref while hunting terrain texture selection. DEAD DATA -- ES2FindAddressRefs on this address returns zero references anywhere in DBSIM, the third confirmed instance of this binary's dead-table pattern after g_MechTextureGroupNames and the RTTI type-name strings. Recorded so a future session does not re-derive it as a live terrain-type selector; note also that only URBAN.DBA exists in retail data (no WASTE/RUINS).

entries.name: ZoneFilenameTemplate
entries.description: Literal string 'zoneXXXX' -- template overwritten in place by _itoa(zoneIndex) to build each zone's base filename (e.g. 'zone504'). Confirmed against real filenames in ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL (ZONE504.DAT, ZONE504.DBA, etc.).

entries.name: maybe_DbaFolderPrefix
entries.description: Literal string 'dba' -- used as a folder prefix when building the per-zone heightmap bitmap path ('dba\zoneNNNN.dba'). Confirmed the target files exist for real (ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL/DBA/ZONE*.DBA) but the exact path-join semantics of FUN_00492ae0 weren't independently proven beyond this.

entries.name: CockpitViewShakeArmed
entries.description: Set by CockpitView_SetShakeBand and tested first by CockpitView_StepShake, which does nothing until a band has been seeded.

entries.name: CockpitShakeReseedAfterSlide
entries.description: Byte. Set by CockpitView_ApplyViewState when a view change clears an armed shake band, cleared on a change to view 4; while set, CockpitView_StepViewTransition ends every slide with CockpitView_SetShakeBand(10).

entries.name: CockpitPaletteSingleton
entries.description: Pointer to the currently-loaded cockpit-family palette object. First loaded lazily (guarded by == 0) as the literal resource 'dpl\\cockpit' (s_cockpit_0049ae69 + CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames[0]="dpl", via ResourcePath_BuildFolderName + ClassItem_LoadTaggedResource) -- confirms DBSIM loads COCKPIT.DPL by a plain literal name, not a derived/offset one, and the real retail file ES2/VOL/simvol0/dpl/COCKPIT.DPL exists under exactly that name. Later swapped to 'dpl\\impactcp' (IMPACTCP.DPL, also a real retail file) as a second, smaller damage/impact-flash palette, whose colors get copied into a 24-entry sub-range of the global active display palette (Palette_InstallRange(0x2a, 0x18, ...)) rather than replacing CockpitPaletteSingleton wholesale. No index-remap/offset was found anywhere in this load path -- decoding a real .HB0 through COCKPIT.DPL with a direct, unmodified index lookup produces a correct, recognizable cockpit image (visually verified against APOCA.HB0/SAMSON.HB0).

entries.name: CockpitOverride_Index
entries.description: int16, the -C name's index in the 13-name table at 0049ac64, written by CmdLine_SetCockpitOverride. The cockpit view manager stores it at +0x27 in place of the machine's when CockpitOverride_Name is set.

entries.name: CockpitOverride_Name
entries.description: char*, the -C name, null unless CmdLine_SetCockpitOverride matched one. Replaces the herc name the cockpit view manager and the canopy-crack art take from the machine.

entries.name: g_TheaterHzline
entries.description: Pointer to the theater's hzline, the sky backdrop. World_LoadTheater stores it (Hzline_Ctor) and fills it from the .WLD's first eight int16s; Scene_DrawTerrainPass reads it once a frame. Every access in 0049aee0-0049aef8 is by absolute address.

entries.name: World_FlatSetSelector
